home_pitcher_note: Myers makes his second straight Opening Day start after a whirlwind 2007 season that ended with him as the team's closer. Myers appears to have made a seamless transition back to the rotation, with a 1.13 ERA in three spring starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chico, who changed his mechanics late in Spring Training, delivered a solid rookie campaign in 2007, going 7-9 with a 4.63 ERA in 31 starts for Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels sputtered through another Grapefruit League season with lackluster results, but the confident lefty isn't concerned. He had a poor Spring Training in 2007, then won 15 games. His biggest goal this season is to stay healthy,  something he'll have to do if he's going to realize his goal of winning 20 games.
away_pitcher_note: Redding said he is feeling better after back problems, so expect him to pitch against the Phillies. Redding acknowledged he was able to relax a little more this offseason because he was able to show he still is a quality pitcher. Last season, Redding was one of the feel-good stories on the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran begins his 22nd season in the Major Leagues with 230 career wins. Fourteen of them came last season, including one on the final day of the season that clinched the National League East.
away_pitcher_note: One of the reasons behind Bergmann's success this spring is the return of his sinker. Last season, Bergmann abandoned the pitch after walking six batters and giving up four runs against the Diamondbacks on April 5.

home_pitcher_note: Signed as a free agent on Feb. 21 to a one-year contract, Fogg earned the No. 4 spot in the rotation during camp. His spot will split up two young and hard-throwing right-handers in Johnny Cueto and No. 5 starter Edinson Volquez. With the Rockies in 2007, Fogg made five starts against Arizona and was 2-1 with a 2.40 ERA, including a victory in the NLCS in which he allowed one run in six innings. In 13 starts lifetime, he is 7-1 with a 3.54 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick's Grapefruit League performance has sparked concern that the NL has caught up to the second-year right-hander. Regardless, Kendrick earned a spot based on his 2007 performance, when he emerged from Double-A and stabilized a desperate rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Harang struggled with control for an inning, giving up two homers and two walks in the third en route to an Opening Day loss. The righty was otherwise effective but still seeks his first win.
away_pitcher_note: Following an up-and-down Spring Training, Eaton�s quest to redeem himself following a disappointing 2007 season begins on Saturday at Great American Ball Park against the Cincinnati Reds.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Volquez's debut with the Reds. The right-hander was acquired in December from the Rangers in the Josh Hamilton trade. While Hamilton tore it up for Texas during Spring Training, Volquez earned the rotation's fifth spot with a sensational spring of his own. The 24-year-old was 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in six spring games, including two starts. He impressed with his ability to change speeds. He could freeze hitters with an excellent changeup that worked off of his mid-90s mph fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Brett Myers said he stunk in his second Opening Day assignment. Without the use of an effective curveball or slider, he had a hard time surviving with just a fastball. The righty paid for it in the fifth inning, surrendering four runs -- three earned -- in an 11-6 loss. He's 2-0 with a 3.74 ERA in seven career appearances against Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo pitched five innings Wednesday, with two of his four runs allowed being earned runs. He gave up four hits and three walks and struck out five but left the game trailing by a 4-2 margin. However, the Reds got him off the hook when they won, 6-5, on Edwin Encarnacion's walk-off homer in the bottom of the ninth. Arroyo did not face the Phillies last season. In six games, including five starts lifetime, he is 1-3 with a 4.34 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels returns to the scene of his Major League debut on May 12, 2006, when the kid allowed one hit in five innings, though he walked five. He is 1-0 with an 0.64 ERA in 14 career innings against the Reds. The lefty is coming off a stellar effort in his 2008 debut, but came on the wrong side of a 1-0 loss to Washington. He was brilliant save for a shaky first-inning and the homer allowed to Ryan Zimmerman.

home_pitcher_note: Perez's '08 debut was a lopsided affair and not only because the Mets scored 13 runs behind him. He buried the Marlins, allowing five singles and a walk and striking out eight in six shutout innings. He'll have five days' rest when he pitches the Mets' opening home game, as Pedro Martinez's stand in, against a team that beat him twice in three games last season.
away_pitcher_note: The venerable lefty didn't have a very good start to his 22nd Major League season, and lasted only 3 2/3 innings. Five of the six runs scored off him came in the first inning, though he wasn't helped by two errors. He's gone 3-3 with a 2.59 ERA in eight starts at Shea Stadium, and 6-3 with a 2.87 ERA in 14 career starts against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey will have gone 11 days without pitching. Not recommended. He has opposed the Phillies once in his 18 big league starts, losing to them in Philadelphia July 1 last year. He allowed two earned runs in five innings. Jim Rollins hit a two-run against him.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick started 2008 in the same manner that allowed him to survive 2007. He put runners on base, then made the right pitch at the right time to keep the damage to a minimum. This has become a Kendrick standard. His outings won't look beautiful, and he won't strike out many, but he won't lose him composure, either, and that counts for a lot. He beat the Mets last season, allowing two runs in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maine needed 96 pitches to complete four innings in his 2008 debut and more offense from his teammates to avoid a loss. The Braves fouled off many pitches and didn't hit him all that hard. Maine has been quite successful against the Phillies -- 4-0 record and 2.13 ERA in six career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Eaton turned in a stellar 2008 debut on Saturday, allowing two runs in 7 2/3 innings. To put that in perspective, he lasted that long in a game once in his 30 starts last season. While one start can't erase the misery of his 10-10, 6.29 ERA year in 2007, Eaton and his teammates were encouraged by his economical outing. He is particularly good against the Mets, with a 5-0 record and a 2.68 ERA against them in seven career outings.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is still trying to find himself after lasting just five innings in each of his first two outings. The righty said he didn't have his best stuff in his first start, then had his best stuff the next time, but still couldn't get any outs. He suspects that he may be tipping pitches. He made his Major League debut against the Cubs on July 24, 2002, and is 5-3 with a save and a 2.53 ERA against them in 11 career appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano had no problems with cramps in his last start. Big Z struck out seven and gave up seven hits over seven innings against the Astros last Sunday. He did not walk a batter, and has issued one walk in his first two games. That's a significant improvement. Zambrano was better on the road than at home last season; let's see if that continues. In 2007, he was 12-4 with a 3.06 ERA away from home, and 6-9 with a 4.96 ERA at Wrigley. He did not face the Phillies last season.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels continued his dominance of the Reds at Great American Ball Park with seven strong innings Monday afternoon. The left-hander allowed just one earned run on five hits. He walked three and struck out four in a 100-pitch outing. Hamels made a stellar effort in his 2008 debut but came on the wrong side of a 1-0 loss to Washington. He was brilliant save for a shaky first inning and a homer allowed to Ryan Zimmerman.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly was cruising through the first three innings of his last start against the Pirates, then threw 35 pitches to eight batters in the fourth before he was pulled. What was mystifying was that he had a 7-0 lead at the time. Lilly was charged with five runs on seven hits and two walks in 3 2/3 innings. He's 1-1 with a 3.46 ERA in two career starts against the Phillies. Manager Lou Piniella thinks Lilly needs to speed things up; Lilly thinks he needs to slow down. We'll see who wins.

home_pitcher_note: The left-handed Moyer rebounded from a poor first outing to limit the Mets to two runs in six innings on April 8, helping to spoil the final home opener at Shea Stadium. The 45-year-old, in his 23rd Major League season, faces the team for which he made his Major League for on June 16, 1986. He is 2-0 with a 3.75 ERA in four career outings against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis was scratched from his start on Thursday against the Pirates because he was ill. If he can't go on Sunday, left-hander Sean Marshall, called up from Triple-A Iowa on Wednesday, will start in his place. Marquis is coming off a no-decision against Houston on April 5 in which he gave up five runs, four earned, on eight hits over 5 1/3 innings. Marshall was a starter this spring, but added as a long man in the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has turned in two quality starts for the Phillies so far in 2008, rebounding nicely from a rough 2007. Eaton held the Mets to three runs in six innings on Thursday, before New York went on to win it in the 12th. Manager Charlie Manuel said that he has been impressed recently by Eaton's aggressiveness in the strike zone. In six career starts against Houston, Eaton is 3-1 with a 4.42 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon turned in a quality start in his last outing on April 8, but he did not factor in the decision. He yielded three runs over six innings in a Houston loss to St. Louis. He had control issues early, throwing more than 30 pitches in a second inning during which he walked three. Chacon said he didn't think he'd go deep in the game after throwing so many pitches so early. Chacon pitched in three games against the Phillies last year, allowing four runs over 2 2/3 innings. In his career, Chacon is 1-2 with four saves and a 5.87 ERA over 10 games vs. the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: The sophomore right-hander had a rough outing Wednesday, walking a career-high six in 2 1/3 innings. When he found the plate and forced the Mets to put the ball in play, his defense let him down, causing only one of the seven runs scored on his watch to be earned. He has never faced the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is 0-3 for the first time in his career. The Houston ace has been hit hard, allowing 16 runs in as many innings and 32 baserunners. Opposing batters are hitting .400 against Oswalt, or 142 points higher than the career batting average against the right-hander. Oswalt is 5-1 with a 3.02 ERA against the Phillies for his career, though he allowed 10 earned runs in 12 innings (two starts) against Philadelphia last season.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Myers looked as comfortable as he's been since his return to the starting rotation. He allowed three runs over eight innings while striking out five and walking none to earn his first win of the season by beating the Cubs. In six lifetime starts against Houston, Myers is 2-2 with a 5.59 ERA. Myers' most recent start against the Astros was his final start of 2007 before becoming the Phils' closer.
away_pitcher_note: Backe teamed up with relievers Geoff Geary, Doug Brocail and Jose Valverde in a combined nine-hit shutout of the Marlins in his last start on Saturday, the righty's first victory since Sept. 29, 2007. Backe needed 105 pitches, including just 58 strikes, to get through five innings in a performance that he called "effectively wild." His defense bailed him out on a several occasions as the Marlins stranded 14 baserunners. Backe will need to have better command against a dangerous Colorado lineup. Backe is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA in three career appearances vs. the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is coming off a win over the Cubs, in which he threw seven innings of scoreless one-hit ball. The lefty has been the Phillies' most reliable starter in the early weeks of 2008, turning in three quality starts in three outings. The 2007 All-Star didn't face the Mets during the Phillies' most recent trip to Shea Stadium, but he is 1-1 with a 2.77 ERA against them in four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Santana lost his second straight decision last Saturday against the Brewers, serving up three home runs in his worst outing yet as a Met. Extending his pitch count to 113, Santana struck out seven and walked two, though the homers accounted for four of the five runs against him. He'll make his first appearance in this rivalry with the Phillies on Friday night, and will also make his career debut at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer is coming off a no-decision against the Cubs on Sunday in which he allowed four runs over five innings, striking out two and walking one. His lone win this season came against the Mets on April 8, when he held New York to two runs in six innings. A matchup to watch here will be Moyer against Mets first baseman Carlos Delgado. Delgado has hit eight home runs off the southpaw, second only to Manny Ramirez's 10.
away_pitcher_note: Though the Mets built an early lead for Perez on Sunday against the Brewers, he quickly lost it, serving up six runs in his second straight no-decision. Perez couldn't escape the fifth inning, allowing eight hits in total -- one of them a home run into Shea Stadium's second deck. The lefty struck out four and walked three. Perez pitched well in his first start against the Phillies, but a high pitch count limited him to only 5 2/3 innings of shutout ball.

home_pitcher_note: In the midst of a nice rebound from a miserable 2007, Eaton has allowed three runs in each of his three outings and pitched at least six innings. The Phillies have been so impressed with him that they juggled their rotation to allow for him to start on April 15, then be in line to toss against the division-rival Mets. The right-hander is 5-0 with a 2.90 ERA in his career against New York.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey pitched the strongest game of his career last Tuesday against the Nationals, completing seven innings for the first time since cracking the big leagues and holding a Major League opponent scoreless for the first time in his life. That's a tough act to follow, but he'll do his best against the Phillies, a team he's already seen once this year. Pelfrey beat them in his season debut, allowing two runs over five innings, and holds a 3.60 ERA against them in 10 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: On Wednesday night, Redman was effective with his changeup while holding the Padres to two runs and three hits over five frames to earn a win. Instead of simply throwing the fastball in the strike zone and having batters chase the changeup, he threw the change for strikes, baffling San Diego. Redman is pitching through a heel injury, but as long as he stays in the strike zone and gets quick outs the pain does not affect his pitching.
away_pitcher_note: After a six-walk performance against the Mets on April 9, Kendrick returned to attacking the strike zone on April 16, and it resulted in his best performance of the season. The right-hander allowed three runs in six innings in a start at Coors Field last season.

home_pitcher_note: After three bad outings -- one wiped out mercifully by rain, two that counted -- Francis was in top form in his last outing. He threw seven shutout innings, gave up three hits and struck out seven at San Diego, but wound up with a no-decision because Jake Peavy threw eight shutout innings. Francis has not been pitching outside effectively, but that didn't matter against the Padres. He was getting strikes and bad swings on the outside part of the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Myers has found a groove. After two subpar starts to start the season, the right-hander has allowed four runs in 15 innings. He's coming off a stellar start in which he held the Astros to one run and five hits in seven innings on April 17. Myers has thrived at Coors Field, with a 4-0 record and a 2.63 ERA there in four outings.

home_pitcher_note: Bush, still looking for his first victory of the season, had his fourth start pushed back to allow for the return of Yovani Gallardo on Sunday. Bush allowed seven earned runs in 10 1/3 innings in two appearances against Philadelphia last season. He's 0-0 with a 6.23 ERA in four career appearances vs. the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Numbers-wise, Hamels' last outing was his worst this season. He surrendered five runs (four earned) on eight hits in a 6-4 loss to the New York Mets on Friday. But Hamels actually pitched well until he reached the eighth. That?s when he imploded, as the Mets scored three runs on four hits. Hamels is 1-0 lifetime against the Brewers, with a 3.60 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan pitched well for 6 2/3 innings Saturday at Cincinnati. He left with a 3-1 lead, but took a no-decision when Joey Votto tied the game with a two-run home run in the eighth off Brian Shouse. Suppan allowed two earned runs on just three hits, walked one and struck out three. It was an improvement from his previous outing at New York, in which he lasted just four innings. Suppan threw just 87 pitches Saturday, meaning he should be well-rested to make his fifth start.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer is coming off two good starts in his last three outings. He went six innings and yielded just two runs on seven hits in losing his first start this season, 4-2, on Saturday against the Mets. Moyer, who saw his ERA drop from 5.52 to 4.79 in the loss, is 8-5 with a 3.69 ERA lifetime against Milwaukee, though ht got thumped in his only start against the Brewers last season, surrendering five runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: For the first time in his now four starts this season, Duke was hit hard due to a lack of command. Though he has given up at least eight hits in each of his first three starts this season, the left-hander had mastered damage control. That is, until he faced the Cubs on Sunday. Duke lasted just four innings, giving up five runs and allowing 12 baserunners. Duke will be making his third career start against Philadelphia. He is 1-1 with a 3.65 ERA against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Eaton gave the Phillies another strong outing in his last start against the Mets on Sunday. In five-plus innings, the righty gave up six hits and four earned runs while striking out four and walking one. Eaton was especially solid until the top of the potent Mets lineup got to him in the fifth. Eaton threw 93 pitches, 56 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: In Morris' last start on April 21 at PNC Park, he got the hook early following two Marlins home runs. The veteran right-hander lasted only four innings and gave up eight runs on nine hits. It was the third consecutive loss for Morris, who hasn't won a game since Sept. 26. However, Morris does have a strong history against the Phillies. He is 5-3 with a 3.57 ERA against the cross-state rival.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander got roughed up in Denver's thin air, allowing five runs on eight hits in five innings. He luckily received a no-decision when the Phillies came back to win. Kendrick has faced the Pirates once, securing a win by allowing one run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Though Maholm said afterward that he didn't possess his best command in his start against the Marlins on Tuesday, the lefty proved to be the stopper a spiraling rotation desperately needed. Maholm had enough command to be able to go to any of his four pitches at any given time, and finished the night with six innings of work. He allowed just one run in four hits while striking out six. Maholm will be making his fifth career start against the Phillies. He is 2-1 with a 6.50 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Myers followed two strong outings with a weaker one, though Coors Field isn't the easiest place to pitch. The right-hander gave up six runs on 11 hits in that contest, including two home runs. He's gone 2-3 with a 2.31 ERA in six career appearances vs. Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 0.82 ERA in his first three outings, Hamels has a 5.79 ERA in his past two, having allowed nine runs in 14 innings. He threw 121 pitches in his April 23 outing against Milwaukee -- striking out 11 -- but lost because he gave up two home runs to Prince Fielder. Hamels has never beaten the Padres, the team for which he grew up rooting, in three career meetings.
away_pitcher_note: Maddux will hope that the third time will be the charm as he tries again for his 350th career win. In his last outing, he was two outs away from that milestone win when closer Trevor Hoffman gave up a game-tying homer in the ninth to Bengie Molina. Maddux had pitched seven scoreless innings, allowing just four hits. He didn't walk a batter and struck out five. He threw 75 pitches, 51 for strikes. This came on the heels of one of his worst outings ever when he allowed six runs in the first inning against the Diamondbacks. In that game he threw 113 pitches, the most he had tossed in a start in 2 1/2 seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Somehow, the 45-year-old Moyer escaped six innings against the Brewers, allowing one run. It was vintage Moyer on many levels, including two pickoffs to erase mistakes. The lefty has allowed three runs in his previous two starts, spanning 12 innings. He has started 16 times against San Diego, posting a 7-6 record with a 4.41 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Other than allowing a home run to Rich Aurilia in his last start, Young didn't allow much else, as he struck out a season-high 10 batters while tying a season-low with three walks. Better still, he only allowed two hits, the home run and Eugenio Velez's double in the fourth inning. Yet, he still got the loss as San Diego failed to score. Young made some mechanical changes that have helped him with his command. "That was his best command and velocity," Padres manager Bud Black said. "We saw that coming in his last start."

home_pitcher_note: Eaton didn't get out of the third inning in his previous outing, Friday in Pittsburgh. A former Padre, he will be making his second career start against San Diego, having picked up a win by allowing two runs in 5 2/3 innings on July 20 last season.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf returns to Philadelphia, where he played from 1999-2006 and was an All-Star in 2003. Wolf suffered his first loss on April 25, when he allowed five runs in four innings in a loss to Arizona. Wolf retired six of the first seven batters he faced before allowing a single to Miguel Montero to start the third. He later allowed an RBI double to Chris Young and an RBI single to Orlando Hudson right before leaving a 2-1 changeup up in the strike zone to Mark Reynolds, who drilled a three-run home run. Wolf had difficulty throwing his curveball for strikes and getting ahead of hitters.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old Kendrick has never faced the Giants in 25 career starts. The only player on the Giants roster he has faced is infielder Jose Castillo, who is 2-for-3 with a double against him. The Phillies are 16-9 when he starts.
away_pitcher_note: Misch was recalled from Triple-A Fresno on Sunday, when right-hander Kevin Correia was placed on the disabled list with a strained left side. Misch pitched that day after Barry Zito allowed eight runs in three innings and saved San Francisco's bullpen by gobbling up the final six innings. Misch surrendered only two runs, both on homers by Cincinnati's Brandon Phillips. Since 2006, Misch is 0-4 with a 3.99 ERA in 20 Major League appearances, including four starts. He's not overpowering, but he's capable of maintaining effectiveness by hitting the corners with his fastball and changing speeds.

home_pitcher_note: Myers struggled in his last outing at Pittsburgh, giving up eight hits and four earned runs in five innings. He seemed to lose some zip off his fastball and had trouble locating his curve ball. Myers has also been hurt by the long ball, allowing 10 homers in 37 innings. Myers has surrendered at least four earned runs or more in three of his past five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cain ended a winless stretch of 10 starts on Monday by pitching 5 1/3 scoreless innings against Colorado. Although Cain still was throwing in the mid-90s in the sixth inning, he had trouble harnessing his stuff, throwing 108 pitches and walking five. The Giants even scored four runs for him, a veritable bonanza. San Francisco has scored no more than one run with Cain on the mound in 17 of his 38 starts dating back to the beginning of the 2007 season. Cain has struggled against the Phillies, posting an 0-2 record with a 9.69 ERA in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels pitched 7 1/3 strong innings in his last start against the Padres while picking up his third win of the season. He allowed only five hits and two earned runs with six strikeouts. Once again, the left-hander was consistently in the strike zone and used his changeup effectively to keep the Padres off balance.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum is coming off his first loss of the season, a respectable 3-2 setback to Colorado on Tuesday, when he worked seven innings and allowed all of the Rockies' runs. Lincecum struck out four in seven innings after entering the game with 36 in 29 1/3 innings. He missed a chance to become only the second San Francisco Giant to open the season's first month with a 5-0 record; John Burkett did so in 1993. Lincecum, who made his Major League debut against Philadelphia last May 6, has no record in two appearances against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer made his Major League debut Tuesday night and it's one that few who watched will forget. The right-hander was summoned from the bullpen with two outs in the third and proceeded to retire all 13 batters he faced. Scherzer, who was the D-backs' No. 1 pick in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, struck out seven and his electric fastball reached 98 mph at times during the dominating performance. Scherzer takes Edgar Gonzalez's spot in the rotation. He throws a slider and changeup in addition to the fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer gave the Phillies 5 1/3 innings in his last outing, Wednesday against the Padres, but he was hurt by the long ball -- a pair of them, to be exact. Moyer gave up nine hits and four earned runs while throwing 98 pitches, 62 for strikes. It was only the second time in six starts that he surrendered more than three earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson scuffled in his last outing against the Astros, allowing six runs on nine hits over four innings. That came on the heels of his best outing of the year when he beat the Padres at PETCO Park for career win No. 285. Johnson allowed just one run over six innings in that game. He has made four starts since beginning the year on the disabled list due to back surgery.
away_pitcher_note: Eaton pitched well in his last start against the Padres, giving up five hits and two earned runs in six innings. He threw 102 pitches, 60 for strikes, and seemed to settle down after allowing two runs in the first inning. Eaton is still searching for his first victory of the season, and he continues to keep the Phillies in the game.

home_pitcher_note: Owings had his poorest outing of the season on Friday against the Mets. The right-hander did not have his good command and struggled from the start as he allowed seven runs on 11 hits over 5 2/3 innings. He has been bothered by a sprained right ankle which occurred in the start before last when he doubled and rolled his ankle when he stepped on second base. In his last two starts, Owings has allowed 12 runs in 10 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander received a no-decision in his previous outing, when he allowed three runs in six innings against the Giants, on eight hits. He uncharacteristically struck out six, matching a career high set last season. While Kendrick will accept the strike outs, he relies on contact and his defense making the plays behind him. He has never faced Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Webb has won all seven of his starts this season. Hot starts are nothing new for Webb, as he started the 2005 season 6-0 and opened the '06 campaign with franchise-best 8-0 mark. In his last outing, the right-hander allowed four runs on five hits over six innings. Three of the runs came on a Carlos Delgado homer in the sixth inning. Webb's changeup has become a valuable strikeout pitch when he gets to two strikes. Webb won the National League Cy Young Award in 2006 and finished second in the voting to San Diego's Jake Peavy last year.
away_pitcher_note: Myers' fastball velocity improved from his previous two outings, and the right-hander used it more to set up his other pitches, as he always should. Myers needs to keep that momentum for his start against the undefeated Brandon Webb. Myers has made five career appearances against Arizona and is 2-1 with a 3.00.

home_pitcher_note: Misch is still looking for his first Major League victory. He saw his ERA blow up from 3.00 to 5.40, after a pair of two-run homers he surrendered against the Phillies' Chase Utley and Pedro Feliz in a no-decision on May 2, at Citizens Bank Park. Misch lasted just four innings against the Phils, giving up five hits and striking out two.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels acknowledged mistakes in his last outing against San Francisco, in which he allowed four runs in six innings, though he left the game with the score tied. On nights when Hamels is on, he's unhittable, and he'll need to be on against Giants ace Tim Lincecum. Hamels is 2-0 with a 3.86 ERA in three career outings vs. the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum received a no-decision in his last start, on May 4 against Philadelphia. He gave up four runs -- all unearned -- but he didn't help himself very much over six innings, though his ERA dropped from 1.73 to 1.49. Lincecum threw two wild pitches in the fifth that led to a pair of Philadelphia runs. He struck out five and walked two. It marked the third time this year Lincecum didn't surrender an earned run.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer danced his way around a dangerous and aggressive lineup of young Diamondbacks hitters to secure his second win of the season. Despite throwing nearly 12 miles and hour than opponent Max Scherzer, Moyer limited the NL West leading D-Backs to two runs in seven innings. He is 4-5 with a 2.73 ERA in 10 career outings vs. San Francisco.

home_pitcher_note: Complaining of a flat mound at Pittsburgh's PNC Park that forced him to elevate his pitches last Tuesday, Sanchez allowed six hits and seven runs in 4 1/3 innings in a 12-6 loss. It was his worst outing since his 2008 debut on April 4, when he yielded seven runs in four innings at Milwaukee. Between those two performances, the Giants won all five of Sanchez's starts as he posted a 2-0 record with a 1.82 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies are praying that Eaton hasn't regressed back to 2007, when he compiled a 6.29 ERA. The right-hander began the season with three quality outings, but has posted a 7.23 in his past four starts. His big mistake on May 6 occurred on a bases-loaded, four-pitch walk to Randy Johnson, the first run of a five-run inning. Eaton can't seem to stay away from crucial lapses.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander's ERA has slowly declined over his last three starts. While he's allowed 25 hits in 19 innings against the Braves, he's limited the damage to three earned runs each time. He's tossed 11 innings spanning two starts, and posted a 4.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Reyes left Thursday's game against the Padres in the third inning after a blister developed on the index finger of his pitching hand. After the game he said he doesn't expect to miss his next scheduled start, his third of the season. Reyes allowed one earned run on five hits in 2 2/3 innings against the Padres. Against the Reds on April 30, Reyes pitched 5 1/3 strong innings, allowing one run on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is stymied by what has been a frustrating return to the starting rotation. He had his worst outing on Thursday, allowing six earned runs on nine hits and three walks in five innings to Arizona. Catcher Chris Coste hopes Myers doesn't try to change to much, since he thought Myers' stuff was plenty good enough. Myers has thrown more innings against the Braves than any other opponent, posting a 4-6 record and a 4.16 ERA in 24 appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Glavine has allowed three earned runs or fewer in each of the four starts that he's lasted at least five innings. Still, for the first time in his career, the 42-year-old southpaw is still winless six starts into a season. He kept the Pirates scoreless before surrendering a seventh-inning, two-run, two-out single in Friday's no-decision. He was 2-0 with a 2.14 ERA in five starts against the Phillies last year.

home_pitcher_note: Despite good overall numbers, Hamels has been in a downward trend since posting an 0.82 ERA in his first three starts. In his next five outings, he went 2-2 with a 4.98 ERA, uncharacteristic results from the team's best pitcher. In those outings, he's allowed fewer than four runs once, though he still logs innings. His six career starts against Atlanta has produced a 3-2 record and a 4.42 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: James pitched six innings in his last start, Saturday against the Pirates, allowing five runs on five hits, striking out seven while walking four. It was James' fourth start with the Braves. He also has made three appearances (two starts) with Triple-A Richmond. James left two pitches over the middle of the plate in Saturday's game and it cost him. Pirates left fielder Jason Bay hammered a two-run home run to right-center field in the fourth inning, and catcher Ronny Paulino hit a two-run double that gave the Pirates a 5-2 lead in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: The 45-year-old is coming off his worst outing of 2008, an effort in which he allowed six earned runs in four innings, and allowed nine hits for the fourth time in eight starts. His ERA is in line with his 2008 performance, and he still has the ability to keep the Phillies in games. The lefty has made 36 appearances vs. Toronto, going  13-8 with a 5.31 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to inclement weather that forced the Jays and Indians to postpone their game on Sunday, Toronto will need an extra starter for the opener of an Interleague series in Philadelphia. The likely candidate is Purcey, who was called up from Triple-A Syracuse to make a spot start for the Jays on April 18. The lefty is 3-3 with a 2.22 ERA in seven starts at Triple-A this season.

home_pitcher_note: Eaton's line against the Giants looked respectable -- two runs allowed in five innings -- only because San Francisco consistently left runners on base. The right-hander was mostly frustrated with walking five batters. He beat the Blue Jays in his only outing against them, tossing six shutout innings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett pitched the first game of a doubleheader against the Indians on Monday and wound up on the wrong end of a tight ballgame. He allowed three runs on five hits over 7 2/3 innings, striking out seven and walking three in a hard-luck 3-0 loss to Cleveland. Burnett is 4-7 with a 4.70 ERA in 15 career games against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick started off rocky before settling down nicely in his last start against the Braves on Tuesday. Despite allowing three first-inning runs, the young right-hander came back to throw six solid frames, allowing six hits and three earned runs. Kendrick did struggle a bit with his control as he walked four. He threw 97 pitches, 53 for strikes but showed signs of the pitcher who won 10 games as a rookie.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum limited Cleveland to just two hits over eight shutout innings in his last start. He was able to get out of a couple of jams, as Cleveland loaded the bases in the second and had a leadoff double in the fourth. Marcum, who depends heavily on finesse and his ability to set up hitters, has a 1.19 ERA over his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Redding pitched six solid innings and gave up one run on two hits against the Mets. He struck out four batters and walked two others. New York took a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the sixth off Redding, when Brian Schneider took a 2-0 pitch and hit the ball over the right-field wall for his second home run of the season. But Redding became the winning pitcher when the Nationals scored four runs in the top of the seventh inning.
away_pitcher_note: Nothing is working for Myers, who has now allowed six earned runs in two straight starts. His velocity was largely there, but location and pitch selection have betrayed him. He seems like an open book, with hitters seemingly knowing what's coming, and teeing off. Myers suspected earlier this season that he was tipping pitches, but pitching coach Rich Dubee had ruled that out. Myers will be the first Phillie to pitch at Nationals Park. He's 7-7 with a 4.91 ERA in 27 career appearances against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: On Thursday afternoon, Bergmann found himself in a pitchers' duel with Mets right-hander Mike Pelfrey. When it was over, it was Bergman who came out on top as Washington defeated New York, 1-0, at Shea Stadium. Bergmann was dominating. He pitched seven shutout innings, gave up three hits, struck out nine and walked two. The weird thing was, Bergmann was in control without having a good fastball. It was his slider and curveball that helped keep the Mets off balance.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels can't be much more dominating than he was May 15 against the Braves, when he tossed a four-hit shutout, throwing 120 pitches. Three of the four hits were singles, and he walked two while striking out six. He's gone 4-3 with a 2.49 ERA in 10 career starts vs. the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: With the Nationals wanting Shawn Hill to rest his ailing right elbow, Chico will face the Phillies. Chico began the season as a starter, but he was demoted to the bullpen after four consecutive bad outings. The major reason for the bad starts was because Chico was pressing on the mound. However, it has been a different story out of the bullpen. He has given up just one run in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer was solid in his last start. He went 6 2/3 innings, surrendering seven hits and three earned runs in a 10-3 victory over Toronto on Friday. It helped to get great run support, as the Phils vaulted out to an 8-0 lead after three innings. It was one of Moyer's best starts, rebounding from two previous poor starts.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt was hit hard in his last start, allowing six runs on 11 hits before leaving the game in the seventh inning with a strained right groin. He is listed as day-to-day and his status for this start is uncertain. Oswalt had recorded six consecutive quality start before the outing at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, and the 11 hits were the most the right-hander had allowed since Opening Day. Oswalt beat the Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on April 16 with a seven inning effort, allowing one run on five hits.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick's previous outing was a wash, literally, when a two-hour, four-minute rain delay ended his day after one perfect inning. Not including that inning, the right-hander has allowed three earned runs in each of his previous four outings, and pitched at least six innings in all of them. He has one career start against the Astros, and lost despite allowing two runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Backe turned in perhaps his best outing of the season in his last start, when he held Texas scoreless for 6 1/3 innings at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington before back-to-back homers by Milton Bradley and David Murphy ended his day in the seventh. Backe did not walk a batter for the first time this season, and combined with his one walk performance in his previous start, it's an encouraging trend for the right-hander.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander continued his downward spiral in his previous start. He was pulled after allowing four runs in five innings and allowed the first three batters to reach in the second inning, then surrendered a grand slam to Rod Barajas. The poor performances threaten his status as a starter, as manager Charlie Manuel could flip Chad Durbin to the rotation and demote Eaton to the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: This may be Moehler's last start, considering Wandy Rodriguez is due to come off the disabled list sometime early next week. Moehler yielded three runs over five innings in a loss to the Cubs, evening his record at 1-1. The right-hander threw a season-high 95 pitches, walking two (one intentionally) and striking out one.
away_pitcher_note: The struggling right-hander made some progress in his previous outing, Monday vs. the Nationals. He allowed three runs in six innings, and had a few positive results in tight spots. Considering how his season has gone, that has to be viewed as an improvement. He's 3-2 with a 4.91 ERA in seven career starts vs. Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson's up-and-down season experienced an upswing during his last start, after he held the Cubs to two runs over 6 2/3 innings in a winning effort that raised his record to .500. The right-hander yielded a two-run homer to Aramis Ramirez in the fourth inning, but retired nine of his next 10 batters. Sampson has not faced the Phillies yet this year. Lifetime versus Philadelphia, he's 0-2 with a 6.19 ERA over four games.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty hasn't given up a run since the fourth inning of a May 9 game against San Francisco, a span of 19 innings. Seven of those frames came in his previous outing against the Nationals, when he allowed four hits and struck out 11. It was almost unfair watching him make it look so easy. In four career starts against Houston, Hamels is 3-0 with a 3.14 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer has had a strong May, going 3-1 with a 4.18 ERA in four starts, including the most recent one, which was his best of the season -- no runs in six innings against the Nationals. Moyer also has walked only four batters this month, covering 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa's numbers for the season aren't good, and his high pitch counts are preventing him from getting deep into games, but in his last three starts, he won one and pitched well enough to keep the Rockies in the other two. On Monday night, he pitched 5 1/3 innings and gave up three runs, two earned, in a no-decision that the Rockies eventually won over the Giants. De La Rosa labored for the first three innings, then corrected himself by slowing down his upper body and pitched well the rest of the time he was in the contest.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick pitched five-plus innings, taking a no-decision in his last start on Thursday at Houston. He allowed five runs on eight hits and a walk, striking out two. In his last seven starts, Kendrick is 2-0 with five no-decisions and the Phillies are 6-1 in those starts. He hasn't lost since April 16 vs. Houston. Kendrick is 0-1 with a 7.00 ERA in two career starts against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez had what may have been the best performance of his career, matching his career high with seven innings and making them all scoreless for the first time. He was extremely efficient, putting his strikeouts on the shelf (only one despite entering the game averaging 8.11 K's per nine innings) in favor of the ground ball, recording 16 of his 21 outs with grounders. He focused on the bottom of the strike zone, getting balls in play rather than the swings and misses that come from his hard breaking ball and slider and his high fastball, and he hit 96 mph in his final inning.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Eaton went seven innings and allowed three runs on eight hits in a 4-3 loss to the Astros. Manager Charlie Manuel called it the best he'd ever seen Eaton, who has seven no-decisions and three losses in his 10 starts this season. Including the Astros loss, he has had five quality starts with nothing to show for them. Against the Rockies, he's 8-12 with a 6.32 ERA in 25 career games.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Reynolds struck out four Mets his first time through the order and entered the sixth inning having given up just two hits. A double play not turned opened the door for Reynolds to give up back-to-back home runs to Carlos Delgado and Fernando Tatis, and he wound up with a no-decision in the Rockies' 13-inning victory. However, Reynolds struck out five in six innings, and used his fastball, breaking pitch and changeup as "out" pitches as he continued to demonstrate the talent and poise that made him the second overall pick in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Myers lost his fourth straight start as he went six innings and allowed four runs on eight hits in a 4-3 defeat at Houston. Myers threw a season-high four walks and tied his season low with only two strikeouts. Myers has five losses and two no-decisions in his past seven starts and hasn't won since April 17 against the Astros in Philadelphia. For his career, he's 5-7 with a 5.01 ERA in 25 games against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday against the Giants, Mark Hendrickson allowed five earned runs, while throwing 97 pitches -- 56 for strikes. He struck out five and walked two, but benefited from four home runs hit by the Marlins to pick up his seventh victory. Hendrickson didn't have his best stuff -- he scattered nine hits -- but did battle out of several jams, including a first-and-third jam with one out in the fifth. Hendrickson struck out Rich Aurilia and Travis Denker to end that threat.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels saw his ERA jump from 2.61, which was fourth in the NL, to 3.18 in his last start as he allowed a season-high six runs on seven hits and a walk. Hamels, who was third in the league in strikeouts with 65 entering the game, also didn't record a strikeout in the four innings, his shortest outing of the season. Against Florida, he has a 2-2 record with a 4.13 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Considering his history against the Mets, Nolasco will take the outcome of his last start. It was a battle, but the right-hander gave up three runs in five innings, while scattering nine hits. Entering that game, Nolasco had a 1-3 career mark with the Mets, including a 10.80 ERA. Still, Nolasco was able to scratch out his fourth win. Nolasco has won three straight decisions, over a four-start span. His best performance came on May 21, when he yielded one run on three hits in a win over Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer lasted seven innings in his most recent start, against Colorado on May 26. The left-hander allowed four runs, striking out seven and walking only one. Moyer allowed a three-run home run to Ryan Spilborghs in the first inning, but was able to bounce back and hold the Rockies to one run through the ensuing six frames. He has enjoyed considerable run support lately -- in his last three starts, the Phillies have pounded opponents for 42 total runs.
away_pitcher_note: Surrendering two-out runs was problematic for Miller in his last start. Three of the four runs he allowed against the Mets at Shea Stadium came with two outs. For Miller, the loss at the Mets marked his shortest outing (4 2/3 innings) in five starts. He also had two strikeouts, which was off the pace of his personal most nine in a May 22 win over Arizona. The 23-year-old lefty still has won four of his last six decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has been giving the Phillies chances to win -- the team has won seven of his last eight starts. In his most recent start, on May 27 against Colorado, Kendrick lasted 7 1/3 innings -- his longest outing of 2008. He gave up two runs while striking out five and walking only one. In two career starts against the Marlins, Kendrick is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo pitched on three days' rest and gave up one run on just three hits with four walks and six strikeouts in six innings of work against the Pirates on Wednesday. Arroyo gave up a season-high four walks through the first 4 2/3 innings. Arroyo has been sensational over his last five starts, compiling a 3-0 record. He last faced the Phillies on April 7 when he gave up five runs on nine hits with no walks and six strikeouts over 5 2/3 innings. He surrendered a season-high four home runs in that start and was credited with the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Eaton has turned in six quality starts in 2008, but hasn't had much to show for his efforts. The right-hander notched his first victory of the year in his most recent start, Wednesday against Colorado. Eaton allowed just one earned run against the Rockies -- his lowest total of the season -- and one walk, which matched his lowest total of the season. He faced the Reds on April 5 and lasted 7 2/3 innings while giving up three runs in a no-decision. In six lifetime starts against Cincinnati, Eaton is 2-0 with a 4.19 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Harang endured his toughest outing of the season in his last start. He lasted just four innings and gave up six runs on 10 hits with two strikeouts in a loss to the Pirates. His fastball, which usually sits in the low 90s, didn't reach the 90-mph mark until the third inning, and struggled to stay there for the rest of the night. Six of the hits he gave up were doubles. The four innings marks the shortest start of the season and ties for his shortest appearance of the year, as he pitched four innings in relief at San Diego on May 25. The two strikeouts were a season low, and the six runs were a season high. The 10 hits tied a season high. Harang's last start against the Phillies came on April 5 when he pitched seven innings and gave up two runs on six hits with three walks and six strikeouts in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander feels he made significant progress in his previous outing, when he allowed three first-inning runs, but no more in an eight-inning stint. He struck out 11 in the game and was pleased with his ability to locate, something he has struggled with all season. He surrendered four runs in five innings to the Reds on April 6.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez pitched six innings and gave up two runs on five hits with three walks and seven strikeouts in receiving a no-decision. It marked just the second time this season that Volquez has given up more than one earned run in a start. He was obviously feeling the affects of pitching 1 2/3 innings in relief during an 18-inning game the previous Sunday against the Padres. Pitching for the third time in a week, his mid-90s fastball hovered in the low-90s for most of the night. His location was also a bit off, as just 59 of his 102 pitches went for strikes. Volquez last faced the Phillies on April 6, when he pitched 5 1/3 innings and gave up one run on five hits with two walks and eight strikeouts in a winning effort. It was hist first win of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has been roughed up a bit in his past two starts, allowing 13 runs in 9 2/3 innings against the Marlins and Astros. Those followed two superb outings, however, as he threw seven innings of shutout ball against the Nationals on May 20 and a complete-game shutout against the Braves on May 15. Toss the past two starts and Hamels is having an exemplary season.
away_pitcher_note: The Reds made official their plans to call up Homer Bailey from Triple-A Louisville to start on Thursday against the Phillies, marking the top prospect's 2008 debut in the Majors. Bailey, 22, was 4-4 with a 4.15 ERA in 12 starts for Louisville this season. Bailey went 4-2 with a 5.76 ERA in nine starts for the Reds in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson left during the seventh inning of Sunday's game with a strained left hamstring, and was reevaluated by Braves doctors on Monday in Atlanta. Before exiting, Hudson allowed four runs -- three earned -- on seven hits and struck out three in six innings. Hudson allowed a home run in the second and third inning, the third time in four starts he has given up two homers in a game. Hudson walked three on Sunday, and it was only the third time this season that he has issued three or more walks in a game.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer earned his team-leading sixth win on June 1 against the Marlins. Moyer allowed two early home runs to Florida's Mike Jacobs, falling behind by four runs. But the veteran lefty battled back, lasting seven innings, striking out three and walking none to earn the win with a little help from his offense. The Phillies' offense has been particularly helpful to Moyer lately. In his last six starts, Moyer has received an average of about 10 runs of support.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes has pitched effectively in five of his seven starts this season and proven that he's at least improved the control issues that plagued him last year. Still, after he allowed three earned runs and issuing just one walk in six innings on Monday against the Marlins, manager Bobby Cox said the 23-year-old southpaw needs to reduce the number of pitches he leaves in the middle of the plate. When Reyes faced the Phillies on May 13 in Philadelphia, he allowed five earned runs and 11 hits in 6 2/3 innings. But he didn't issue a walk and threw first-pitch strikes to 27 of 32 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick lasted 5 1/3 innings in his last start, June 2 against the Reds. The right-hander held Cincinnati scoreless through the first three innings before running into trouble with home runs to Jay Bruce and Edwin Encarnacion. Kendrick has started three games against the Braves in his career and is 2-0 with a 4.24 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo gave up two home runs to Dan Uggla in his start Tuesday against the Marlins. In his 16 previous appearances this season, Campillo had allowed just one homer. He also didn't pitch into the fifth inning for the second time in his past three starts. Braves manager Bobby Cox pulled Campillo after he reached the 80-pitch mark, hoping that Campillo will be able to throw about 100 pitches against the Phillies. The four earned runs Tuesday were three more than he had allowed in 15 previous innings as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Eaton lasted 6 1/3 innings Tuesday against Cincinnati, giving up one run and three hits while striking out five and walking none. It was Eaton's third quality start in a row, his best stretch since his first three starts of 2008. Eaton did not face the Braves when they visited Citizens Bank Park in May, but he has eight lifetime starts against them. Eaton is 3-3 against Atlanta with a 6.14 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco had his four-game winning streak snapped in his last start, losing 7-5 to the Braves in Atlanta. He worked 5 2/3 innings and allowed 12 hits, three of which were home runs. He pitched against the Phillies on May 31 in Philadelphia, earning the victory. He went 6 2/3 innings, giving up four hits and two runs.  He struck out five and walked two. Nolasco is 2-2 in his career against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Myers kept a no-hitter going into the seventh inning of his last start, on Wednesday against the Reds. However, the right-hander conceded a run that inning and ended up taking the loss. Still, his last two starts have shown that his season is looking up after starting out 2-5 with a 5.76 ERA through his first 10 starts. In 19 career starts against the Marlins, Myers is 6-7 with a 4.89 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: At least in the first inning, Miller's last outing started off pretty promising. He fanned the first two batters he faced, but he labored after that. In a loss to the Reds, the 23-year-old gave up four runs in a 3 1/3 innings, matching his season low for innings pitched. He has now dropped two of his last three decisions. On June 1 at Philadelphia, he worked five innings, but was not involved in the decision. He exited with a two-run lead that wasn't preserved.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels was back to his old self in his most recent start. He threw the second shutout of his career, holding the Reds to three hits while striking out four and walking three. The lefty was happy with his ability to locate fastballs low in the zone against Cincinnati, something he had struggled with in his two previous starts, when he allowed 13 runs over 9 2/3 innings. In five career starts against the Marlins, Hamels is 2-3 with a 5.46 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen pitched perhaps the best six innings he's thrown all year during his last start against the Reds on Saturday. But his defense left him with his third straight no-decision. Olsen registered six full innings without giving up an earned run on four hits, a walk and five strikeouts. But shaky defense on the infield made him leave in a 4-4 game. Olsen -- who retired 13 straight batters at one point -- had two outs in the sixth inning when Brandon Phillips' ground ball went off third baseman Jorge Cantu's glove, allowing a run to score. Then, after first baseman Wes Helms let a grounder go off his glove, Andy Phillips hit a three-run double down the left-field line to tie the score. In the bottom half of that inning, Olsen -- who had an RBI single earlier in the game -- was replaced for a pinch-hitter after throwing 85 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer gave up two runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings, and was in line for the loss Friday if not for a Braves error with two outs in the ninth. Moyer surrendered a two-run homer and a triple in the sixth, before leaving with one out. In his last five starts, Moyer is 4-0 with a 3.94 ERA (14 ER in 32 innings). He hasn't lost in his last five starts, and has pitched at least six innings in that same span. Against the Braves, Moyer struck out four and walked three, which tied a season high.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer sat out his last scheduled start with an inflamed right elbow, but he's back on track to start Saturday. In his last start, Wellemeyer pitched six scoreless innings and gave up just five hits with a walk and five strikeouts against the Nationals. The five hits tied a season high, but it was the second time he's held an opponent to no earned runs. He hasn't lost a start since April 28.
away_pitcher_note: Kyle Kendrick was effectively erratic for five innings on Saturday against the Braves, but he gave up a two-run homer in the sixth inning to spoil his opportunity for a sixth win. Kendrick pitched 5 1/3 innings, and his teammates said after the game that they wished the 23-year-old right-hander could pitch deeper into games. Still, the Phillies are 10-4 in games started by Kendrick this season, which has to help his confidence as he continues to learn on the fly. Kendrick is 2-0 lifetime against St. Louis. Both wins came last season. In his last start against the Cardinals, on Sept. 17, 2007, Kendrick allowed three runs on seven hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse gave up a long, long home run to Houston's Lance Berkman in his last start Sunday and not much else. He limited the Astros to five hits and three runs over six innings, striking out three and walking two. He has won his last four starts and hasn't lost since May 9. This will be Lohse's first appearance this year vs. Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: pitched six innings and threw 99 pitches in hot and humid conditions on Sunday, but didn't factor in the decision against Atlanta. He gave up three runs on six hits, and his only real mistake was a pitch up in the zone to Mark Teixeira that he hit for a two-run homer in the first inning. Eaton stranded seven baserunners, working in and out of jams in the second, third and fourth innings to keep the Phillies in the game. Eaton is 1-4 with a 6.82 ERA in seven career starts against St. Louis. He has allowed six earned runs in each of his past two starts against the Cardinals, both of which came last season. In his most recent start against them, on July 15, 2007, he surrendered six runs on 10 hits in four innings and got the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Boggs was solid in his first Major League start on Tuesday while filling in for Todd Wellemeyer, who was nursing an inflamed right elbow. He pitched five innings and gave up two runs on four hits with three walks in a 7-2 victory over the Reds. He made his professional debut June 6 against the Astros, when he pitched two innings in relief and allowed a solo home run.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies hope Myers' outing on Tuesday wasn't a regression to his early-season form. The right-hander was sloppy against the Marlins, allowing five runs on three home runs and fell behind in too many counts. He had a 2.35 ERA in his previous two outings, including a 7 1/3-inning, one-hit performance on June 4. If his location and breaking pitches continue to be poor, he'll continue to struggle.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels stuck out 13 on Wednesday against Florida, his highest total of 2008. For the second consecutive start, the 24-year-old lefty looked firmly in command, walking only one and giving up two earned runs on three hits over eight innings in earning a no-decision. Hamels has never faced the Red Sox during his first three seasons in the Majors, meaning he'll have to contend with some of baseball's most explosive hitters -- such as Manny Ramirez and David Ortiz -- for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: The big righty has been one of the best early-season stories in baseball. The man who was unemployed in February has won four of his first five starts for the Red Sox. Colon has given up three earned runs or fewer in four of his five outings. Colon has made four starts in his career against the Phillies, going 1-1 with a 4.00 ERA. This will be his first start at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer is coming off his longest and best outing of 2008, one in which he beat the Marlins in Miami with eight shutout innings and allowed only two hits while walking one and striking out three. The 45-year-old lefty is now 5-0 in his last six starts. The Red Sox will be somewhat of a familiar foe for Moyer, who spent most of his career in the American League and is 6-11 in 20 lifetime starts against Boston. One matchup to watch out for is Moyer vs. slugger Manny Ramirez, who has tagged the lefty for 10 home runs, more than any other hitter.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has thrived of late, earning victories in his last two starts. In his last outing, he allowed seven hits and two runs over seven innings in a win over the Orioles. Two starts ago, he defeated the Rays, giving up eight hits and a run over 6 1/3 innings. Lester has given up three earned runs or less in six of his last eight starts. Lester is holding opponents to a .249 average.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick turned in a workmanlike performance while receiving staggering run support in his last outing. The right-hander went seven innings and allowed just two runs (one earned) in a 20-2 win. Kendrick's ability to focus with a big cushion was pleasing to manager Charlie Manuel. The Phils are 10-1 in Kendrick's last 11 starts and 11-4 overall in his starts. Kendrick got through seven innings on 94 pitches and allowed just one walk and eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, the right-hander suffered his first loss in the Majors -- but had one of his best outings. He set new career bests in innings (6 2/3) and strikeouts (nine) while walking three. Masterson was undone by the home run ball, giving up long balls to Jay Bruce on a slider and Adam Dunn on a sinker. This could be Masterson's last start if Daisuke Matsuzaka is cleared to return from a mild strain of his right rotator cuff.

home_pitcher_note: Eaton enters this game with a string of five consecutive quality starts. He went 6 2/3 innings against St. Louis on Saturday and allowed just three runs. The big issue for Eaton is getting out of the first inning without surrendering a home run. In each of his last two starts, Eaton has given up a first-inning homer (Mark Teixeira and Adam Kennedy) before settling down and pitching effectively.
away_pitcher_note: Santana cruised through the first four innings against the Braves on Saturday, but ran into trouble in both the fifth and six innings. He lasted 5 2/3 innings, allowing six earned runs on nine hits, including solo home runs to Brandon Jones and Kelly Johnson. He didn't pitch at least six innings for only the second time this season and picked up his third loss. Santana has never faced the Phillies, but is 5-1 with a 3.50 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Myers' 3-8 start to 2008 is his worst in seven Major League seasons. At times this season, the Phils' Opening Day starter has pitched effectively and kept his team in games. But that wasn't the case Sunday against the Cardinals, when Myers imploded for six runs in six innings, allowing two home runs to increase his league-leading total to 20. In one career start against the Angels in 2003, Myers lasted 5 2/3 innings, allowing five runs and taking the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders bounced back from his worst start of the season to blank the Braves for 7 1/3 innings on Sunday. He mixed his 91-93 mph fastball with a nasty sinker to allow just five hits while striking out five and walking two. He became the third American League pitcher to win 10 games. Saunders has never pitched against the Phillies, but carries a 5-1 record with a 1.77 ERA on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels held the Red Sox to two runs in seven innings on Monday. His seventh win of the season puts him into a tie for the Phillies team lead. Hamels has now put together a string of three consecutive quality starts, and the Phils are now 10-5 when he takes the hill. Hamels' matchup against the Angels will mark his second consecutive start against a team he has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver's roller-coaster ride continues. Coming off one of his finest efforts against the Rays, he was pounded by the Mets for six earned runs on eight hits, including a pair of Carlos Beltran homers, across 6 1/3 innings on Monday night. Weaver had appeared to find his rhythm with three scoreless innings when he yielded a pair of hits and departed, both runners scoring. He's facing the Phillies for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton had his worst outing of the year the last time out, as he surrendered eight earned runs and seven hits in just three innings of work against the D-backs at Chase Field. After being the victim of a lack of run support in recent games, Blanton lacked command right out of the chute, allowing five runs in the first and three more on a Dan Haren bases-loaded double in the third. The A's are 4-12 (.250) in his starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer struggled with his control Tuesday against the Red Sox, walking five in five innings of work. The free bases cost the veteran lefty, as Boston built an early lead that the Phillies' offense could not surmount. The loss to Boston was Moyer's first since losing in San Francisco on May 10. In 43 lifetime starts against the Athletics, Moyer is 17-15 -- including two shutouts -- with a 4.46 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Smith will be making his 15th start of the year after getting a no-decision in his last start against Arizona. He gave up one run on just three hits in five innings against the Diamondbacks, marking the second consecutive game he posted those exact numbers. Smith has never faced the Phillies in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick hit an early wall against the Red Sox on Wednesday. He allowed back-to-back home runs in the first inning and ultimately left the game after allowing six runs in three innings. The rough outing against the defending World Series champs may prove to be just one blemish on Kendrick's season. The Phillies have, after all, won 10 of his last 12 starts. Kendrick has not yet faced Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Harden got his sixth no-decision of the season in his last start against Florida. In 5 2/3 innings, he gave up just one run on five hits while walking two and striking out five in a back-and-forth game that eventually ended in a 7-6 A's win. It was the eighth time this season he had allowed two runs or fewer and the fourth time he walked two batters or fewer. Harden has never faced Philadelphia but is 2-0 with a 0.69 ERA in Interleague Play this season.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander regressed after a string of five straight quality starts when he allowed 12 hits in five innings on Friday to the Angels. Eaton was in trouble all evening, starting with a first-inning, two-run home run allowed to Vladimir Guerrero. Still, with nine quality starts this season, Eaton has kept his team in the game. He is 1-1 with a 4.91 ERA in his career vs. the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Gabbard earned his second win of the season and first since April 4 with a 13-3 victory over the Nationals on Saturday. He is now 1-1 with a 5.73 ERA in two starts since returning from a two-start trip to Triple-A Oklahoma. In 11 innings, he has allowed 14 hits and five walks while striking out nine. He is 0-1 with a 5.63 ERA in three starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington this year. He has never faced the Phillies in his short career.
away_pitcher_note: A promising Saturday outing for Myers was damaged by the righty's propensity for surrendering home runs. Of the six hits Myers allowed in seven innings, three were home runs. Myers' total of 23 home runs allowed leads the Major Leagues. Myers has never faced the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla is facing the Phillies for the first time since they traded him to the Rangers after the 2005 season. Padilla pitched for the Phillies from 2000-05 and was 49-49 with a 3.98 ERA in 162 games, including 111 starts. He enters the game with a record of 8-1 with a 3.28 ERA in his last 11 games. He is 3-2 with a 3.00 ERA in six starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels had a quality start Sunday against the Angels that was spoiled by a lack of Phillies offense. In seven innings, Myers allowed three runs on six hits while striking out four in taking the loss. Still, the Phils are 10-6 this season when Hamels has taken the hill. His outing against the Rangers will be his third consecutive start against an American League team that he has never before faced.

home_pitcher_note: Hurley lost to the Astros, 4-3, on Tuesday despite allowing just two runs in six innings. In three Major League starts, opponents are hitting .258 off him with 17 hits in 17 innings. He has walked five, struck out nine and allowed three home runs. Opponents are just 1-for-14 off him leading off an inning. Left-handed hitters are batting .242 off him while right-handers are hitting .273 off him.
away_pitcher_note: One bad pitch ruined a brilliant start for Moyer against the A's. He entered the seventh inning having allowed one hit through the first six innings, and striking out nine. Two bloop singles and a three-run home run by Emil Brown handed him a loss. In 13 career starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, the lefty is 4-5 with a 5.50 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has given the Braves three solid outings to start his Major League career, yet the 24-year-old right-hander now has two losses. He was dealt another tough-luck loss on Tuesday night, when he allowed four runs -- two earned -- on six hits in six innings against the Brewers. He has two quality starts in three outings, but the Braves haven't been able to manufacture runs until he is out of the ballgame. While Morton has been in the game, the Braves have scored just two runs in his past two starts, a span of 12 innings. Morton will get a taste of a division rivalry when he faces the Phillies for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old turned in the longest and best start of his career against Oakland on June 25, throwing eight shutout innings, walking one and striking out four. The win moved Kendrick into a three-way tie with Jamie Moyer and Cole Hamels for the team lead. He's started twice against the Braves in 2008, and pitched well in both outings, allowing a combined five earned runs over 11 1/3 innings. This year, the Phillies are 12-4 in Kendrick's starts -- the best record among Phillies starters.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo has become more than just a pleasant surprise for the Braves -- he's a bona fide starter with an entire arsenal of pitches. The 29-year-old right-hander tossed seven strong innings Wednesday against the Brewers, allowing two runs on four hits and picking up his first home win of the season. After allowing two run-scoring doubles, Campillo retired the next 12 batters he faced. He said his start June 15 against the Angels was better -- two runs in a complete-game effort -- but he was equally dominant against the Brewers. Campillo got a no-decision against the Phillies on June 8, when he allowed three runs on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings. He also allowed six hits in two relief appearances against the Phillies, which totaled 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has given up three or fewer runs in 12 of his 16 outings this season, and the Phillies are 7-9 overall when he starts. His June 26 performance was another example of this trend. Unfortunately, two of the three runs he allowed came in the first inning, and Oakland starter Rich Harden sailed from there. Eaton has made one other start against the Braves this season, and gave up three runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens limited the Blue Jays to three hits in eight strong innings, and has not allowed an earned run in his last 23 2/3 innings. The three hits off Jurrjens on Friday were singles. The 22-year-old right-hander has not lost since May 12, and he has lowered his ERA to 2.94. He has pitched at least six innings in each of his past four starts. Jurrjens will be making his first career start against the Phillies. He is 5-0 with a 2.49 ERA in eight home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels is coming off an outing in which he allowed four runs in seven innings to the Rangers, a considerable accomplishment against the highest scoring team in the American League. He pitched a four-hit shutout against the Braves on May 15 in Philadelphia, walking two and striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Happ's second Major League start. The 25-year-old left-hander faced the Mets on June 30, 2007, and allowed five runs on seven hits in four innings. After that start, he was sent back to Triple-A Ottawa, where he battled a balky pitching elbow. Manuel said Happ's command is much better this season, and he has thrown at least six innings in seven of his past 10 starts with Triple-A Lehigh Valley. Happ was 5-6 with a 3.54 ERA in 17 starts with the IronPigs this season. He last pitched on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Santana was outdueled in Saturday afternoon's contest vs. the Yankees, as the Mets lefty let up three earned runs in six innings to Andy Pettitte's two over the same timeframe. Despite leaving with the Mets in a hole -- a series of walks and a balk dooming him in the fourth inning -- Santana kept a struggling offense in the game by allowing only four hits and striking out eight batters. June has been Santana's best month in terms of ERA (2.27), but his record in that month fell to 1-4 after Saturday's loss. Santana has had limited work against the Phillies, as he is 1-0 with two starts vs. Philadelphia with a 3.09 ERA in 11 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer lost his third straight start Sunday, when he allowed three runs on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings against the Rangers. He struck out six and walked four. Moyer has been uncharacteristically wild in his past three starts, issuing 10 walks. But he has also struck out 19 in that span. Moyer will pitch Saturday on an extra day of rest. The veteran left-hander took a loss April 19 against the Mets, giving up two runs on seven hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Four consecutive Cardinals reached base to open Maine's most recent outing in St. Louis, and three fielding errors also conspired against him. By the time Maine's night was through, he had allowed five runs -- three of them earned -- on seven hits and three walks. He lasted four innings and 81 pitches. Maine battled similar control problems the last time he faced the Phillies, walking five batters in six innings. But the Mets won that game, and Maine improved to 4-0 with a 2.05 lifetime ERA against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Kyle Kendrick pitched well for six innings in his last start, at Atlanta, but ran into trouble in the seventh when he allowed a two-run double. He left with no outs and was frustrated that he let an otherwise great outing slip away. Kendrick still got the win, however, his eighth of the season. He is now 6-0 in his past 11 starts against National League teams, and the Phillies are 11-0 in those starts. Kendrick last faced the Mets on April 9, when he allowed seven runs -- one earned -- in 2 1/3 innings. He walked six batters that game.
away_pitcher_note: Though Tony Armas won his debut with the Mets last Tuesday, he won't earn another start. Instead, the Mets will insert Oliver Perez into his slot, aiming to separate the two lefties in their rotation. Perez hasn't started a game since holding the Yankees to one run on three hits last weekend -- his strongest performance of the year. He held the Phillies scoreless when he last saw them in April, though a high pitch count prevented him from completing six innings and stuck him with a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Eaton finally got some run support against the Braves on Wednesday, and he also finally got a win, his first since June 3. Eaton allowed one run on five hits in five-plus innings. He has allowed just four runs in his past two starts, a span of 12 innings. It was the third outing this season that Eaton had allowed less than two runs. Eaton has yet to factor in a decision in two starts against the Mets this season. He has allowed seven runs on 11 hits in 11 innings against them.
away_pitcher_note: The first six batters Martinez faced last Wednesday in St. Louis hit the ball hard, and four of them wound up scoring. Martinez never recovered. Instead, he waded through his third straight ineffective outing, giving up five runs in five innings. His ERA over that three-game stretch is 10.20, and he'll be hard-pressed to find improvement against the Phillies, one of the most potent offensive teams in the league. Martinez did find success against them last September, striking out nine Phillies and allowing one run over six innings. But he took a no-decision in an eventual Mets defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels was one out away from recording his third complete game of the season on Thursday against the Braves. But with his pitch count already at 125, manager Charlie Manuel didn't risk keeping Hamels on the mound. His rationale was that Hamels has two more starts to make before the All-Star break and a whole second half of the season to pitch. So Hamels had to settle for one run on five hits in 8 2/3 innings. He has pitched at least six innings in each of his past six starts. Hamels is 2-0 with a 4.26 ERA in four career starts against the Cardinals. In his last start, Sept. 18, 2007, Hamels gave up three runs on five hits in three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro has had a rough going for the past two months. In his last nine starts, Pineiro is winless with seven no-decisions.
