Over this time, Pineiro has pitched effectively for the Cardinals, but will be coming off a rather poor outing against the Mets on Wednesday. Over five innings, Pineiro gave up four runs and scattered 11 hits -- most of which were hit with authority. Pineiro said after the game that it was just one of those nights where he had shaky command and kept missing his spots.

home_pitcher_note: Happ made his first start of 2008 on Friday, lasting 4 2/3 innings, allowing two runs on three hits, striking out three and walking four. Manager Charlie Manuel was noncommittal regarding whether Happ's Friday outing had earned him another start, though he said he was pleased with Happ's command. The lefty was called up to fill in for Brett Myers, who was optioned to Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: With the Cardinals sending rookie right-hander Mitchell Boggs down to Triple-A Memphis, Mulder will make his first start of the year and his first since Sept. 16. Thus far, Mulder has made two appearances out of the bullpen for the Cardinals and with mixed results. In his first trip out of the 'pen, Mulder threw one inning and gave up two hits. But in his most recent appearance, Mulder struggled and lasted only one-third of an inning while giving up two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer earned his ninth quality start of 2008 on his way to a no-decision against the Mets Saturday. He lasted 6 2/3 innings, giving up three runs on seven hits. He did not start against the Cardinals the last time the Phillies faced St. Louis, but owns an all-time record of 4-1 against them in 10 starts. The Phillies started out the season 10-4 in Moyer's first 14 starts, but have lost his last four starts in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Looper could not have asked for a much better start against the Cubs on Friday. But Looper's two mistakes cost him and the Cardinals the game. While his team was unable to support him with a good deal of runs, Looper gave up two solo home runs to the Cubs and that was enough for the rivals to win. Looper is coming off throwing 120 pitches in seven innings, so it will be interesting to see how his arm rebounds after that kind of start. He said the arm felt fine and the day off between the Phillies series shouldn't hurt.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick turned in his third consecutive quality start Sunday against the Mets, allowing one run in six innings. Though Kendrick allowed eight hits and two walks, he was able to work out of several jams. In three different innings Sunday, Kendrick stranded a runner on third base. The Phillies are now 13-5 in Kendrick's starts this season, the best record among Phillies starters. Kendrick earned the victory in the Phils' 20-2 win over the Cardinals on June 13, in which he pitched seven innings, allowing one earned run.
away_pitcher_note: If it weren't for a couple mistake pitches to Scott Hairston, Davis might have had a different result his last time out against the Padres. Davis had his longest outing of the season, throwing eight innings and 122 pitches, allowing three runs on seven hits. He pitched well enough for the win, but like it has been the case for him several times this season, Davis picked up the tough-luck loss. Davis is 2-1 with a 2.92 ERA in six starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Eaton is coming off a clunker against the Mets, as he allowed eight runs -- six earned -- in a career-low 2 2/3 innings. The right-hander allowed 10 hits and a walk. His first loss against New York pushed his career ERA against the Mets to 4.08. He'll try his luck this time against a struggling Diamondbacks team. He is 3-5 with a 4.23 ERA in 14 career starts against Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson was back in vintage form in his last outing against the Padres, allowing just one run on three hits, striking out 10. The Big Unit picked up his first win since May 16 after losing his last six starts. After working on mechanics with pitching coach Bryan Price, Johnson is now just 11 wins away from 300. Against the Phillies, Johnson is 10-3 with a 2.61 ERA in 19 starts in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels will take the Phillies into the All-Star Break with his only start of the season against Arizona. The lefty is coming off a nice outing against the Cardinals, though the Phillies lack of offense left him with a no-decision. He surrendered three hits, though two of them were home runs. Hamels is a likely candidate to start the first game after the Break as well.
away_pitcher_note: Webb, who entered the weekend leading the Major League lead in wins with 13, is having another stellar season and could very well win 20 for the first time in his career. He is coming off a start in which he threw six shutout innings against the Nationals. All four of his losses, however, have come in his past 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: The team's most impressive pitcher in the first half, Nolasco is being rewarded. The right-hander will take the mound in the first game of the second half in an important series with the Phillies. Nolasco has won five straight decisions. Before the break, Nolasco was 4-2 with a 3.35 ERA in eight home games, including two starts. Early in the season, the 25-year-old pitched out of the bullpen. In his final outing before the break, Nolasco was impressive again. In six innings at Dodger Stadium, he gave up two runs on five hits with six strikeouts and one walk in a no decision.
away_pitcher_note: The 45-year-old continues to defy hitters nearly half his age, with his slow, slower and slowest pitches. He's posted a 2.63 ERA in two July starts and is coming off an effort in which he allowed one run in seven innings. He dominated the Marlins on June 12 at Dolphin Stadium, surrendering two hits in and one walk in eight shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old closed out his first half with an impressive victory, limiting the Padres to one run on four hits in eight innings. Olsen snapped a string of 11 straight starts without a victory, dating back to May 6, when he went 8 2/3 innings against the Brewers. The lefty logged 119 1/3 innings in the first half, and the long break should be beneficial, considering he has had a lack of velocity in the first half compared to how he's thrown in past years.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander continues to give the Phillies a chance to win, and the team is 14-5 in his starts. He was sailing along in his previous outing, before a troublesome seventh inning cost him a decision. He's 1-0 with a career 2.57 ERA in two starts against Florida, having allowed four earned runs in 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: As far as returns go, Johnson answered a lot of questions in his season debut. Rebounding from Tommy John surgery, Johnson threw five innings, giving up three runs against Los Angeles at Dodger Stadium on July 10. He threw 87 pitches. It was his first MLB appearance since July 4, 2007. Johnson was not involved in the decision, but he exited with a one-run lead. His fastball was clocked as high as 97 mph, and he struck out six without issuing a walk.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty held the Diamondbacks to two runs in seven innings on July 13, but earned a no-decision in a win over Arizona. It was the third consecutive start that Hamels had allowed two runs or fewer. He is 2-3 with a 4.78 ERA in six career starts vs. the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Santana, often hurt by home runs, surrendered consecutive home runs along with a single, double, and triple in one grotesque inning, the fourth, against the Reds Thursday. He allowed five runs, equaling the most he allowed in any start this season, but for the first time, all five runs were earned. He threw 92 pitches on a warm night. With an off-day Monday, he should be fully rested for the Phillies. He has allowed five runs and no walks and struck out 16 in 15 innings in two starts -- a victory and a no-decision -- against the Phillies this year.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton will have some extended rest when he makes his debut with the Phillies on Tuesday. The 27-year-old hasn't pitched since July 9, when he got shelled for six runs off nine hits in six innings against the Mariners. Blanton was scheduled to start on Friday with the Athletics, but after the trade, the Phillies moved him back to his next scheduled outing. The fifth-year pitcher will be debuting against a Mets team he has had great success against in the past. In two previous starts against New York, Blanton has thrown 15 shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: With his loss to the Reds on Friday, Maine has gone four starts without a victory -- he had lost twice -- and he has pitched merely 19 innings in the process. He has been neither effective nor particularly lucky. Maine's two starts against the Phillies this season have produced modest performances and no decisions, but each was a part of a Mets victory. His career numbers against them before this season include a 4-0 record and 2.13 ERA. And he's been more successful at Shea than he has been elsewhere -- 4-1 in nine starts -- this year.
away_pitcher_note: Myers will make his return to the Phillies' rotation in the pressure-filled atmosphere of Shea Stadium. Myers was optioned to the Minor Leagues last month to rediscover his fastball and swagger, which the righty feels he's accomplished. He made four starts at three levels, with positive results. He has not faced the Mets this season.

home_pitcher_note: The modest requirements of a quality start suggest Perez pitched well against the Reds Saturday night. He surrendered three runs, two earned, in six innings. But he emerged as the losing pitcher and not only because the Mets' offense fell short behind him. Perez walked successive batters to start the fourth; the first base runner scored. He later surrendered a go-ahead, two-out single to the No. 8 hitter. Facing a batting order with four left-handed hitters, he retired the side in order once. But now he has four straight quality starts -- and a .500 record.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer is coming off another masterful outing against the Marlins, as he limited them to two runs in six innings. The 45-year-old lefty has been equally impressive against the Mets this season, posting a 3.37 ERA against them in three outings.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick set career highs for earned runs allowed and home runs surrendered in his loss to the Marlins Saturday. Florida tagged him for seven earned runs, including three homers, in 4 1/3 innings. Still, Kendrick remains one of Philly's most reliable starters. Philadelphia has recorded a 14-6 record in his outings, the best mark among the team's starters. In five career starts against the Braves, Kendrick is 3-0 with a 4.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: A lengthy layoff during the All-Star break seemed to affect Jurrjens' control on Saturday, when he allowed the Nationals five earned runs in 6 1/3 innings. The 22-year-old rookie right-hander has lost two of his past three starts, including his July 3 outing against the Phillies. The three homers he surrendered that evening matched the total he’d allowed in his previous five starts combined. He has been inconsistent since not allowing an earned run in his final three June starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels had only two blemishes in his last start, against the Marlins on Sunday. But those two mistakes, solo home runs to Cody Ross and Jeremy Hermida, were enough to hand the lefty a no-decision. Other than that, the 24-year-old was in fine form, giving up four hits while striking out seven through eight innings before leaving with 96 pitches under his belt. Hamels had a no-hitter through three innings and retired nine straight batters at one point. His velocity, however, was down a few mph after the long layoff with the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton will make his first Major League start in 35 months Saturday when he pitches the second game of a critical three-game set against the Phillies. The 35-year-old left-hander has strained his left pectoral muscle twice this season and had his recent rehab assignment derailed by a strained left groin. But after tossing an incident-free bullpen session on Tuesday, manager Bobby Cox said Hampton would get the start Saturday in place of young lefty Jo-Jo Reyes, who has lost five consecutive starts. Hampton is 32-20 in three injury-shortened seasons with the Braves. He hasn't pitched in a Major League game since Aug. 19, 2005. He missed the entire 2006 and 2007 seasons after having separate surgeries on his left elbow.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton did not get a decision in his Phillies debut against the Mets on Tuesday at Shea Stadium, surrendering five runs in six innings. He gave up a few untimely walks and left two breaking balls up that resulted in home runs. Still, the Phillies will continue to look to the right-hander to be an innings-eater and take the place of the struggling Adam Eaton in the Phils' rotation. Blanton, having just moved to the National League from Oakland, has never faced the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: With the Braves in dire need of a win, Campillo pitched his finest outing since he became a starter in mid May. He scattered two hits -- both singles -- over seven shutout innings on Monday, needing just 91 pitches. Campillo's array of offspeed pitches fanned six Marlins, which matched his total over his past three starts. The two hits allowed were the fewest since May 24, when he pitched four innings against the D-backs before leaving with a blister. In his last start against the Phillies, on July 2, Campillo allowed five runs on eight hits in five innings and took the loss. Campillo is 0-1 with a 5.27 ERA in four games (two starts) against the Phillies this season, surrendering eight runs in 13 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Balester registered a solid outing in his last start in San Francisco. He pitched five innings, allowing just six hits and three runs for his second lowest total in four Major League starts. He also struck out two and walked two, and he threw 44 strikes in 74 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Myers allowed three runs in five innings in his return to action against the Mets on Wednesday after a three-week stint in the Minor Leagues. The 27-year-old got off to a rough start, walking four consecutive batters in the first inning. He eventually settled in, ultimately retiring the last six batters he faced. Another positive was that Myers did not allow a home run after allowing a Major-League-leading 24 before being optioned. Myers has faced Washington twice this season, recording an 0-1 record and allowing six earned runs in 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Redding picked up his first win in 10 starts on July 11 against Houston, snapping a streak of nine straight no-decisions. He pitched six innings, allowing no runs and striking out six. The seasoned right-hander said after the game that he felt comfortable with his fastball, which helped him get ahead of hitters routinely in the Nationals 10-0 win over Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer threw his fourth consecutive quality start on Thursday against the Mets -- an effort that was undone by a lack of Phillies offense in a 3-1 loss. The 45-year-old churned out seven innings, allowing one run on two hits. Moyer has been as steady as a rock for the Phils rotation, keeping opponents to three runs or fewer in each of his starts since June 1. In that span, he is 3-3 with a 2.86 ERA. Moyer is 1-0 in two starts against Washington this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals' promising young left-hander turned out another solid performance in the city of Angels on Friday night, but it wasn't enough in a 3-2 loss. Lannan threw just 101 pitches over seven innings, surrendering three earned runs -- all in one frame -- and striking out three. He tossed 62 strikes and allowed six hits.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old righty turned in a six-inning, one-run performance against the Braves Friday night that helped him bounce back from his seven-run outing against Florida on July 19. Kendrick said that his sinker, a pitch that lacked its usual bite against the Marlins, was working better against the Braves. The only run he allowed against Atlanta came on a Brian McCann home run. Kendrick has not yet faced Washington.

home_pitcher_note: As his manager is fond of saying, "even Sinatra cleared his throat once in a while." Lohse, who had been consistently excellent for the better part of three months, endured a clunker his last time out. He's still been the Cardinals' most dependable starter this year, and he's got a big assignment with the opener of a three-game series against the potent Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels endured his harshest outing of 2008 Saturday against the Braves, giving up nine runs -- four of them earned -- in one inning. He left after 3 2/3 innings on the hill, his shortest outing this season. The Phils' bats, however, exploded for seven runs in the fifth to give Hamels the no-decision. Hamels lost his only outing against St. Louis this season, when he gave up two runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Looper faces a tough task in the hard-hitting Phillies, a team that made him labor three weeks ago. In that start, at Citizens Bank Park, Looper needed 112 pitches to go six innings. However, he's coming off a very solid game in Atlanta, a game in which he righted a recent problem -- the long ball. He didn't allow a home run against the Braves, after serving up 10 in his previous six starts. If he keeps it in the park, he should be fine.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton's start against the Braves on Sunday was cut short when the game was halted for a two-hour rain delay. In two innings of work prior to the delay, the Phils' new addition surrendered two runs on three hits. Blanton will make his third start for the Phillies against the Cardinals, a team he has not yet faced, having just joined the National League after about 3 1/2 seasons with the Athletics. Before joining Philadelphia, the 27-year-old right-hander went 5-12 with a 4.96 ERA for Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer may be getting it back together after a rough stretch that followed his return from an elbow injury. His last time out he struck out five, his highest total since the injury and an indication that his offspeed offerings are coming around. The Cards have been careful with him; he hasn't gone more than 6 1/3 innings or 98 pitches since the injury.
away_pitcher_note: Myers allowed one unearned run in seven innings Tuesday night against the Nationals in securing his first win since May 30. The victory over Washington could signal a breakthrough for the 27-year-old, who was optioned to Triple-A after beginning his season with a 3-9 record and 5.84 ERA. In his second start since his return, he didn't try to overpower hitters, and he ended up walking one while scattering four hits through seven. In nine career starts against St. Louis, Myers is 3-2 with a 5.43 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: So far, Moyer has been a can't-miss starter against the Marlins. In 10 career starts, the 45-year-old is 10-0 with a 3.03 ERA against the Fish. Moyer most recently shut them down on July 18, allowing two runs in six innings. The veteran lefty recorded his fifth consecutive quality start on Wednesday night, allowing three runs in six innings against the Nationals to earn his 10th victory of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson won his first game in four starts since coming back from Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery when he held the Mets to four runs in 6 2/3 innings on Wednesday. The Marlins are now 4-0 in games he starts this season. Johnson was cruising through the first six innings, giving up one run and throwing just 79 pitches in the process. But in the seventh, he ran his pitch count into the triple digits and, with two outs, the last batter he faced hit a three-run homer. In his other start against the Phillies this season, Johnson gave up two runs in 6 2/3 innings in the no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick notched his second consecutive quality start with a win on Thursday against the Nationals, allowing two runs on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings. The Phillies are now 15-7 in the 23-year-old's starts this season, the best mark among Philadelphia starting pitchers. Kendrick last faced the Marlins on July 19 and endured perhaps the roughest start of his young career. The right-hander allowed seven runs on three home runs -- both career highs -- in 4 1/3 innings in taking the loss. In three career starts against the Marlins, Kendrick is 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note:
In his first start in almost 15 months, Sanchez picked up the win after giving up just two runs on six hits in 5 2/3 innings. Sanchez retired six of the first seven batters he faced, threw first-pitch strikes to 15 of the 25 hitters and left the game with the bases loaded and two outs after throwing 95 pitches -- 56 for strikes. 
Prior to a rough sixth inning, Sanchez only allowed three runners to reach scoring position. He finished off the night with four strikeouts and two walks.

home_pitcher_note: It's been more than one month since the Phils' ace last recorded a win, July 3 against the Braves. On Friday night, Hamels was hit hard for the second consecutive outing, yielding five runs -- four earned -- in six innings, including two home runs. Afterward, the lefty said he had left too many pitches up in the strike zone. Hamels won his only career start against the Pirates, a 2006 outing in which he surrendered three runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad wasn't his usual, sharp self in a loss to the Rockies on Friday. Making his fourth Major League start (fifth appearance), the 21-year-old rookie gave up a career-high five runs in a career-low five innings, giving up eight hits while striking out six and walking three. All of the runs charged to Volstad came with two outs. He left after throwing 93 pitches, and had his pitch count at 53 by the end of a two-run third.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton earned his first win on Saturday since joining the Phillies in mid-July. He came over from the West Coast with a reputation as a guy that could carry a team into the late innings, but his previous outing -- July 27 against the Braves -- had been cut short because of a long rain delay. Facing a Cardinals lineup Saturday that featured five hitters batting higher than .300, Blanton posted seven innings, allowing one run on four hits to earn the win. Blanton has never faced the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm's last start was an anomaly from the left-hander's dominant string of performances in recent weeks. He allowed five runs on eight hits in six innings after surrendering more than three runs in a game only once in his previous eight starts. His troubles on Saturday could boil down to one thing: location. Maholm struggled keeping the ball down, and the Cubs thrived off the mistakes. This shouldn't be too much of a setback, however, as Maholm has always shown a knack for bouncing right back.

home_pitcher_note: Myers continued to make strides since his return from a Minor League stint with a six-inning, two-run effort against the Cardinals on Sunday night in which the right-hander allowed four hits, struck out three and did not walk a batter. During the season's first three months, Myers posted a 3-9 record and 5.84 ERA before being optioned to Triple-A Lehigh Valley. In three starts since his return, Myers is 1-0 with a 2.50 ERA. Though the 27-year-old allowed a Major League-leading 24 home runs through the end of June, he has allowed just one home run since his return from the Minors. In seven career appearances against the Pirates, Myers is 2-4 with a 2.92 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Snell exited his last start due to a combination of lower back stiffness, high pitch count and inefficiency. His back tightened in the second and never loosened up, though it is not expected to cost him a start. The right-hander allowed four runs in four innings and has now pitched four or fewer innings eight times this season. On Sunday, he simply never found his fastball and never located his command. Snell is 3-2 with a 4.50 ERA in five career starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer's string of five consecutive quality starts and 10 consecutive victories against the Marlins came to an end on Tuesday against Florida. The veteran lefty yielded two runs in five innings, struggled with his command throughout the night, walking three and yielding six hits. In 11 career starts against the Dodgers, Moyer is 3-5 with a 5.19 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Davis has been named the latest in a revolving door of fifth starters for this rotation. He takes the place of Yoslan Herrera, who lasted just 1 1/3 innings in his fourth and likely final start this season. Davis started for Triple-A Indianapolis until being called up in late July to serve in a bullpen role with the Bucs. He pitched seven innings in that role and allowed two runs. In 21 games (20 starts) with Indianapolis, Davis went 6-9 with a 4.41 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Lowe was given a lead by his offense and couldn't protect it. Instead, he had his worst start and earliest exit of the year, pounded for eight runs on 13 hits in only 3 1/3 innings. Lowe's ERA at Dodger Stadium is 2.72; on the road it's 5.88. He's 3-1 with a 2.84 lifetime against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick held the Marlins scoreless on four hits in beating them on Wednesday night at Citizens Bank Park. Though he walked five, he was able to successfully work out of pressure situations. Kendrick was pleased with how well his sinker was working against Florida, a pitch he relies on heavily. The 23-year-old has made two starts against the Dodgers, going 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, the 20-year-old Kershaw has gotten very good. He didn't quite match his back-to-back six scoreless innings of his previous two starts, but in his most recent start he might have been more impressive in limiting the Cardinals to one run over seven innings because of the way their explosive offense had scored 15 runs the two previous games. Kershaw has never faced the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels has now gone six consecutive starts without earning a win, the longest winless drought of his career. In that span, Hamels has been hit hard at times, but also fallen victim to a lack of run support, such as his loss to the Marlins on Thursday afternoon. Hamels tossed 6 1/3 innings, allowing three runs -- two earned -- as the Phils were shut out for the seventh time in 2008. During his past six starts, the 24-year-old is 0-3. Hamels has never faced the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Penny returned from seven weeks on the disabled list and looked like he had just been on the disabled list, rarely surpassing 90 mph with his fastball. Somehow, he limited the Giants to only one hit in five innings and snapped a seven-game losing streak with his first win since May 2. But he walked three without a strikeout, further evidence of his rustiness.
away_pitcher_note: Though the Phillies ended up losing on Friday to the Pirates, Joe Blanton came up big, tossing seven innings of one-hit ball. In four games with the Phils, he has just one win, but he has compiled a solid 3.27 ERA and has held batters to just a .205 average.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda is coming off back-to-back strong starts, now that he is able to finish off breaking balls without worrying about his shoulder being sore. In his most recent start, the only run he allowed the Giants in eight innings scored on a sacrifice fly in an inning extended by a wild pitch third strike. It was the fourth time this year he's pitched at least eight innings. He's never faced Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Myers is cruising since his return from a July Minor League stint, recording a 2-0 record with a 2.10 ERA since re-joining the Phils. On Saturday night, he limited the Pirates to one run in 7 2/3 innings, striking out six and walking one. Myers' competitive spirit got the best of him as he exchanged heated words with manager Charlie Manuel when the skipper removed him in the eighth. In nine career starts against the Dodgers, Myers is 3-1 with a 2.76 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres decision not to trade Maddux -- or, better yet, Maddux's decision not to waive his no-trade clause for just any team -- continued to pay dividends on Aug. 9, when Maddux won his third consecutive start, which marked just the second time he's done that in his one-plus seasons in San Diego. Maddux allowed two runs over six innings, and even drove in a run with a bunt single, his first bunt single in nearly a decade. Better still, Maddux pitched into the seventh inning and did so using just 71 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer held the Pirates to three runs in six innings Sunday afternoon. The 45-year-old has now allowed three runs or fewer in each of his last 12 starts, a stretch not accomplished by a Phillies pitcher since 1967. Moyer is 7-7 with a 4.53 ERA in 17 career starts against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Reineke will make his Major League debut starting in the place of Chris Young, who is on the 15-day disabled list with a strained right forearm. Reineke, who is being called up from Triple-A Portland, is 5-10 with a 4.37 ERA in 23 games (22 starts) with Portland and Triple-A Round Rock in the Houston Astros organization. He is 0-1 with a 4.41 ERA in three starts in Portland.
away_pitcher_note: A start after tossing six shutout innings, Kendrick allowed a career-high seven runs in a start against the Dodgers. The right-hander lasted 3 1/3 innings, his second-shortest outing. He loaded the bases with one out in the third inning, then allowed six runs. He survived that inning but was taken out in the fourth after again loading the bases with one out. He has faced the Padres one other time, and he allowed one run in six innings in that outing.

home_pitcher_note: Baek didn't make too many mistakes in his last start on Tuesday against the Brewers, but there's certainly one pitch he would like back -- a fastball he left out over the plate to Prince Fielder in the fourth inning that became a three-run home run. Baek allowed four runs over six innings and was hurt when his bullpen allowed an inherited runner to score in the seventh inning. Baek continues to confound, actually pitching better away from spacious PETCO Park than when at home. He's allowed four runs in three of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: One of these days, the Phillies' ace will receive a win following one of his sterling performances, but that hasn't been the case since July 3. The lefty's streak of no-decisions reached seven Tuesday when the bullpen couldn't hold a lead against Los Angeles. He's 0-3 with a 3.60 in that span. The Phillies are 14-11 in his 25 outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander turned in his shortest non-rain-shortened outing as a member of the Phillies in his last start, when he surrendered nine hits and four runs in five innings to the Dodgers. Handed a 4-0 lead after one inning and a 6-1 advantage after two innings, Blanton kept Los Angeles in the game. He left with a two-run lead that the bullpen surrendered. He has faced the Nationals one other time in his career, and he lost.
away_pitcher_note: Bergmann had his worst outing of the season as the Nationals were pounded by the Mets, 12-0, at home last Wednesday night. Washington needed Bergmann to go deep into the game because the relievers pitched 18-plus innings in the previous five games, but he didn't get the job done. He lasted three innings, gave up 10 runs -- six earned -- on eight hits, walked six batters and struck out one. The last Nationals pitcher to give up 10 runs in a game was right-hander Jason Simontacchi on June 19, 2007, against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Myers has been a different pitcher since returning from the Minor Leagues, posting a 2.48 ERA in five starts. He was the victim of poor run support in his previous outing against the Dodgers on Aug. 14. In his last outing against the Nationals, the right-hander allowed one unearned run in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Balester lasted six innings and gave up five runs on four hits against the Mets in his last start. He struck out three batters and walked five. Balester was sharp the first three innings, but he had problems during his final three. During those last three innings, he had a tough time throwing strikes and keeping the ball down. It was a case of Mets batters making adjustments the second time around.

home_pitcher_note: What else can you say about the 45-year-old pitching master, who extended his streak of allowing three or fewer runs in starts to 13. He is coming off an outing in which he outdueled fellow veteran Greg Maddux, 1-0, at PETCO Park, a performance Padres center fielder Scott Hairston called "Pitching 101." He has found a rhythm in his 22nd Major League season, and continues to outsmart opponents.
away_pitcher_note: Redding pitched well in his last start but was plagued by a three-run fifth inning in which all of the runs that scored came with two outs in a 4-3 defeat against the Rockies. The veteran right-hander walked just one and struck out five, throwing 107 pitches. Seventy of his pitches found the strike zone in the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick is finding it increasingly difficult to survive when his sinker isn't quite right. After a strong rookie season and a promising start to 2008, the sophomore has compiled a 6.90 ERA in his past six outings. He was unable to last five innings for the sixth time this season, and allowed six or more runs for the fifth time. That happened once each last season.
away_pitcher_note: Look who's back. Maddux resumes his Dodgers career, acquired to replace the injured Brad Penny in the starting rotation. Maddux was slipped into this start because he just did a pretty good job neutralizing the potent Phillies lineup, allowing only a solo home run to Pat Burrell in seven innings for the Padres last week. Putting Maddux back to back with rookie Clayton Kershaw could result in some short starts and put a burden on the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels' brilliance finally translated into a win, as he broke a seven-start stretch in which he went 0-3 with four no-decisions. He went eight innings against San Diego and allowed one run in his hometown. He's starting against the Dodgers for the second time this month. He limited them to two runs in seven innings on Aug. 12, but Chad Durbin allowed the tying runs to score in the eighth.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw continued his impressive turnaround against Milwaukee's potent lineup with a fifth consecutive quality start, during which his ERA is 1.45. It might have been a win, but manager Joe Torre is exercising a quick hook with Kershaw, more to protect his young arm than to indicate he can't get the job done. Against the Brewers, Kershaw allowed only one run in six innings on 96 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Though his ERA in August is 3.38, Blanton is coming off a second straight outing in which he allowed four earned runs in five innings. He received no-decisions in each of those starts. The first of the two came against the Dodgers, on Aug. 13, when the right-hander struggled to protect a 6-1 lead.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda allowed the explosive Rockies lineup four runs over the first 2 1/3 innings, then held them scoreless over the next 3 2/3 innings. He served up a home run to Brad Hawpe immediately after taking a smash off his left ankle. He said it didn't effect him on the pitch and wasn't sore afterward, but it was heavily taped to minimize swelling and could pose a problem in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Myers has been a completely different pitcher than the one who compiled a 5.84 ERA through June 27 and required a head-clearing trip to the Minors. In six stats since his return, the right-hander has posted a 1.94 ERA and the team has won four of those outings. He's coming off a shutout of the Nationals, his first shutout in more than four years, and he's restored the organization's confidence in him.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley left his most recent start against the Rockies leading, but the victory got away when the bullpen allowed an unearned tying run. Nonetheless, he pitched in with another quality start, grinding out six innings despite allowing baserunners in each of them. His key moment was pitching into a bases-loaded situation with no outs and limiting the damage to only one run.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year veteran ran his streak of allowing three runs or fewer to 14 with a fine effort against Washington. In that game, he surrendered one earned run in 6 2/3 innings, but he received a no-decision. In 18 career starts against the Mets this season, the lefty is 7-4 with a 2.85 ERA. He has faced them four times this season, giving up three, two, two and one run in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: By the time Martinez handed the ball to manager Jerry Manuel with one on and no outs in the eighth inning Thursday, his veteran trickery had worn out against the Braves, who tacked on four runs in seven innings. Manuel doesn't foresee Martinez, whose fastball is consistently working in the mid-80s mph, to last more than a couple of rotations through an opponent's lineup. But Martinez seemingly surpassed those expectations, striking out six, taking the mound to start the eighth, and surpassing 100 pitches. In his last outing in Philadelphia, Martinez allowed two earned runs in 5 1/3 innings and won.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick is still fighting the ups and downs that come with a hurler's first full season in the Major Leagues, but showed significant progress Friday against the Dodgers. The 23-year-old went 5 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and walking two to earn the victory. The win came on the heels of a six-start stretch in which Kendrick recorded a 6.90 ERA to raise his season mark to 5.01. He is now in a three-way tie with Jamie Moyer and Cole Hamels for the team lead in wins. In three career starts against the Mets, Kendrick is 1-1 with a 2.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Santana delivered another impressive performance on Friday night, posting seven shutout innings against the Astros. It marked the second straight game that Santana held opponents scoreless, bringing his streak to 16 innings. His pitch count built up to a career-high 121, but he has thrown six innings or more in his last seven starts, including two complete games. He bounced back after early struggles led to 62 pitches through the first three innings. Santana scattered eight hits, striking out five with one walk. He has not recorded a loss since June 28, and he has limited opponents to three runs or fewer in nine of his last ten games.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster will be going for a personal-best 16th win in his next start. He picked up No. 15 in his last start, against the Nationals, giving up one run on eight hits over 7 1/3 innings. He now has 18 quality starts. He will face the Phillies for the first time this year. The right-hander also has been productive at the plate and leads the Majors with 16 sacrifice bunts.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels enjoyed Saturday's offensive outburst after receiving an average of two runs of support during his previous four starts. The Phils' ace went seven innings, allowing two runs on five hits to earn the victory. Hamels is now in a three-way tie with Jamie Moyer and Kyle Kendrick for the team lead in victories, with 11. In four career starts against the Cubs, Hamels is 3-1 with a 3.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Harden struck out 11 over seven innings in his last start against the Nationals to match his personal high. The only other time he fanned 11 was on June 26 this year against the Phillies. He now has seven double-digit-strikeout games in his career, and five have come since joining the Cubs on July 8. He gave up one run and has an 0.47 ERA in his last three starts. Harden also did not walk a batter, the sixth time in his career he's avoided that in a start.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday night, Blanton turned in his third quality start in seven outings since joining the Phillies in July. The right-hander held the Dodgers to one run on six hits in six innings, striking out four and walking three. Blanton has recorded a 3.00 ERA in his past five starts. He has never faced the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly wasn't spectacular in his last outing against the Pirates, but he wasn't bad, either. The lefty threw seven strong innings and was able to keep Pittsburgh hitters off balance with a good changeup and a mesmerizing curveball. His only two mistakes came on home runs to two left-handed hitters, but the damage meant little after the Cubs' offense put up 12 runs of support. Lilly will look to keep things going vs. the Phillies, who he is 1-2 with a 5.19 ERA against in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The 28-year-old continues to roll since making his return from a July stint in the Minor Leagues. On Monday, Myers held the Dodgers scoreless in seven innings. The right-hander has now logged 16 scoreless innings in a row, starting when he threw a complete-game shutout against the Nationals on Aug. 20. Since returning from the Minors, Myers is 4-1 with a 1.66 ERA. In eight career starts against the Cubs, Myers is 6-3 with a 2.63 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Marshall fills in for Carlos Zambrano, who was scratched a few hours before game time.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer's streak of allowing three runs or fewer in 14 consecutive starts was snapped by the Mets on Tuesday. New York pounded the veteran left-hander for six runs on nine hits in three innings, his shortest outing of 2008. Still, Moyer remains in a three-way tie with Cole Hamels and Kyle Kendrick for the staff lead in wins, with 11. On Sunday, the veteran will be facing the Cubs, the team with which he broke into the Major Leagues in 1986. Moyer faced them once already this season, allowing four runs on nine hits in five innings on his way to a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start on Wednesday, Redding lasted six innings and gave up three runs on eight hits against the Dodgers. All three of the homers Redding gave up came on breaking balls, and he was reluctant to throw them after the fifth. Redding ended up winning his first game since Aug. 4 against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick lasted five-plus innings against the Mets on Wednesday, allowing two earned runs in earning the no-decision. It was the second solid start in a row for the young right-hander after struggling through a six-start stretch in which he endured a 6.90 ERA to raise his season mark to 5.01. In four career starts against the Nationals, Kendrick is 1-1 with a 3.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: On Thursday, it looked like Lannan was going to have his third straight lackluster outing, but he ended up having a quality start against the Dodgers. In the first inning, Lannan got off to a slow start as he gave up a two-run homer to Manny Ramirez. After walking Jeff Kent and hitting James Loney with a pitch, Lannan retired eight straight batters and didn't give up another run in the next 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Though it's not reflected in wins and losses, Hamels has been spectacular for nearly two months, posting a 2.69 ERA in his previous 16 starts, spanning 113 2/3 innings. Opponents are hitting .216 off him during that span. He pulled himself out of his last turn after throwing 108 pitches -- saying he had enough -- then watched the bullpen give up a three-run lead and the game. The lefty is 4-3 with a 2.25 ERA in 11 starts vs. Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Perez ended up winning his sixth game of the season Friday, as he gave up three runs -- two earned -- in 6 1/3 innings. The Braves had chances to score more runs off Perez. In the first inning, they had the bases loaded and one out, but Yunel Escobar hit into a double play to end the inning. All three runs charged to Perez scored in the fifth inning. Greg Norton highlighted the Braves' scoring with a pinch-hit, two-run homer. Martin Prado made it a 5-3 game when he doubled to score Josh Anderson.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton has done well enough, posting a 3.92 ERA in eight starts with his new team, but hasn't gone as deep into games as the team would've liked. Though he allowed only two runs to the Cubs in his previous outing, he walked five batters, tying a career high, and was very frustrated with himself afterward. The righty received a no-decision in his previous turn against Washington, surrendering four runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's bid for a third consecutive complete game fell 2 1/3 innings short last Saturday in Miami, as did his bid for a fourth straight win. But the Mets certainly had no qualms with the way Pelfrey pitched. The two runs he allowed would have been enough to win on many other nights, and his inefficiency -- 99 pitches through six innings, and 116 through 6 2/3 -- was an aberration in the context of the month. Pelfrey completed August with a 4-1 record and 2.93 ERA, and will commence September against the Phillies, whom he has beaten once in two attempts.
away_pitcher_note: Myers continued his second-half turnaround with a dominating win over the Cubs on Saturday afternoon. Against the best offense in the National League, Myers tossed seven-plus innings of two-run ball. He gave up 11 hits (all singles), walked none and struck out eight. At one point, the right-hander retired 11 hitters in a row. Myers is 5-1 with a 1.78 ERA since the All-Star break. Only two other pitchers, both acquired in July trades, boast better ERAs during the second half. The Brewers' C.C. Sabathia (6-0, 1.41) and the Cubs' Rich Harden (4-1, 1.66) have received widespread attention for helping their teams in the playoff push.

home_pitcher_note: Despite allowing the Marlins just two runs last Sunday, Martinez needed 101 pitches to do so. And so he lasted only six innings in Miami, striking out four and walking one. The outing was the third straight in which Martinez had thrown more than 100 pitches, after doing so just once in his previous five starts. And his season high in pitches, 111, also came last week against the Phillies, whom he will face on Saturday. Martinez is 3-2 against the Phillies since joining the Mets in 2005.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer held the Cubs to two earned runs in 5 1/3 innings to earn his team-leading 12th victory Sunday against the Cubs. He has been the Phils' most consistent starting pitcher this season, holding opponents to three earned runs or fewer in 15 of his past 16 starts. Moyer is 1-1 with a 4.40 ERA in five starts against the Mets this year.

home_pitcher_note: Santana once again pitched well enough to win Monday, when he threw six good, not great, innings against the Brewers. But he came away with an ERA one point higher than it had been, and this piece of self-satisfaction -- the Mets have a 9-3 record in his 12 most recent starts and are unbeaten in his past six. He struck out 10, equaling his high for the season, walked one and allowed seven hits. But he was denied a victory by his defense and offense and his own balk. Now he is to oppose the Phillies for the fifth time in his first National League season. Despite a 3.10 ERA in 29 innings against the Phillies, Santana has a 1-0 record is the first four starts. They're batting .213 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels, the Phillies' ace, turned in 7 1/3 innings of shutout ball against the Nationals on Tuesday night in Washington, lowering his ERA to 3.01, his lowest mark since May 20.

home_pitcher_note: Aside from a rain-shortened outing in July, Wednesday's no-decision against the Nationals was Blanton's shortest outing since he joined the Phillies midseason. The right-hander lasted four innings, giving up four runs on six hits. The right-hander was billed as an innings eater when he came over from Oakland, but he has lasted seven innings only twice in nine starts with the Phillies. Blanton has yet to face the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez was locked up in a wild one in his last start on Tuesday. Despite logging his career shortest start -- three innings -- the 24-year-old was not involved in the decision. Sanchez was tagged for six runs on eight hits in his showdown with the Braves. With his command off, he threw 64 pitches, 43 for strikes. Sanchez has faced the Phillies already this season, tossing five innings in a loss at Citizens Bank Park on Aug. 6. The right-hander gave up four runs that day, three of which were earned.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has struggled against the Marlins this season with a 6.10 ERA in two outings. Kendrick was skipped in the rotation after posting a 9.14 ERA in his past five starts, and will be looking to redeem himself.
away_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old rookie continues to turn in fine performances. Pitching into September for the first time, Volstad has logged 62 1/3 innings at the big league level thus far. Add in another 91 during his tenure in the Minor Leagues, and Volstad has 153 1/3 innings total this season. Volstad comes off a no-decision against the Braves where he gave up three runs on six hits in six innings. He did walk five, which is a personal high. On Aug. 7 at Philadelphia, Volstad threw six shutout innings in a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Myers continued to dominate on Friday against the Mets, keeping New York scoreless on three hits over eight innings. It was just the latest chapter of what has been a remarkable turnaround for Myers since he was sent down to Triple-A Lehigh Valley in July. Since his return to Major League action on July 23, the right-hander is 6-1 with a 1.55 ERA. He was beaten by the Marlins on June 10, giving up five runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco had a strong outing last Friday against the Cardinals, but a lack of run support forced him to take a no-decision. Nolasco allowed just one run through seven innings while fanning four and not issuing a walk. Opponents are hitting just .240 against Nolasco. Having already recorded 184 2/3 innings, Nolasco is well on his way toward reaching the 200-inning plateau.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer, who threw seven shutout innings in the first game of Sunday's doubleheader, has been the Phils' most consistent starting pitcher in 2008. He leads the team in wins (13) and has held opponents to three runs or fewer in 16 of his past 17 starts. The 45-year-old does will be pitching on three days rest, something he has not done in his two-plus seasons with the Phillies. Moyer earned a no-decision earlier this season against the Brewers, holding them to one run in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets shook off injury concerns and demonstrated just how important he is to the Brewers in his last start, on Saturday. Sheets threw his third shutout of the season -- after having just one in his career entering 2008 -- and recorded his career-best 13th victory in a 1-0 outdueling of Jake Peavy and the Padres. The electric performance came one start after left groin tightness caused Sheets to leave a start, and he also shook off the effects of numbness in his fingers, the result of a Peavy slider off the end of Sheets' bat. He gets a big start in the opener of a four-game set against the team's closest competitor in the National League Wild Card race, the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels arrived in New York last weekend on the heels of a 17-start stretch in which he had posted a 2.53 ERA. But he allowed the Mets three runs in the first inning and labored the rest of the way, needing 110 pitches to get through five innings. Still, it was only the third time since June 28 that Hamels has allowed four earned runs in a start. In four career starts against the Brewers, Hamels is 1-1 with a 4.76 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Parra gave up six runs in five innings on Sunday, though five of those were unearned after a pair of infield gaffes led to a big inning against the Padres. Parra would have had to seriously deal to keep up with opposing starter Chris Young, who lost a perfect game with four outs to go, but it was another in a growing series of short starts. Parra has one victory in his past six decisions and has worked beyond the sixth just once since July 20.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Blanton earned his second win as a Phillie since his July trade from Oakland. In five innings against the Marlins, he allowed four runs, walking three and striking out one. The right-hander's control has been shaky in his first 10 starts with the Phillies. In a span of 52 2/3 innings with his new team, Blanton has walked 26. For Oakland last season, he issued only 40 in 230 innings. He has never faced Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was on track for his 10th win before Salomon Torres surrendered three Reds runs on Monday. Bush, who had lost his previous start after a 4-0 August, scattered seven hits in eight innings and allowed two runs, his first eight-inning outing since July 10. He faced the Phillies on April 23 at Miller Park and allowed four runs on eight hits in six innings, but took a no-decision in a Brewers win.

home_pitcher_note: Myers, who will be pitching on three days' rest, lost to the Marlins on Wednesday, allowing four runs in 7 1/3 innings, striking out nine and walking one. He threw 117 pitches, among his higher pitch counts of 2008. He has started on three days' rest only once before in his career, on Oct. 3, 2004. He beat the Marlins that day, holding Florida to three runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan took a shutout into the fifth inning against the Reds on Wednesday, then allowed four runs in the span of two innings. The real damage came in the sixth, when he surrendered a two-run home run to Edwin Encarnacion followed by a solo shot to Jay Bruce that put the Brewers in a 4-1 hole. The Brewers have lost both of Suppan's September starts after winning five of six in August. He limited the Phillies to a run on five hits in seven innings at Miller Park on April 24, but settled for a no-decision in a 3-1 Brewers loss.

home_pitcher_note: Other than the fact that his bullpen denied him a second win on Wednesday, Parr's career has started as impressively as he could have ever wished. The 22-year-old right-hander has tossed six scoreless innings during each  of his first two Major League starts. Without an overpowering fastball, Parr has found early success with his slider and changeup. Dating back to his final three starts with Triple-A Richmond this year, he's allowed one earned run in his past 29 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on three days' rest, the rock-steady Moyer struck out five and walked one in beating the Brewers on Thursday. Moyer has been the Phils' most consistent starting pitcher this season, holding opponents to three runs or fewer in 17 out of his past 18 starts. His 14 wins lead the team. He earned a no-decision in his only start this season against the Braves, holding Atlanta to two runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens showed some of his top velocity while recording a career-high 10 strikeouts and winning his second straight start on Thursday against the Rockies.  Per John Smoltz's advice, the 22-year-old right-hander has limited his running exercises between starts and consequently he says he's regained some of the leg strength he lacked while winning just one of his previous seven starts entering this month.  One of his finest starts of the season came against the Phillies on July 25, when he allowed three hits over eight scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: With Kyle Kendrick struggling mightily the past few weeks, there was an opening for Happ in the Phillies' rotation. Happ was chosen because of the Braves' unfamiliarity with him, and also because of the presence of several prominent left-handed hitters in their lineup. Happ has not started a game for the Phillies since July 9, but has performed well in that role. He has a 5.71 ERA overall, but has compiled a 3.27 mark in two starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton allowed two runs over six innings Saturday, but against Johan Santana, that effort was not enough to earn the 36-year-old a decision. The Braves would wait to claim victory after Hampton exited with 90 pitches (47 strikes). A lack of consistent location --  totaling five walks and six hits allowed -- put Hampton into a couple of bases-loaded jams, but he recovered for the most part, inducing double play groundouts in both situations.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels beat the Brewers Saturday, holding Milwaukee to two runs in 6 1/3 innings, striking out four and walking three. The 24-year-old, now in his third Major League season, is setting a career high in innings pitched with each successive start. Right now he's at 214 1/3. But the left-hander has been steady, recording a 4-1 record with a 2.21 ERA in his last six starts. In three starts this year against the Braves, Hamels is 2-0 with a 2.11 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: It could've been yet another dominant night for Johnson on Saturday against the Nationals. But it was pretty successful either way. The 24-year-old limited Washington to just two runs on six hits while walking just one and striking out a career-high nine to get the win. Through the first five innings, Johnson gave up just three hits and kept the Nationals scoreless, but Washington tacked on two runs with a two-out rally in the sixth to shorten Johnson's night. He has now recorded eight straight quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Don't be fooled by his record. The Brett Myers that began this season for the Phillies and the Brett Myers that returned after a July stint in the Minor Leagues are two totally different pitchers. Before being optioned to Triple-A Lehigh Valley, Myers was 3-9 with a 5.84 ERA. Since returning, he's  7-2 with a 1.80 ERA in 11 starts. Myers' latest dominant effort came Sunday night, as he took the ball on three days rest to pitch the second game of a doubleheader against the Brewers. Nine innings later, the right-hander had his second complete-game victory of the season, holding the Brewers to one run on two hits. Myers is 1-2 with a 5.23 ERA against the Marlins this season.

home_pitcher_note: Even though he is coming off a no-decision, Sanchez is encouraged by his outing against the Nationals. After two straight starts where he didn't last longer than three innings, the fact Sanchez went seven innings in his no-decision shows progress. The 24-year-old right-hander matched his season high for innings. He also threw seven innings in a loss at St. Louis on Aug. 11. His seven innings and three runs (two earned), marked his first quality start since Aug. 11. Sanchez has been working on his fastball command, and the results were seven strikeouts. On Sept. 8 at Philadelphia, Sanchez was roughed up for five runs in 1 1/3 innings in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: In working seven innings on Sunday, Blanton turned in his longest effort since Aug. 8. The righty allowed three runs on five hits and two walks. He had posted a 5.58 in six outings before that, during which he was battling right bicep tendinitis.

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old has two more starts to go. After this one, he is lined up to face the Mets at Shea Stadium on Sept. 26. The rookie is getting a big taste of a pennant race. Thus far, he is up to the task. In his last outing, he shut down the Astros, limiting them to one run on five hits in eight innings. It was his second-blongest outing of the year. On July 11, in his first MLB start, he lasted 8 2/3 innings against the Dodgers. Had he been working on a shutout against the Astros, manager Fredi Gonzalez said Volstad would have come out for the ninth inning in hopes of the complete game.
away_pitcher_note: Though he's given up six runs twice in his previous five outings, Moyer has posted a 3.38 ERA overall in his previous 19 outings and is still going strong at 45. He said he was trying to force things in his previous outing and may have been feeling some effects of working on three days' rest in a Sept. 11 outing.

home_pitcher_note: Happ will make his second start against Atlanta in five days. The rookie lefty dazzled them with six shutout innings on Wednesday, allowing just three hits, and has a 2.12 ERA in his three starts this season. Manager Charlie Manuel would love an encore.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens surrendered four runs during a 43-pitch first-inning against the Phillies on Wednesday and then held them scoreless while needing just 57 pitches to complete his final four innings. The early damage prevented the 22-year-old rookie from winning his third straight start and equal the success he had at Citizens Bank Park on July 25, when allowed three hits in eight scoreless innings against the Phillies. Facing the same lineup for the second time in five days, Jurrjens will look to be more aggressive in the strike zone and fight the temptation of showing too much respect to specific hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has been the team's most consistant pitcher and has posted a 2.73 ERA in his previous 10 starts. Already into uncharted territory as far as innings, Hamels isn't going to stop now until he gets the Phillies into the postseason. This could be his final start of the regular season, unless the Phillies don't have a spot clinched by Sept. 28.
away_pitcher_note: Two unearned runs and Pat Burrell's sixth-inning two-run homer prevented Hampton from beating the Phillies on Thursday night in Atlanta. This will be Hampton's third start of the season against the Phillies and likely his final opportunity to audition for a contract next season. While pitching into the seventh inning in each of his past seven starts, the injury-prone 35-year-old lefty has at least erased some of the durability issues that have surrounded him.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is coming off the worst start of his career, an outing in which he allowed 10 earned runs in four-plus innings. He had posted an 1.80 ERA in 11 starts prior to that, indicating that the poor start was a bump in the road, and not a severe regression to his first half, when he posted a 5.84 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Reyes' final opportunity to make the positive impression that he's been unable to provide while going 0-7 with a 7.79 ERA in his past 12 appearances. The 23-year-old hurler agitated Braves manager Bobby Cox while allowing the Mets five earned runs in just 3 1/3 innings on Friday. It marked the seventh time in 11 starts that he didn't complete at least five innings.  He is 0-2 with a 7.56 ERA in three appearances (two starts) against the Phillies this year.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton has not quite fulfilled the innings-eater reputation he had when he was traded from Oakland to Philadelphia in July. In 12 starts with the Phillies, Blanton has lasted seven innings only three times. He has also struggled with his control, issuing 30 walks in 64 2/3 innings with the Phillies after he allowed 35 in 127 innings with the Athletics before the trade.  Still, Blanton has been effective enough, as the Phils have posted an 8-4 record in his starts. Blanton has made two starts against the Nationals this year and earned a no-decision each time.
away_pitcher_note: Last Friday was one of Balester's worst outings. He lasted five innings and gave up five runs on nine hits against the Padres. The game seesawed back and forth in the first eight innings. After two innings, the Nationals had a 2-0 lead off right-hander Dirk Hayhurst, but San Diego would come back and take a 4-2 lead by the top of the fourth inning against Balester. Kevin Kouzmanoff highlighted the scoring with a two-run homer. Washington would tie the score in the bottom of the fourth. With Mike Ekstrom on the mound, Balester hit an RBI single and Emilio Bonifacio walked with the bases loaded. The runs were charged to Hayhurst. Both teams would score a run in the sixth inning. Will Venable would drive in the go-ahead run off Balester, while Clay Hensley gave up a sacrifice fly to Bonifacio.

home_pitcher_note: The 45-year-old Moyer has been Philadelphia's most consistent starting pitcher this year, leading the club in wins. He is 2-0 with a 2.82 ERA against Washington this season, but perhaps his most memorable start against the Nationals came in 2007. On the final day of the regular season last year, Moyer took the hill and shut down the Nats for 5 1/3 innings, lifting the Phillies to a division-clinching victory.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan endured two bad innings on Saturday evening, and they proved to be costly, as the Nationals were topped by the Padres, 6-1, at Nationals Park. Lannan was cruising until the fifth inning. After walking Nick Hundley, who advanced to second base on Chris Young's sacrifice bunt, Will Venable hit a grounder to second baseman Emilio Bonifacio, who committed an error, allowing Hundley to score. Edgar Gonzalez followed with a two-run homer. None of the three runs was earned. Two innings later, Young hit his first big league home run. Lannan lasted seven innings and gave up four runs, but only one was earned.

home_pitcher_note: A 6.45 ERA in a nine-start stretch forced the Phillies to yank Kendrick from the starting rotation, but he will start Sunday in Cole Hamels' place after the Phillies clinched the division. Kendrick's issue in the second half has been the lack secondary pitches, and opponents buried him. Left off the playoff roster for the Division Series, the right-hander could re-join the team in the NLCS, should the Phillies advance.
away_pitcher_note: Perez may have pitched his last game at Nationals Park. If so, the free agent-to-be gave the hometown fans a quality start. Unfortunately, Perez didn't get the win, as the Padres defeated the Nationals, 6-2, on Sunday afternoon. Perez pitched six innings, giving up three runs on five hits. He also struck out a career-high 11 batters. However, Perez experienced two bad innings. In the first inning, Perez gave up a two-run double to Kevin Kouzmanoff. Five innings later, Adrian Gonzalez hit a home run.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies' leader in innings and ERA among starters (3.09) will be making his second Game 1 start after working against the Rockies to kick off the NLDS last season. A rough second inning doomed him in a 4-2 defeat, and he didn't get another chance as the Rockies won the next two games for a sweep. The Phils' lefty ace will be facing the Brewers for the sixth time in his career, and has a 4.41 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: In choosing Gallardo, Brewers manager Dale Sveum picked raw talent over experience. He could have used postseason stalwart Jeff Suppan (5-2 with a 3.00 ERA in nine career postseason starts) on regular rest or Dave Bush on three days' rest. Instead, Sveum went with Gallardo, the Brewers' most promising young pitcher, but also a 22-year-old less than five months removed from a major right knee injury. He had surgery to repair a torn ACL in May and was back in Milwaukee's rotation on Sept. 25 for a start against the Pirates. He threw 67 pitches in four innings and allowed one run on three hits, including a Steve Pearce solo home run. He looked extremely good on the mound but in his only at-bat, Gallardo never took the bat off his shoulder. It was sign that the Brewers did not want him on the basepaths with a surgically repaired knee.

home_pitcher_note: Myers' second-half resurgence gave the Phillies an acquisition as valuable as CC Sabathia or Rich Harden. The righty posted a 1.80 ERA in 11 starts -- and dominated. There is some concern regarding his final two outings of the season, in which he allowed 14 earned runs and 19 hits in 8 1/3 innings. He has a 1.77 ERA in eight career appearances against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Make it four straight starts on three days' rest for Sabathia, who continues to cement his status as the greatest midseason pickup in Major League history. Sabathia carried the Brewers to their first postseason bid in 26 years on Sunday in Milwaukee, allowing an unearned run on four hits in a complete-game, 122-pitch win over the Cubs. Less than an hour later, after a Mets loss, the Brewers won the Wild Card. The Brewers squeezed every ounce of energy out of their prized rental. Sabathia threw 334 pitches the last nine days of the regular season, starting three straight times on three days' rest.

home_pitcher_note: Bush went 7-3 over his final 18 regular-season appearances with a 3.23 ERA and was charged with three or fewer earned runs in 13 of those 17 starts. But Bush, who was 4-0 in August with a 2.12 ERA, was not immune to the Brewers' September swoon. He was winless in five September starts with a 4.97 ERA before working three scoreless frames in Milwaukee's next-to-last game of the year. That September streak included a loss in Game 1 of a Sept. 14 doubleheader in Philadelphia. Bush was charged with three runs on five hits in that game, a 7-3 Brewers loss.
away_pitcher_note: No one will be more prepared for the big game than Jamie Moyer, who pitched the division-clinching game for Philadelphia for the second straight season. Moyer won 16 games, tying Phil Niekro for the most wins by a pitcher beyond  his 45th birthday, and recorded the most wins since winning 21 in 2003. The lefty has a 2.43 ERA in five career postseason starts.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan was bumped all the way to Game 4 after struggling to an 0-3 record and a 8.44 ERA in five September starts. But this is precisely the kind of situation Brewers officials envisioned for Suppan when they gave him a four-year, $42 million contract on Christmas Eve 2006. In fact, when general manager Doug Melvin gathered his baseball staff at a Scottsdale, Ariz., restaurant that October to begin planning for the postseason, a television carried Game 7 of the 2006 National League Championship Series, Suppan?s signature performance. He worked seven strong innings against the Mets that night to help send the Cardinals to the World Series. He is 5-2 in his nine career playoff starts with a 3.00 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton will be making his first career postseason start. He worked two innings in relief against Detroit in 2006. The right-hander was acquired in July for three Minor Leaguers and has gone 4-0 with a 4.20 ERA in 13 starts for Philadelphia. He has allowed three or fewer earned runs in eight of those outings. He will be working on eight days' rest.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is coming of one of the best starts of his career on one of the biggest stages. He shut down the Brewers in Game 1 of the National League Division Series, holding Milwaukee scoreless on two hits in eight innings. Hamels made that start on seven days of rest, and he will have the same luxury when he takes the ball against the Dodgers on Thursday. Manager Charlie Manuel said that the extra rest has been crucial for the 24-year-old Hamels, who finished second in the National League with 227 1/3 innings pitched. Hamels has made two starts against the Dodgers this year, going 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers can start Lowe in Game 1, bring him back on three days rest for Game 4, then have him on regular rest for a Game 7, if the series lasts that long and they so choose. It's a nice situation to be in, having someone on the staff who's already pitched winning clinchers in a Championship Series and World Series, as Lowe did with the Red Sox in 2004. Lowe again showed that the spotlight is no issue for him when he set the tone for the Division Series by containing the Cubs for a two-run, wind-blown home run over six innings at Wrigley Field last week. He has a very successful history pitching in Wrigley Field and the same is true for the right-hander at Citizens Bank Park, where he's 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in three career starts, none of those occurring this year. He is 4-1 with two saves and a 3.02 ERA in his career against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Heading into the National League Division Series, no one was sure which Brett Myers would take the mound for the Phillies: the one who dominated hitters for a 10-start stretch in July and August -- in which he went 7-2 with a 1.56 ERA -- or the Myers who had been beaten badly in his final two starts of the regular season, giving up 14 earned runs in 8 1/3 innings for a 15.12 ERA. Fortunately for Philadelphia, the dominant Myers was on the hill against Milwaukee in Game 2. He held the Brewers to two runs on two hits in seven innings. The Phils will be hoping for more of the same against the Dodgers Friday night. He is 1-1 against L.A. this season with a 1.93 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley showed the baseball world why the Dodgers drafted him in the first round when he tamed the Cubs for six scoreless innings and got the win in Game 2 of the National League Division Series. Billingsley finally wavered in the seventh, but with seven strikeouts and one walk in front of a hostile Wrigley Field crowd, he was pretty convincing as the Dodgers' future ace. That experience should serve him well as a prep for this assignment at Citizens Bank Park, where he had control problems in his only start this year, walking five while allowing three runs in six innings of a 5-0 loss on Aug. 25.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda had never pitched in a postseason game until he clinched the National League Division Series against the Cubs, when he didn't look like a rookie in pitching 6 1/3 scoreless innings. He pitched well in a tough no-decision in Philadelphia on Aug. 24, allowing one run in six innings. He was even better beating the Phillies in Los Angeles 10 days earlier, allowing one run in seven innings. He will be pitching on eight days' rest. His ERA this year with more than four days' rest is 2.86.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer struggled in his NLDS start against the Brewers. He threw 34 pitches in the first inning, more than he threw in any first inning of 2008. After four innings on the hill, manager Charlie Manuel lifted Moyer for a pinch-hitter. Still, Moyer has provided consistency to the Phils' starting rotation this season, leading the team in regular-season victories, with 16. He also has League Championship Series experience under his belt, having won in his only start for the Mariners during the 2001 ALCS against the Yankees. Moyer has not faced the Dodgers in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: By pitching Lowe on three days' rest in Game 4, Dodgers manager Joe Torre has set up his rotation so that if the NLCS goes the distance, his top three starters will go on full rest. He said that sinkerballer Lowe would be able to better handle the rigors of going on short rest. Lowe is 2-1 with a 5.09 ERA in 23 innings over four starts on three days' rest, but also pitched a gem under those conditions to defeat Torre's Yankees in Game 7 of the 2004 ALCS.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton delivered against the Brewers in Game 4 of the NLDS, his biggest start since being traded to Philly from Oakland in mid-July. The right-hander earned the win in the Phils' series-clinching victory over Milwaukee, holding the Brewers to one run on five hits in six innings. Despite struggling with his control at times during the past two months, Blanton did not walk a Brewers batter. Blanton has started twice against the Dodgers this season and earned a no-decision each time, allowing a total of five earned runs in 11 innings for a 4.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Whether the Dodgers' season will extend past Wednesday depends very heavily on which Chad Billingsley shows up. If it's the Billingsley that ranked seventh in the league with a 3.14 ERA and won Game 2 of the NLDS against the Cubs, Los Angeles has a strong chance. But if it's the Billingsley that lasted just 2 1/3 innings in his last start against the Phillies, winter will likely arrive in a hurry. Working in Billingsley's favor is a 1.65 ERA in his last eight starts at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels has lived up to his status as the Phillies' ace so far this postseason, shutting down the Brewers to open the National League Championship Series and then doing the same to the Dodgers in the NLCS opener. In Game 5, the 24-year-old finds himself on yet another big stage, this time with the chance to send his team to its first World Series since 1993. Including the postseason, Wednesday's start will be his fourth against the Dodgers this year. Hamels has pitched well against Los Angeles, posting a 2-0 record and allowing only six earned runs in 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir experienced a subpar outing in Game 2 of the ALCS but rebounded nicely at Fenway Park in Game 5 when he scattered two hits over six scoreless innings, though he did not get the win as the Red Sox erased a 7-0 deficit after Kazmir left the game. Kazmir used his slider more in Game 5 �- to go along with a plus fastball and changeup -� and the results were encouraging. Rays manager Joe Maddon believes that the left-hander's Game 5 performance will serve as a growth experience for his next start.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old Hamels has been nothing short of outstanding this postseason, winning all three of his starts while posting a 1.23 ERA and holding opponents to 13 hits, and striking out 22 of them, in 22 innings. He won the NLCS MVP award for holding the Dodgers to three runs in 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Shields was 0-2 with a 3.46 ERA in two ALCS starts. In Game 1 on Oct. 10, the right-hander allowed just two runs over 7 1/3 innings, but he was outdueled by the Red Sox's Daisuke Matsuzaka, who allowed only four hits in seven-plus scoreless innings of the Rays' 2-0 loss. In Game 6 at Tropicana Field on Saturday, Shields surrendered four runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings in Tampa Bay's 4-2 loss. The 26-year-old right-hander's best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus fastball and curve and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handers.
away_pitcher_note: Myers has proven to be a better pitcher at Citizens Bank Park, where he produced a 3.01 ERA in the regular season and two wins in the playoffs. On the road, by contrast, he was 3-8 with a 6.21 ERA. Yet manager Charlie Manuel chose to start Myers on the road in Game 2.

home_pitcher_note: Concern followed Moyer after he endured his year's worst outing in the National League Championship Series, allowing six runs over 1 1/3 innings in Game 3. And that occurred eight days after he lasted just four innings in a Division Series loss to the Brewers. The Phillies have lost two games this postseason, and Moyer has started both of them.
away_pitcher_note: Garza was simply dominant en route to his ALCS MVP award. The offseason acquisition from the Twins posted a 1.38 ERA in two starts. In Game 3 at Fenway Park on Oct. 13, allowed only one run over six-plus innings of the Rays' 9-1 victory. In the pennant-clinching victory Sunday night, Garza again allowed just one run and two hits over seven dazzling innings of work. The 24-year-old right-hander has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton started once in each of the Phillies' series, winning in the Division Series against the Brewers and getting no decision in a five-inning start against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine, who posted a career-high 13 wins in just his second big league campaign, got the win in Game 4 of the ALCS on Oct. 14 in Boston. The righty allowed the Sox four runs on six hits over 7 1/3 innings to give the Rays a commanding 3-1 ALCS lead. Sonnanstine is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to set up the other pitches.
