In his lone start against the Phillies last year, Hudson allowed one run in 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Consider Happ a tentative starter for the moment. He strained his intercostal muscle before his scheduled Sept. 7 against the Houston Astros at Minute Maid Park. He missed that start and Saturday's start against the Mets at Citizens Bank Park. Left-hander Jamie Moyer pitched in Happ's place in both of those games, and he would take his place again if he is unable to pitch Friday against the Braves at Turner Field. The Phillies certainly would love to have Happ back in the rotation. He is a National League Rookie of the Year candidate.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez dominated the Cardinals during his second complete-game effort of the season on Sunday.  His line -- two earned runs and seven hits -- didn't provide indication of how impressive he was.  Before surrendering four straight singles in a two-run ninth, he had allowed just two hits and thrown 79 pitches.  The 33-year-old right-hander has won three straight decisions and allowed a total of two runs in those three victories.  Each of the four runs he surrendered against the Phillies on Aug. 16 came via the two homers he surrendered to Ryan Howard.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez has been terrific since signing with the Phillies, especially his last outing on Sunday night. In that game, the right-hander threw 130 pitches, 80 for strikes and exited to a standing ovation at Citizens Bank Park during a 1-0 win over the Mets. Martinez seems to have recaptured the magic he lost with the Mets last season. He had command of all of his pitches and kept the Mets hitters off balance all night.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson has worked 17 consecutive scoreless innings and surrendered just two runs over his last 24 innings. One of those runs came via the Ryan Howard solo shot he allowed during his rain-shortened two-inning stint against the Phillies on Aug. 28. That outing also accounted for the only loss he's experienced during an eight-start stretch that has included a 5-1 record and 2.42 ERA. The 23-year-old right-hander surrendered one hit through six innings against the Mets on Tuesday and then allowed two more singles before concluding his seven scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: In Lee's last start vs. Washington, he was terrific with a complete-game performance. He allowed six hits while walking three and striking out nine en route to a shutout. After three mediocre starts, Lee was virtually unhittable this time around as he frustrated the Nationals hitters. When Lee has control early, he's that much tougher to beat. Lee has tossed six complete games this season between his stint in Cleveland and his time with the Phillies. Getting the injury-ravaged bullpen a rest is always huge.

home_pitcher_note: After two straight five-inning starts, Johnson recorded his 23rd quality start in his 30th start. The All-Star strives to become the first Marlin pitcher with more than 15 wins since Dontrelle Willis won 22 in 2005. Since 2000, the only Marlins to win more than 15 are Willis and Carl Pavano -- 18 in 2004. Johnson extended his personal high total innings to 194 1/3. He has faced the Phillies twice this year and is 1-0 with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton was not overly dominant Thursday against the Nationals, who lined into two double plays and had other miscues on the basepaths, but he threw six scoreless innings in the victory. He allowed just five hits and four walks and struck out seven. It was an important recovery from his last outing, when the same Washington squad battered him for eight runs in 4 2/3 innings. "Just as hitting is contagious, pitching is, too," Blanton said. "You see this guy have success, that guy, that guy, and that kind of thought gets in your head. ... You don't even think about it, but it gets in your mind a little bit. It breeds confidence."

home_pitcher_note: His record is less than impressive, but Sanchez is coming off a decent performance against the Reds that should provide him with some confidence. Although he threw 39 pitches in the first inning while allowing three runs in his last outing, he shut out Cincinnati the next four innings before taking the 3-2 loss. Sanchez simply was off target in his last appearance, and the fact he hasn't won since Aug. 21 has to bother him heading into the second game of this doubleheader.
away_pitcher_note: Phillies manager Charlie Manuel said Moyer could pitch the second game of Tuesday's doubleheader against the Marlins at Land Shark Stadium. Moyer allowed seven hits and five runs in seven innings on Sept. 12 against the Mets at Citizens Bank Park. He is 2-0 with a 3.08 ERA in five appearances (two starts) since right-hander Pedro Martinez bumped him from the rotation and into the bullpen, although with J.A. Happ still hurting, Moyer could be back in the rotation for the immediate future.

home_pitcher_note: After coming off a shortened start on Sept. 8 because of back stiffness, VandenHurk returned to form last Friday against the Reds, tossing six innings and allowing one run on four hits. It was perhaps his best start of the season, and he'll need that momentum when he faces Phillies left-hander Cole Hamels in the finale of one of the most important series of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels was sensational in his last outing, against the Nationals on Thursday. He tied his season high with 10 strikeouts and allowed five hits and one earned run in eight strong innings. Hamels retired the first 15 Nationals before giving up a single to Mike Morse leading off the sixth inning. Hamels had good command the entire game and made big pitches when needed. He especially did a good job of throwing his offspeed pitches for strikes. Overall, he threw 109 pitches, 73 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan has worked seven quality innings in each of his last two starts, including a win over the Astros on Saturday in which he set a season high with seven strikeouts. It was Suppan's third win at Miller Park in 14 home starts; he's 3-7 with a 5.92 ERA at home and 4-3 with a 3.56 ERA in 13 starts on the road. Suppan missed the Phillies when the Brewers went through Philadelphia in April, but he's 3-6 against them in his career with a 6.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Happ left Friday's game after just three innings for precautionary reasons. He had missed his previous two starts because of a strained right intercostal muscle, and when he appeared to favor it on a play in the third inning, Phillies manager Charlie Manuel decided to take him out of the game. Happ said he was fine. He said he felt no pain or discomfort, but because the Phillies already were without left-handers Scott Eyre, J.C. Romero and Jack Taschner in the bullpen, Manuel wants to make sure Happ is healthy in case he needs him in the bullpen in the postseason.

home_pitcher_note: This is Yovani Gallardo's slot and the Brewers will give it to Parra, who has not started since developing a stiff neck and exiting a Sept. 8 start against the Cardinals. Parra declared himself "100 percent healthy" after throwing a series of bullpen sessions this week and will have two starts to author a positive finish to his disappointing season. He has the highest ERA of any Major League pitcher with at least 80 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lee pitched just four innings Sunday against the Braves at Turner Field, but only because of a 1 hour, 51 minute rain delay. He had allowed five hits and one run to that point. Lee wanted to run back out there, but the Phillies told him it wasn't worth the risk. It made sense. While it would have been nice to have Lee pitch a few more innings, they want to make sure he is healthy for the postseason. He is 7-2 with a 2.65 ERA since he joined the Phillies on July 29.

home_pitcher_note: Looper surrendered two more home runs against the Cubs on Monday to set a dubious club record. He's surrendered 37 homers this season, most in the Majors and one more than former Brewers lefty Wayne Franklin allowed in 2003. He pitched six scoreless innings in his start against the Phillies on April 22, one of only six starts (of 32) this season in which Looper hasn't allowed at least one home run. He's surrendered one in 11 of his last 12 starts, but remains tied for the team lead in wins.
away_pitcher_note: Pedro Martinez was scratched from his start on Saturday with a stiff neck in the hopes that he'll be ready to go in more meaningful games later on. Replacing him is Kyle Kendrick, who finished 9-7 with a 3.34 ERA as a starter on the Triple-A level before joining the Phillies this month after rosters expanded. Kendrick is 2-0 in two appearances (one start) since returning to the Majors, with a stellar 1.59 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Five days after he beat the Cubs at Wrigley Field, Bush surrendered more earned runs -- five -- than he recorded outs -- four -- in a loss at Miller Park. Bush lasted only 1 1/3 innings in his shortest start of the season and lost for the first time in three starts. He'll face the Phillies for the first time since April 23, when Bush took a no-hitter into the eighth inning only to lose it on a Matt Stairs home run. He still won that day, allowing one run on two hits in a season-high 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed just two hits and two walks and struck out nine in seven scoreless innings in a 9-3 victory over the Marlins in Game 1 of a doubleheader Tuesday at Land Shark Stadium. Combined with six shutout innings the previous Thursday against the Nationals at Citizens Bank Park, Blanton (11-7) has now thrown 13 consecutive scoreless innings. Blanton threw a career-high 18 consecutive scoreless innings Aug. 16-31, 2005, when he pitched for Oakland. Blanton is 9-4 with a 2.78 ERA in 21 starts since May 21 in Cincinnati, where he allowed five runs in five innings. His ERA ranks 10th in the Majors and seventh in the National League in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has been pitching much better recently. He went 7-8 with a 4.78 ERA after his first 24 starts this season. The Phillies were just 12-12 in those starts, and his ERA was fifth-highest in the National League through Aug. 21. But he is 3-1 with a 2.01 ERA in his past six starts to get Phillies fans thinking he and Cliff Lee could be pretty dominating in the postseason.
away_pitcher_note: Bazardo is still searching for his first win in eight games with the Astros. He made his fourth start of the season Tuesday against St. Louis and retired seven in a row to start the game before having trouble getting outs. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings, giving up six hits and six runs to fall to 0-2. He's appeared in one career game against the Phillies, giving up two hits and one run in one inning.

home_pitcher_note: Happ hopes to continue to build his case for National League Rookie of the Year in what might be his second-to-last start of the season Tuesday against the Astros. He allowed six hits, two runs, two walks and struck out seven in 5 2/3 innings Thursday in a victory over the Milwaukee Brewers at Miller Park. Happ improved to 11-4 with a 2.79 ERA. His ERA is 10th-best in franchise history amongst rookies.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez is scheduled to make his first Major League start in place of Bud Norris, who was shut down Friday because of a concern for the number of innings he pitched. Lopez has appeared in five Major League games and has no decisions and a 10.38 ERA. He was 4-5 with a 4.73 ERA in 29 games, including 15 starts, at Double-A Corpus Christi this year.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez's start is tentative based on how the right side of his neck feels. He strained his neck Sept. 19 in Atlanta, which forced him to leave after three innings. He missed Saturday's start in Milwaukee as a result. He said he could have pitched if it were absolutely necessary, but with the postseason so close he did not want to risk further injury and an opportunity to pitch in the postseason, when he really wants to be at top form.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler gave up eight hits and seven runs in 2 1/3 innings in Friday's loss to Cincinnati in his shortest start since going 2 1/3 innings in his second outing of the season April 13. He's 1-6 with a 5.63 ERA in 12 starts since July 26. He got a no-decision against the Phillies on Sept. 7 after giving up five hits and three runs in 5 2/3 innings and is 2-3 with a 6.19 ERA in 12 career games, including eight starts, against Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Cliff Lee allowed nine hits and seven runs in just six innings Friday in an 8-4 loss to the Brewers at Miller Park. Lee went 5-0 with a 0.68 ERA in his first five starts with the Phillies, but is 2-3 with a 6.35 ERA in his last six. He has allowed 49 hits, 24 earned runs and three walks and struck out 29 in 34 innings in those six starts. Opponents have hit .336 against him. Lee has thrown 226 innings this season, which led the Majors after Friday. "I feel strong, if that's what you're getting at," Lee said. "I feel as strong as I have all year. That's what you work all offseason for is to prepare for a long season and hopefully something extra there at the end. I feel like I've done everything I need to do to be in a position where I'm at right now."
away_pitcher_note: Paulino was solid to start September with a 3.52 ERA in his first four starts, but fell apart on Saturday against Cincinnati, allowing eight runs on nine hits in five innings while taking the loss. He's been the victim of poor run support for much of the season, including his first three starts in September, when the Astros didn't score a run while he was on the mound. He hasn't faced the Phillies in his young career.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton struggled somewhat in his last start -- at Milwaukee -- giving up seven hits and five earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. He walked four and struck out four and wasn't able to throw his array of pitches consistently for strikes. The home run ball has been a problem all season for Blanton, who has allowed 30 homers in 30 starts. Still, the right-hander has been extremely effective in eight of his past 10 starts and he has been able to keep the Phillies in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Initially, Sean West was in line to make this start, but now the nod is going to VandenHurk, who will be making his 11th start of the season. The right-hander last started on Sept. 23 in a no-decision against the Phillies. He gave up four runs on seven hits with five strikeouts in six innings. VandenHurk has worked six innings in each of his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Astros, Hamels didn't pitch all that poorly despite allowing nine hits and six earned runs in 6 2/3 innings. Hamels gave up a couple of bloopers and the Astros capitalized. He walked three and struck out five and appeared to have some pop on his fastball. Having one more real good start before a potential trip to the postseason would certainly be a confidence boost for the Most Valuable Player of last year's NLCS and World Series.
away_pitcher_note: Control was a big issue in Sanchez's last start. The right-hander opened the Marlins' road trip on Monday at Atlanta, and he issued a career-high eight walks over five innings. Of his 91 pitches, 49 were balls. Twice previously, Sanchez walked as many as seven, but not since 2007. Prior to his appearance in Atlanta, Sanchez beat the Phillies on Sept. 22 in the second game of a doubleheader. He worked eight scoreless innings that day, allowing two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Happ allowed nine hits, four runs, one walk and two home runs in 5 2/3 innings Tuesday in a 7-4 victory over the Astros. He also struck out six. One of those runs were unearned. Happ threw seven shutout innings against the Marlins on July 19 at Land Shark Stadium. It was his third scoreless start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: In line for his 16th win on Tuesday in Atlanta, Johnson settled for a no-decision after exiting with a 4-1 lead. Johnson did top the 200 innings plateau for the first time in his career, as he now has 204 1/3. In the first game of a doubleheader on Sept. 22, Johnson suffered a loss to the Phillies, giving up four runs in five innings. The last Florida pitcher to win more than 15 games was Dontrelle Willis, who had 22 in 2005. Johnson has pitched five innings in four of his five September starts and six innings in the other.

home_pitcher_note: Lee, the reigning American League Cy Young Award winner, went 7-4 with a 3.39 ERA in the 12 starts he made after the Phillies acquired him from the Indians on July 29. The 31-year-old southpaw registered nine strikeouts and limited the Rockies to one run over seven innings on Aug. 6.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday night, with the Rockies still in position to win the National League West, Jimenez turned in a gem, holding the Dodgers to one run and two hits in six innings of a 4-3 victory. After the All-Star break this season, Jimenez went 9-3 with a 3.08 ERA. He's capable of going into the 120-pitch range and still being effective. In two career regular-season starts, Jimenez is 0-1 with an 8.10 ERA. But in Game 2 of the 2007 NLDS at Citizen Bank Park, Jimenez shut the Phils down -- 6 1/3 innings, one run, three hits. Although he didn't figure in the decision, the Rockies won.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed three hits, three runs and two walks in three innings Saturday against the Marlins. Hamels finished the season 10-11 with a 4.32 ERA, and is 0-2 with a 7.02 ERA in his last three starts. But Hamels proved himself to be a big-game pitcher last postseason, when he went 4-0 with a 1.80 ERA in five starts to earn World Series and NL Championship Series MVP honors. "Now I have to put it together, but this is the time where everything really matters and really counts," Hamels said.
away_pitcher_note: Cook has held opponents to one run in 13 innings in two starts after missing five weeks with a sore shoulder. Both of those games were at Coors Field, where an effective sinker is a great weapon. That's perfect preparation for Citizens Bank Park and its bandbox-tight dimensions. Last time Cook pitched at Citizens Bank Park, he gave up three runs on seven hits in five innings and had to leave because he aggravated a turf-toe problem. He is 1-1 with a 3.75 ERA in two starts at CBP.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel battled inconsistency early in the season but turned into a threat to win against high-quality lineups when he decided to eliminate a sinker and go with his four-seam fastball. The sinker was a good idea, considering that balls hit in the air at Coors Field can be dangerous. However, he didn't control it as well as the four-seamer, so he went with what was working for him. Of late, Hammel has been efficient in early innings. That was the improvement he needed to make to last longer in games. There is one red flag, though, as the Rockies head into Game 3. he was 3-3 with a 5.63 ERA in 16 regular-season starts at Coors Field, as opposed to 7-5, 3.13 on the road. Nonetheless, his strong second-half performance led manager Jim Tracy to pick him over Jason Marquis for the start.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez went 5-1 with a 3.63 ERA in nine starts for the Phillies. He is 2-3 with a 4.31 ERA in 10 career appearances against the Rockies. The 37-year-old right-hander is 6-2 with a 3.40 ERA in 13 postseason games, 11 of them starts. That includes a 4-0 record and 2.84 ERA in Division Series games. He last pitched in the postseason in Game 3 of the 2004 World Series, throwing seven shutout innings in Boston's 4-1 win over the Cardinals. Martinez has pitched once since Sept. 19, going four innings against the Astros on Sept. 30. He allowed three runs on six hits.

The sinker was a good idea, considering that balls hit in the air at Coors Field can be dangerous. However, he didn't control it as well as the four-seamer, so he went with what was working for him. Nonetheless, his strong second-half performance led manager Jim Tracy to pick him over Jason Marquis for the start.
away_pitcher_note: The Game 3 start that was originally supposed to go to Pedro Martinez is now Happ's, after the originally scheduled game for Saturday was bumped back to Sunday due to wintry conditions in Colorado. Happ, who will be making his first postseason start, was struck on the left leg with a line drive during a seventh-inning relief appearance during Game 2 on Thursday.  The rookie left-hander threw just four pitches during the outing and has since said that his leg isn't bothering him.  One of the leading candidates to be named the National League's Rookie of the Year, Happ went 10-4 with a 2.99 ERA in the 23 starts that he made this year.  He tossed a four-hit shutout against the Rockies on Aug. 5 at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez was strong for nearly four innings in Game 1, until he started missing up in the zone and over the plate. He gave up five runs in five innings and took a 5-1 loss. It's possible that if the Rockies had made the most of their chances in the first two innings, he'd have been in better position. But Jimenez did not pitch to his regular-season standards, when he went six innings in 29 of his 33 starts. He was 8-5 with a 3.4 ERA in 15 starts at Coors Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: While making his first career postseason appearance in Game 1 at Citizens Bank Park on Wednesday afternoon, Lee fell one out shy of completing a shutout.  The reigning American League Cy Young Award winner also limited the Rockies to one run and six hits in seven innings on Aug. 6.   Now Lee will be asked to conquer the challenge that will be presented as he pitches in Coors Field for the first time in his career. During Wednesday's dominant effort, the 31-year-old left-hander had retired 16 straight batters before surrendering a two-out seventh-inning double. The frigid conditions that were present this weekend are supposed to disappear before Monday, when game-time temperature is projected to be in the low 50s.

home_pitcher_note: In Game 1 of the NLCS against the Philadelphia Phillies, the Dodgers will hand the ball to the 21-year-old lefty Kershaw. The decision comes after Kershaw threw 6 2/3 innings of two-run ball against the Cardinals in the NLDS in the Dodgers' comeback win. Kershaw didn't show any nerves in his first-career postseason start as he was able to get out of jams and keep the Cardinals from capitalizing on run-scoring opportunities. Kershaw was the Dodgers' most electrifying pitcher this season, using his four-seam fastball and his curveball to pile up strikeouts and limit hitters to a .200 average. He went 8-8 with a 2.79 ERA in 2009 but was 0-2 with a 5.23 ERA in two starts against the Phillies this year.
away_pitcher_note: With an impressive resume against the Dodgers and the benefit of six days' rest, Hamels is set up well to open the National League Championship Series against the Dodgers. During a 2009 regular season that was at times a rough followup to his 2008 heroics, Hamels pitched a shutout at Dodger Stadium on June 4, one of his two on the season. That was after going 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in two starts against them in last year's NLCS to earn series Most Valuable Player honors, and he is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA in four career regular-season starts against them. However, Hamels finished the 2009 season 10-11 with a 4.32 ERA, and was 0-2 with a 7.02 ERA in his last three regular-season starts. His NL Division Series Game 2 start against the Rockies didn't alter that trend much, as he allowed four earned runs in five innings of work in a 5-4 loss. He left that game following his exit from the mound to attend the birth of his first child, and remained in Philadelphia to work out as the Phillies clinched their second consecutive NLCS berth in Denver.

home_pitcher_note: Vicente Padilla, a former Phillie, has resurrected his career in a big way after being released by the Rangers. He's unbeaten as a Dodger with four regular-season wins and the first-round clincher in St. Louis, when he threw seven scoreless innings and looked perfectly capable of finishing it up. Padilla had a dicey reputation with the Rangers as headhunter, but has been a model citizen with the Dodgers, impressive enough against the Cardinals to get moved up in the rotation. His teammates watch a sinking fastball that stays around 94 mph and can't believe he was released. He's faced the Phillies only once, allowing seven runs in a six-inning start in 2008. He's had plenty of experience at Citizens Bank Park, going 10-11 with a 4.98 ERA in his last two years with the Phillies after going 15-15 with a 2.97 ERA at Veterans Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez will be making his first postseason appearance since beating the Cardinals in Game 3 of the 2004 World Series. The 37-year-old right-hander, who joined the Phillies in August, has pitched just seven innings since Sept. 13.  But after watching the veteran hurler complete a simulated game on Tuesday, Phillies manager Charlie Manuel once again reiterated that he's comfortable putting him out there as a starter. Martinez has gone 3-5 with a 4.02 ERA in nine career starts against the Dodgers. This is his first appearance against them since 2006. In 13 career playoff appearances, the three-time Cy Young Award winner has gone 6-2 with a 3.40 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lee has shown he is more than ready to pitch in the postseason. He looked dominant in Games 1 and 4 of the National League Division Series against the Colorado Rockies. He allowed one run and six hits in a complete-game 5-1 victory over the Rockies in Game 1 at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed just one earned run in 7 1/3 innings in a dramatic 5-4 comeback victory in Game 4 at Coors Field. Lee scuffled a bit late in the regular season, but it appears the postseason has energized him. He seems to want to make the most of the moment. The Cleveland Indians left him off their 2007 postseason roster, which is something he hasn't forgotten. He won the American League Cy Young last season before the Indians traded him and outfielder Ben Francisco to the Phillies on July 29 for prospects Jason Knapp, Carlos Carrasco, Lou Marson and Jason Donald.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda passed a final exam Tuesday, proving to Joe Torre and Rick Honeycutt that the herniated disk in his neck was healed enough to take the ball after being left off the roster for the first round against the Cardinals. While it will be almost three weeks since Kuroda pitched in a Major League game, management believes he's enough of a gamer to give him the first start in a hostile Citizens Bank Park. That conclusion was reached based in large part on how clutch Kuroda was in last year's playoffs, having been the only Dodgers starter to beat the Phillies. In his only start against them this year, he threw six scoreless innings in a no-decision. In three regular-season starts against them he's allowed only two earned runs in 19 innings. It's been a nightmarish season for the Opening Day starter, from a strained oblique muscle to the line drive he took off his head to the herniated disk, but all will be forgotten if he can duplicate last October's success.

home_pitcher_note: Phillies manager Charlie Manuel picked right-hander Joe Blanton over left-hander J.A. Happ for this start. Pitching out of the bullpen, Blanton made two appearances in the NL Division Series against the Rockies, allowing two earned run in 4 2/3 innings. Blanton was 12-8 with a 4.05 ERA in 31 starts during the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: Randy Wolf, another former Phillie, took a demotion to make this start after getting the Game 1 nod in the first round against the Cardinals. On a generally short leash during the regular season, even though he led the club in innings pitched, Wolf got yanked from his first career postseason appearance after allowing only two runs in a shaky 3 2/3 innings. That said, he went 6-1 down the stretch and held opposing left-handed hitters to an average of .159, which should serve him well against a Phillies lineup loaded with lefties. On the other hand, Wolf was 1-1 with a 5.11 ERA against Philadelphia this year and is 9-7 with a 4.30 ERA at Citizens Bank Park, although most of those starts had the Phillies lineup supporting him, not facing him. His 2.78 road ERA was fifth in the league.

home_pitcher_note: Last year's NLCS and World Series MVP has not been sharp this postseason, allowing eight earned runs in 10 1/3 innings (6.97 ERA). Hamels pitched well in Los Angeles in Game 1 before encountering trouble in the fifth. He would earn the win, but he allowed four runs in 5 1/3 innings. With a victory Wednesday, Hamels will seal the Phillies' second consecutive NL pennant.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Joe Torre tends to go with the hot hand, so he selected Vicente Padilla to start what has turned into a do-or-die assignment with the Dodgers facing elimination. Padilla, released by Texas in August, is as close as the Dodgers have to an ace in October. When he starts, the club expects to be in the game. He is coming off a rousing no-decision duel with Pedro Martinez against his former club, allowing only one run over 7 1/3 innings. And that followed seven scoreless innings in the NL Division Series clincher in St. Louis. In fact, Padilla hasn't lost since signing with the Dodgers. He's handled pressure starts, pitched well on the road and impressed the staff with a devastating hard sinker that he throws consistently for strikes.

home_pitcher_note:
Sabathia has been a rock for the Yankees all season and certainly a nice return on a heavy financial investment (seven years, $161 million). This is what they're paying him for, the kind of starts he's had in the postseason.

The big left-hander earned ALCS MVP honors for winning his two starts against the Angels, Games 1 and 4, after allowing just two runs in 16 innings (1.13 ERA), along with nine hits, three walks and 12 strikeouts. Overall in this postseason, Sabathia is 3-0 with a 1.19 ERA (three earned runs in 22 2/3 innings), 20 strikeouts and three walks.

In Game 1 of the World Series at Yankee Stadium, Sabathia (the 2007 AL Cy Young Award winner) faces former Indians teammate -- and 2008 AL Cy Young Award honoree -- Cliff Lee in a matchup of ace southpaws. In a start at the Stadium against the Phillies on May 24, Sabathia allowed three runs in eight innings on nine hits, with no walks and four strikeouts, in a no-decision. The Yankees lost that game, 4-3, in 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note:
2008 AL Cy Young winner Cliff Lee will face off against former teammate and 2007 AL Cy Young Award winner CC Sabathia in Game 1 of the World Series at Yankee Stadium. Lee is 4-4 with a 5.02 ERA in nine career starts against the Yankees, but is 2-1 with a 1.89 ERA in his last three against them. That included a 10-2 victory over the Yankees in the opening of new Yankee Stadium on April 16, when Lee still pitched for the Cleveland Indians.

The 30-year-old lefty, who had no prior playoff experience, has done nothing but dominate in October. He allowed three hits over eight shutout innings in the Phillies' 11-0 Game 3 victory over the Dodgers in the NLCS, lowering his 2009 postseason ERA to 0.74. Lee allowed one run during a complete-game victory in Game 1 of the Division Series against Colorado. In Game 4 of that series, he allowed three runs (one earned) in 7 1/3 innings. All told, that's two earned runs in 24 1/3 innings.

In his NLCS start, he almost got a chance to put up another zero and to become the third pitcher in the Wild Card era to toss two complete games in a single postseason. Phillies manager Charlie Manuel let Lee hit in the bottom of the eighth -- he singled -- and was going to send him out for the ninth. But once Shane Victorino hit a three-run home run, Manuel decided to entrust an 11-run lead to the bullpen. Lee had already thrown 114 pitches, but didn't appear to be tiring: He struck out two in a 10-pitch eighth inning.

"I don't think I ever doubted myself," said Lee, who had been demoted to Triple-A during the 2007 season before his breakout 2008 campaign. "I always had confidence in myself and felt like I could pitch in a big game. But you never know until you get the opportunity. It's a challenge."

home_pitcher_note:
After two wild yet effective starts, Burnett finally faltered in his third career playoff outing, in Game 5 of the American League Championship Series. Though Burnett improved greatly as the day went on, throwing five shutout innings after allowing the first four batters of the game to score, the early damage was enough to keep the Angels in the series for one additional game.

Burnett will look to improve in Game 2 of the World Series against the Phillies, a team that beat him earlier this season at Yankee Stadium. Three homers -- all on fastballs -- were at the root of his troubles that day, which perhaps bodes well for a reversal. In three postseason starts, two of them at home, Burnett has not allowed a single home run.
away_pitcher_note:
It makes a great story to have Martinez pitch Game 2 of the World Series at Yankee Stadium, but does it make the most sense? Martinez is 11-11 with a 3.20 ERA in 32 career starts against the Yankees, and is 1-2 with a 4.71 ERA in six postseason appearances against them.

"I think he's still got quite a bit left," Manuel said. "I was watching those playoff games that he pitched in. His velocity was sitting 87 to 91 mph, and he was even better than that at Dodger Stadium. That was a couple years ago when he pitched those games against the Yankees. He knows how to pitch. His command is good. He uses all of his pitches. His command is absolutely outstanding. He doesn't rely on throwing the ball by people anymore, but he's a pitcher."

home_pitcher_note:
Hamels is 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in three postseason starts. He has allowed 20 hits, 11 runs, two walks and six home runs in 14 1/3 innings. He has struck out 12 and opponents have hit .328 against him. Hamels is 0-1 with a 2.77 ERA in two career starts against the Yankees.

"I look at Hamels and I still feel like he's got the game in him," Manuel said. "Baseball is a funny game. I say that all the time. He's very capable of throwing a good game. He was getting hit around a little bit the other night and he didn't have the command that he usually has, but at the same time, he's the guy. He's very capable of throwing a shutout every time he goes out there."
away_pitcher_note:
As much as ever this season, Pettitte is in a groove. In all three of his postseason outings, he has pitched 6 1/3 innings, never allowing more than three runs or fewer than one. Most importantly for Pettitte, the control problems that have plagued him at times this season have vanished -- over his three postseason outings, he has struck out 15 batters and walked just three.

In his last start, Game 6 of the American League Championship Series against the Angels, Pettitte allowed one run on seven hits, striking out six and becoming baseball's all-time postseason wins leader.

Though Pettitte's low-velocity offerings don't strike quite the same fear in Philadelphia's lefty sluggers as CC Sabathia's pitches do, Pettitte has handled that group just fine. Ryan Howard is just 1-for-9 in his career off Pettitte, who has been markedly better on the road this season than at home. Chase Utley is 1-for-7 off him and Raul Ibanez, the best of the bunch, is 6-for-21.

Pettitte has not pitched at Citizens Bank Park since 2006, but he held the Phillies to four runs over seven innings in an Interleague no-decision at Yankee Stadium in May. He has a career 2-2 record with a 3.67 ERA in seven regular season starts against the Phillies. In 11 career World Series starts, Pettitte is 3-4 with a 3.82 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Phillies manager Charlie Manuel has opted to go with Blanton in Game 4 instead of ace Cliff Lee, who would be operating on short rest, to make this start. Blanton made one start in the NL Championship Series, allowing three earned runs in six innings against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia has been a horse for the Yankees rotation and will start on three days' rest for the second time this postseason on Sunday night. Sabathia threw 113 pitches in Game 1's loss, holding every Phillies hitter not named Chase Utley -- who homered twice -- to just two hits over seven innings. He suffered the loss in the Phillies' eventual 6-1 win.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies pin their World Series championship hopes on left-hander Cliff Lee, who has been incredible this postseason. He is 3-0 with a 0.54 ERA in four postseason starts. That is the best ERA of any pitcher in a single postseason who has pitched 30 or more innings. It is the seventh-best single postseason ERA of all time. Lee threw a complete game against the Yankees in Game 1. He allowed no earned runs and no walks and struck out 10 to pick up the 6-1 victory. They don't need perfection, but they need something close from him if the Phillies are going to extend the Series and send it back to New York for Game 6 on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: After a rocky first three innings in Game 2 in which he threw 61 pitches, Burnett settled down in his first World Series start and was near unhittable, outdueling Phillies starter Pedro Martinez as the Yankees won, 3-1, to even the Classic at a game apiece. Burnett struck out nine and walked two while turning in his third quality start in four postseason outings. He is 1-0 with a 3.55 ERA in those contests, but take out one bad first inning against the Angels and his ERA is a sterling 2.13.

home_pitcher_note: While Pettitte is expected to make the start, Yankees manager Joe Girardi said after the Game 5 loss that nothing has been officially decided. "Physically I've got to see how he is," Girardi said. "He threw a side [Monday] and felt good.  But I'll check with him [Tuesday]."
away_pitcher_note: Phillies right-hander Pedro Martinez gets a chance to add to his legend at Yankee Stadium in Game 6 of the World Series. Martinez allowed three runs in six innings in a 3-1 loss to the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium in Game 2. He will be pitching on five days' rest, while Yankees left-hander Andy Pettitte will be pitching on three days' rest. That could be an advantage for Martinez, although he knows there are few easy outs in the Yankees lineup. But Martinez, who called himself the most influential player in Yankee Stadium history, certainly is not going to shy away from the situation.

summary: 2010-03-03 - Florida State Seminoles @ Philadelphia Phillies (Completed Early)

home_pitcher_note: Happ has allowed six runs over 16 1/3 innings this Spring Training for a 3.31 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm, making his final start before the regular season, has allowed 19 hits and 11 runs -- nine earned -- this spring.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan will be making back-to-back Opening Day starts for Washington. Last year, he lasted three innings and gave up six runs on six hits against the Marlins on the road. Lannan is hoping that things will be different when he faces Phillies ace Roy Halladay. Last season, Lannan was clearly the Nationals' best pitcher. Although he is getting the Opening Day nod, Lannan made it clear that Jason Marquis is the leader of the Nationals' pitching staff. Marquis leads by example, Lannan said. Lannan is expected to pitch twice during the first week of the regular season. Besides Opening Day, Lannan will face the Mets on April 10.
away_pitcher_note: This is the debut Phillies fans eagerly have been waiting for. Halladay joined the Phillies in December as arguably the best pitcher in baseball. Fans liked what they have seen in Spring Training, but now it matters. Halladay waived his no-trade clause to join the Phillies because he wants to play for a team that has a chance to win the World Series. If Halladay is healthy and is as effective as he has been in the past, he could win 20 or more games pitching in the National League with one of the game's best lineups behind him.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis, 31, is coming off one of his best seasons, going 15-13 with a 4.04 ERA with the Rockies. He also represented Colorado in the All-Star Game. During his 10-year career -- which has included stints with the Braves, Cardinals, Cubs and Rockies -- Marquis has won 94 games and posted a 4.48 ERA. He is a groundball-type pitcher and relies heavily on a sinker. Marquis has had three seasons of 200 innings or more. Washington also signed Marquis because he is an above-average hitting pitcher. He has a career .202 batting average with five home runs and 48 RBIs. Marquis also is considered a good baserunner.
away_pitcher_note: One of the reasons the Phillies felt they could trade left-hander Cliff Lee to Seattle is that they were confident Hamels will bounce back following a disappointing 2009. Hamels rededicated himself in the offseason, throwing more than he ever has before. He entered camp in great shape, throwing well and working on establishing a more effective curveball and introducing a cutter. Hamels had a lot of success in the past as a fastball-changeup pitcher. He hopes being able to throw four pitches keeps hitters guessing and gets him back to being the dominant pitcher he had been in the past.

home_pitcher_note: Of the five starters named by manager Jim Riggleman, Stammen appeared to be a longshot when Spring Training began. Stammen had bone ships removed from his right elbow last September and it appeared he would start the season in the bullpen or be sent down to the Minor Leagues. It turned out he was the second-best pitcher behind right-hander Stephen Strasburg. Stammen allowed five earned runs in 14 1/3 innings and struck out 10 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick battled left-hander Jamie Moyer for the fifth spot in the rotation and ultimately lost to start the season in the bullpen. Except that Kendrick will start the season in the rotation because right-hander Joe Blanton has opened the season on the 15-day disabled list with a strained left oblique. Blanton could miss anywhere from three to six weeks, but this is going to be a good opportunity for Kendrick to show the Phillies that he deserves to keep a spot in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Norris was roughed up in his final spring outing Saturday against Toronto at Minute Maid Park. He has never faced the Phillies in his brief career, as he appeared in 11 games, including 10 starts, for the Astros in his Major League debut last year. He went 6-3 with a 4.53 ERA, going 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA in his final four starts of the year before being shut down as a precaution due to a heavy workload. He was named the Pacific Coast League Pitcher of the Year in 2009, going 4-9 with a 2.63 ERA in 19 starts at Triple-A Round Rock.
away_pitcher_note: Happ enters the 2010 motivated. He finished in second place in the 2009 NL Rookie of the Year voting to Marlins outfielder Chris Coghlan. He also has heard sabermetricians predict that he will regress after being the recipient of some good luck last season. Time will tell, but Happ has worked on a sinker this spring, which he hopes adds another dimension to his pitching repertoire and keeps hitters from making all the adjustments they need to make.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino battled back spasms at the end of Spring Training and was scratched from starting Saturday's exhibition finale against Toronto at Minute Maid Park, even though he told manager Brad Mills he was ready to pitch. The Astros wanted to be cautious with the often-injured right-hander who won the No. 5 spot in the rotation by having a good spring (1-1 with a 3.78 ERA in five games, including four starts). Paulino went 3-11 with a 6.27 ERA in 23 games (17 starts) for the Astros last year. He's 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in one career start against Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer had three offseason surgeries, which many thought might put him behind schedule once Spring Training began in February. But Moyer came into camp in good shape and pitched well, earning him the fifth spot in the Phillies' rotation over right-hander Kyle Kendrick. It is nothing short of an accomplishment. Moyer is 47 years, 5 months old. Just five pitchers in baseball history have pitched at an older age: Hoyt Wilhelm (at 48 and 49 in 1970-71), Phil Niekro (48 in 1987), Jack Quinn (48-49 in 1931-33), Nick Altrock (48 in 1924) and Satchel Paige (58 in 1965).

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt makes his first appearance since holding the San Francisco Giants to seven hits and three runs in six innings in an Opening Day loss. He needs one win to pass Larry Dierker for sole possession of second on the club's all-time wins list. He and Dierker have 137 wins. Oswalt has pitched well against the Phillies in his career, going 6-1 with a 3.23 ERA in 11 games (nine starts). In his only start against them last Sept. 5 in Houston, he held the Phillies to four hits, two runs and struck out eight batters in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay stepped on the mound on Opening Day with high expectations. The Phillies sent three top prospects to the Blue Jays for him, and they also traded Cliff Lee to Seattle to clear salary and get prospects in return. Halladay allowed one run in the first inning against the Nationals, but finished throwing six scoreless innings in an 11-1 victory. Halladay allowed six hits, one run and two walks and struck out nine in the opener. The Phillies hope for more of the same against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is hoping to finetune his command in time for Monday's home opener against the Nationals at Citizens Bank Park. He threw 103 pitches, just 63 strikes, in Wednesday's 8-4 victory over the Nationals at Nationals Park. In five innings, he allowed five hits, three runs (two earned runs) and four walks. He struck out five. It was just the fourth time since his rookie season in 2006 that he had walked four or more batters.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis will be facing the Phillies for the second time in less than a week. This past Wednesday, Marquis, making his Nationals debut, looked like the player who had serious control problems early in Spring Training. In the first inning, Marquis threw 28 pitches, walked three batters and allowed two runs. After walking his third batter in the inning, however, Marquis retired eight of the next nine hitters he faced, but he got himself into trouble again in the fourth. With one out, Marquis allowed an RBI single to Phillies starter Cole Hamels. In the next inning, with the game tied at 3, Marquis didn't retire a batter. With a runner on second, Chase Utley singled to left to drive in Placido Polanco, giving Philly the lead. Then, Ryan Howard came to the plate and hit a two-run homer, effectively putting the game out of reach. Marquis, who left the game after the Howard homer, pitched four-plus innings, giving up six runs on eight hits.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick followed a fantastic Spring Training with a disappointing season debut Thursday against the Nationals at Nationals Park. He allowed six hits, five runs and one home run in just four innings. He struck out two. Kendrick left too many balls over the plate in the first inning. He retired nine consecutive batters at one point, but Willie Harris hit a hanging changeup in the fourth inning to ruin any thoughts of a nice recovery.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen didn't figure in the decision last week against the Phillies as the Nationals won the game, 6-5. Stammen, who was victimized by sloppy defense, allowed four runs in five innings. If there was good news in the game, it was that Stammen was 100-percent healthy. He was in pain all last year because of bone chips in his right elbow. The injury was the reason he was unable to throw his breaking pitches effectively.

home_pitcher_note: Happ threw five scoreless innings Friday against the Houston Astros at Minute Park. He allowed six hits and two walks and struck out five. But he wasn't as efficient as he would like to be, throwing 103 pitches in the process. Happ is hoping to be a little more economical in the series finale against the Nationals. If he does that, he should pitch deeper and give the bullpen a rest.
away_pitcher_note: With Garrett Mock optioned to Triple-A Syracuse, the Nationals will promote Olsen in time for this game. Olsen didn't make the 25-man roster because the team wanted him to build arm strength after having shoulder surgery last summer. In his first start for Syracuse, Olsen pitched 6 1/3 innings and gave up four runs on eight hits. He didn't figure in the decision. While the numbers didn't look great, it appears that Olsen's fastball is back where it should be. It was clocked in the low 90s in the game.

home_pitcher_note: It doesn't get much better than Halladay's performance against Houston, his second start in a Phillies uniform. So far, the former AL Cy Young winner's transition to the National League has been a piece of cake. His complete-game gem against the Astros lasted two hours and 21 minutes, with only seven hits allowed, no walks and eight strikeouts. Sure, his initial two outings have come against the Nationals and Astros. But Doc's just getting his feet wet in a new league. He's faced the Marlins twice in his career, and is 0-1 with a 5.00 ERA against them. It will be his first start at home, though, and that should give Halladay an additional edge.
away_pitcher_note: Aggressively pounding the strike zone is what the Marlins have been looking for out of Sanchez. For the most part, the 26-year-old did that in his first start. In six innings, he struck out five and walked just one against the Dodgers. He did have a rough fourth inning, giving up four runs. Sanchez wasn't involved in the decision. The right-hander will make his first road start. For his career, he is 2-4 with a 5.40 ERA against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer had an interesting debut Saturday against Houston. He retired the first eight batters he faced. He then allowed the next eight batters to reach base to give the Astros a 5-4 lead. He retired seven of the final nine batters he faced. In six innings, he allowed nine hits, five runs, one walk and two home runs. He at least kept the Phillies in the game. They came back to beat the Astros, 9-6.
away_pitcher_note: The long ball haunted Nolasco in his last start against the Reds, when he gave up three home runs -- two to Scott Rolen and one to Orlando Cabrera -- in a no-decision on Monday. The 27-year-old, pretty much unhittable in Spring Training, finished after giving up five runs on nine hits and a walk while striking out four and firing 92 pitches. The last time Nolasco had given up three home runs was June 5, 2008, against the Braves. For his career against the Phillies, Nolasco is 5-3 with a 4.23 ERA in 11 games (eight starts).

home_pitcher_note: Hamels earned his second win of the season on Monday in Philadelphia's home opener against the Nationals, but it wasn't as uplifting an outing as the Phillies would have liked from their No. 2 starter. Hamels labored through 5 2/3 innings, allowing four runs on six hits and 109 pitches. Still searching for his efficiency, Hamels has struggled hitting his spots and mixing in a new cut fastball. Though his performance was a step up from his first start, Hamels is still not at the level Philadelphia expects from him. He has typically struggled in day games throughout his career, and Sunday's matinee against Florida will represent his second straight. He is just 2-6 in his career against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: It could have been worse for Robertson in his last start. The lefty gave up six runs (three earned) in five innings against the Reds. He trailed by as many as five runs, but settled for a no-decision. The lefty has worked five innings in each of his first two starts and was taken deep for homers twice by the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson has been inconsistent with his command while issuing seven walks and registering 14 strikeouts in the 11 1/3 innings that have encompassed his first two starts. After being doomed by a pair of solo shots in his April 8 season debut, the 23-year-old right-hander came back on Wednesday and limited the Padres to one run in six innings.   Hanson is 7-3 with a 2.54 ERA in his past 13 starts.   Two of his losses during this span have come courtesy of the Phillies, who tagged him for five earned runs in seven innings that were completed in rain-interrupted games.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick's last outing couldn't have been much worse -- 1 2/3 innings, six hits, six runs, three walks and only 23 total strikes to 14 hitters. The 25-year-old right-hander hasn't exactly secured anything since he took over for the injured Joe Blanton to start the season. Despite a solid Spring Training, Kendrick has struggled with his command and the location of his off-speed pitches. He'll be happy not to see Washington again, although Atlanta's lineup won't be any easier. With Blanton due off the disabled list shortly, Kendrick's time in the rotation is likely limited, and questions already arose about whether he would even make his next start. But the Phillies want him to be an option as a starter down the road, so they may be more patient with him.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson felt he battled a tight strike zone while issuing five walks (highest total since 2006) and allowing two earned runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Padres on Thursday. This marked the first time since Aug. 25, 2007 that he completed a start that didn't include a strikeout. As shaky as he was against the Padres, Hudson proved every bit as dominant six days earlier when he limited the Giants to two earned runs and three hits in seven innings.  The veteran right-hander went 4-2 with a 2.68 ERA in his first six career starts against the Phillies. But in his past nine starts against the reigning National League champs, he is 0-4 with a 4.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay said in Spring Training that he didn't mind being compared to Cliff Lee this season. So far the comparisons are more than a little interesting. Lee went 3-0 with a 1.13 ERA in his first three starts for the Phillies last season. Halladay has the identical record and ERA in his first three starts for the Phillies. Things figured to get a little tougher for Halladay on Wednesday, facing a Braves lineup that seems to be more potent than the lineups Halladay has faced in Washington and Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe's perfect start to the season has been aided by the fact that the Braves have scored at least seven runs in each of the first three games that he started. The veteran sinkerballer has uncharacteristically allowed three home runs in the first 17 1/3 innings that he has completed this year. He had completed 83 2/3 innings before he allowed his third homer last year. Lowe is 5-0 with a 2.08 ERA in his past six starts against the Phillies dating back to the 2006 season. In his three starts against them last year, he worked 19 2/3 innings and allowed just three earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer has been unable to avoid the big inning in his first two starts. He allowed five runs in the first inning in his last start Saturday against the Marlins, but threw five scoreless innings after that. Of course, five runs is five runs and the Phillies lost the game, 5-1. But with J.A. Happ hurting and Kyle Kendrick struggling, the Phillies really need a better effort from Moyer.

home_pitcher_note: Benson was signed to a Minor League deal on March 17 and began the season at Triple-A Reno. He made one start at Reno and pitched well enough to get the call when the D-backs needed a fifth starter. Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey were the candidates who Benson beat out for the spot. His first start for the D-backs was last Saturday night in San Diego. He pitched out of bases-loaded jams in the first and second innings and managed to last six innings and allow just two runs. Last season he appeared in eight games (two starts) for the Rangers, going 1-1 with an 8.46 ERA. Benson missed the entire 2007 season after having shoulder and elbow surgery. In one appearance for Reno this year, he allowed two unearned runs in five innings while pitching in 40-degree weather. Benson was the first overall pick by the Pirates in the 1996 First-Year Player Draft.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies lost to the Marlins on Sunday, 2-0, but it almost felt like a victory. Almost. Why? Because Hamels pitched like the '08 Hamels, not the '09 Hamels. He allowed just two runs in eight-plus innings, which has many Phillies fans hoping Roy Halladay and Hamels can be the 1-2 punch everybody envisioned before the season started.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy was victimized by a poor outing by the bullpen in his last start against the Padres on Sunday at PETCO Park. The right-hander worked five scoreless innings, striking out seven while allowing just two hits. He left the game with a 2-0 lead, but Arizona relievers allowed five runs in the seventh inning as the Padres rallied for a 5-3 win. Kennedy has not been able to get past the fifth inning in any of his three starts because of high pitch counts. He allowed six runs to the Dodgers in his second start of the year and three runs over five innings in his first start. He appeared in just one game for the Yankees in 2009 and four in Triple-A after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. He came to Arizona in the three-team trade with the Yankees and Tigers that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies turn to Figueroa because they just placed left-hander J.A. Happ on the disabled list. They could have called up a pitcher from Triple-A Lehigh Valley, but they chose Figueroa because he has started in the past and has pitched successfully in three relief appearances as the Phillies' long man.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez battled hard in his last start, getting through seven innings to help rest a tired bullpen. The right-hander held the Cardinals to two runs on seven hits while walking four and striking out three. Two of his three outings so far have been outstanding. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. Lopez came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff earlier in the decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick figured out a couple things Tuesday, when he threw eight scoreless innings against the Braves at Turner Field: get aggressive and throw his sinker. He did both and easily pitched his best after compiling a gaudy 17.47 ERA after his first two starts. Kendrick hopes to keep it going in the series finale against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants believe Sanchez didn't get what he deserved the last time he was on the mound, and understandably so. He tossed a one-hitter in a 1-0 loss to San Diego. It was the Giants' first loss in 24 one-hit efforts since the franchise moved to San Francisco in 1958. He struck out 10 against the Padres, his second consecutive double-digit total. In the second inning, he walked the bases loaded, but struck out the side.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is having his way four starts into his National League career. He already has thrown one shutout and one other complete game. He has walked just three batters. He has struck out 28. He is one of just three pitchers to start 4-0 with an ERA under 1.00 ERA in his first four starts with a team. Fernando Valenzuela (Dodgers in 1981) and Cliff Lee (Phillies in 2009) are the others.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer owns an 8.67 ERA, the result of three poor outings. His worst was April 16 against the Dodgers, when he allowed seven runs, six hits and three walks in four innings. He went 6 1/3 innings and allowed four runs, three hits and four walks in a loss to the Padres on April 21. He's been better against right-handed hitters, with a .182 average against, but left-handers are batting .385.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer took a step forward Thursday in Atlanta, where he allowed four hits and two unearned runs in six innings against the Braves. Phillies starters not named Roy Halladay have struggled this season, so Moyer could provide the Phillies a boost with consecutive solid performances. Moyer is 0-2 with a 7.36 ERA in two career appearances at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Even on a night when Lincecum didn't have his best control in the early going Friday against the Cardinals, the two-time Cy Young winner still struck out eight and allowed just one run in the 4-1 win that stopped a four-game losing streak. Even if he didn't have it all flowing, his grittiness in the outing impressed his fellow teammates and showed something in itself. With runners on first and second and none out, he got Albert Pujols to pop out and Matt Holliday to ground into a double play. Lincecum has at least seven strikeouts in each start this season and boasts a 1.00 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Just when it looks like Hamels is about to take a step forward, he takes a step backward. He allowed four home runs Friday against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. If he encounters similar problems Wednesday against the Giants, it likely would not result in a good outcome for the Phillies. They are facing Giants ace Tim Lincecum.

home_pitcher_note: Just when it looked like Kyle Kendrick had taken a step forward, he took a step backward Sunday in a start against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. He threw eight scoreless innings against the Atlanta Braves on April 20 and had thrown four more scoreless innings against Arizona before he allowed five runs in the fifth inning in an 8-6 loss. Kendrick is going to have to start pitching better with right-hander Joe Blanton and closer Brad Lidge expected to rejoin the team soon.
away_pitcher_note: After four starts, Niese still is seeking his first extended and successful start, not to mention his first victory. His next chance comes on Friday night against a team he never has faced. Because of the Mets' off-day Thursday, Niese will have abnormal rest -- five days -- before he opposes Chase Utley, Ryan Howard, et al. Extra rest is not a bad thing to have when pitching in that adversarial arena. Niese has allowed one home run in 22 innings, that to Ryan Spilborghs in Denver, and four in 61 2/3 innings in his career. But CBP can change a pitcher's ERA and home run total quickly. Niese has been more effective against left-handed hitters than right-handed thus far this season, and that constitutes a change from his two previous -- and abbreviated -- big league tours. He does appear more inclined to pitching inside to them, and his cutter now gives him a weapon for right-handed hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay proved he is human on Monday in a loss to the San Francisco Giants at AT&T Park. He allowed 10 hits and five runs in seven innings to pick up his first loss of the season. Halladay wasn't as sharp as he had been in his previous four starts, but the Giants also hit some pretty good pitches. This will be Halladay's first taste of the Phillies-Mets rivalry, and the slumping Phillies will be counting on him to throw well.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey hasn't allowed a run in 24 innings. How he extended his streak from 19 to 24 was attributable to his increased repertoire. With his fastball and newly-minted cutter failing him Sunday night, he threw a variety of pitches to keep the Braves off-balance and emerged with another victory. He surrendered five hits and five walks and struck out three in five innings, throwing 61 pitches in the first two innings and 106 over all. He has been moderately successful against the Phillies in the last three years -- a 4-2 record and 4.82 ERA in nine starts. But his appearances in Citizens Bank Park haven't been too rewarding -- 1-1 record and 7.17 ERA in four starts. Pelfrey, who has allowed no home runs in 26 innings this season, has allowed merely 37 in his 505 career innings -- 10 at Shea Stadium, six at Citi Field and six at Citizens Bank. Chase Utley has hit four against him, at least one at each site.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer pitched well enough to win Tuesday in a loss to the San Francisco Giants at AT&T Park. He allowed 10 hits and four runs in six innings, which is good enough for the Phillies offense on most nights. But the Phillies have been struggling offensively and provided Moyer no support. Moyer will have to be much better Sunday against the Mets. He is facing Mets ace Johan Santana, so runs figure to be even more scarce.
away_pitcher_note: On a chilly day in the Windy Citi, Santana persevered through 115 pitches, a season high for him, and shut down the Dodgers for six innings Tuesday. His work led to a shutout victory and set him up to face the Phillies in their small ballpark. The Mets usually opt to have Santana get as much rest as possible, and with an off-day two days after his start against the Dodgers, they could have afforded him five days' rest. But he would have missed the Phillies that way. And, worse, the Mets would have Ollie Perez pitching Sunday. This way, their Sunday night starter will be one who has a 4-1 career and 2.98 ERA in eight starts against the Phillies in the last three years and a 1-1 record and 3.21 ERA in four starts at CBP in the same span. Ryan Howard and Chase Utley have hit three home runs each against Santana. And Raul Ibanez is batting .350 in 40 career at-bats against the Mets starter.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton makes his 2010 season debut after spending the first month of the season on the disabled list with a strained left oblique. The Phillies don't expect Blanton to have perfect command in his first start of the season, but they certainly hope he performs better than most of the rest of the rotation this season. Phillies starters not named Roy Halladay entered Sunday with a 5.19 ERA, which has put a strain on the bullpen and the offense. The Phillies like to call Blanton an innings eater. Six-plus innings would be welcomed Monday.
away_pitcher_note: It's another tough test for Garcia, who's seen plenty of them already this year. This time it's not so much the opposing starter -- no Tim Lincecum or Johan Santana -- as it is the opposing lineup and the ballpark. Garcia will be facing the National League's best lineup, and a team that last year was also as good as any against left-handed pitching. And he'll be doing it in the claustrophobic confines of Citizens Bank Park, one of the toughest parks on pitchers in the league. Good luck, kid.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is coming off another so-so outing against San Francisco, in which he struck out a season-high 10, but allowed another four earned runs in six innings with four walks and nine hits. His velocity worked its way up to 93, which is a good sign for the Phillies left-hander. But April wasn't a strong month, and Hamels carries a 5.28 ERA and 1.47 WHIP into his first start in May. The Phillies may bump Hamels to Tuesday if they decide to activate Joe Blanton off the 15-day disabled list to start Monday. That would split up the left-handers Hamels and Jamie Moyer in the Phils' rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright is coming off his least-impressive start of the year, but that just tells you how good he's been in 2010. When three runs in six innings counts as not-up-to-snuff, you're going pretty well. Over Wainwright's last 32 starts, dating back to mid-May of last season, he's 20-8 with a 2.23 ERA, 209 strikeouts, 53 walks and 13 home runs allowed in 229 2/3 innings. Wainwright has held his own nicely at Citizens Bank Park, with eight shutout innings over two career appearances (one start).

home_pitcher_note: Many Phillies fans wondered if Kendrick would get another chance to start, carrying a 7.61 ERA after five starts. But the Phillies have little choice but to stick with him with left-hander J.A. Happ still on the disabled list. "We need Kyle to step up," pitching coach Rich Dubee said. "We need him to be more efficient. We need him to pitch down in the strike zone. We need his temp to pick up so we have energy playing behind him. And he's aware of those things. Now he has to put them in play."
away_pitcher_note: Penny looked a bit shaky for the first time as a Cardinal his last time out, and he still turned in an effective outing. He wasn't helped by brutal weather conditions, and he came out of the game with a quality start, but he walked five in six innings. He's one of a pretty short list of pitchers with a history of success at Philadelphia's tough Citizens Bank Park. Penny is 2-0 in three starts at the Phillies' home stadium, with a 1.71 ERA and one homer allowed in 21 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay has been the real deal since he joined the Phillies. He is 5-1 with a 1.47 ERA. He has thrown three complete games, including two shutouts. He leads the Majors in wins, shutouts, complete games, innings (49) and strikeout-to-walk ratio (9.75). He is fourth in strikeouts (39). Halladay has delivered, but so far he has not rubbed off on the rest of the rotation. He can't help that, but he can continue to win. They hope he does that Thursday against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: If Lohse has really found something, an already good year may be about to get even better for the Cardinals. He's coming off his best start in nearly a year, seven excellent innings against the Reds with eight strikeouts. Lohse got ahead, threw strikes and kept the ball down, which is a pretty good plan for nearly anybody. He'll be returning to a park he briefly called home, but it's worth noting that pitching away from Busch Stadium has not suited Lohse well since he joined the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer benefitted from an offensive outburst against Johan Santana and the Mets, but he pitched solidly enough to earn his third win of the season --- six innings, five runs on six hits. He gave up two early home runs, including a 3-run shot by David Wright in the first inning, and his struggles this season have typically been caused by one or two bad innings in his starts. If he can avoid that, his numbers may turn around. The 47-year-old left-hander is 5-9 with a 5.18 ERA in his career against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe ended a two-game losing streak on Sunday, when he limited the Astros to one run and six hits in five innings.  The 36-year-old sinkerballer has benefited from the fact that the Braves have scored seven or more runs in four of his first six starts. During his April 22 start against the Phillies, Lowe surrendered five runs -- four earned -- in five innings. A botched double play hurt him during a three-run, third-inning that evening.  Over the course of his past four outings, Lowe has allowed opponents to hit .282 and compile a .333 on-base percentage.  He is 4-0 with a 1.60 ERA in five career starts at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton came off the disabled list and pitched well against St. Louis on Monday, until three runs in the seventh spoiled his night. The right-hander, who started the year on the DL with a strained oblique, threw 94 pitches and allowed 10 hits, four runs, one walk and four strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings. The numbers are misleading -- Blanton had allowed only one run through six innings before a pinch-hit home run by Nick Stavinoha opened up the scoring. He went 1-1 with a 5.23 ERA in five starts against Atlanta last season.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen was assigned this spot start on Wednesday after Jair Jurrjens was placed on the disabled list. Medlen, who allowed two earned runs and four hits in the 2 1/3 relief innings he worked during an April series against the Phillies, will be making his first start since July 12. The versatile reliever threw a season-high 44 pitches during a three-inning appearance against the Cardinals on April 29. The Braves are hoping that Medlen will be able to complete four or five innings before reaching an assigned pitch count that will likely rest between 70-75.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels answered more than a few questions with his dazzling start against St. Louis on Tuesday, in which he took a 1-0 lead into the ninth inning. He gave up the game-tying RBI double and was replaced without receiving a decision, but it was a dominating performance in a tight game. He struck out eight with two walks and eight hits allowed. Hamels had his best velocity in years, and he mixed in his cutter and curveball effectively. He had struggled in previous starts to find consistency, but has battled against aces Adam Wainwright and Tim Lincecum his past two starts. He had 18 strikeouts of his last 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami will be looking to notch his first win of the season while facing a potent Phillies offense that he handled in successful fashion last year. During the two starts he made against the reigning National League champs, the Japanese hurler went 1-0 with a 3.65 ERA. Unfortunately, Kawakami has been able to build upon the promise he created during the latter part of the 2009 season. He has allowed opponents to hit .298 and compile a .342 on-base percentage against him this year.

home_pitcher_note: Smith left Tuesday night's game with a 2-1 lead over the Padres, but he lasted just five innings. Five walks and 95 pitches suggested an inefficiency that more often than not will lead to trouble. Smith at times has shown a knack for making the pitch that will get him out of a tough inning, but getting ahead of hitters with quality strikes remains his assignment.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick may have saved his spot in the rotation --- or in the big leagues --- with his performance against St. Louis, a seven-inning gem, in which he allowed only six hits, no walks, no runs and three strikeouts. It's been feast or famine this season for Kendrick, who had another great start against Atlanta on April 20 but has been hit hard in his other four starts before Wednesday. The sinkerball pitcher must keep the ball down in order to be successful. If it's sailing up even a little bit, it could be a very long night.

home_pitcher_note: Cook seemed to be in control of Wednesday's game against the Padres until giving up four runs in the fourth inning. For most of his time on the mound, he was forcing weak contact and getting ground balls. However, he elevated three key pitches, and those were the hits that drove in four runs. Manager Jim Tracy acknowledged after the game that Cook has been inconsistent, but he expects him to go on one of his patented streaks of success at some point.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay continues to churn out wins for the Phillies, which is exactly why they brought him to Philadelphia in December. Halladay has done it all, until Tuesday. He pitches at Coors Field in Denver for the first time in his career. That is noteworthy because Coors can be a difficult place to pitch, but also because Halladay grew up in Colorado. If Ubaldo Jimenez can pitch successfully in Colorado, why can't Halladay?

home_pitcher_note: Cook seemed to be in control of Wednesday's game against the Padres until giving up four runs in the fourth inning. For most of his time on the mound, he was forcing weak contact and getting ground balls. However, he elevated three key pitches, and those were the hits that drove in four runs. Manager Jim Tracy acknowledged after the game that Cook has been inconsistent, but he expects him to go on one of his patented streaks of success at some point.
away_pitcher_note: Following Tuesday's rainout, Halladay is expected to start the first game of Wednesday's day-night twin bill. He'll be pitching at Coors Field in Denver for the first time in his career. That is noteworthy because Coors can be a difficult place to pitch, but also because Halladay grew up in Colorado. If Ubaldo Jimenez can pitch successfully in Colorado, why can't Halladay?

home_pitcher_note: Hammel is slated to make his first start since April 26 when he comes off the disabled list for Wednesday's finale with the Phillies. Hammel made some adjustments after his pulled groin put him out of commission, realizing his stride may have been a bit long. More importantly, from his perspective, he recaptured the mental approach that led to his success in 2009, when he won 10 games for the Rockies and posted a staff best 3.17 strikeout-to-walk ratio.  Hammel has been haunted by the big inning this season -- topping out with a seven-run second inning in Atlanta in April -- but he is returning to the rotation with new focus and rejuvenated energy.
away_pitcher_note: What can Moyer possibly do for an encore? He became the oldest pitcher in baseball history to throw a shutout, at 47 years, 170 days old, when he twirled a two-hitter Friday against the Braves at Citizens Bank Park. Moyer has his work cut out for him. He is 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA in two regular-season appearances in Colorado, although he allowed one earned run in six innings in Game 3 of the 2007 National League Division Series at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: The former Phillie notched his third win on Saturday with six solid innings and another huge night by the Brewers' offense, which has scored a whopping 44 runs in Wolf's three wins and no runs in his two losses. Wolf has aided that offense; with seven hits in seven starts he's already four hits shy of his output in 33 starts for the Dodgers last season. Wolf had his best offensive seasons with the Phillies, including a 14-hit season in 2003 with 11 RBIs. Wolf is trying to keep his hitting success a secret this season. "I like to lay in the weeds," he said.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer had been scheduled to pitch Wednesday in Colorado, but a rainout pushed everybody in the Phillies' rotation back a day. That means Moyer will open the three-game series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Friday night at Miller Park. Moyer is coming off a shutout against the Braves, which made him the oldest pitcher in baseball history to throw a shutout at 47 years, 170 days.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson has stabilized the fifth slot in Milwaukee's starting rotation since he replaced veteran right-hander Jeff Suppan on April 24. In three starts, Narveson is 2-0 with a 3.78 ERA including a win at Arizona last weekend in which he allowed only one run in 5 2/3 innings and contributed an RBI single. Narveson has never faced the Phillies in his brief Major League career.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is making just his third start this season after spending most of the year on the disabled list with a strained left oblique. He is 0-2 with a 4.97 ERA in his first two starts, but the Phillies had chances to win both games. He pitched better than his line indicated on May 3 against St. Louis with the bullpen allowing a couple of his runners to score in a 6-3 loss. The Phillies then lost Saturday to Atlanta, 4-1. If Blanton can get a little more comfortable, and the offense can give him a little more support, he should be fine.

home_pitcher_note: Doug Davis was scheduled to make this start, but he was scratched hours before first pitch due to unspecified medical reasons. In his place will be Bush, who was in line to start on Monday in Cincinnati but will make Sunday's start on regular rest. Bush enters the start having allowed three or fewer runs in six of his seven outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels did not follow up his masterful performance against St. Louis last week -- one run in eight innings -- with another.
