He allowed three runs in five innings Sunday against the Braves, struggling to get out of the fifth inning with just three runs scoring. The key for Hamels is to put together a few quality starts in a row. He will try to start that streak up again Saturday against the Milwaukee Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed four runs in six innings in his last start last week against the Rockies. It wasn't great. It wasn't bad. But he kept the Phillies close. He had suffered four bad starts and two good starts to start the season. This one was somewhere in the middle, so maybe it is a sign that Kendrick can be a little more consistent on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Morton's last start was another encouraging one for the right-hander even though it ended up in the loss column. Morton continues to appear back on the right track now with two consecutive quality starts. He's pitching aggressively and not falling victim to big innings as he was earlier in the season. Two solid starts in a row should also be a boost mentally for Morton, who has talked about that mental side often being the hardest to overcome. Morton is 0-1 with a 7.88 ERA in two career starts against Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay grinded through 6 1/3 innings Wednesday in a loss to the Rockies at Coors Field. Phillies manager Charlie Manuel said Halladay had difficulty gripping the ball, although Halladay wouldn't use it as an excuse. But after he allowed a two-run double to Brad Hawpe to tie the game, Manuel pulled him. He had thrown 121 pitches. Manuel would have liked to pitch Halladay longer, but he knows he needs him later in the season, too.
away_pitcher_note: Duke's fastball command left him again on Wednesday, and as has become the story of his season, he couldn't pitch through it. The left-hander lasted just five innings and gave up five runs in a loss to the Reds. He remains winless since April 10, when Duke moved to 2-0 to start the season. Half of his eight starts haven't gone more than five innings, and Duke has shown that if he doesn't have a sinker to rely on, he can't be all that effective. Duke is 1-3 with a 4.78 ERA in four career starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer allowed four earned runs in 6 1/3 innings in a victory Friday over Milwaukee at Miller Park. Moyer has pitched fairly well this season. He has kept the Phillies in almost every game he has pitched, which accounts for his 5-2 record after seven starts. Moyer allowed three homers to the Brewers, giving him 501 homers allowed in his career. That is second in baseball history. Only Robin Roberts has allowed more with 505, but that is a mark based on longevity more than anything.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe being on the road will get Gorzelanny on track. The lefty has not won away from Wrigley Field yet but has a 2.50 ERA in his three starts. At home, he's 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA. In his last outing, which was at home, the lefty did not get a decision, giving up a season-high five runs on nine hits over five innings. He did strike out seven. Gorzelanny has made one start in his career against the Phillies and lost.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton looks at his 5.49 ERA and wonders how he got there. He actually has pitched better than his ERA has indicated. In Saturday's victory over Milwaukee at Miller Park, Blanton allowed five runs in seven innings. But he had allowed just two until Corey Hart hit a three-run home run with two outs in the seventh. If Blanton hadn't allowed that homer, he would be entering Thursday's start against the Cubs with a much improved 4.11 ERA. That said, he can't change that and hopes to have everything working Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster got off to a rough start in the first inning of his last game, against the Pirates. He threw 30-plus pitches in the first and ended up with the loss, giving up three runs on four hits over seven innings. It was the right-hander's fourth straight loss. However, three of those losses have been quality starts. So far this month, Dempster is 0-3 with a 4.71 ERA. He's 4-4 with a 4.99 ERA in his career against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels was one strike away from throwing six scoreless innings Sunday against the Brewers, but he allowed back-to-back solo homers to Casey McGehee and Gregg Zaun to spoil his night. Hamels still finished with a nice line -- he allowed six hits, two runs and three walks and struck out three in 6 2/3 innings -- but he knew it could have been better. Still, Hamels has a 3.20 ERA in three starts in May, a sign that he could be putting things together.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off a mediocre start at Detroit, where he gave up nine hits and five runs over seven innings in a loss. Lackey's last two starts have been below expectations. He earned a win against the Blue Jays on May 10, but didn't pitch particularly well, giving up eight hits and six runs over six innings. Opponents are hitting .284 against him. Lackey has made three road starts this season, going 1-1 with a 3.91 ERA. This will be his first career start at Philadelphia. He won his only career start against the Phillies, giving up five hits and one run over 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick was very sharp in his last start on a rainy night against Pittsburgh -- eight innings, two runs -- and may have turned the corner after a rough first month of the season. The 26-year-old right-hander is 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in his last three starts. The Phillies would still like to see more consistency from him, but they like where the trend is going. He's walked only six batters in his last four starts after walking nine in his first four.
away_pitcher_note: Dice-K continues to be haunted by one bad inning. Last time around, he gave up a five-spot in the first inning of a no-decision against the Yankees. In that one, he gave up nine hits and seven runs over 4 1/3 innings, walking three, striking out three and throwing 103 pitches. Two starts ago, Matsuzaka put together one of his best performances in a Boston uniform, giving up three hits and a run over seven innings against Toronto, walking none and striking out nine. Matsuzaka has struggled on the road thus far, going 0-1 with a 12.54 ERA in two starts. He hopes to have better success in Philly this year than he had in 2009, when he gave up seven hits and four runs in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay suffered his second loss of the year on Tuesday despite making one of his grittiest starts of the season against the Pirates. He threw a complete game with 132 pitches -- one shy of his career high, and the most thrown by any pitcher in the Major Leagues this year. It was Halladay's fourth complete game in nine starts, but the Phillies offense couldn't back him in a 2-1 loss. Halladay remains one of the top pitchers in baseball, and he hasn't allowed a home run in 32 1/3 innings. He will face a familiar foe in Boston on Sunday, against whom he is 14-14 with a 4.28 ERA and six complete games in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer will make a return to the rotation for at least two starts, while Josh Beckett recovers from a lower back strain. Wakefield has made five starts for Boston this season, going 0-2 with a 5.06 ERA. The righty is searching for career win No. 190. Wakefield hasn't won a game since July 8, 2009. He has been in position to win four times over that span -- three of them starts -- but leads have been squandered after his exit. Wakefield's next win will be No. 176 in a Boston uniform, putting him 16 behind Roger Clemens and Cy Young for the club lead. Wakefield's last start was on May 12, when he held the Blue Jays to five hits and three runs over seven innings. Wakefield will get to swing the bat in this one. Wakefield has taken 103 at-bats in his career, hitting .126 with a homer and four RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: After flirting with the idea of using Raul Valdes against the Phillies, Mets manager Jerry Manuel ultimately decided on Dickey. Dickey will be the second consecutive knuckleballer to face the Phillies, as Boston's Tim Wakefield threw eight shutout innings against Philadelphia on Sunday. The Mets' soft tosser will be making his second start of the season. Dickey logged six innings and two earned runs in a no decision against Washington. This will be Dickey's first career starts against the Phillies and first career start in Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Nobody really knew what to expect from Jamie Moyer this season. He struggled last season and spent time in the hospital in the offseason recovering from a couple surgeries. But Moyer, 47, has pitched well. He is 5-3 with a 4.20 ERA through eight starts. He is 2-1 with a 2.42 ERA in his past three starts, and 4-2 with a 3.35 ERA in his past six. He has pitched at least six innings in each start this season, which has been huge for the rotation and the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Making his Major League starting debut against one of the game's most potent offenses, Takahashi blanked the Yankees over six innings on Friday at Citi Field. Limited to a relatively strict pitch count, Takahashi went beyond that, throwing 101 pitches, allowing five hits and one walk and striking out five in what manager Jerry Manuel called an audition for future starts. Needless to say, Takahashi passed, and will take the mound Wednesday against the Phillies. He has faced them once before, allowing one run in 1 1/3 innings of relief earlier this month in Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton pitched well in his first three starts this season, but he didn't have the numbers to prove it. He finally got some of those numbers last week in a 5-4 victory over the Chicago Cubs at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed five hits and three runs in seven innings, which added to the recent string of strong pitching performances from the Phillies rotation. If Blanton can pick up where he left off last week, it will solidify a rotation that has been one of the best in baseball in May.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey dropped his ERA below 3.00 by allowing just one run in six innings against the Yankees on Saturday. Mets manager Jerry Manuel said he will be counting on him and Johan Santana for consistent results with the rotation currently in flux. The Phillies, however, roughed up both of those starters when the teams last met. Pelfrey was tagged for six runs in four innings and came away with his only loss of the season. He is 4-3 against Philadelphia for his career, but his ERA is 5.43.
away_pitcher_note: It looks like Hamels is finally putting everything together. He allowed just three hits, one run and one walk and struck out eight in seven innings Friday in a 5-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox at Citizens Bank Park. Hamels' ERA has not been under 4.00 this late in the season since 2008. He is 3-0 with a 2.36 ERA in four starts this month, compared to a 2-2 mark and a 5.28 ERA in April. The Phillies had high hopes for Roy Halladay and Hamels atop the Phillies' rotation in 2010. They think they've seen flashes of what they'd hoped for already this month.

home_pitcher_note: Riding a three-game losing streak, Volstad looks to get back on the winning track. Although the right-hander last won on May 7 at Washington, he hasn't pitched that poorly. He comes off a quality start at Chicago, where he gave up three runs in six innings to the White Sox. At home, Volstad is 2-2 with a 2.67 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick seemed to have things working in his favor until he allowed four two-out runs in the fifth inning Saturday in a 5-0 loss to the Boston Red Sox at Citizens Bank Park. Kendrick lasted just 4 2/3 innings, allowing eight hits, five runs and two walks and striking out two. It was the first time since April 14, when Kendrick lasted just 1 2/3 innings against the Washington Nationals, that a Phillies starter had not pitched at least five innings. Phillies starters entered that night 20-10 with a 3.34 ERA, which ranked third in the National League. They had pitched six or more innings in 18 of their previous 19 starts to that point. Kendrick hopes to pitch deep against the Marlins in the series opener Friday night.

home_pitcher_note: Wins are common for Johnson. Not recording a strikeout isn't. In his previous start, at the White Sox, Johnson tossed six shutout innings. However, for the first time in his career as a starter, he failed to log a strikeout. As a rookie in 2006, he threw three innings of relief against the Reds without posting a strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay has pitched brilliantly for much of the season, but he suffered his worst start with the Phillies on Sunday against the Red Sox at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed eight hits, seven runs and two walks and struck out just one in 5 2/3 innings. He struggled following a 132-pitch effort in his previous start, which had many wondering if Halladay is tired of throwing a lot of pitches this season. He said he is fine. After throwing just 99 pitches Sunday, he should be.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez continued what is looking like a resurgent 2010 season with a win against the Braves on Tuesday, when he gave up two runs in 6 1/3 innings and exited with one out in the seventh and 116 pitches under his belt. The 26-year-old has now given up no more than two runs in seven consecutive starts. On Tuesday, he scattered five hits and four walks but was constantly able to pitch out of trouble and rack up six strikeouts -- two against rookie sensation Jason Heyward. Sanchez's worst start of the season came against the Phillies, when he gave up five runs in six innings on April 16.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer had thrown six or more innings in every start this season, until he struggled a bit in an 8-0 loss Tuesday to the Mets at Citi Field. Moyer allowed seven hits, four runs and two walks in five innings, his shortest outing of the season. But Moyer has had great success against the Marlins in his career. He is 13-5 with a 3.18 ERA in 18 starts against Florida. The Phillies could use some of that magic in the series finale against them Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Other than conceding a career-high eight runs in just 1 2/3 innings against the Reds on May 20, Hanson has had electric stuff this season. In fact, if that forgettable outing is factored out, the 23-year-old righty has a 2.89 ERA. Further, he has completed at least six innings in five of his past six starts and hasn't walked more than five batters in an outing all season. This control has enabled Hanson to develop into one of the NL East's most dependable starters. Against the Marlins during his last start, this efficiency was on full display in a six-inning, 89-pitch outing.
away_pitcher_note: It might just be a coincidence. It might not be. But one thing is certain through Joe Blanton's first five starts this season: He looks like Cy Young through the fifth inning before imploding after that. He has a 1.80 ERA (five earned runs in 25) innings in the first through fifth innings this season. He has a 14.46 ERA (15 earned runs in 9 1/3 innings) in the sixth and seventh innings. Blanton needs to be able to pitch deeper in games, regardless of the reason. He gets a chance against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson wanted to come out for the fifth inning on May 27 against the Marlins. So what if there had just been a 77 minute rain delay? The 34-year-old has been nearly unhittable in six starts this month. He's won four and has a stunning ERA of 1.59. Take away his rain-shortened start against the Marlins, and the righty has thrown at least six innings in each of his five other starts this month. Hudson matched that six-inning plateau against the Phillies on April 14, but also allowed two runs -- giving him the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lost in the midst of a scoreless streak that reached three whole games after Thursday's loss to the Mets was another solid outing by Hamels, in which he gave up three runs (only two earned) in 6 1/3 innings. Hamels had a chance to give up just one earned run in seven innings, but Placido Polanco bobbled a chance at turning an inning-ending double play in the seventh, which put runners on first and second with one out and eventually allowed two runs to score. In five May starts, Hamels is 3-1 with a 2.45 ERA. In his only game against the Braves this season, the 26-year-old gave up three runs in five innings on May 9.

home_pitcher_note: Evidently, something changed for Derek Lowe and his pitching approach after his last start against the Phillies on May 7. On that day, the 37-year-old sinkerballer surrendered seven runs and 11 hits in five innings. Afterward, Lowe admitted to relying on his go-to pitch, the sinkerball, way too much. He vowed to make changes, and recently, things couldn't be going much better for him. Since his disappointing outing against the Phillies, Lowe has won three of four starts with a 2.88 ERA. He's completed seven-inning starts on two occasions and has kept his pitch count below triple digits each time.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick wasn't hit particularly hard early, but he still struggled to get through his first three innings, as he needed 67 pitches to get into the fourth. Charlie Manuel said Kendrick's main problem is that he needs to establish a better tempo on the mound, something the Phillies' skipper told him in the middle of this start. Kendrick apparently paid attention. The 25-year-old started to get going after the third, as he retired 10 of the last 11 batters he faced and finished giving up just two unearned runs in six innings. The two runs came when Kendrick short-armed a throw to first on a soft grounder in the first inning. Kendrick has yet to record a quality start in back-to-back outings despite having three previous chances to do so this year.

home_pitcher_note: So, how does Halladay top his previous outing? Well, we'll see. Because Halladay was, in every sense of the word, perfect when he took the mound against the Marlins on Saturday. That night, the 33-year-old became the 20th pitcher in Major League history -- and second this season -- to throw a perfect game when he set down all 27 hitters he faced with a season-high 11 strikeouts. Halladay, who struck out four of the first six batters, didn't allow a walk despite getting into seven three-ball counts and running the count to 3-2 on six of those batters. It just so happened that the best start of Halladay's career came after his worst of the season. On May 23 against the Red Sox, he gave up seven runs (six earned) in a season-low 5 2/3 innings. But thanks to a useful tip from the ageless Jamie Moyer during his final bullpen session heading into Saturday -- mostly about building more momentum going toward the plate -- the Phillies' ace rebounded in the biggest way possible. Halladay joined Jim Bunning (1964) as the only Phillies pitcher to throw a perfect game and the 10th in franchise history to hurl a no-hitter. Barring a couple of nifty plays from shortstop Wilson Valdez and third baseman Juan Castro and a deep fly ball center fielder Shane Victorino was able to track down for the first out of the ninth inning, Halladay didn't need too much help defensively.
away_pitcher_note: Latos allowed two runs on four hits over six innings to win his fifth game. He was at the 94-pitch mark after six innings and the Padres had a two-run lead. Manager Bud Black decided to go to his bullpen and save some wear and tear on the arm of the 22-year-old Latos. "It felt like it was the best thing to do," Black said. "Mat worked hard the first three innings and pitched great the last three. But he wasn't going to go eight, and we had a fresh bullpen." Latos struck out eight and walked three. Latos settled down after allowing two runs in the second inning. "I saw a guy who regrouped and regained his composure," Black said. "The sixth inning was his best inning. He made some pitches the last three innings."

home_pitcher_note: Moyer allowed just four hits and one run in six innings Sunday in a 1-0 loss to the Florida Marlins at Sun Life Stadium. Moyer typically carves up the Marlins, but lately he has pitched fairly well against everybody. He is 2-3, but has a 2.97 ERA in his last five start. Run support has hurt him in two of those losses. Run support has been tough to come by lately, so Moyer will need to continue to keep the score as close to zero as humanly possible to give his team a chance.
away_pitcher_note: Though he did not factor into the decision, Garland (6-2) was sharp again for the Padres on Sunday against the Nationals. He allowed five hits -- two of them being solo homers to Ryan Zimmerman for his only earned runs -- in seven innings while striking out four and walking one. Garland is now tied for fifth in the Major Leagues with a 2.15 ERA and has not lost since April 11 at Colorado. He retired the side in order in the second, third, fifth and seventh innings on Sunday and recorded his 1,000th career strikeout when he got Josh Willingham swinging in the fourth inning. But, probably more importantly for Garland, 15 of his outs came on ground balls. "When guys are pounding them on the ground like that, it's key," Garland said. "It's huge. That's what I want."

home_pitcher_note: Just six starts into his season, the numbers do not look pretty for Blanton. He allowed eight hits, six runs, four earned runs in six innings in a 9-3 loss Monday to the Atlanta Braves at Turner Field. Blanton typically has cruised early in the game, but has struggled mightily once he hits the later innings. He is trying to be more consistent, especially these days, when the Phillies offense has been struggling.
away_pitcher_note: Correia didn't have his best start on Monday against the Mets, but he didn't need to, as the Padres put up 18 runs in their record-setting win at PETCO Park. Correia (5-4) allowed six runs on seven hits to earn his first win since April 28. He struck out three and walked one batter. "I threw four innings really well, and then they started scoring some runs, so I was like, 'Why waste a good outing today?'" Correia joked after Monday's blowout. "When we're going to score so many runs, I might as well save [a better start] for a day where I'm not going to get so many runs." While the Padres scored a total of six runs in their Correia's previous four starts prior to Monday, he is still getting more than eight runs of support per game.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels threw just 24 pitches and lasted just two-thirds of inning in his last start Tuesday against the Atlanta Braves at Turner Field, but it wasn't because of ineffectiveness. Sure, Hamels allowed a three-run home run to Troy Glaus in the first inning, but a 1-hour, 4-minute rain delay ended his opportunity to make things right. The Phillies said they did not want to bump up Hamels' turn in the rotation because they like the way the rotation sets up right now. He'll be facing his hometown team in the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc lost his fourth consecutive start Tuesday, allowing two runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Mets to fall to 2-4 on the season. LeBlanc got out of a first-inning jam when he allowed four base runners but just one run and then gave up a leadoff home run to David Wright on the first pitch of the sixth inning. LeBlanc struck out four batters on Tuesday but also walked four. Of the 93 pitches LeBlanc threw, 51 were for strikes, and Padres manager Bud Black said that LeBlanc's control needs to improve as he continues to develop. "The ball-strike ratio wasn't where a starting pitcher needs it to be overall," Black said after Tuesday's game. "There were some good sequences, some good at-bats, and then some other at-bats that got away from him."

home_pitcher_note: After Phillies manager Charlie Manuel criticized Kendrick for his pace on the mound May 28 in Florida, Manuel said Kendrick had his best start of the season Wednesday against Atlanta at Turner Field. Kendrick allowed just one run in seven innings in a 2-1 loss to the Braves. Kendrick liked his pace, too. It probably is not as simple as that, but he would like that to continue against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old seeks his first victory since May 7 at Washington. Volstad had dropped his last four decisions, but in his last start he was in line for a victory. Against the Brewers, he exited with a one-run lead in the sixth, but he wasn't involved in the decision. Volstad faced the Phillies on May 28, giving up three runs in 6 1/3 innings. He took the loss.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Halladay's reunion against the team he accomplished history against less than two weeks before, and the Marlins will be under a lot of pressure to get a hit -- any hit -- against the Phillies ace who threw a perfect game vs. them on May 29. Halladay wasn't perfect on Friday, but he earned his eighth win by shutting down San Diego for two runs in seven innings. The Padres hit him well, but Halladay worked out of trouble and bared down when he had to. He gave up three hits and one run in the first inning, and another run in the fifth, but overall had another solid outing to snap Philadelphia's losing skid.
away_pitcher_note: When he last faced the Phillies, on May 29, Johnson was on the losing end of Major League history. Roy Halladay tossed the 20th perfect game in MLB history that night at Sun Life Stadium. Johnson gave up one unearned run over seven innings, striking out six in the loss. In his last start, the right-hander beat the Brewers, giving up one run in seven innings with eight strikeouts. Johnson has allowed one earned run in his past 32 innings.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Halladay's reunion against the team he accomplished history against less than two weeks before, and the Marlins will be under a lot of pressure to get a hit -- any hit -- against the Phillies ace who threw a perfect game vs. them on May 29. Halladay wasn't perfect on Friday, but he earned his eighth win by shutting down San Diego for two runs in seven innings. The Padres hit him well, but Halladay worked out of trouble and bared down when he had to. He gave up three hits and one run in the first inning, and another run in the fifth, but overall had another solid outing to snap Philadelphia's losing skid.
away_pitcher_note: When he last faced the Phillies, on May 29, Johnson was on the losing end of Major League history. Roy Halladay tossed the 20th perfect game in MLB history that night at Sun Life Stadium. Johnson gave up one unearned run over seven innings, striking out six in the loss. In his last start, the right-hander beat the Brewers, giving up one run in seven innings with eight strikeouts. Johnson has allowed one earned run in his past 32 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The big righty is coming off one of his best starts in a while, when he allowed seven hits and two runs over seven innings against the Orioles. He took a no-decision in a game the Red Sox lost in 11 innings. In six Fenway starts this season, Lackey is 4-1 with a 5.60 ERA. This is his second start of the season against the Phillies. On May 21, he took the loss, giving up six hits and four runs over five innings. Opponents are hitting .296 against Lackey on the season, 32 points above his career average. Lackey has given up four earned runs or more in four of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer is quietly turning into one of the better stories in the National League in the first half of this season. The 47-year-old wonder threw his second complete game of the season on Saturday and earned his 100th win since turning 40. Only two other pitchers -- Jack Quinn and Phil Niekro -- have done so, and Moyer is making it look pretty easy as of late. He has a 2.83 ERA over his past six starts, and he worked quickly and efficiently against San Diego. His complete game took 99 pitches and just over two hours to finish.

home_pitcher_note: The Japanese right-hander might be settling into a rhythm as he's pitched well in three of his last four starts. Most recently, Matsuzaka fired eight shutout innings, walking two and striking out five in a win over the Indians. This is his second start of the season against the Phillies, and the first one was memorable. That was the night he came four outs away from firing a no-hitter. In that contest, he gave up one run over eight innings, walking two and striking out five. Matsuzaka has pitched four times at Fenway this season, going 3-1 with a 4.56 ERA. Opponents are hitting .228 against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton has continued to struggle, but he's hoping it's a case of deja vu. He is 1-4 with a 6.07 ERA through seven starts. That is not good, but he was 2-3 with a 7.11 ERA through eight starts last season. Blanton recovered nicely. He went 10-5 with a 3.16 ERA in 23 starts to finish the season, making him one of the most consistent and successful starting pitchers in the National League. Blanton would like to start his turnaround against the Boston Red Sox, a team the Phillies have struggled to beat in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer achieved quite the milestone in his last start, passing Roger Clemens as the all-time innings leader in Red Sox history. Wakefield has pitched 2,777 innings since coming to Boston in 1995. More importantly to Wakefield, he got the win in that outing, holding the Indians to four hits and one earned run over 7 1/3 innings. This will be Wakefield's fifth start back in the rotation since Josh Beckett went on the disabled list with back woes. Wakefield turned in one of his best starts of the season against the Phillies, pitching eight shutout innings in a May 23 victory. As a starter this season, Wakefield is 2-4 with a 5.37 ERA. Lifetime at Fenway, Wakefield is 91-72 with a 4.37 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning Monday against the San Diego Padres at Citizens Bank. He then allowed back-to-back home runs to Adrian Gonzalez and Scott Hairston, which proved to be too much in a 2-1 loss. Hamels has pitched well this season, especially lately. He is 3-3 with a 3.02 ERA in his past seven starts, a sign that Hamels has turned a corner after a frustrating 2009. The only thing he needs now is a little run support, but every Phillies starter is looking for that these days.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia was terrific in shutting down the Orioles last time out, but the Yankees have seen that movie before. The left-hander allowed two runs on nine hits in seven innings of a 4-2 win over Baltimore on Wednesday to earn his fourth win of the season against the O's. Sabathia hasn't beaten another team since April 16, and he's a pedestrian 2-3 against everyone besides Baltimore. He's 1-1 with a 4.35 ERA in three career regular-season starts against the Phillies and 0-2 against them in three postseason starts. In last season's World Series, Sabathia allowed five runs in 13 2/3 innings against the Phils.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay has been Halladay, which means he has been very good. He dominated the Florida Marlins on Thursday at Citizens Bank Park, yielding just one run in eight innings on just six hits and one walk. He struck out eight. The Phillies, however, couldn't muster a run against Marlins ace Josh Johnson, so Halladay took his fourth loss of the season. Halladay, like Cole Hamels, could use a little run support. Until then he needs to keep putting up zeros.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett lost his second consecutive start on Thursday in Baltimore, yielding four runs on eight hits in 6 2/3 innings. After serving up only four home runs in his first 11 starts, Burnett has matched that total in his past two outings -- a stretch of 12 2/3 innings that has seen him surrender 10 earned runs. Burnett is 5-8 with a 4.75 ERA in 17 career games against Philadelphia, and he went 1-1 in last year's World Series. The last time he faced the Phillies at Yankee Stadium, he submitted one of the finest efforts of his career, yielding just one run on four hits over seven frames while striking out nine in the Yanks' 3-1 Game 2 win.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer will try to recover from the worst start of his career in the series finale against the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium. Moyer allowed nine runs in one-plus inning in a 12-2 loss Friday to the Boston Red Sox, his worst start since he allowed 11 runs in 3 2/3 innings on Aug. 9, 2000, against the Chicago White Sox. Moyer's ERA jumped from 3.98 to 5.03. It was the third time a Phillies starter had allowed nine or more runs in one or fewer innings since 1951. It was the first time it happened since April 20, 2006, when Ryan Madson allowed nine runs in one inning against the Washington Nationals at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: It's reached the point where Pettitte's tremendous start to the season might just be Pettitte's tremendous season. The veteran left-hander moved to 8-1 last Friday by allowing three runs (two earned) on four hits in 7 1/3 innings against his former team, the Astros. It was Pettitte's 200th victory as a member of the Yankees. In seven lifetime regular-season starts against the Phillies, Pettitte is 2-2 with a 3.67 ERA. Pettitte did earn two more victories over Philadelphia in last year's World Series, when he gave up seven runs in 11 2/3 innings in wins in Game 3 and in the clinching Game 6.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick expressed his disappointment following his start Tuesday against the Florida Marlins at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed six hits, six runs, one walk and two home runs in just five innings. Kendrick had a 2.79 ERA in his previous six starts, but as long as J.A. Happ is on the disabled list, Kendrick will need to keep proving himself. He gets a chance against a vaunted Yankees lineup at Yankee Stadium -- the first time the Phillies have played at Yankee Stadium since losing Game 6 of the 2009 World Series.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton is trying to recover from one of the worst starts of his career. He allowed nine runs in four innings Saturday in a 10-2 loss to the Boston Red Sox at Fenway Park. He is 1-5 with a 7.28 ERA after eight starts. Interestingly, he was 2-3 with a 7.11 ERA through eight starts last season. He went 10-5 with a 3.16 ERA in his final 23 starts, which is a silver lining for Blanton. He has been in dire straits before. He is hoping he can recover like he did last season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn had a solid outing against the Braves on Saturday. He gave up only two runs on six hits through his seven-inning outing. His five strikeouts in that game were the most he has had this season. After going undefeated in his starts during the month of May, Blackburn has gotten off his hot streak, recording a record of 0-2 in three starts in June. He has an ERA of 8.10 in June as well. Blackburn is not known to walk batters, walking only two against the Braves. He hasn't walked more than two batters in a game all season.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels stepped up and shut down the Red Sox to avoid a sweep at Fenway Park on Sunday, giving his fifth straight quality start (not counting the rain-shortened outing against Atlanta on June 1). Hamels allowed only five hits and one run in seven innings while striking out eight to earn his first win since May 21. Since the beginning of May, the left-hander has a 3.08 ERA. More importantly, he's given up seven home runs in nine starts since allowing four in one start in Arizona on April 23.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey had a rough outing against the Braves on Sunday. He gave up four runs -- three earned -- in the first inning alone. He ended his 4 2/3-inning stint with five earned runs (six total) on nine hits. He gave up two home runs that night and also had a wild pitch. The outing snapped a personal three-game winning streak and was Slowey's first loss since May 11 against Chicago. One bright spot in that outing against Atlanta was his six strikeouts, which were the most he has had since he recorded six against Cleveland on April 20.

home_pitcher_note: In a much-anticipated matchup between Halladay and Yankees ace CC Sabathia at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday, Halladay came up short, allowing six runs in six innings to drop his fourth game in his past six starts. Halladay didn't have his cutter working as effectively as he wanted, and he tied a career high with three home runs allowed. He also wasn't too pleased with home plate umpire Lance Barksdale's strike zone. It's the second time this season Halladay has dropped back-to-back starts, but he hasn't lost three in a row since last August.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano had a solid last outing against the Rockies on Tuesday. He gave up three runs off of five hits, two of those runs coming off of solo blasts. He pitched seven innings, marking Tuesday's game as the 10th time this season he has pitched seven or more innings. He had five strikeouts and one walk in that game. His strength this season has come in being able to successfully use all of his pitches, with his breaking ball being able to easily throw batters off balance. Pavano has the least amount of run support of any Twins starter, but his offense rallied behind him on Tuesday, scoring nine runs.

home_pitcher_note: A night after Phillies ace Roy Halladay was battered around in the Bronx, the 47-year-old Moyer shut down the Yankees. After giving up nine runs in one-plus inning against Boston -- one of the worst starts of his 22-year career -- he allowed only three hits and two runs in eight innings on Wednesday night. Moyer kept the Yankees hitters off balanced all evening, and his command was exceptional (he has walked only three batters over his past three starts). Aside from two solo home runs by New York, Moyer needed to pitch out of the stretch only twice all night. Not including his nine-run blowup at Fenway, Moyer is 2-1 with a 1.95 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot surrendered a career-high eight runs on 13 hits over 5 2/3 innings in an 8-4 loss to the Mets on Wednesday night at Progressive Field. The rookie right-hander did not walk a batter and struck out three in the 95-pitch outing. He has posted a 2.56 ERA in six road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: After being skipped a start, Kendrick was terrific against New York on Thursday, shutting down the Yankees for just four hits and one run in seven innings. He continued a baffling trend of inconsistency, something likely to continue the rest of the season. In his previous start, he allowed five runs in five innings to Florida, a far lesser offensive opponent than New York. Overall, though, he has won three of his past four decisions and has lowered his ERA from 5.87 at the start of May.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook overcame a lack of sharpness to grind out a seven-inning effort Thursday night, allowing five runs on 11 hits in the Indians' 6-4 loss to the Mets at Progressive Field. The 32-year-old right-hander walked two and struck out five in the 109-pitch outing. He has logged seven innings or more in five of his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton didn't allow a hit for the first five innings Friday against Minnesota, keeping the ball down and forcing groundball outs by 10 of the first 14 batters he faced. Things unraveled a bit in the sixth and seventh, and he eventually gave up seven hits and three runs. But he did enough to earn his first win since May 15 and rebounded well from a nine-run outing against Boston. He still has a long way to go to get his stats back to where they should be, but he took a step in the right direction.
away_pitcher_note: Following his best start of the season, Carmona looked as sharp as ever through six innings against the Pirates on Friday, when he struck out seven and gave up just two hits, facing more than three batters just once. Things unraveled for the right-hander in the seventh, when he was given a three-run lead. The first four batters he faced reached base, resulting in three runs, but Carmona and his relievers survived in a 4-3 win. It marked the 12th time in 14 starts this season that Carmona had not allowed more than three runs, as he climbed back over .500. The 26-year-old has never faced the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: On Saturday against San Francisco, Litsch looked more like the pitcher he was down the stretch in 2008 for Toronto. The right-hander blanked the Giants for seven innings, scattering three hits, striking out three and walking none. One start earlier, making his first appearance for the Jays after a year-long recovery from Tommy John surgery on his right elbow, Litsch allowed seven runs in 2 1/3 innings on the road against Colorado. He has gone 0-1 with a 7.71 ERA in two career games against the Phillies and 1-4 with a 6.14 ERA in seven career Interleague contests.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay has downplayed his first start against the Toronto, but it is a big deal to Blue Jays fans. The Blue Jays drafted Halladay in 1995 and he played for them from 1998-2009. He won a Cy Young for them. He went to six All-Star Games. Halladay has been a force in the National League, although his record does not reflect that. He is 8-6, but that is mostly due to poor run support.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum played damage control through a five-inning outing at home against the Giants on Sunday. The right-hander ate up a lot of pitches with season highs in strikeouts (eight) and walks (five), but found a way to limit San Francisco to two runs (one earned) on four hits in a no-decision. Marcum has gone 1-0 with a 2.25 ERA over his last two starts, rebounding from a seven-run, four-inning disaster against the Rays on June 9. The righty has gone 5-1 with a 3.55 ERA in 10 career Interleague games, striking out 50 and walking 17 over 50 2/3 innings. Marcum is 1-0 with a 5.14 ERA in two career games against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels gave up three runs in the first inning last Saturday against the Minnesota Twins, but followed that with six scoreless innings. He was in line for the win until the Phillies blew a lead in the ninth inning. But the good news is that Hamels appears to have returned to form that made him a force in the 2008 postseason. The Phillies are optimistic Roy Halladay and Hamels will be a dominant 1-2 punch in the second half, when they hope to win their fourth consecutive National League East championship.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Cecil allowed six runs on eight hits over five innings against the Cardinals, sending the lefty to his second loss in a row. Cecil has gone 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA over his last two starts after going 5-0 with a 1.59 ERA in his previous five trips up the hill.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer tied a trio of Hall of Famers on Tuesday against the Cleveland Indians. In allowing just two hits and one run in eight innings in a 2-1 victory, he matched Bob Feller and Eppa Rixey with 266 career wins. He also allowed his 505th home run, which tied Robin Roberts for the most home runs allowed in baseball history. Take away his disastrous June 11 start against the Red Sox (nine runs in one inning) and Moyer has a 3.57 ERA this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto has not been treated well by the Phillies in two career starts against them. Both occurred last year, and in the first, Cueto pitched seven solid innings, allowing four runs in a 4-3 loss. But the last time out, Cueto pitched just two-thirds of an inning and was tagged for nine runs.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick continues to search for consistency. He allowed six runs in five innings June 8 against the Florida Marlins. He allowed one run in seven innings June 17 against the New York Yankees, and five runs in four innings Wednesday against the Cleveland Indians. Kendrick either seems to be on or off, and the Phillies will need him to show more consistency, although the Phillies are hoping left-hander J.A. Happ will return to the rotation soon.

home_pitcher_note: In an effort to limit the amount of innings Leake will pitch this season, the Reds moved their rookie pitcher back two days. Leake rebounded from a pair of five-run outings by giving up just one run in six innings at Oakland on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton has had two consecutive quality starts, which is a sign he could be turning things around. The Phillies need it after starting the season very slowly. He allowed three runs in 7 2/3 innings Thursday against the Indians. He hopes it continues against Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Harang finally got some run support in his last start. After the Reds were shut out in his two previous outings, Harang was the winning pitcher in a 10-3 Cincinnati win against Cleveland last Friday. He walked a season-high five batters in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is back on track after struggling in his last two starts. He threw seven scoreless innings Friday against the Toronto Blue Jays, his former team. It snapped a personal three-game losing streak for Halladay, which has not enjoyed much run support lately.

home_pitcher_note: McCutchen is plugging the rotation vacancy left by Zach Duke. The righty remains winless this year and has only pitched past the fourth in one of four starts. His rotation spot remains tenuous, and unless he dazzles, he's likely to go back to Triple-A when Duke returns.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels had his worst start in nearly a year on Saturday against the Blue Jays, allowing six runs in five innings, including three homers, against the team that leads the Majors in homers. But Hamels has pitched well since April. He hopes to get back on track.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf hasn't won in 11 starts this year, though he did not allow an earned run in his last outing. If Ohlendorf can pitch better out of the stretch and avoid being plagued by the big innings, he should be on his way to a victory soon.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer became just the 40th pitcher in baseball history to throw 4,000 or more innings in a career in his last start Sunday against the Jays. He also allowed the 506th homer of his career, an all-time record.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Maholm became the first Pittsburgh starter to finish eight innings this season, and he did it bouncing back from a career-worst one-inning start. Maholm's sinker and changeup in the game were as good as the pitches have been for the lefty at any point this year.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick is 1-1 with a 6.04 ERA in his last four starts. J.A. Happ is getting closer to rejoining the team, so Kendrick will need to show something Saturday to convince the Phillies to keep him in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: A pair of two-out solo homers stung Karstens in his last outing, but the right-hander continues to be a reliable piece of Pittsburgh's rotation. He has allowed two earned runs or fewer in six of his nine starts and has pitched into the sixth all but once.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is showing signs of improvement. He is 2-0 with a 3.80 ERA in his last three starts after carrying a 1-5 record and a 7.28 ERA through his first eight starts. Blanton credits a mechanical adjustments for the improvement.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay has given up at least two homers in three of his past four starts, his only win during that span coming in the start he didn't give up a home run. He had not given up more than one homer in a game until that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran sinkerballer has been fairly effective in his past four outings, completing 26 1/3 innings with a 3.08 ERA. Although Lowe has surrendered 25 hits during that period, he has also struck out 16 batters. During his latest start, the 37-year-old allowed four runs.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels tossed his fourth quality start in his past five outings Thursday, but the Phillies' bats gave him no help as he fell below .500. He has struck out at least six in each of those four starts while not allowing more than five hits.
away_pitcher_note: It had been nearly two months since his previous start, due to a strained left hamstring, but Jurrjens returned to Major League action by completing five innings while allowing one run on Wednesday. The 24-year-old struck out six and was slowed only by fatigue.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer is 9-7 with a 4.13 ERA, but remove a June 11 start against the Boston -- nine runs in one inning, making it the worst of his career -- and he has a remarkable 3.38 ERA. Not bad for a 47-year-old. He earned some minor buzz for All-Star consideration.
away_pitcher_note: Since solidifying himself in the starting rotation, even with the return of Jair Jurrjens, Medlen has continued to excel. During his past two outings, the 24-year-old has completed 13 innings while surrendering two runs. He's even struck out 10 during that span.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick had been 1-1 with a 6.04 ERA in his previous four starts before he threw the first complete game of his career Saturday against the Pittsburgh Pirates. Kendrick needs to show more consistency to remain in the rotation, especially with J.A. Happ coming back soon.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto didn't allow a run in his last start at Chicago, but he only lasted five innings because of seven hits and five walks. The Reds went on to lose the game, but Cueto didn't get a decision and still has lost just once since April 24.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton was rudely greeted in his last start, giving up two runs in the first. He settled down to throw five hitless innings before a four-pitch sequence in the seventh resulted in three hits and a run, preventing him from his fourth consecutive quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Leake has won just twice since mid-May, but he got nice run support his last time out, as the Reds put up 14 to back up his six-inning, three-run outing against the Cubs. Leake recovered from his previous start, which was against the Phillies and saw him allow six runs.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay went the distance Monday for the seventh time this season, the most by any pitcher prior to the All-Star Game since Halladay himself had seven in '08. He allowed five hits and one run against Atlanta with seven strikeouts for his 10th win.
away_pitcher_note: Wood moved up a day for his last start because of Aaron Harang's injury, and his pitch count rose quickly. He threw 98 pitches in just 4 2/3 innings with three earned runs (five total) allowed. In his debut July 1, he threw 91 pitches in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels will try to carry the Phillies into the All-Star break with a victory. He is 4-5 with a 3.54 ERA in his past 12 starts, which shows he has had very little run support. The Phillies scored just seven runs in those five losses (1.4 per game).
away_pitcher_note: Maloney made a sudden, surprise 2010 debut when Aaron Harang went on the DL. He pitched well -- three runs in 5 2/3 innings -- but couldn't overcome a Johan Santana shutout. With the All-Star break coming up, this could be his last chance before Harang returns.

home_pitcher_note: In his final start of the season's first half, Dempster allowed three D-backs runs on eight hits and fanned six over five innings. He threw just 98 pitches, but that was by design: Lou Piniella said it was the prudent thing to do, given the righty's long lay-off.
away_pitcher_note: A year ago at this time, left-hander Jamie Moyer's spot in the Phillies' rotation appeared shaky at best. That proved true as right-hander Pedro Martinez replaced him in August. But Moyer has done a better job, solidifying his spot in 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly has struggled in his last two starts, giving up 16 runs over 10 1/3 innings. He's having issues with his mechanics and his pitches are flat and over the center of the plate. It's not a good combo.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Joe Blanton had a disappointing first half. He started the season on the disabled list with a strained right oblique, and has struggled for most of the season. The Phillies will need a much improved Blanton in the second half if they hope to catch the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Wells has had success vs. the NL East, posting a 1-1 record and 1.80 ERA in three starts. He seems to have bounced back from a rough June in which he was winless in five starts. His home/road ERA numbers are identical.
away_pitcher_note: Left-hander Cole Hamels had a rough April, but has looked like the second half of the 1-2 punch the Phillies hoped they could team up with right-hander Roy Halladay before the season started. If Hamels keeps it up, few teams can boast two pitchers like the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny is coming off a win against the Dodgers in which he struck out seven over six innings. It was his third start since returning to the rotation and he's looked better each outing.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Roy Halladay has lived up to the billing. He has thrown a perfect game. He has third-best ERA in the National League. The only thing that has held him back is run support. If the offense picks up in the second half, Halladay should win a lot of games.

home_pitcher_note: Slowly but surely, Hawksworth has been developing into a decent back-end starter. The Cardinals have been given a chance to win in each of his last four starts and he has lowered his ERA to an acceptable 4.72 after seeing it higher than six earlier this year.
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Kyle Kendrick started the season in the rotation because Joe Blanton was hurt. He remained there when J.A. Happ got hurt. He has had his moments, but he needs to be more consistent in the second half to keep his job with Happ possibly back at some point.

home_pitcher_note: After suffering a three-game mini slump prior to the All-Star break, Carpenter recovered nicely against the Dodgers, tossing eight innings of one-run ball while striking out six. His improved command of the curveball helped last time, and he will need to show it again.

Garcia suffered his second-worst performance of the season last time out, managing just 3 1/3 innings before exiting the game. The All-Star break may have messed with Garcia's preparation, and the rookie felt uncomfortable with his delivery.

He doesn't lead in any single category, but no other pitcher makes as many appearances as high among the National League leaders as Wainwright. He's simply having a brilliant season, especially at home. Wainwright is 10-0 with a 1.31 ERA at Busch Stadium this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cole Hamels has enjoyed July -- posting a 2.20 ERA in four starts -- and seems to have recovered from a rough start to the season. He'll try to continue that trend against a first-place Cardinals team that's won eight straight games.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay allowed five earned runs in six innings vs. the Cubs last time out after surrendering just one run over 18 combined innings in his previous two starts. Look for a rebound Friday at home, where he's posted a 1.87 ERA in 11 starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cook threw seven scoreless innings in his last start, at Cincinnati, his first road win. He retired 11 of the final 12 batters he faced. Cook returns to Citizens Bank Park, where he pitched the Rockies to their only victory in last year's 3-1 NLDS loss to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies optioned Kendrick to Triple-A Lehigh Valley on Tuesday, indicating they had something planned to improve their rotation. But after Jamie Moyer injured his left elbow on Tuesday, putting his season in jeopardy, the Phillies will go with Kendrick.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez was hurt by an error, then gave up a three-run homer on a split-finger when a fastball might have been better in his last start. Only a late rally (the Rockies ultimately lost) saved him from his second loss. Jimenez has given up five homers in his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: It has been a long road back for Happ, who has not pitched since April because of a left elbow injury. Still not where the Phillies wanted him to be after rehab in the Minors, the Phillies optioned him to Triple-A Lehigh Valley. He returns because of Moyer's injury.
away_pitcher_note: Francis spotted his fastball inside, used his fastball and curve outside, and mixed in his dangerous changeup while throwing seven scoreless innings in a win over the Marlins Tuesday. It was a major bounce-back for Francis, who had an 8.03 ERA in his previous five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton is 2-1 with a 4.79 ERA in his previous seven starts. In four of those starts, he has allowed three earned runs in seven or more innings. He has shown improvement, but Blanton is still looking for that truly impressive performance.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel left his last start wanting two innings back in a 5-2 loss in Florida. Two runs came with two down in the first and three came on a homer with two down in the second. It comes down to the consistency with which he gets ahead of batters and locates his fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels looks like the pitcher that dominated the NL in 2008. He allowed just one hit and one walk in eight scoreless innings Thursday against the Cardinals at Busch Stadium. He dominated a tough lineup in brutal heat, and has shown signs of breaking through.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez assumes the slot of Dan Haren, who was traded. On Thursday vs. the Giants, Lopez suffered his second straight defeat, yielding three earned runs on five hits, including another homer, over seven innings. He said he needs to improve upon controlling the running game.

home_pitcher_note: Doc finally got some run support Friday and shut down Colorado for his 11th win. A five-run fifth gave him a cushion, only the fourth time in his past 14 starts he's received more than three runs of support. Halladay hasn't faced Arizona since '04.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson pitched well enough to win on Friday against the Giants. He just didn't field his position: two throwing errors toward first base led to three runs. He also yielded two Aubrey Huff solo shots and has allowed five home runs over his past three starts, all losses.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick proved to some that it was a mistake to demote him following his poor start in St. Louis. His inconsistency is still troubling: he's gone 6-plus innings and allowed two or fewer runs eight times; in his 11 other starts, he has an 8.73 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is expected to join the D-backs on Tuesday and will make his Arizona debut against the Phillies two days later. The lefty is coming off a strong start on Friday. He allowed one Rangers run on seven hits over seven innings and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: Stammen is coming of a no-decision in a 7-5 loss to the Brewers on Friday night. He allowed three runs on five hits in five innings and hasn't won since June 29. Stammen is 0-0 with a 15.63 ERA in two career starts against Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies acquired longtime Houston ace Oswalt on Thursday, and with him on track to start Friday, they slotted him in against the Nationals. Oswalt, who has 120 K's in 129 innings, has pitched far better than his 6-12 record.

home_pitcher_note: In his first game since recovering from hip surgery, an 8-3 loss to the Brewers, Detwiler had a rough outing. He allowed five runs on three hits with an additional three walks. Detwiler is 0-2 with a 6.00 ERA in two career starts vs. the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed just two runs in six innings Monday against the Colorado Rockies at Citizens Bank Park. That is not spectacular, but it was the first time since Sept. 22, 2009, Blanton had allowed two or fewer runs in a start.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan will be making his first start for the Nationals since June 20 against the White Sox. In that game, he allowed five runs in four innings and was sent to Double-A Harrisburg the next day.

After posting a 4-3 record at Triple-A New Orleans, West was promoted to fill Alex Sanabia's rotation spot. At New Orleans, West had a 4.12 ERA. In his last start, July 27, he threw a shutout. West had 20 starts in '09 for Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay returns to Florida, where he enjoyed his best individual pitching performance -- a perfect game on May 29. He also will try to help the Phillies win the opening game in a road series for the first time since May 28 against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: You have to go back to Sanchez's no-hitter in 2006 to find an outing better by the 26-year-old right-hander. Sanchez comes off a gem at San Francisco, tossing a one-hit shutout. He matched a career high with eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick is 1-0 with a 1.35 ERA since the Phillies demoted him to Triple-A Lehigh Valley on July 21. They called him back up after Jamie Moyer injured his left elbow, and he hasn't missed a beat. He hopes the trend continues Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Fresh off a win at San Diego, Volstad looks to stay on track. Before July 30, he hadn't won since June 13 at Tampa Bay. On June 8, he gave up six runs (five earned) in a no-decision against the Phillies. He has walked three in three straight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt certainly is hoping for improvement in his second career start with the Phillies. His first was shaky at best. He allowed seven hits, five runs, two walks and hit two batters in a loss Friday to the Washington Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Keep an eye on Joe Blanton in the first inning and after the fifth inning. He has a 7.94 ERA in the first inning this season, a 3.36 ERA from the second through fifth innings and an 11.86 ERA from the sixth inning on. Early and late damage have hurt.
away_pitcher_note: The Mets skipped Hisanori Takahashi's turn in the rotation so that Niese can pitch the opener in Philadelphia. Though Niese allowed a career-high seven runs in his last start, manager Jerry Manuel feels he gives them a better chance vs. the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed four runs in seven innings Sunday against Washington, but he pitched much better than that. In fact, that was just the second time since April that he had allowed more than three earned runs in a start.
away_pitcher_note: Some early struggles and iffy defense doomed Santana in Atlanta, where he took a loss Monday despite striking out a season-high 11 batters. More important was Santana's run total -- four in seven innings -- which will have to go down in Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay appears quite ready to demonstrate his value as the playoff races begin to heat up. The veteran right-hander believes any summer doldrums are behind him now and it looked that way as he continued his mastery of Florida on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Relying on what he called guerrilla warfare, Dickey overcame wet and rainy conditions at Turner Field -- a knuckleballer's nightmare -- to hold the Braves to two runs in six innings Tuesday. He shut out the Phillies over six innings back on May 25.

home_pitcher_note: Since being demoted briefly -- and he never played at Triple-A because of Jamie Moyer's injury -- Kendrick has been a different pitcher. On Wednesday he registered his third straight quality performance, this one against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla threw a two-hit shutout over the Padres in his last start, carrying a no-hitter into the seventh inning. Since June 25, Padilla is second in the majors with a 1.32 ERA, four points off Adam Wainwright's pace.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt pitched better against the Marlins on Thursday than in his Phillies debut, but he was left with no decision when the Phillies lost a 2-0 lead. Oswalt revealed afterward that he is going through a "dead arm" period that crops up every year.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley is one victory away from his fourth consecutive double-digit wins season. He's fared well at Citizens Bank Park in three career starts, going 1-1 with a 2.25 ERA, 19 strikeouts in 20 innings and no home runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton enjoyed his best start of the year Friday in a 7-5 victory over the Mets. He allowed seven hits, two runs, no walks and struck out four in seven innings. The Phillies are hoping that's just a start for Blanton, who has been inconsistent.
away_pitcher_note: If Adam Dunn's out of the equation, Kershaw's last start on Friday was right in line with the rest of the season. Kershaw let up two three-run homers to Dunn, but still struck out nine in six innings. His career ERA against the Phillies is 6.64.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey's roughest start as a Met came at precisely the wrong time, in a critical game at Citizens Bank Park. For his third start of the year against the Phillies, he will need to follow the formula that resulted in six scoreless innings back in May.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels continued his impressive 2010, and the Phillies offense continued to offer him no run support. He allowed just one run in seven innings Saturday to the Mets and the Phillies scored no runs for him while he was on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Mets manager Jerry Manuel didn't commit to naming a starter for Saturday until before Friday's game, when he confirmed that the nod will go to Misch, who is 11-4 with a 3.23 ERA for Triple-A Buffalo this season.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay allowed five runs Sunday but got the win, 6-5, over the Mets, finally getting some run support. He hasn't had much help this year, but he hasn't needed it. If the Phils score five or more runs the rest of the way, he should win a lot.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey is coming off seven shutout innings vs. the Rockies, when he appeared to regain some of the early-season form. He earned his first win since June 25 and snapped a run of 30 earned runs in 30 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick went 2-0 with a 1.86 ERA in three starts before he allowed six runs in 3 1/3 innings Tuesday against the Los Angeles Dodgers. The Phillies optioned Kendrick on July 20, but they need him after losing Jamie Moyer for the season.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt had his best start for the Phillies on Wednesday against the Dodgers, allowing five hits and two walks in seven scoreless innings. He also struck out five in the 2-0 victory. Oswalt is now 1-1 with a 2.79 ERA in three starts with the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up two solo homers in a no-decision against the Cubs, Zito now has surrendered at least one home run in five consecutive games (eight total homers). The last time that happened was June 20-July 11, 2004, while he was with Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton continued his trend of putting the Phillies in an early hole Thursday against Los Angeles. He allowed four singles and two walks in the first inning to hand the Dodgers a 3-0 lead. Blanton has an 8.53 ERA in the first inning this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cain battled through a 31-pitch first inning in his last outing, pitching six innings while taking a no-decision against the Cubs. Despite Cain's high pitch count, he was effective in pounding the zone, as 82 of his 121 pitches were strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is 1-2 with a 1.81 ERA in his last seven starts, and 5-7 with a 2.85 ERA in 19 starts since April. But the Phillies continue to give him no run support. He has lost his last two starts by 1-0. He hopes for a better showing Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Sanchez came up short in his guarantee the Giants would sweep the Padres, as the lefty allowed three runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings. Sanchez is 2-1 with a 3.38 ERA in eight games (four starts) against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay improved to 15-8 with Saturday's 4-0 victory over the New York Mets. If he continues to pitch like he has, and he continues to get some run support, there is no reason to think he can't finish the season with 20 wins.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis signed a two-year, $15 million contract last offseason to improve a starting rotation in need of help. But after a year full of poor pitching and injury, it appears Marquis is the one searching for answers.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick helped the Phillies take two games in a three-game series last weekend against the New York Mets in Citi Field, when he allowed one run in 6 2/3 innings Sunday. He is 3-1 with a 3.07 ERA in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg was much better his last time out than he was in his previous outing. On Sunday against the Diamondbacks, Strasburg lasted five innings and allowed three runs -- only one of which was earned.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt is fitting nicely into the Phillies rotation. He allowed six hits and three runs and struck out seven in seven innings Tuesday in a 9-3 victory over the Giants. Oswalt has boosted the rotation, which could be tough down the stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen was pitching a perfect game until the fourth inning on Tuesday, when Braves infielder Omar Infante led off with a single. Suddenly, Olsen couldn't get anyone out in the bottom of the sixth inning and was lifted after facing three hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton has been somewhat inconsistent this season, but the right-hander shined last time out against the Giants. In 6 1/3 innings, Blanton allowed just two earned runs while striking out seven and walking none.
away_pitcher_note: Myers continues to fall victim to a lack of run support. The veteran took a no-decision last time out, against the Mets, despite allowing just two earned runs over seven innings. In his last 10 starts, Myers' ERA is 2.97.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty hasn't picked up a win since July 11, despite tossing several gems in that span. But Hamels stumbled in his last start, against the Giants, allowing five runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: After battling inconsistency earlier this season, Norris has turned in back-to-back stellar outings and won four straight decisions. After striking out 14 Pirates, Norris tossed a two-hit gem through seven innings against the Mets his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay continues to amaze in Philly, where he hasn't allowed a run in his last 15 inning in wins over the Mets and Nationals. The Phils' ace aims for his 17th win against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Happ will face his former squad for the first time since the trade that sent him south for Roy Oswalt. The young lefty makes his sixth start since joining the Astros, a span that's seen him go 2-2 (4.62 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick continued his up-and-down season Saturday in a loss to the Nationals. He allowed nine hits, five runs and four walks in 5 2/3 innings. In 24 starts, he's allowed five or more earned runs nine times (37.5 percent).
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez continues to grind out solid to outstanding performances. In his last game, he struck out 10 and gave up two earned runs in a loss to the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Latos has allowed two or fewer runs in each of his last 12 starts and three or fewer runs in his last 19 stars. Against the Cubs on Aug. 19, the 22-year-old struck out a career-high 10 in seven innings. His ERA actually went up, from 2.32 to 2.33.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt has pitched as advertised with the Phillies. He is 3-1 with a 3.42 ERA in five starts since the Astros traded him to the Phillies. He has a 1.65 ERA in his past four starts. He threw seven scoreless innings Sunday in a win over the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Garland picked up his 13th win in his last start, against the Brewers, allowing two runs over 5 1/3 innings. He's been very good in August, going 4-1 with a 2.01 ERA. He'll be pitching at home against the Phillies, where he's 7-2 with a 2.49 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton had his best start of the season Monday against the Astros at Citizens Bank Park, where he allowed just six hits and one run in seven innings. He struck out nine in a losing effort, but is 2-1 with a 3.63 ERA in his last eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Richard allowed more walks (five) than hits (three) Tuesday vs. the D-backs, but none of them came back to bite him as he fired six shutout frames for his career-best fifth straight win. He fanned eight, tying the second-highest total of his career.
away_pitcher_note: The good news is the Phillies actually scored a run for Hamels when he was on the mound Tuesday against Houston. It was the first time they had scored for him since Aug. 1. Bad news: it wasn't enough. He has a 2.74 ERA in his last 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda picked up his first win in more than a month last week against the Brewers, but once again he's pitched better this season than his record shows. He continues to eat innings, seven in each of his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: If Roy Halladay finishes the season strong, he could be the first Phillies pitcher to have a 20-win season since Steve Carlton in 1982. Halladay allowed six hits, three runs and two home runs in seven innings last week against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Monasterios gets another fill-in start for disabled Opening Day starter Vicente Padilla. The Dodgers came away with a win in Monasterios' last start against Milwaukee, even though he lasted only 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick hopes the final month of the season is better than his last four starts. He is 1-3 with a 6.23 ERA in that span, which included Thursday's start, when he allowed four runs in six innings against the Astros in Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw continues to pitch like an ace. In his most recent start, he allowed only one run over six innings at Coors Field, but worked hard enough to make 115 pitches. He allowed the Phils only two runs in 6 2/3 innings on the road in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt has been a big pickup for the Phillies since they got him July 29 in a trade with the Astros. He allowed five hits and one run in eight innings on Friday against San Diego and is 3-0 with a 1.24 ERA in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin has been stellar his last two outings, striking out 16 and allowing just one run in a combined 14 2/3 innings. The only time he faced the Padres this season was out of the bullpen, giving up two runs and two hits in 1 1/3 innings on July 11.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton seems to have turned around his season. He is 3-1 with a 3.41 ERA in nine starts since the All-Star break. He allowed just two runs in his last 13 innings over two starts, which is what the Phillies are looking for from their No. 4 starter.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels received an avalanche of run support Sunday in a 5-0 victory against the Padres at PETCO Park, where he allowed just four hits in eight scoreless innings. Hamels has had some of the worst run support in baseball, but got plenty that day.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano, a free agent after the season, gets another shot to show what he can do in the rotation. His return to a starting role didn't go well Saturday against the Pirates, as he surrendered six runs and didn't make it to the fourth inning.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay should have 20 wins, but the Phillies have not given him much run support. He allowed three runs in seven innings Monday against the Dodgers, but Philadelphia was one-hit. The offense needs to do a better job with Doc on the mound.
away_pitcher_note: Bush worked seven innings Sunday for the first time since June 15. Last year in Philadelphia, Bush took a no-hitter into the eighth inning but lost it when Matt Stairs hit a two-out home run off the right-field foul pole.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick needs to pitch better down the stretch. He allowed four runs in five frames Tuesday in a win over the Dodgers, but he has a 6.41 ERA in his last five starts. With the offense struggling and the Braves leading the NL East, he must improve.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf became the first Brewers pitcher ever to steal a base on Monday. But he didn't fare as well against the Reds on the mound, allowing eight hits and three runs on 106 pitches in five innings. The Brewers' defense limited the damage to three runs.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies have not said Worley will start Monday against the Marlins, but they pulled him after one inning Friday in a start with Triple-A Lehigh Valley. That's a sign he will pitch. He is 1-3 with a 3.77 ERA in eight starts with the IronPigs.
away_pitcher_note: Called up from Triple-A New Orleans, Mendez, 28, will get the starting nod in the first game. The right-hander was 5-4 with a 4.14 ERA in 28 games, including nine starts at New Orleans.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt continues to deal. He allowed one hit, six walks and struck out six in 6 1/3 scoreless innings Wednesday in a victory over the Dodgers. Oswalt is 4-1 with a 1.89 ERA in seven starts since he joined the Phillies following a July 29 trade.
away_pitcher_note: Since the All-Star break, Sanchez is 4-2 with a 2.21 ERA, striking out 55 in 57 innings. But on the road for the year, he's 7-5 (3.84). Sanchez has gone 1-2 (5.09) vs. the Phillies this season.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton struggled in the Phils' one-day trip for a makeup game in Colorado, yielding six runs (four earned) on 10 hits and two walks. Blanton gave up three homers, accounting for five of the Rockies runs off him.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad has won three straight decisions and four of his last five. In his last outing, Volstad worked five innings and collected the win over the Nationals before he was ejected after throwing behind Nyjer Morgan.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has a 2.00 ERA in his last 11 starts. He also has thrown 18 consecutive scoreless innings, dating to an Aug. 24 start against the Houston Astros. Hamels is looking good, despite a continued lack of run support. Lately, he hasn't needed it.
away_pitcher_note: Miller beat Atlanta in his last start, giving him his first win since July 4, 2009. In five innings, he struck out six and allowed one run. This will be his fifth game and third start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Mejia showed flashes in his starting debut on Saturday vs. the Cubs but was generally inconsistent. This time, the 20-year-old righty makes another debut of sorts: his first start in front of the faithful at Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay has not been his usual self in his last two starts. He has thrown 221 innings this season. Could it be fatigue? It could be, although pitching coach Rich Dubee thinks it's more of a mechanical issue. Of course, that could be stamina related.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's streaky year continued on Labor Day, when the Nats tagged him for six runs in 3 2/3 innings. He'll look to get back on track against the Phillies, who have a .273 average against him this season, having beaten him twice in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick gets another chance to start. He is 2-4 with a 7.04 ERA in his last six starts, which had the Phillies thinking they might pitch rookie Vance Worley instead. Kendrick allowed one run in 6 2/3 innings at Citi Field earlier this season.

home_pitcher_note: Niese's struggles continued last Sunday, when he gave up five runs to the Cubs in six innings. That prompted the Mets to shift their rotation to give an extra day of rest to Niese, who has an 8.27 ERA and eight walks over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt allowed four runs in seven innings Monday in a victory over the Marlins. He is 5-1 with a 2.30 ERA in eight starts since the Astros traded him to the Phillies on July 29. His biggest starts are yet to come with possibly two against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Miller draws the Phillies for a second straight start. He hopes for better results. Last time, he gave up seven runs on 11 hits in four innings. Falling behind in counts hurt. Miller has struck out 16 and walked 13 in 19 innings this year.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton has pitched better since the break, which gives the Phillies four quality starters. He is 3-1 with a 3.67 ERA in 11 starts since the break. He will get four more starts this season. He would like to finish strong.
