home_pitcher_note: Mendenz made his MLB debut on Monday, and it was a successful one. He tossed six shutout innings at the Phillies, allowing one hit while striking out six. He even had a single at the plate. But on the hit, he pulled up. He said it was a cramp.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels is on a roll. He has thrown 25 consecutive scoreless innings, which is the 12th longest streak in Phillies history. It also is the longest streak for a Phillies starter since Randy Wolf's 27 consecutive scoreless innings in 2002.

home_pitcher_note: Sosa will make his first MLB start since 2007 when he was with the Mets. The veteran is getting the call in what is being called a "bullpen game" because the rotation is depleted by injuries and suspensions. He will likely go about three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay re-tied the league leaders in wins with another strong effort vs. the Mets, whom he has beaten four times this year. He went 7 2/3 innings and threw 116 pitches but allowed four runs -- the third straight game he has allowed at least three.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies bumped up Oswalt's turn in the rotation from Saturday to Friday so he could pitch next Wednesday against the Braves at Turner Field. Oswalt is throwing well, coming off a shutout Sunday against the New York Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis is 2-5 with a 3.77 ERA in seven starts since missing three months with elbow problems. He has won two of his past three decisions and has allowed eight runs over 30 innings in his past five outings.

home_pitcher_note: This might be Kendrick's second last start of the regular season because the Phillies have the option of skipping him to have Roy Halladay, Roy Oswalt, Cole Hamels and Joe Blanton pitch as much as possible down the stretch. He hopes to make it count.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann took the loss in his fourth start with the Nationals, lasting just three innings against the Marlins on Sunday. He had allowed just one hit in six scoreless innings against Florida on Aug. 31, striking out nine and walking none.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed five hits, one run and two walks and struck out six Monday against Florida to improve to 7-6 with a 5.00 ERA. He is 4-1 with a 3.50 ERA (29 earned runs in 74 2/3 innings) in 12 starts since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: One bad inning has done in Maya in both of his first two Major League starts. He allowed four runs in the second inning against the Braves on Monday, committing two balks. But he steadied after that, just like he had against the Mets earlier.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels struck out 13 batters Tuesday against the Marlins. He also threw a career-high 127 pitches, although he will be pitching on extra rest. He has allowed just one run in his last 31 1/3 innings, and is 5-3 with a 1.79 ERA in his last 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old rookie who gets the spot start in place of Jair Jurrjens has a tall task in his Major League debut against the Phils. Beachy, signed as an undrafted free agent, went 5-1 with a 1.73 ERA this year in the Minors.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay has a 4.41 ERA in his last five starts, but he got an extra day of rest before this big start against the Braves. He hopes it helps. Halladay is trying to become the first Phillies pitcher since Steve Carlton in 1982 to win 20 games.
away_pitcher_note: Since impressing in his first four career starts, Minor has seemingly battled fatigue in his past three outings. But the rookie left-hander at least looked better against the Nationals on Wednesday other than allowing Justin Maxwell's grand slam.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies changed the rotation last week to have Oswalt pitch the Wednesday against Atlanta. Oswalt is 0-3 with a 7.58 ERA in seven regular-season starts against the Braves, but is 3-0 with a 2.89 ERA in three postseason starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson endured a rough second inning vs. the Mets Friday and then impressed while retiring 13 of the final 14 batters he faced. He'll be looking to duplicate the success he experienced May 31, when he limited the Phils to three hits in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed four runs in six innings Sunday in a start against the Washington Nationals at Citizens Bank Park, but it almost looked much better. He allowed a three-run homer with two outs in the sixth to ruin his line.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time this season, Dickey gave up 10 hits in a start, dropping a 6-3 game last Sunday against the Braves. Next up are the Phillies, which may bode well for Dickey: He's 2-1 with a 2.00 ERA in three starts against them this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies originally skipped Kendrick's turn in the rotation, but returned him to Saturday to get Cole Hamels, Roy Halladay and Roy Oswalt an extra day of rest before their next starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gee's first start against a legitimate playoff contender went nearly as smoothly as his previous two, despite a hard-luck loss last Saturday to the Braves. But the road grows only tougher now for Gee, who will make his first appearance in Philly.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is on fire. He is 6-3 with a 1.74 ERA in 14 starts since July 10, which is the second-best ERA in baseball. (Only Seattle's Felix Hernandez has been better with a 1.59 ERA). Hamels also is 5-0 with a 0.49 ERA in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: In an effort to give Mike Pelfrey and Jon Niese extra rest, the Mets will insert Misch into the rotation. Misch has faced the Phillies twice this season, posting a 1.42 ERA in one start and one relief appearance.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Lannan started for the Nationals and earned his 12th quality start of the season. He pitched seven innings and allowed three runs on six hits. His only trouble came in the first inning, when the Astros scored those three runs.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay became the first Phillie to win 20 games in a season since Steve Carlton in 1982, and the first Phillies right-hander to win 20 games since Robin Roberts in 1955. Halladay has thrown a lot of innings, so they will watch him closely.

home_pitcher_note: On Wednesday, Marquis made up for his last outing in a big way. He was solid for six-plus innings, allowing two runs on seven hits after an effort Friday in which he allowed six runs to the Phillies over just one-third of an inning.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt said he feels rejuvenated since joining the Phillies following a July 29 trade with the Astros. He sure is pitching like it. He is 7-1 with a 1.76 ERA in his first 11 starts with the Phillies. He gets an extra day of rest before this start.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler has been shelved twice this season by a right hip injury. But when healthy, he has showed the Nationals that he deserves a shot to be in the rotation next year.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton makes his final start of the regular season Wednesday against the Nationals. It also could be his final start until the NLCS, if the Phillies get that far. The Phillies could pitch only Roy Halladay, Roy Oswalt and Cole Hamels in NLDS.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy has proved effective while making his first two career starts over the past two weeks. He allowed the Phillies just one earned run in his Sept. 20 debut, which was marred by Jason Heyward's three-base, fifth-inning error.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies have clinched the NL East, so they will try to rest some of their top pitchers this weekend in Atlanta. Roy Halladay will not pitch, which means Kyle Kendrick gets one more start before the National League Division Series.

home_pitcher_note: Despite a 3.41 ERA and 19 quality starts, Hanson carries a sub-.500 record into his final start of the season. That's due to a team-low 2.4 runs of support per start. In three starts vs. Philly this year, he has a 1.43 ERA and .186 BAA.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies are giving Roy Halladay the weekend off to prepare for Game 1 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday. They will start rookie right-hander Vance Worley instead. He has made three appearances this season, including one start.

home_pitcher_note: Atlanta's leading winner will make his second attempt at win No. 17, and his second straight start on three day's rest. He'll finish with a sub-3.00 ERA for the first time since 2003 and his lowest ERA since his career-best 2.70 that year.
away_pitcher_note: This is nothing more than a final tuneup for Hamels, who will start Game 3 of the National League Division Series on the road Oct. 10. Hamels will pitch a few innings and make way for Roy Oswalt, who also will pitch a few innings.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay finally gets his shot at the postseason. The National League Cy Young favorite led the league with 21 wins, four shutouts, nine complete games, 250 2/3 innings and a 7.3 strikeout-to-walk ratio. He finished third with a 2.44 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: A tweak of his mechanics has helped Volquez get back to form after some inconsistency following his comeback from Tommy John surgery. In four starts since his recall from Class A Dayton, he is 1-1 with a 1.95 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt is 23-3 with a 2.81 ERA in 34 career games against the Reds. Only eight pitchers in MLB history have more wins vs. the Reds. The list includes Warren Spahn (62), Tom Glavine (27), Greg Maddux (24), Juan Marichal (24) and Robin Roberts (24).
away_pitcher_note: The only Reds starting pitcher with postseason experience, Arroyo hasn't been there since 2005 with the Red Sox. In 10 postseason games totaling 17 innings, including two starts, he has a 7.41 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has a 3.20 ERA at home this season, compared to 4.10 ERA. Having not pitched since Sept. 29, the layoff could be a concern. Cueto tends to be too strong with too many days off, and that could affect his control.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels made his big league debut in 2006 in Cincinnati and has fared well against them ever since. He is 6-0 with a 1.07 ERA in seven starts against Cincinnati, including 3-0 with a 1.67 ERA in four starts at Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: In his playoff debut, Halladay tossed a no-no vs. the Reds in the NLDS. He did have his troubles in his lone start vs. the Giants this season, yielding five runs on 10 hits over seven frames.
away_pitcher_note: By beating the Braves in four, the Giants are set up to tab their ace for the NLCS opener. He was magnificent in the NLDS, fanning 14 in Game 1. Philly knows what it's in for: "The Freak" fanned 11 Phils in an April no-decision at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt gave up four runs in five innings in Game 2 of the Division Series, which the Phillies won after rallying, but his career postseason is 4-0, including three wins for Houston in 2005. He was 1-3 against the Giants this season.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez warmed up for the postseason by posting a 4-1 record and a 1.01 ERA in six September/October starts. He got a no-decision in Game 3 of the NLDS, but dominated, allowing one run and two hits while striking out 11 in 7 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cain was 8-4 with a 2.93 ERA in 16 starts at AT&T Park this year. Though Tim Lincecum gets most of the headlines, Cain led the staff with 223 1/3 innings, marking the fourth year in a row that he has exceeded the 200 level. He walked a career-low 61.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels, outstanding in 2008 but less so last year, threw a complete-game, five-hit shutout against the Reds in the Division Series. He was 0-1 with a 7.36 ERA in two starts San Francisco this season, surrendering 16 hits in 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner threw six innings in the NLDS clincher against Atlanta, allowing two runs. He said that his focus that day was on keeping his emotions in check, and that will once again be his focus against Philadelphia in Game 4.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton hasn't started since Sept. 24 at Washington and hasn't pitched since a relief stint on Oct. 3 against the Braves. He beat the Giants on Aug. 18 in Philly, allowing two runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 IP, striking out seven and walking none.

home_pitcher_note: Like his counterpart Halladay in the much-ballyhooed Game 1 matchup, Lincecum allowed two homers in a less-than-stellar outing. But Lincecum did enough for the win, fanning eight in seven innings while walking three to improve to 2-0 this postseason.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander followed up his historic NL Division Series no-hitter with a rare loss at home in Game 1 of the NLCS. Halladay struck out seven in seven innings but was victimized by two home runs -- both off the bat of Giants outfielder Cody Ross.

home_pitcher_note: Can Oswalt rebound from his unexpected inning of relief in Game 4, when he gave up a run and took the loss? The Phillies would much rather get the guy who threw eight innings of three-hit, one-run, nine-strikeout ball in Game 2.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez was effectively wild in Game 2, striking out seven, walking three and allowing three runs -- two earned -- in six innings, but Oswalt was simply better that night. Sanchez has a 2.03 ERA and 18 strikeouts in 13 1/3 postseason innings.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay has a tough act to follow. He won the National League Cy Young Award in 2010, throwing a perfect game in the regular season and a no-hitter in the postseason. Hopes are high, and he gets things started Opening Day.
away_pitcher_note: Myers, coming off a season in which he went 14-8 with a 3.14 ERA in his first year for the Astros, is making his fourth Opening Day start in five years. He made three in a row (2007-09) for the Phillies, his former team.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is the reason why Phillies fans are so excited about the 2011 season. He gives the Phillies arguably one of the greatest rotations in baseball history, although Lee is quick to mention they haven't thrown a pitch yet.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struggled with his command in the spring for the second year in row, and the Astros can only hope it doesn't translate into another slow start. He started 3-10 in 2010 before finishing strong with a second half.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt helped propel the Phillies to the postseason last year, when he arrived in a July trade from the Houston Astros. He actually put up better numbers than Roy Halladay and Cole Hamels down the stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Norris finished his first full season in the Majors with a 9-10 record and a 4.92 ERA in 27 starts. He ranked fifth among all NL starters in strikeouts per nine innings with 9.25, the highest ratio by an Astros starter since 1988.

home_pitcher_note: Three years ago Hamels won World Series and National League Championship Series MVP honors. Now he's the Phillies' fourth starter, which shows just how good the Phillies' rotation is. But Hamels has Cy Young potential.
away_pitcher_note: Among the brightest stories of spring was Young, who posted a 1.78 ERA in six starts. The question with Young has never been talent. But after shoulder injuries derailed his career, Young must prove he can stay healthy.

home_pitcher_note: The Phils shopped Blanton in the offseason, but held onto him when they couldn't find a deal they liked. It might be the best decision they made. He gives the Phillies incredible depth and insurance should there be injuries.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's problems in Miami leaked into 2011, when the Marlins tagged him for five runs in 4 1/3 innings on Opening Day. Though he has not fared much better vs. the Phillies in his career, Pelfrey did beat them twice with a 3.91 ERA last year.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay pitched well enough to win on Opening Day on Friday, but the Phillies waited until the ninth inning to get their offense going in a victory over Houston. Halladay went 4-0 with a 2.56 ERA last season against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: A poor start gave way to a strong finish for Niese, who gave up two runs in the first inning Saturday, but held the Marlins to one hit the rest of the way. Though the Phillies represent a stiffer test, they hit .208 vs. Niese in three 2010 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson retired the final 17 batters he faced against the Nationals on Sunday. He allowed the Phillies just two hits in seven innings on the last day of 2010's regular season. He went 11-5 with a 2.48 ERA in 18 starts at Turner Field last year.
away_pitcher_note: Lee will not get the same reception he got in his Phillies debut Saturday against Houston at Citizens Bank Park, but the Atlanta crowd should not bother him. He is 1-1 with a 5.06 ERA in his career against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Beachy's fifth career start and third against the Phillies. He allowed three earned runs in 10 innings against Philladelphia last year. The 24-year-old hurler produced six solid innings in Monday's season debut against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt looked good in his first start of the season Sunday against the Houston Astros. He allowed five hits, two runs and one walk and struck out six in six innings against his former team, which he faced for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe allowed one run against the Brewers Tuesday but fell to 6-1 with a 1.07 ERA in his past seven starts dating to last year. He rebounded from two tough games vs. the Phils last year and allowed three runs over 15 innings in his final two.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels suffered the second-worst start of his career Tuesday in a 7-1 loss to the New York Mets. He allowed seven hits, six runs, two walks and hit one batter in just 2 2/3 innings. He certainly is hoping for better results Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Outfielder Jayson Werth will get the most attention in this game because he will face his former team, the Phillies, for the first time. However, Hernandez must do better than he did in his last outing against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton called Wednesday's effort against the New York Mets an ambush. He looked good through four innings before everything fell apart quickly in the fifth. He allowed 10 hits, seven runs, two walks and one home run in 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan is looking to win his first career game against the Phillies. He is 0-8 with a 6.09 ERA against them. In his last start, Lannan lasted five innings and allowed three runs on seven hits against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay already seems to be in midseason form. He threw seven shutout innings on Thursday in an 11-0 victory over the Mets at Citizens Bank Park, and he has allowed just one run in 13 innings this season. He hopes that continues against the Nats.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Zimmermann lasted 5 1/3 innings and allowed two runs on six hits against the Mets. He threw 99 pitches, with 68 strikes. It was the most pitches he threw in a game since his rookie year in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Lee allowed 10 hits and six runs in just 3 1/3 innings on Friday in a 6-3 loss to the Braves. It was his worst start since Sept. 4, 2009, when he allowed nine hits and six runs in three innings at Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt is off to a good start. He beat the Astros in his first start of the season, and beat the Braves on Saturday when he allowed just five hits and one earned run in six innings at Turner Field.
away_pitcher_note: After a dreadful season debut in which he walked five and allowed seven runs (four earned), exiting in the third inning, Vazquez held Houston to four runs on two walks over six innings on April 9, earning the win and cutting his ERA nearly in half.

home_pitcher_note: Phillies fans booed Hamels after his first start, but he dominated the Braves in his second. He allowed just four hits and one walk and struck out eight in seven scoreless innings Sunday against the Braves at Turner Field.
away_pitcher_note: After posting a 1.89 ERA in five spring starts, Sanchez looks to rebound from a loss to Houston in which he allowed six runs on 13 hits in 4 2/3 innings. The competition gets no easier, with Cole Hamels starting behind a relentless Phillies offense.

home_pitcher_note: Phillies fans booed Hamels after his first start, but he dominated the Braves in his second. He allowed just four hits and one walk and struck out eight in seven scoreless innings Sunday against the Atlanta Braves at Turner Field.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez will make the start on Sunday in place of Chris Volstad, who was initially scheduled. Volstad will be pushed back to Monday, when the Marlins face the Piirates.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton is hoping to turn around his season. He has been hit hard in each of his first two starts. Blanton thought he might have a problem pitching from the stretch. Pitching coach Rich Dubee said it's a matter of location.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum allowed just four hits in seven scoreless innings on Wednesday, striking out four in Milwaukee's 6-0 win over the Pirates. He now owns a 2.55 ERA and 1.19 WHIP through 17 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay is coming off a complete game at Washington in which he struck out nine and allowed two ninth inning runs in a 3-2 win. In three games he has amassed 22 innings in which he has walked just three.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf's 10-strikeout performance against the Pirates on Thursday was the 14th double-digit strikeout game of his career. It was also a springboard to a start in Philadelphia against his former team.

home_pitcher_note: Lee dominated Washington in a 3-0 shutout in his last start. Lee needed just 99 pitches to get through 30 Nationals hitters in the win. The win was a good sign after he allowed 6 runs in 3 1/3 innings in his previous start at Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Narveson surrendered his first runs of the season when he issued consecutive bases-loaded walks Friday. Before walking three batters in that inning, the lefty had only walked four in his first 14 innings of 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Latos is still looking for his first win of the season, one year after establishing himself as one of the National League's best young starters. He allowed five earned runs in 6 1/3 innings, losing to Houston in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt threw well in his last start, a 4-3 loss to Florida. Oswalt left that game after six innings with what has been diagnosed as a slight back strain but he is still on target to start in the final game of the Milwaukee series.

home_pitcher_note: Richard, battling a cold, struggled in his last start against the Astros, allowing six earned runs over 5 1/3 innings. He had allowed a combined four runs in his previous three starts. He has a 2.75 career ERA at PETCO Park.
away_pitcher_note: After a tough first start to the season, Hamels has pitched well. He is 1-0 with a 1.29 ERA in his last two starts. He has pitched seven innings in both of those starts, and has allowed just 14 hits, two runs and three walks. He has struck out 15.

home_pitcher_note: Stauffer matched his career-high outing by throwing seven shutout innings in his last start at frigid Wrigley Field. The former first-round pick is now 3-3 with a 2.56 ERA in 10 starts since being inserted into the Padres' rotation last Sept. 6.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton struggled in his first two starts, but put together a good one Monday. He allowed seven hits, two runs, one walk and struck out four in seven innings. Blanton always has been a slow starter, but he hopes this is a sign of improvement.

home_pitcher_note: The Padres are expected to turn to left-hander Wade LeBlanc to make a spot start Sunday, as the team attempts to right it rotation after a doubleheader on Wednesday. LeBlanc has a 6.87 ERA after three starts with Triple-A Tucson.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay suffered his worst start since June, when he allowed 10 hits and six runs in 6 2/3 innings Monday in a loss to the Brewers. His line looked worse than it was. He was a ground-ball out from finishing with three runs allowed in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy followed up one of his worst outings with one of his best. After allowing a career-high 9 earned runs in three innings in his previous start, Kennedy gave up just one run on four hits in 5 1/3 innings on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Lee followed his shutout on April 14 against the Washington Nationals with six innings Wednesday in a victory over the Milwaukee Brewers. He got the no-decision, but he allowed eight hits and two earned runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson retired 12 straight during one stretch on Thursday at Cincinnati, but he couldn't overcome a nightmarish first inning in which he allowed four runs on three hits and walked three, including two with the bases loaded.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt bounced back splendidly from a strained lower back Thursday in a 3-0 victory over the Padres at PETCO Park. Oswalt allowed just one hit and two walks in six scoreless innings. He struck out seven. He said afterward he had no back issues.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders pitched well against the Mets his last time out, but came away with a no-decision thanks to a bullpen meltdown. Saunders allowed just two hits through the first six innings before being removed after a walk to lead off the seventh.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels pitched brilliantly on Thursday in a 2-0 victory over the Padres at PETCO Park. He allowed four hits and three walks (one was intentional) and struck out eight in eight innings. Hamels threw 126 pitches to help out the Phils' overworked 'pen.

home_pitcher_note: Worley will start against the Mets in place of Joe Blanton, who was placed on the 15-day disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey pitched through an illness to pick up his first win of the season in a seven-inning, one-run effort against the D-backs. The righty pitched past the sixth inning for the first time, striking out four and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay comes off  a 3-1 victory over the Padres in San Diego when he threw 130 pitches before giving up a run and being pulled with two outs in the ninth. He's allowed three runs and 17 hits in his three wins, six runs, 10 hits in his loss.
away_pitcher_note: Niese snapped a personal six-game losing streak when he beat the D-backs on Sunday. He struck out three and walked two and has pitched six or more innings in four of his five starts this season. He has now allowed two homers in 30 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lee threw a five-hitter against the D-backs in Phoenix, but recorded his second loss because Arizona made the most of those hits to score four runs. He whiffed 12 to match a season high. His career high is 13 in 2010 vs. the A's.
away_pitcher_note: One of several Mets battling the flu this week, Young will be making his second appearance since a bout of right biceps tendinitis landed him on the disabled list in mid-April. In Young's first start back, he allowed three runs over 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is 3-0 with a 1.55 ERA in his last four starts. Opponents have hit just .186 against him. He allowed three runs in seven innings in his last start last week against Arizona, following a 126-pitch effort April 22 against San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez is the Nationals' workhorse and allowed three runs (two earned) and seven hits with five strikeouts and a walk in a 4-3 victory over the Mets on April 28. He also got an RBI with a sacrifice bunt.

home_pitcher_note: Worley made a fine debut Friday against the Mets at Citizens Bank Park. Replacing injured right-hander Joe Blanton, he allowed two hits, four walks and struck out five in six scoreless innings. He hopes for a repeat performance against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Marquis is on his way to one of his finest seasons as a pro. In his last outing, he pitched a shutout against the Giants, outdueling ace Tim Lincecum on April 29. Marquis allowed just five hits and no walks with seven strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay threw the 60th complete game of his career Saturday against the Mets at Citizens Bank Park. He threw 18 consecutive strikes to start the game, not throwing a ball until the third inning. He needed just 107 pitches to go nine.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan suffered a hard-luck loss in his most recent outing vs. the Giants. He allowed six hits and three walks in 6 2/3 innings, but he issued a bases-loaded walk in the seventh and the Nats lost, 2-1.

home_pitcher_note: Lee allowed eight hits, one run and two walks in seven innings Sunday night in a 2-1 loss to the Mets in 14 innings. He is pitching on normal rest instead of getting an extra day, because Roy Oswalt missed his turn in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe has pitched into the sixth in all but two of his starts, and would have in his last outing, but he was lifted for a pinch-hitter. He's allowed three runs or fewer in six of his starts, but has been saddled with a team-low 1.4 runs of support.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick takes Roy Oswalt's place in the rotation, as Oswalt is expected to be placed on the disabled list with a strained lower back. Kendrick threw 46 pitches in relief Sunday, so the Phillies think he could throw around 65 pitches Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran, ranked as MLB.com's second-best right-handed pitching prospect, will be making his MLB debut. The 20-year-old has posted a 1.80 ERA and limited opponents to a .118 batting average in five starts for Triple-A Gwinnett this year.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is developing into one of the best left-handers in baseball. From May 5, 2010, through Tuesday, Hamels is 14-10 with a 2.68 ERA. In 218 2/3 innings, he has allowed 181 hits, 65 earned runs and 61 walks. He has struck out 215.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has thrown at least 100 pitches in each of his first four starts and regained his successful form. The 25-year-old right-hander notched a 114-pitch complete game on April 26 and tossed 7 2/3 strong innings against the Brewers Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez watched a four-run lead slip away in his last start, and he worked 5 2/3 innings, giving up six runs (four earned) in a no-decision at St. Louis. He threw 110 pitches, his most since 117 a year ago when he was with the Yankees at Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is expected to rejoin the rotation after missing two starts because of a medial impingement in his right elbow. Interestingly, as Blanton's elbow felt, he pitched well after struggling in his first two starts.

home_pitcher_note: JJ is human after all. In his last start, he set season highs with five runs on eight hits in 7 1/3 frames at St. Louis. He's thrown at least 114 pitches in three straight outings. Johnson is 5-3 with a 3.34 ERA vs. Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Halladay faced Josh Johnson in May, he threw a perfect game. Halladay might need to throw another one the way Johnson is pitching. But Halladay is an incredible 18-1 with a 1.56 ERA in 19 starts against the NL East since last season.

home_pitcher_note: Ricky Nolasco recorded his 12th career 10-strikeout game in the Marlins 3-2 loss to Washington May 6. The right-hander pitched seven innings, and allowed six hits and two runs while striking out 11.
away_pitcher_note: Lee is coming off a 5-0 loss to Atlanta in which he fanned 16, including 14 of his final 15 outs, tying Steve Carlton for most K's in one game by a lefty in Phillies history. He would've preferred a win as he fell to 2-3 with a 3.69 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy has proven to be much more than a feel-good story. The undrafted free agent has posted a 1.44 ERA and limited opponents to a .140 batting average in his past four starts. He has 28 strikeouts in his past 25 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels kicks off a big series for the Phillies, who lost two of three last weekend to the Atlanta Braves. He is 4-1 with a 1.80 ERA in his last six starts. He allowed five hits and three runs in seven innings last weekend against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens was strong into the seventh inning and limited the Phillies to one run Sunday night in Philadelphia.  He has won each of his four decisions since missing the season's first two weeks with an oblique strain.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton returned to the rotation Monday after spending time on the disabled list with a medial impingement in his right elbow. Blanton allowed eight hits and three runs in five innings against the Marlins, but he still felt soreness in the elbow.

home_pitcher_note: Shoddy defense plagued Hudson as he allowed a pair of homers and lost to the Nationals on Tuesay night.  The veteran hurler allowed two earned runs in 7 2/3 innings while beating the Phillies on April 8.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay outlasted and outpitched Josh Johnson on Tuesday in Florida, but an eighth-inning error from Jimmy Rollins allowed an unearned run to score to cost the Phillies the game. Halladay should have no problem bouncing back. He usually does.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook is coming off a disconcerting start in which took a step back after it appeared he had banished his early funk. The Phillies will present a good challenge for Westbrook, who struggled against them last June.
away_pitcher_note: Lee has pitched fairly well other than one start in Atlanta, but the problem lately has been a lack of run support. The Phillies had not scored a run while Lee was pitching in 27 innings before snapping it Wednesday in Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia keeps impressing. In his last start, he wasn't at his sharpest but still battled through seven strong innings. If he can have games like that, succeeding while not at his best, he's going to have a huge year.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is expected to make his first start since landing on the 15-day disabled list with lower back inflammation. He made a rehab start Thursday with Class A Clearwater with the expectation he would rejoin the rotation if he felt OK.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed four runs in six innings in his last start Friday against the Braves. It was the most runs he had allowed since his first start of the season. Hamels is 4-1 with a 2.29 ERA in his last seven starts. He faces a good offensive team.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa earned a win his last time out despite what was his shakiest performance of the season -- five runs allowed on nine hits in 5 2/3 innings. He has struggled in his career against the Phillies (0-3, 9.78 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Keep an eye on Blanton, whose velocity has been down in his two starts since returning from the disabled list. Blanton said his right elbow feels better, but as long as there is discomfort, even the Phillies said it bears watching.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin had a six-run lead in the seventh against the Padres on Saturday when bad pitch decisions and his own poor fielding set in motion a bitter loss. Before then, his fastball and secondary pitches were effective.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay is hoping for a little better luck and some offensive support Friday. He has pitched two consecutive complete games, but both games have been losses. The Phillies managed just three runs in those games. Halladay allowed five.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson went just five-plus innings against the Angels on Sunday, throwing 104 pitches and allowing four runs (two earned). It snapped a run of five consecutive starts with him pitching seven or more innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lee has pitched better than his record indicates so far in '11, but struggled with his command his last outing. He walked a career-high six batters in a loss to the Cards on Tuesday, in which he allowed three earned runs on six hits with four K's.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis dazzled in his last start against the White Sox on Monday, hurling a five-hit shutout while fanning seven. He lowered his ERA to a season-best 3.81 with the stellar effort.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt's first start after returning from the disabled list went well on Tuesday in St. Louis. He allowed one run on seven hits, struck out three and walked one in five innings. He threw 76 pitches, 48 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison was solid in his most recent outing against the White Sox last Tuesday, giving up three runs over seven innings of work with six strikeouts. He took a no-decision, however.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels continues to pitch well. He allowed just one run in eight innings Wednesday against the Colorado Rockies. He threw a five-hit shutout against the Reds in Game 3 of the 2010 NLDS to sweep the series.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo was essentially undone by two pitches Wednesday against the Pirates. Both went for home runs that accounted for all five runs against him. The one pitch that really hurt was a changeup he left up to Pedro Alvarez, who smoked a three-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: Worley replaces Joe Blanton in the rotation, who is on the disabled list with right elbow inflammation. Worley made two starts earlier this season when Blanton was on the DL, going 2-0 with a 0.75 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto had his first lackluster outing since returning from the disabled list. During a loss to Pittsburgh on Thursday, a 31-pitch second inning hurt badly and put him out of the game with 94 pitches in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay got his first win since May 5 in a 3-2 victory Friday against Texas. He had run into bad luck lately, pitching and losing two consecutive complete games because of a lack of run support. But three runs was all he needed against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Wood was baffled after his no-hitter vs. the Indians imploded in the sixth inning. His undoing was a 30-pitch inning, during which he couldn't retire a hitter after losing the no-no. Last July in Philly, Wood lost a perfect game in the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: Lee earned a win for the first time since April 14 in a 2-0 victory Saturday against the Texas Rangers. Lee allowed five hits, two walks and struck out 10 in eight scoreless innings. He'd have a better record with more run support.
away_pitcher_note: It was literally one bad pitch by Bailey that ruined his day in Saturday's loss to the Indians. After retiring 17 of 18 batters, he missed on locating a first-pitch fastball in the seventh inning. It went for a two-run homer by Travis Buck.

home_pitcher_note: Capuano fell victim to the long ball in his Saturday start at Yankee Stadium. He saw his season homer total jump from five to nine in giving up six runs in 5 1/3 innings. The fly ball shouldn't be as lethal this time around at cavernous Citi Field.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt suffered his first career loss at Citizens Bank Park on Sunday, but it wasn't because he pitched poorly. He allowed just one run in seven innings against the Rangers, but the Phillies offered him no help in a 2-0 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey was cruising through six innings May 22 against the Yankees before a ground-ball single, a walk and a hit-by-pitch undid him in an eight-run seventh. In two starts against the Phils this year, he has allowed 10 earned runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed five hits, three runs, two walks and struck out four in six innings Monday against the Cincinnati Reds. He certainly wasn't his best, but he was good enough and finally got a little run support. He would welcome more against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Multiple errors led to four unearned runs last Tuesday for Niese, who lowered his ERA six points despite giving up six runs in five innings. Niese is 0-2 against the Phillies this year with a 6.97 ERA, both outings coming at Citizens Bank Park.
away_pitcher_note: Worley is taking Joe Blanton's spot in the rotation. Blanton has an elbow injury. Worley didn't have his best command Tuesday against the Cincinnati Reds. He allowed six hits, three runs, four walks and struck out three in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez finally got some run support in his last start, but the bullpen faltered. He lost a chance at victory when Tyler Clippard and Henry Rodriguez each gave up two runs late in a 7-6 loss at Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is 4-2 with a 2.10 ERA in his past seven starts. He is 5-0 with a 1.15 ERA in five starts against Washington since joining the Phillies and is 10-1 with a 2.01 ERA in 14 career appearances against the Nationals/Expos in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis is 5-8 with a 5.61 ERA in 25 games against the Phillies over his career. In his last start against Milwaukee on Wednesday, he gave up four runs in six innings while taking his second loss of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Lee is 2-2 with a 2.98 ERA in six May starts. The Phillies scored five runs for him in those first five starts before scoring 10 runs for him Thursday in a victory over the Reds. Lee is 3-0 with a 1.44 ERA in three career starts against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan has more career starts against the Phillies than any other team, but he is 0-10 in those 13 outings. The lefty enters the game off of his best start of 2011, when he allowed two hits over 7 2/3 innings in a no-decision against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt allowed nine hits and one earned run in six innings Friday in a victory over the Mets at Citi Field. Oswalt is 0-1 with a 1.50 ERA in three starts since returning from the disabled list (lower back inflammation). He said he has felt fine.

home_pitcher_note: After a nine-day layoff between starts, Karstens battled through five innings in his last one against the Cubs on Sunday. He allowed just two earned runs in the outing, and he's now given up two or fewer earned runs in six of his eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels earned his win at Citi Field on Saturday, allowing two runs and striking out 10 in seven innings in a 5-2 victory against the Mets. The Phillies have won nine of Hamels' last 10 starts. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton pitched well in his last outing against the Mets, but fell victim to a string of well-placed ground balls and two passed balls. He gave up 11 singles and three runs, but he did not allow an extra-base hit and two of the runs came unearned.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies scheduled Kendrick to make a spot start after optioning right-hander Vance Worley on Monday. Kendrick is no stranger to starting, but he is not stretched out. He said he thinks he could throw at least 65 pitches against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald allowed one run in the first inning against the Mets on Tuesday, but did not allow another in his six innings. He has now gone three straight starts in which he has pitched at least six innings and given up two earned runs or fewer.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay struggled Monday in his start against the Nationals. He allowed 10 hits, four runs and three home runs in seven innings. The three homers against Washington were one short of his career-high four, which he set last season against Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Lee will try to bounce back from one of his worst starts of the season. He allowed seven hits, six runs, three walks and two home runs in 5 1/3 innings in a loss to the Nationals. Lee who walked just 18 batters last season has walked 19 this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers have rotated wins and losses in each of Lilly's 12 starts this season. The trend would indicate he's due for a loss, but his recent performance wouldn't -- three consecutive quality starts and a steadily declining ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt allowed six hits and two runs in five innings Wednesday against the Nationals. He has allowed five earned runs in 23 innings (1.96 ERA) since returning from the disabled list, but has pitched more than six innings just once in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: This will be De La Rosa's first Major League start, taking over for injured Jon Garland. Up from Double-A, he has seemed at ease in this setting, considering he started last season at Class A. Along with his stuff, he seems fearless.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start in Pittsburgh on Friday, Hamels pitched well enough to win what would have been his fourth consecutive start for the third time in his career, but he received a no-decision after allowing one run on one hit over eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda battled through six innings in Cincinnati with less than his best stuff, allowing two runs when he got too careful with the middle of the order and walked Joey Votto and Jay Bruce. He's looking to snap a three-game losing streak.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing on June 4 in Pittsburgh Kendrick got the spot start for the Phils, tossing five innings in a 6-3 loss to the Pirates. He allowed four runs on eight hits and was tagged with the loss.
away_pitcher_note: If not for 95-degree heat and Albert Pujols, Wells might have gone deeper in his last start. He gave up three hits -- two to Pujols -- over 5 2/3 innings and did not get a decision. This will be his third start since coming off the DL.

home_pitcher_note: The reigning NL Cy Young winner pitched well enough to stop the Phillies' losing streak in his last outing on Sunday in Pittsburgh. Halladay pitched seven effective innings as Philly snapped a season-high four-game skid.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano was denied a win on Sunday in his last start when the Cardinals rallied for a 10-inning win. He criticized his teammates after the game. It will be interesting to see how they -- and he -- respond.

home_pitcher_note: Lee returned to his dominant self in Monday's 3-0 victory over the Dodgers. He allowed seven hits, one walk and struck out 10 in seven scoreless innings. Lee got knocked around in his previous start against Washington, but had no problems Monday.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Garza's second start since coming off the disabled list. He threw 81 pitches over four innings against the Reds in his last outing, giving up six hits and walking three. He was hitting 94 mph on the radar gun, a good sign.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt had one of his worst starts of the season Tuesday in a loss to the Los Angeles Dodgers. He allowed eight hits, four runs, two walks and struck out one in six innings. He had allowed four or more runs just one other time.
away_pitcher_note: Davis is still winless in five starts. He's made eight career starts against the Phillies and is 2-2 with a 3.71 ERA. In his last outing, he gave up seven hits over 4 1/3 innings, and the leadoff batter got on in four of five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels continued to establish himself as one of the game's best left-handers against the Los Angeles Dodgers. He allowed six hits and struck out nine in eight scoreless innings. Hamels has the fifth-best ERA in baseball (2.66) since May 1, 2010.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Volstad had a no-hitter through five against the Braves, but gave up three runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings. He has lost his last five decisions, and has not won since April 26. Volstad is 2-4 with a 4.45 ERA against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies have not made an announcement, but if Kendrick remains in the rotation, he is likely to pitch the first game of the doubleheader. He has been in the rotation since Vince Worley was optioned to Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: An extra starter was needed for the doubleheader, so Villanueva was called up for his MLB debut. The 24-year-old was 4-5 with a 5.23 ERA in 13 starts at Triple-A New Orleans. The right-hander threw six shutout innings on Thursday against Memphis.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies have not made any announcements, but Halladay is on track to start Wednesday. He threw seven scoreless innings in Friday's 7-5 victory over the Cubs. He allowed six hits and struck out nine to pick up his Major League-leading ninth win.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez has logged eight strikeouts in three of his last four outings, and the Marlins have won eight of his 13 starts, including six of the last seven. Sanchez allowed three runs in 6 2/3 innings in a win over the D-backs on June 10th.

home_pitcher_note: Lee turned in another solid outing his last time out against the Cubs. He pitched eight innings and allowed just one run on four hits, striking out seven. He's won his last four home starts, allowing five runs and striking out 35 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Over his last two starts, Vazquez has allowed 13 runs on 15 hits in 7 2/3 innings. The right-hander gave up six runs (five earned) on nine hits in 4 1/3 innings on May 9 against the Phillies at Sun Life Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: The big rookie gave up eight hits, six runs and five earned runs in 5 1/3 innings in an 8-1 loss to the Tigers, all career highs. He's now lost two in a row and gone four starts without a win after opening the year 6-2.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt snapped a four-game losing streak in his last start, holding the Cubs to three runs. The seven innings pitched tied a season high, and his five strikeouts were the most since April 21 in San Diego. He's 1-0 in two starts against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez dug deep to beat Detroit on Sunday, needing 126 pitches to work around nine hits and five walks over eight innings in a 7-3 win. He'll have an extra day's rest after an off-day on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Worley is making his first start for the Phillies since a May 29 loss to the Mets, when he surrendered eight runs on 12 hits in just three innings. He has since worked back into his regular routine at Triple-A Lehigh Valley and built up his velocity.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas gave up a pair of home runs to Vernon Wells in a 6-3 loss to the Angels on Monday, allowing five runs in seven innings. The lefty has gone seven or more innings in seven of his last nine starts and is 4-2, 3.50 ERA in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels has been one of the game's best pitchers in this season, but he left Tuesday's start because of tightness in his back. He said he is fine, which the Phillies hope is true. Hamels and Roy Halladay have been the best 1-2 punch in baseball.

home_pitcher_note: McClellan will be looking for a longer outing in his second game back from the disabled list. He was often very good but occasionally erratic in his return to the roster, throwing strikes but sometimes missing up in the zone.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is taking a second crack at his 10th win, coming off a slow start in his last outing against Florida, when he gave up four runs on six hits over seven innings, striking out eight. It's his first start against the Cardinals this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has come back to earth a bit after a hot start, allowing four runs in each of his past three starts. Most disconcerting is that he's allowed five homers in those three games after allowing just three in his first 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lee is red hot, winning his last three starts and giving up just 13 hits, one run and striking out 21 in 24 innings. But this will be his first road start since May 31, when gave up six runs on seven hits over 5 1/3 innings against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter just needs some luck. He's throwing strikes and getting swings-and-misses and ground balls, but the ball keeps finding holes. Philly has been tough on him historically, so this may be a difficult assignment.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is 1-4 with a 3.40 ERA in seven starts since returning from the disabled list May 17. He has had some of the worst run support in baseball in that span, but also has been putting a ton of runners on base. Both have caught up with him.

home_pitcher_note: Worley earned another start after a solid five-inning, one-run outing against Seattle on Saturday in a spot start. Worley will take the hill for the second time since being recalled from Triple-A Lehigh Valley on June 17.
away_pitcher_note: Moscoso didn't pitch deep enough to earn a decision, but A's manager Bob Melvin said he wouldn't call the righty's effort a "bad" outing. Moscoso tossed 4 2/3 and gave up two runs, neither of which was earned, on three hits and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels lost his first game in over a month in his last outing against Seattle, but recieved no run support. The left-hander has pitched at least seven innings in four of his last five starts, and the California native has never faced Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: The righty was masterful against the Giants, going eight innings and allowing just one run while striking out seven. He retired 16 of the last 17 batters he faced (including a stretch of 10 in a row) and allowed only one hit after the third inning.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay scattered four hits over six innings and allowed one run in his last start against the Cardinals. The right-hander has won four starts in a row and the Phillies have won each of Halladay's last seven outings.
away_pitcher_note: Outman surrendered two runs (one earned) and two walks with four strikeouts in six innings of work to defeat the Mets on Tuesday. He has fired quality starts in five of his six outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is in as hot a stretch as any in baseball and looks every bit worth the money the Phils signed him for this offseason, allowing just one earned run in his past four starts, spanning 33 innings. He's pitched back-to-back shutouts.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett will be pitching on nine days' rest after being scratched from his Tuesday start due to a stomach illness. The Major League-leader in ERA has allowed just two earned runs in two career starts against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Worley took a no-hitter into the sixth inning in his last start against the A's. He has found his early-season success since rejoining the rotation on June 18, posting an 0.82 ERA in two starts, giving up one run in 11 innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey had three solid starts after returning from the 15-day disabled list in early June, but in his last start, he allowed five runs in just 3 1/3 innings in a loss to the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is trying for the third time to win his 10th game this season. He's continued to pitch as well as anyone in baseball, allowing a combined four runs in his past two starts. But the offense has given him just one run of support in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester took a hard-luck loss Friday against the Pirates in which he allowed just two earned runs. He has given up three earned runs or less in each of his past four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Romero starts the series opener vs. Philly with some serious momentum. Over his last three starts, the 26-year-old has allowed just three earned runs while striking out 21. Romero has pitched at least seven innings in each of his last nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick is making his first start since he allowed one run over seven innings in a win against the Marlins on June 15. Kendrick is pitching in place of the injured Roy Oswalt, who has mild bulging discs in his back and is out until at least August.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva is coming off a solid six-inning effort in which he allowed just five hits and two runs in a 6-3 win in St. Louis. He had recorded seven successive winning decisions prior to a 2-1 loss in Cincinnati on June 19.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is making his first start against his former team since being traded in 2010. The Phils have won the last eight games he has started. He pitched a complete game in his last outing against the A's, allowing just one earned run on eight hits.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes allowed a season-high six earned runs during his last outing against Pittsburgh. He surrendered nine hits and one walk over just 3 2/3 innings. It was the fifth time this season he has failed to pitch at least four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lee enters Sunday's start against the Blue Jays riding a career-high 32-inning scoreless streak, which ranks fifth in Phillies history. He has thrown three consecutive shutouts and finished June 5-0 with a 0.21 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco was masterful against the A's in his last start. After dropping four straight decisions, the righty hurled a five-hit shutout -- his first complete game since April 17, 2010, and just the second shutout of his career.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies are without Roy Oswalt and Joe Blanton in the rotation, but Worley is easing the pain. He continues to pitch well, including last week's start against Boston. He allowed five hits and one run and struck out five in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad picked up his second consecutive victory, allowing an unearned run on seven hits over seven innings against Oakland on Monday. Volstad had been in a winless drought from April 26-June 25, including a loss to the Phillies.

Sanchez lost for the second time this season and for the first time since April 10 in a 15-5 loss to the Rangers. He allowed seven earned runs in 3 2/3 innings. The loss snapped a career high six-game winning streak.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed eight hits, six runs, one walk and two home runs and hit two batters in seven innings Friday against the Toronto Blue Jays at Roger Centre, but he was in line for the win before allowing a two-run homer to Jose Bautista.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay is having another Cy Young season and he soon will learn if he is starting in Tuesday's All-Star Game in Phoenix. But before that, Halladay has a chance to pitch against the Braves, who are keeping close to the Phillies in the NL East.
away_pitcher_note: Beachy, who suffered his first loss since returning from the disabled list on Sunday, hasn't had much success against the Phillies. They've accounted for all three of his career losses and have scored 10 runs off him in 18 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lee had been the hottest pitcher on the planet until he allowed seven runs in 7 1/3 innings Sunday in Toronto. The NL Pitcher of the Month went 5-0 with a 0.27 ERA in June, including three straight shutouts. He tries to get back on track Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson continued his All-Star-caliber season in his last start against the Rockies, allowing a run in seven innings. He has gone 5-0 with a 1.97 ERA in his past five starts, and his 2.52 ERA is among the best in the National League.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels learned last Sunday he had made his second All-Star Game, but he won't get to pitch in Phoenix because he is facing Atlanta on Sunday at Citizens Bank Park. Hamels picked up his 10th win in his last start Tuesday in Miami.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe has been victorious in each of his past two starts after going winless in the nine before it. It's been a slow start for Lowe, whose five wins match his September total last season. He is 1-1 in two starts this year against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey pitched well in a no-decision against the Giants despite pain in his foot and a tight left gluteal muscle. He threw seven innings, allowing two runs on seven hits while striking out four, and he hoped the time off would heal his injuries.
away_pitcher_note: Worley was sent down to Triple-A Lehigh Valley after his last start to stay on routine. He last pitched for the Phillies on July 4, tossing seven scoreless innings and scattering two hits. He's allowed one run or fewer in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Niese won his eighth game, giving up three earned runs on five hits and a walk in seven innings against the Dodgers. The lefty is 1-2 vs. the Phillies in 2011, winning his most recent outing on May 29 by allowing one unearned run in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels is a legitimate NL Cy Young candidate, posting an 11-4 record and team-best 2.32 ERA in the first half. He pitched eight innings and allowed one run on three hits in his last start against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey finished up the first half by yielding two runs over six innings in a losing effort against the Giants. The right-hander has struggled against the Phillies, owning a career 5.01 ERA and 1.44 WHIP against them despite a 6-5 record in 16 games.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies send Kendrick to the mound in an effort to get top two starters Roy Halladay and Cliff Lee some extra rest to start the second half. Kendrick is 3-5 with a 3.07 ERA vs. the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez is 1-1 with a 4.03 ERA in five starts with the Cubs. In his last outing before the break, he gave up three runs on eight hits over six innings against the Pirates. He did face the Phillies earlier but that was in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is making his first start since pitching two perfect innings in last week's All-Star Game. The extra rest figures to help deep in the season, as he leads the league in innings pitched. He threw seven scoreless innings June 10 against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Garza deserved better in his last start against the Marlins. He threw seven shutout innings and left with a lead, but the bullpen imploded. Garza now is 3-1 in his last five home starts with a 2.62 ERA, including a complete game.
away_pitcher_note: Looking for his 10th win, Lee is the beneficiary of extra rest after pitching two innings in the All-Star Game. He allowed one earned run on four hits with seven strikeouts in eight innings in his only other outing against the Cubs this year.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster opened the second half by throwing eight shutout innings vs. the Marlins, striking out nine. There was no arguing, either, with manager Mike Quade over how long he would pitch. Dempster is 4-2 with a 1.82 ERA in his last eight home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Worley has been producing far more than the Phillies could have hoped when injuries to Roy Oswalt and Joe Blanton pinched the rotation. Worley hasn't allowed more than one earned run in any of his five starts since returning last month.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels plans to rebound from a horrible start Saturday at Citi Field. He has been pitching brilliantly for much of the season, so there's no reason to think he won't rebound in the series opener.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Luebke was, as he's been in each of his four starts this season, solid. Since moving into the rotation he's gone 2-1 with a 1.50 ERA, 26 strikeouts and four walks. Opponents are hitting .148 against him in those four games.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick gets another shot after pitching well Sunday. He is in the rotation until Roy Oswalt returns from the disabled list, which could happen early next month. Until then, Kendrick has a chance in some important games for the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Latos has strung together a set of solid starts, however each one appears to be a bit of a grind. He's given up 25 earned runs in his last 10 starts, but never more than four in a game. In his last start, Latos surrendered three runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay left Monday's start against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field in the fifth inning because of heat exhaustion. He said he should be ready to go Sunday against the Padres, but it will be interesting to see if he has fully bounced back.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer threw six shutout innings in his last start, giving him his eight consecutive quality starts. He has the third-best ERA in the Major Leagues (1.33) among starters since June 7. His four-pitch mix continues to give hitters fits.

home_pitcher_note: Lee started slowly Tuesday against the Cubs at Wrigley Field, but retired 15 of the final 18 batters he faced. In six innings, he allowed eight hits, two runs and struck out six. He could have pitched longer but was pulled for a pinch-hitter.

away_pitcher_note: Karstens had a blip in his efficiency, lasting only five innings and throwing 96 pitches on Tuesday. He went into his last start leading the Majors in fewest pitches-per-inning. Karstens has allowed more than three earned runs only once in 18 starts.
