home_pitcher_note: Halladay had a Cy Young-caliber season, although Clayton Kershaw is likely to win it. But Halladay pitched splendidly on arguably baseball's most dominating rotation in decades. He is the aces of the aces, and don't let anybody tell you differently.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse might have been an easy choice for Game 1. The 32-year-old got the better of Roy Halladay on Sept. 19, when he went 7 1/3 innings without allowing an earned run in a 4-3 victory at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lee spurned more money from the Yankees and Rangers and lived up to his the hype in his return campaign with the Phillies. He threw a remarkable six shutouts and proved nearly unhittable in both June and August. Can he repeat in October?
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter has never started on short rest in the Major Leagues, and that has to be a bit of a concern. But he's coming off an efficient game in Houston, and his history as a big-game and playoff pitcher is well-established.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has been very successful against the Phillies, who have a rougher time against left-handed pitchers than right-handers in general. He's also much more effective at Busch Stadium than on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels, who is 6-4 with a 3.33 ERA in 12 career postseason starts, lost his only outing against the Cardinals this season, allowing seven hits and four runs in seven innings Sept. 18 in St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: This is quite a pitcher to call upon in a Game 4. Jackson has been arguably St. Louis' best starter since late July. He allowed two or fewer earned runs in nine of 12 starts, pitching at least six innings in 10 out of 12.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Oswalt pitched in St. Louis in the postseason he sent the Astros to their first and only World Series. He is looking forward to repeating the feat, either sending the Phillies to the NLCS or keeping their season alive for a Game 5.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies traded for Halladay in December 2009 with games like Friday in mind. He's the ace of a rotation full of aces, and they'll be counting on him to keep their season alive in the team's first Game 5 in a postseason series since the '81 NLDS.
away_pitcher_note: If the Cardinals have a must-win game, Carpenter is the man they want pitching. He scuffled on short rest in Game 2, but on full rest, there's no reason to think he can't be his best. He'll be facing an old friend in Roy Halladay.

summary: 2012-03-15 - Philadelphia Phillies @ Tampa Bay Rays (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Bedard makes his third Opening Day start -- his first since 2008, when he was with the Mariners -- as well as his NL debut. The Bucs' key offseason free-agent signing is hoping to have his first uninterrupted healthy season since 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay has been everything fans could have imagined when the Phillies acquired him before the 2010 season. He won the 2010 NL Cy Young and finished second in the voting last season. He hopes to finally get a World Series ring in 2012.

home_pitcher_note: The Bucs' most consistent starter the second half of '11 begins this season locked into a rotation for the first time in his career. He has prepared well, posting a 2.12 ERA in 17 exhibition innings. He excelled in two starts vs. the Phils last year.
away_pitcher_note: Lee returned to Philadelphia to help the Phillies form one of baseball's most formidable rotations. He lived up to the hype, finishing third in NL Cy Young Award voting.

home_pitcher_note: None of the Pirates are as glad for Spring Training to be over than McDonald, who gets to push the reset button after a shaky preseason. He won't miss injured Phils Ryan Howard and Chase Utley, who have a combined .555 average against him.
away_pitcher_note: Roy Oswalt and Joe Blanton suffered injuries last season, but Worley picked up the slack. He finished third in NL Rookie of the Year Award voting, proving to be a valuable piece of the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is one of the big three, but he gets the fourth start of the season because the Phillies want him to pitch the home opener against the Miami Marlins. It's a nice honor for Hamels, who can become a free agent following the season.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez missed time with right shoulder soreness early in Spring Training. He made 32 starts in 2011, striking out 202 in 196 1/3 innings. He was 2-5, 3.74 ERA against NL East teams. He was 0-1 in three starts at Philly.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay looked like his typical dominant self in Thursday's 1-0 victory over Pittsburgh at PNC Park. He allowed just two hits and struck out five in eight scoreless innings, silencing some concerns about his rough spring.
away_pitcher_note: Opening Night was a battle for Johnson, who matched his career high by allowing 10 hits to the Cards. While healthy, Johnson admits that the consistent sharpness of his pitches is not quite there. It's a work in progress.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies didn't need their fifth starter until April 15, but they didn't want Blanton to wait that long to pitch, so he's going to make his debut in the series finale against Miami. He's hoping to rebound from an injury-marred 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle made his Marlins and NL debut on April 5 at Cincinnati. He labored early, needing 28 pitches to get through the first inning. He lasted six innings, giving up two earned runs on seven hits over 108 pitches. He walked two and struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: Lee pitched splendidly in his 2012 debut Saturday against the Pirates at PNC Park. He allowed just two hits, one run and two walks and struck out four in six innings for a no-decision. He's hoping for a little more run support this time.
away_pitcher_note: Wind may have played a role in Dickey's control issues in his first start, when the knuckleballer walked four Braves batters but escaped with the win. Dickey did not pitch at Citizens Bank Park last year and has never won there in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Worley, who finished third in voting for the 2011 National League Rookie of the Year Award, picked up where he left off last season on Sunday against the Pirates at PNC Park, allowing just one run in six innings. He hopes for continued success.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start after signing a five-year, $25.5 million extension, Niese carried a no-hitter into the seventh vs. the Braves. The lefty lost all three games he pitched at Citizens Bank Park last season, posting a 10.05 ERA in the process.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed four runs in 5 1/3 innings in Monday's 6-2 loss to the Marlins, but he pitched better than his line indicated. He struck out nine, but allowed too many leadoff hitters to reach base. He looks to improve upon that against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey's first start included 10 hits, a career-high eight strikeouts and a no-decision. He'll look to earn his first win against the Phillies, who scored 25 runs in 28 innings against him last season. That included a 9.49 ERA at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum is coming off the shortest start of his career, 2 1/3 innings Wednesday at Colorado, a 76-pitch outing in which he gave up six runs and eight hits but avoided a loss in the Giants' 17-8 defeat.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay struggled this spring with a 5.73 ERA, but you wouldn't know it by his start in April. He has looked like one of the best pitchers in baseball, going 2-0 with a 0.60 ERA in his first two starts to the season.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner pitched 5 1/3 innings of no-hit ball in Colorado on Thursday, with only the game's leadoff hitter getting a ball out of the infield during the span. He pitched for quick outs rather than strikeouts, lasting 7 1/3 innings and 117 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton on Thursday made his first true start in the Phillies rotation since May 14, 2011. He pitched superbly, allowing just three hits, one run, one walk and striking out three in seven innings in a victory against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Only a sixth-inning single by opposing pitcher James McDonald separated Cain from a perfect game last Friday against Pittsburgh. Flirting with history is commonplace for Cain, who has taken no-hitters into the seventh inning five times in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Lee allowed four earned runs against the Mets on Friday but pitched better than that stat would indicate. His location was off slightly in his first two outings, but the Phillies are confident he'll quickly make the needed adjustments.

home_pitcher_note: Wieland had a rough time in his Major League debut against the Dodgers, allowing two home runs to Matt Kemp and one to Andre Ethier. He settled down thereafter, retiring 10 of the last 12 batters in a five-inning stint where he allowed six runs.
away_pitcher_note: Worley left some pitches up in the strike zone last week in a 5-0 loss to the Mets. He allowed eight hits, four runs, four walks and two home runs in six innings. He is looking to make some adjustments against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez suffered some command issues in his last start, walking five in five innings against the Dodgers. He allowed four runs and six hits, one of which was a home run to Matt Kemp. He's still looking for his first win with the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: After beating the Mets on Sunday, Hamels was the winning pitcher for the first time since September. Before then he made five appearances without a victory, partly due to elbow problems and partly because of a lack of run support.

home_pitcher_note: Luebke had his best start of the year, effectively mixing a well-spotted fastball, slider and newly honed changeup to hold the Rockies to one run on six hits and a walk over seven innings. Luebke was aggressive in the zone, getting 12 groundouts.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay has been his typical dominant self, but he is looking for a little more consistency in his mechanics. He has started slowly but finished strong. Scary to think what he could be if he fine-tunes his mechanics like he wants.

home_pitcher_note: Bass made progress against the Rockies, giving up three runs on four hits and three walks while striking out seven in five innings. He used a good slider and changeup, but he is working on being more efficient with his pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton looks to bounce back after struggling Tuesday in San Francisco, where he allowed 11 hits and four runs in five innings in a loss to the Giants at AT&T Park. His debut went better, allowing one run in seven innings against Miami.

home_pitcher_note: With Daniel Hudson on the disabled list, the D-backs will turn to reliever Wade Miley for Monday's opener with the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Kyle Kendrick will fill in for Cliff Lee, whom the Phillies placed on the 15-day disabled list on Saturday for a strained left oblique. It will be Kendrick's first start of the season. He started 15 games and went 8-6 with a 3.22 ERA last season.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter took the loss on Thursday against the Braves but turned in a much better outing than in his first two starts. He gave up four earned runs on six hits through 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Worley struck out a career-high 11 in seven innings and picked up his first victory of the season on Thursday against the Padres. He also dealt through vision issues when his goggles got foggy.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing just two runs in his first two starts for the D-backs, Cahill gave up seven to the Braves on Friday. Only four were earned, but Cahill took his first loss of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Returning to his hometown San Diego in his last start, Hamels battled, allowing a run and six hits in six innings against the Padres. He struck out four, walked one and was called for two balks.

home_pitcher_note: The way the Phillies are swinging the bats, Philadelphia pitchers have almost no margin for error these days. So Halladay is going to have to be close to perfect in the series opener against the Cubs. Fortunately, he mostly has been.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm is hoping to build off his first win with the Cubs. He held the Reds to one run on four hits over six innings in his last start. He's 3-2 with a 4.50 ERA in seven starts in his career vs. the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Sloppy defense ruined Blanton's last start last weekend against the Padres at Petco Park, where he allowed six runs (three earned) in six innings. In three starts, Blanton has a 4.00 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Wells' second start in place of Ryan Dempster, on the DL with a strained right quad. In his first game, against the Reds on Sunday, Wells escaped some jams and gave up two runs on six hits and five walks over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick suffered the team's worst start since 2010 when he allowed seven earned runs in three-plus innings Monday against the D-backs in Phoenix. He needs to pitch much better than that while Cliff Lee is on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Garza deserved better in his last start when he gave up two runs over seven innings and didn't get a decision. He's struggled on the road, serving up more runs in one start away from Wrigley than three games at home. That needs to change.

home_pitcher_note: Worley gutted through six innings Tuesday in a victory over the D-backs at Chase Field. He allowed one run and five hits in six innings, but he had to work for it. But so far he is proving his 2011 rookie season is no fluke.
away_pitcher_note: The Cubs flipped Volstad and Jeff Samardzija so Samardzija could get an extra day. Volstad is looking for his first win since July 10. In his last outing vs. the Cards, he was cruising until the sixth and then missed locating some of his pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy has pitched into the seventh inning in three consecutive starts. His streak of 19 2/3 consecutive innings without allowing an earned run ended as he allowed the Dodgers two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels retired 18 consecutive D-backs at one point in Wednesday's 7-2 victory at Chase Field. He allowed just four hits and two runs and struck out seven in eight innings, looking like another strong All-Star candidate.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson has lasted at least six innings in three consecutive starts and allowed two runs or fewer in his past two. His fastball has been livelier in his past two outings, and he seems more comfortable than he was in early April.
away_pitcher_note: Roy Halladay will try to end his first losing streak in nearly a year but will need help from an offense that's scored one run in each of his last two starts. He's gone at least seven innings and allowed three or fewer runs each time out this season.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado has shown his youth while struggling through his past two outings. Not commanding his curve, he primarily remains a fastball-changeup pitcher. He limited the Phillies to two runs in five innings on Sept. 26.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton had one of his best starts in years in Saturday's 5-2 victory over the Cubs at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed just two hits and eight hits and struck out eight in 7 1/3 innings. He hopes to keep the ball rolling against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg was dominating against the Dodgers last Saturday.  He pitched seven innings, allowed one run on five hits, and struck out nine batters without walking a batter. Strasburg, who is on an innings limit of 160 this season, threw 101 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick bounced back from a rough start to allow two earned runs in six innings in Sunday's 5-1 loss to the Cubs at Citizens Bank Park. He also tied a career high with seven strikeouts. Kendrick is pitching in place of Cliff Lee, who is injured.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez lost his pitch control in the sixth inning vs. L.A., walking three batters and allowing two to score on a James Loney single after cruising for the first five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Worley allowed five hits and one run, with two walks and five strikeouts in seven innings Monday against the Cubs. He is 13-4 with a 2.81 ERA in 26 starts since last season. He has allowed just two earned runs in his last 22 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann allowed four runs -- three earned -- in 6 1/3 innings Tuesday. In Zimmermann's five starts, the Nationals have averaged fewer than three runs per game. Zimmermann said he doesn't feel he has to be perfect every time he pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed six hits, two runs, two walks and struck out six in six innings Tuesday against the Braves. He hopes to go a little deeper in what could be an important game in the series finale against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay blew a six-run lead in Wednesday's 15-13 loss to the Braves. His teams are 110-9 when they spot him a four-run lead, but he couldn't hold it this time. He allowed 12 hits and eight earned runs in just six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros snapped Niese's streak of four consecutive quality starts to open the season last Tuesday, scoring five runs on him in three innings. Niese blanked the Phillies over 6 2/3 innings earlier this season.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed just three hits and struck out six in nine scoreless innings against Atlanta on Thursday. It was Blanton's first shutout since June 2, 2007. He said he hasn't felt this good since '07 in Oakland. He has been pitching like it.
away_pitcher_note: Unsatisfied with Chris Schwinden's work in the rotation, the Mets ask Batista to plug the hole that the injured Mike Pelfrey left in his wake. The Giants hung six runs in 3 2/3 innings on Batista in his only spot start this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is expected to make his return to the rotation after spending time on the disabled list since April 19 because of a strained left oblique. He said he felt fine after throwing a bullpen session Friday, so the Phillies hope he is good to go.
away_pitcher_note: Gee has posted a 3.46 ERA over his last two outings, and he has averaged more than 112 pitches per start while doing it. Gee will look to continue pitching deep into games against the Phillies, who hit .347 against him in two games last season.

home_pitcher_note: Worley is looking to rebound after a bad start Saturday in a 7-1 loss to the Nationals, when he allowed 11 hits, five runs, two walks, two home runs and struck out four in six innings. He has allowed one or fewer runs in four of his six starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Richard held the Marlins to one run in seven innings before allowing two runs in the eighth. Helped by his defense, Richard scattered nine hits, struck out a season-high seven and walked one. His only win came in his first start.

home_pitcher_note: Perhaps incredibly, the Phillies are winless in Halladay's last four starts. He has not won since April 16 in San Diego, carrying a 5.13 ERA in his past four starts. Halladay needs to get back on track against one of the worst teams in baseball.
away_pitcher_note: On regular rest, Volquez is pitching in place of the injured Joe Wieland on Saturday. In his last start, Volquez earned his first victory of the season, though he wasn't particularly sharp. He allowed two runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed just five hits, one run, one walk and struck out eight in a badly-needed victory over the Nationals on Sunday. Hamels also copped to intentionally hitting Bryce Harper with a pitch, escalating the rivalry between both teams.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan was solid in his last outing, allowing one run in the first inning before throwing four scoreless innings Tuesday against the Rockies. He's given up one run in 10 innings since filling in for the injured Cory Luebke.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton, who can be a free agent at the end of the season, has shown signs of turning himself around after going 1-3 with a 4.34 earned run average in his first four appearances. In his last three starts he's 2-1 with a 2.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell has lasted just 5 1/3 innings in his previous two starts but is 1-0 in that span. He got a no-decision last time out after holding the Marlins to six hits and two earned runs. The team is 2-5 in his seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is still looking for his first win of the season despite a 2.17 earned run average and a .192 opponent's batting average. The Phillies, 0-4 when he starts, have scored two or fewer runs in three of his four games.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Lyles' second start of the season. He was recalled and started on April 29 at Cincinnati, allowing three runs in 6.0 innings of work in a 6-5 loss to the Reds (had no decision). He was optioned back to Triple A after that game.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since being sidelined with the flu, Garza lasted five innings against the Brewers. That matched his shortest outing of the season. Garza had a tough time finding his rhythm because of the layoff.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick gets the spot start, replacing Vance Worley. Worley did not make the team's trip to Chicago on Tuesday and will miss Wednesday's start against the Cubs at Wrigley Field because of soreness in his elbow.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad cruised through five scoreless innings against the Brewers, then everything fell apart in the sixth. Again. He's had trouble with one inning in each of his starts and is winless in his last 18 starts, dating back to July.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay twirled seven innings of two-run ball, scattering seven hits with one walk and 10 strikeouts in Saturday's tough-luck loss to the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels hasn't lost a game since his first start of the season April 9 against the Marlins. In six starts since, he's 5-0 with a 1.93 ERA. In 42 innings he's walked nine and struck out 40. The Phillies are undefeated in those games.
away_pitcher_note: The righty wasn't pleased with his command in his last start, but still earned the win, allowing one run on six hits while walking four and striking out two. He has a 3.00 ERA over the first five innings of his starts and 10.29 ERA thereafter.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton just might be the best fifth starter in baseball the way he is throwing the ball. He is 3-0 with a 2.10 ERA in his past four starts, including his first shutout since 2007 when he threw one on May 3 in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: The power lefty is coming off his best start of the season, a complete-game gem against the Mariners. Lester walked one and struck out six, allowing one run. Lester is 2-0 with a 0.43 ERA in three career starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Lee can't catch a break. The Phillies scored a combined three runs in his first three starts and the bullpen blew leads in his last two, keeping him winless through five starts for the first time in his career. He's due for some better luck.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett was brilliant in his last start, firing seven shutout innings aginst the Mariners. He walked two and struck out nine. Beckett likes hitting in Philadelphia, where he has two career home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed three hits and one earned run in six innings Wednesday in a victory over the Cubs at Wrigley Field. He has a 2.12 ERA in his past three starts this season and a 2.96 ERA in 13 starts dating to last season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez leads the National League in strikeouts with 60 and will make his first start on the road against a divisional rival. In his most previous outing, Gonzalez allowed three runs in seven innings of a win over the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay picked up his first win since April 16 in Thursday's victory over the Cubs. He allowed seven hits, three runs and struck out four in seven innings. Halladay hopes Thursday was the beginning of some positive momentum for him.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann struggled in his most previous outing against the Pirates, allowing a season-high four runs and seven hits with six strikeout and one walk through six innings. The Nats have scored fewer than three runs in seven of his past eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cole Hamels continued his strong season with a win against the Red Sox on Friday night. The lefty allowed three runs on six hits, struck out nine and walked just one in his sixth consecutive victory.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson had one of his best outings in Friday's 2-1 loss to Baltimore. He allowed just the one run on five hits and one walk while striking out eight over eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook didn't pitch as poorly last time out as his line would suggest, as he was hurt by his defense. Still, he's now allowed at least three earned runs in three of his last four starts. He hadn't given up more than two in any of his first four.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton struggled in his shortest start of the season, allowing a career-high four home runs in just 4 1/3 innings in a loss to Boston. The defeat ended a four-game stretch in which Blanton went 3-0 with a 2.10 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The bullpen cost Lohse a win on Sunday, though the righty was also not his sharpest. He allowed 11 hits, a season high. Though Lohse has won just once in his last four starts, he has allowed more than three earned runs in only one of nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lee allowed nine hits and five runs in seven innings in his start Sunday against the Red Sox. Remarkably, Lee is winless this season after six starts, but that's mostly because of an uncooperative offense.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia was in line for the win on Monday before his bullpen lost the lead. The lefty has turned in two straight quality starts after allowing two runs in seven strong innings Monday. He has walked just three batters in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick has a 2.25 ERA in his last four starts, but he has nothing to show for it with an 0-2 mark. That has everything to do with the Phillies' offense, which hasn't given him much support. He hopes for more against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright had far and away his best outing of the season on Tuesday, tossing a shutout over the Padres. The right-hander scattered four hits and struck out nine, and afterward said he had never been more satisfied after an outing.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay had one of his worst starts of the year, allowing five runs over six innings on Tuesday to the Nats. Halladay's 3.63 ERA is the highest it's been this late in a season since he finished with a 3.71 ERA in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Niese looked like a different pitcher last time out against the Pirates, jumping ahead of batters and allowing one run in 7 2/3 innings. He's 1-0 with a 1.54 ERA in two starts against the Phillies in 2012, with both of those outings coming in Philly.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels pitched splendidly in a game the Phillies desperately needed to win Wednesday against Washington. He allowed four hits, three walks and struck out six in eight scoreless innings. Seems like an All-Star lock.

home_pitcher_note: A rainy night doomed Hefner, as the Padres touched the rookie for six earned runs in 3 2/3 innings. Although Terry Collins initially put Hefner's next turn in jeopardy, it appears the righty will get a chance to redeem himself.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is coming off two of the worst performances of his career. He gave up seven runs on 10 hits in 4 1/3 innings against St. Louis on Thursday. He gave up a career-high four home runs to Boston on May 19.

home_pitcher_note: Gee registered a career-high nine strikeouts in his last outing, and he's won back-to-back starts for the first time this season. The right-hander is 2-1 with a 7.50 ERA in five career starts against the Phillies, three of which occurred last season.
away_pitcher_note: Despite still being winless on the year, Lee also has the second-best ERA (2.82) of all Phillies starters. Lee went seven innings against the Cards in his last start, allowing three runs on eight hits while fanning seven.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick is coming off statistically the best performance of his career. Kendrick tossed the first shutout and second complete game of his career in his last start. He gave up seven hits to the Cards and didn't walk a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle turned in a vintage performance against the Giants, tossing 7 1/3 innings of two-run ball. He was efficient early, throwing 56 pitches through five innings, and flashed his Gold Glove-caliber defense late as he improved to 4-0 in May.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels became the first pitcher in the big leagues to win eight games Monday in a victory over New York. He looks Cy Young worthy. The Phillies will lean on him even more now that Roy Halladay is on the DL with a strained right lat.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco was solid through seven innings against the Giants. He pitched well enough to keep Miami in the game, but unfortunately he ran into hot-hitting Melky Cabrera. Nolasco gave up three runs on five hits (four off Cabrera's bat) to take the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton started the season 4-2 with a 2.81 ERA in his first seven starts, but things have taken a turn for the worse. He is 0-2 with a 12.51 ERA in his last three starts, which comes at a bad time with Roy Halladay on the DL.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano showed his arm is fine after a solid six-plus-inning start against the Nationals. He came out on the winning end after seeing his velocity dip in a May 23 loss to the Rockies. Zambrano struck out five vs. Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Vance Worley will come off the disabled list at just the right time. Worley slips into Roy Halladay's spot in the rotation on Monday for his first start since going on the DL with right elbow inflammation on May 12.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw is coming off back-to-back losses, the most recent of which he tied a season high by giving up five runs. The southpaw is 0-4 with a 5.18 ERA in his career vs. the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is still in search of his first win of 2012. This is by far the longest into a season Lee has gone winless. Maybe June will be kinder to him than the first two months. It was last season, when he went 5-0 with a 0.21 ERA for the month.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley, who is looking to end a nine-start winless stretch, allowed four runs over six innings of a loss to the Brewers last time out. He struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick kept the Phillies in the game in his last outing, coming back to pitch after a 48-minute rain delay in the fifth. He continues to give the club a chance to win, as he has not surrendered more than two runs in any of his starts.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano let his frustration at not having his best control snowball vs. the Rox Friday. He gave up seven hits and four walks, allowing four earned runs and three more on four errors. He grinded it out but made a costly miscue failing to cover first.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels had arguably his worst start of the season his last time out, giving up two home runs to Miami's Hanley Ramirez in a 5-4 loss. The loss snapped a personal eight-game winning streak for Hamels. The lefty will look for a bounce-back performance.
away_pitcher_note: Harang ended L.A.'s five-game skid with a dominant outing Saturday, holding the Rockies to one run on four hits and three walks over six innings.  His fastball command was excellent, and his curve was effective in keeping hitters off balance.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta is fighting for his rotation spot, having gone 0-5 with a 7.96 ERA in his past six starts. The 26-year-old Opening Day starter lasted 4 2/3 innings against the Rays on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: After starting the season with a 4-2 record and a 2.81 ERA in his first seven starts, the right-hander has struggled. In his past four starts, he owns a 10.98 ERA and has allowed 10 home runs. He need to pick it up with Roy Halladay on the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter was optioned to Triple-A Norfolk on May 29, but he is returning Saturday to fill out the rotation. He has struggled to keep his fastball down in 2012, giving up six runs (five earned) in three innings during his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Worley, off a three-week stay on the DL with right elbow inflammation and a bone chip, started Monday and was held to 80 pitches over four innings. He looked a little rusty, allowing three runs on five hits with three walks and four strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel tied his season-low with five innings, although the defense behind him didn't help much. The 29-year-old allowed two runs (one earned) to Boston on Tuesday night.
away_pitcher_note: Since the National League started to track earned runs in 1912, no Phillies pitcher has been winless with a 3.00 ERA or better after his first nine starts in a season until Lee this season. He hopes that streak ends in Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn, making his first start since May 16 after spending more than two weeks on the DL with a strained left quad, allowed two runs on five hits over five innings against the Royals on Wednesday, arguably his best start of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed four hits, five runs, five walks and struck out six in 5 2/3 innings in Wednesday's loss to the Dodgers. He snapped a streak of six consecutive starts of allowing two earned runs or fewer, so he hopes to bounce back vs. the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Walters had trouble keeping the ball in the park against the Cubs on Friday, as he served up two homers. He allowed five runs on eight hits and a walk over five innings and was stuck with the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: It has not been a good stretch for Hamels, who has a 5.23 ERA in his previous three starts. To make matters worse, he blew three-run leads in losses to Miami on June 2 and to Los Angeles on Thursday. The Phillies need better with the team struggling.

home_pitcher_note: Diamond continued his impressive run, as he held the Cubs scoreless over six innings on Saturday to pick up his staff-leading fifth win. The lefty scattered seven hits and struck out five.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed seven hits, five runs, one walk, one home run and struck out seven in 6 2/3 innings on Friday against Baltimore. It was his best start in his last five in which he has a combined 9.91 ERA (29 earned runs in 26 1/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Hutchison pitched well Saturday against the Braves aside from giving up a pair of home runs. He has shown good command since coming up from the minor leagues in late-April. He has 48 strikeouts and 19 walks in his first 58 innings with the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Worley continues to make his way back from an elbow injury. He allowed five hits and one earned run in six innings in a 6-4 loss in 12 innings to Baltimore on Saturday. He threw 93 pitches, so he should be able to go a little further this time.

home_pitcher_note: Romero has given up four runs in three straight starts and is coming off his shortest outing of the season Sunday. Romero has pitched much better at Rogers Centre. In almost exactly as many innings, his ERA is more than a run lower at home.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies scored just 16 runs while Lee was pitching in his first nine starts this season, but he couldn't use a lack of run support as an excuse on Sunday in Baltimore. He blew a 4-1 lead to keep him winless entering the middle of June.

home_pitcher_note: Cecil is set to make his season debut after a successful run in Double-A. With New Hampshire, Cecil went 3-2 with a 3.32 ERA in nine starts. He is taking the spot of Brandon Morrow, who is on the 15-day DL with a strained left oblique muscle.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick suffered through a bad start on Tuesday in Minnesota, allowing eight hits, six runs, two walks and two home runs against the Twins. With Roy Halladay on the disabled list, the Phillies will need better efforts from Kendrick.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has blown two three-run leads and nearly blew a six-run lead in his last three starts, including Wednesday's 9-8 victory over the Twins at Target Field. Hamels has a 6.08 ERA in his last four starts, so he is hoping for a rebound.
away_pitcher_note: Outman was in position to win his last start, when he battled through his team's sloppy defense and gave up five runs and six hits in five innings of the Rockies' eventual 10-8 loss to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton's 9.91 ERA from May 19-June 13 was the worst in baseball, but he pitched his second complete game of the season on Thursday in a 6-1 victory over the Twins at Target Field. He hopes to build off that success against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: White developed a finger blister early in his last start and was pulled after giving up four runs, two earned, and seven hits in four innings of an 8-2 home loss to the Athletics. White said he is fine. He'll have to trim walks (five the last game).

home_pitcher_note: Worley was a hard-luck loser his last time out, getting no runs of support over seven innings. The 24-year-old dropped to 3-3 on the year but lowered his ERA to 2.80 -- tops in the rotation. This will be his first career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: After being rocked for 10 hits and eight runs in his Rockies season debut, Francis gutted out five innings and gave up four runs Friday night in Detroit. He did not get a decision, but the game ended a losing streak at eight.

home_pitcher_note: Lee's winless streak extended to 11 games after surrendering a season-high 12 hits to Toronto in his last start. Despite a solid 3.24 ERA, the lefty has an 0-3 record. Lee gets the Rays next, whom he hasn't faced since the 2010 playoffs.

Kendrick has lost three consecutive starts, surrendering at least five runs in each outing. The 27-year-old fell to 2-7 with a 5.29 ERA after losing his last game to the Blue Jays. He will face a Rays team that he has never met before.
away_pitcher_note: Shields gave up three unearned runs on eight hits in 7 2/3 innings, striking out five. He didn't factor into the decision in a 15-inning game with the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, a win against the Rockies, Hamels gave up a run in the first inning but settled down and put together a very good start. He allowed six hits, two runs, three walks and struck out seven in eight innings, earning the win.
away_pitcher_note: Price chalked up his eighth quality start of the season Tuesday in Washington when he held the Nationals to three earned runs on seven hits to earn his ninth win of the season. Price is 0-1 with a 10.38 ERA in one career start against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Lee takes the mound yet again looking for his first win of 2012. The left-hander was supposed to start on Friday before the rainout. He warmed up on Friday, so the club decided to push his start back to Sunday evening to give him more recovery time.
away_pitcher_note: Ramos gets a spot start in the second leg of a doubleheader. It will be his 10th appearance of the season and first start. He last pitched on June 14.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton has allowed a troubling 16 home runs in 41 1/3 innings over his last eight starts. He also has allowed five or more earned runs in six of his last seven starts to give him a 7.44 ERA in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens makes his long-awaited return, from mostly shoulder inflammation and more recently a hip-flexor tweak. This will be his first start since April 17, when he departed after one inning with the shoulder issue.

home_pitcher_note: Worley allowed four hits, two runs, two walks, one home run and struck out two in seven innings Thursday against Colorado. He has a 2.78 ERA this season and a 2.25 ERA in four starts since returning from the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard stopped a three-start slide (14 runs in 14 innings) by hurling four-hit ball for six innings his last time out, but now needs to halt a road skid. He's allowed 16 runs in his last three away starts, covering 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Valdes will start Wednesday's game against the Pirates. It's a bullpen game after the Phillies used Cole Hamels and Cliff Lee in a doubleheader Sunday against the Tampa Bay Rays. It's Valdes' second big league start.
away_pitcher_note: The night the Miami Heat won the NBA title, McDonald was baseball's King James, hurling his first career complete game. He hasn't allowed more than three runs in any of his 14 starts, recording the National League's fourth-lowest ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has really struggled in his past four starts, carrying an 8.10 ERA in that span. To make matters worse, he has lasted just four innings twice and has pitched six innings just once. He's hoping for better Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett goes for his eighth consecutive winning start, which would match the run Dock Ellis had for the 1974 Pirates. Though comfortable at PNC Park, Burnett has had issues on the road, giving up five homers in 26 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Despite not earning a decision, Johnson was brilliant against Toronto, giving up just one run and two hits, both singles, over seven innings. He held the Blue Jays hitless through four, struck out seven and retired the final nine batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Lee has a 5.10 ERA in his last seven starts. He has blown four leads in that span: two three-run leads, one two-run lead and one one-run lead. He has allowed five earned runs in each of his last two starts. The Phillies hope for better Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle became the all-time leader for wins in Interleague Play with a solid outing against Toronto. He threw seven shutout innings, scattering seven hits and striking out seven while Miami's bats came to life and the Marlins snapped a six-game skid.
away_pitcher_note: He struggled for a stretch recently, but is 10-3 with a 3.03 ERA. He threw seven scoreless innings Sunday in a loss to the Tampa Bay Rays, when the bullpen could not hold a one-run lead.

home_pitcher_note: While he didn't dominate, Nolasco was solid against the Cardinals in his last outing. The righty held St. Louis to just one unearned run on four hits over 6 2/3 innings. Nolasco did not earn a win as Miami's 'pen blew a four-run lead in the ninth.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton has struggled lately, but he allowed seven hits, two earned runs, two walks, one home run and struck out eight in seven innings Monday against the Pirates. He has allowed 17 home runs in 48 1/3 innings over a span of eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Niese appeared to flip a switch in June, going 3-1 with a 1.89 ERA after posting a 1-2 record and 6.07 ERA in May. The lefty's first July start will come vs. the Phillies, who are batting .183 against him in three starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Worley is 1-2 with a 2.70 ERA in five starts since returning from the disabled list because of inflammation in his right elbow. He allowed three runs in six innings in Tuesday's victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: With each passing start, Young feels he is regaining the arm strength and sharpness that right shoulder surgery robbed of him last summer. He certainly showed it Thursday in L.A., striking out six and walking none over 6 1/3 innings of two-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has allowed five or more earned runs in three consecutive starts, carrying an 8.64 ERA in that span. He has a 5.68 ERA in his last eight starts, blowing two three-run leads, one two-run lead and one one-run lead.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey made six June starts, going 5-0 with a 0.93 ERA, three complete games and two shutouts. Just as remarkably, he allowed 21 hits in 48 1/3 innings, striking out 55 and walking eight. His first July start will come at Citi Field, where he is 6-0.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels will make his first start since being named an All-Star again. He earned a no-decision in his only start against the Braves this season, allowing two runs in six innings. The left-hander has given up three runs or fewer in 13 of his 16 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed five runs within the first six batters he faced in Thursday's 5-4 loss to the Pirates. He retired 19 of the final 23 batters he faced, but the damage was done. He has a 7.67 ERA in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson is coming off a poor start Sunday vs. the Nats, when he allowed six runs in six innings. Four of the runs came in the first when he struggled with his command. Hudson uses a good sinker to get plenty of grounders from opposing hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton allowed just three runs over six innings in his last start against the Marlins, but took the loss to even his record. In his lone start this year against the Braves, he pitched a complete game three-hit shutout with six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson has allowed at least one homer in each of his last three starts and has yielded six in his last 18 1/3 frames. Aside from that, however, Hanson has pitched well during that stretched, yielding just four walks while fanning 18.

home_pitcher_note: Worley suffered one of the worst starts of his short career Tuesday vs. the Mets. He allowed 10 hits, six runs and one walk in four innings. He had not allowed six runs in a start since Aug. 10, 2011, when he allowed six in four innings in L.A.
away_pitcher_note: In three starts since returning from Triple-A, Jurrjens has a 1.47 ERA. He is not fanning many batters (six in 18 1/3) and is mostly throwing his fastball 88-89 mph. But he has improved his command and has walked just four batters in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Friedrich, a rookie, was in a 1-0 game with the Cardinals in his last pre-break start when he lost his delivery, gave up a walk to the pitcher and saw the game spin out of control. He has been learning.
away_pitcher_note: Lee downplayed its importance to reporters, but he picked up his first win of the season in his 14th start of 2012 on July 4 against the Mets at Citi Field. Lee is hoping for a much better second half than first half, which was a big disappointment.

home_pitcher_note: In each of his two starts since rejoining the rotation, Guthrie has allowed just two runs on six hits over six innings. His last start was on Sunday, the last game before the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Worley missed some time in the first half because of an elbow injury, but he ended up being one of the Phillies' most consistent starters. They really need him to pitch well if they have any chance at a Wild Card.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz held the Nationals scoreless on one hit in 6 1/3 innings in his last start while earning his first win. He has held opponents to one unearned run in two starts since being recalled from Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Could this be one of Hamels' last starts for the Phillies? They could trade him before the July 31 Trade Deadline if the Phillies decide to be sellers. That's a definite possibility with the way they played in the first half.

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi deserved better than 1-5 at the break, considering the Dodgers' offense scored four runs total in his five losses. He's coming off his first win, allowing one run to Arizona in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton gave up five earned in 6 1/3 in a loss to the Braves. The righty has allowed a home run in 11 straight games, but is facing a Dodgers team that is tied for last place in the National League with 52 homers.

home_pitcher_note: Fife makes his Major League debut. He's gone 7-5 with a 4.53 ERA in 18 starts with Triple-A Albuquerque this season.
away_pitcher_note: All eyes will be on Halladay, who is expected to make his first start since May 27 (right lat strain). The two-time Cy Young winner will operate under a closely-held pitch count. Halladay is 3-1 with a 2.15 ERA in his career at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: After throwing 27 pitches in the All-Star Game, Kershaw saw his pitch count rise quickly in his first start after the break. He made it through only six, but he picked up the victory by allowing only one earned run on six hits.
away_pitcher_note: Even in notching his 10th quality start, Lee wasn't able to improve on his win count Friday vs. the Rockies. He gave up nine hits, but yielded two earned in six innings while striking out four. Lee held the Dodgers to two runs in their last meeting.

home_pitcher_note: Worley went 6 2/3 innings while beating the Rockies in his last start, scattering eight hits and striking out two. It was his seventh quality start in the last eight outings. Worley also hit a two-run double.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum resembled his two-time Cy Young self in his last outing, shutting down the Astros for eight scoreless innings at AT&T Park. He'll be tested on the road, where he is 1-6 with a 9.00 ERA compared to 2-4 with a 3.43 ERA at home.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels pitched a gem Sunday in Colorado, with a bunch of scouts on hand. He could be traded before the July 31 Trade Deadline, so the baseball world is watching and waiting to see if the Phillies will sign him to an extension or deal him.
away_pitcher_note: The winning pitcher of the 2012 All-Star Game started the second half by allowing two runs (one earned) in 6 1/3 innings against the Astros. Cain is 1-2 with a 3.75 ERA in three career starts at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton threw well in Monday's 3-2 win over the Dodgers in L.A. He allowed six hits, two runs and struck out seven in eight innings. It was the first time since May 8 he had not allowed a home run. The Phillies need more of that against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Last Tuesday at Atlanta marked the fourth time this season that Zito had pitched at least seven shutout innings. That doubles the total number of such games he had over the previous two seasons combined.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay rejoined the rotation after spending nearly two months on the DL because of a strained right lat. He allowed five hits, two runs and struck out six in five innings Tuesday vs. the Dodgers in L.A. He hopes to build on that Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf beat the Cardinals on Tuesday for his first win since April 30, a "nightmare" stretch, Wolf said. He's 11-4 with a 3.42 ERA in 23 career starts against the Reds, but has yet to face them this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lee allowed two hits, one run, one walk and struck out four in eight innings in a loss to L.A. on Wednesday. He pounded the strike zone with nearly flawless command of his pitches, throwing just 89 pitches. He has a 2.05 ERA in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Brewers skipped Greinke's last start so he could recharge his batteries, to borrow GM Doug Melvin's characterization. He has a 9.00 ERA in July and is coming off a stretch in which he started three straight Brewers games.

home_pitcher_note: Worley had a Jekyll and Hyde night Friday in a loss to San Francisco. He retired 13 of the first 14 batters he faced, striking out seven, before allowing eight of the final 13 batters to reach. He allowed six runs in six innings in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada remains winless despite pitching reasonably well since coming off the DL in late June. He has not surrendered more than three runs in any of his four starts since then, and has 45 strikeouts in 24 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets has tossed six scoreless innings in both of the the starts he has made since missing two years while recovering from elbow surgery. His fastball has rested between 90-91 mph, and he still has his effective curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels, who received a a six-year, $144 million contract extension on Wednesday, is 11-6 with a 3.69 ERA in his career against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Minor has turned his season around while posting a 2.33 ERA and limiting opponents to a .182 batting average in his past three starts. He has been more successful pounding hitters inside with his fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is 1-0 with a 2.81 ERA in his last two starts. He has gone eight innings in both starts, which has been welcomed, considering the Phillies have had a shaky bullpen this season. He has walked just 17 in 126 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson has overcome the left ankle discomfort that plagued him earlier this year.  He limited the Phillies to four hits in seven scoreless innings on July 6 and has lasted at least seven inning in his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: He allowed six runs in six innings against the Brewers on Monday. Halladay has a 4.32 ERA this season. He has two more months to pitch, but he has not finished a season with an ERA higher than 3.71 since he had a 4.20 ERA in 2004.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg dominated the Mets on Wednesday, striking out 11 and making only one mistake that turned into a solo homer. The righty allowed four hits and walked none in seven innings, and he has struck out 11.6 batters per nine innings in 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Lee allowed 12 hits, six runs, one walk, four home runs and six strikeouts in seven innings during a comeback victory over the Brewers. He has a 5.10 ERA in his past seven starts, although his three previous before the Brewers game were good.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson threw seven scoreless innings on Thursday night against the Brewers. Known for being "effectively wild," he has only 35 walks in 19 starts this year. Jackson allowed three runs in seven innings against the Phils on May 23 but took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Worley is looking to find some consistency. He is 1-2 with a 6.43 ERA in his last five starts, with opponents hitting .353 with a .954 on-base-plus-slugging percentage against him. The Phillies need to see more from Worley down the stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Detwiler cruised early but struggled with two outs in the fourth and fifth as he took his first loss since May 19 on Friday against the Brewers. The lefty gave up four runs before getting a quick hook after 83 pitches and 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels suffered one of the worst starts of his career Friday in Atlanta, based solely on his lack of command. He walked a career-high six batters and threw more balls (56) than strikes (53) for the first time when throwing 100 more pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Joe Blanton was originally slated to pitch, but he was traded to the Dodgers, so Kendrick makes his first start since July 6.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy appears to be finally hitting his stride. He is 3-0 with a 2.42 ERA in his last three starts. Last time out against the Mets, Kennedy allowed three runs, all of which came on solo homers by Ike Davis.

home_pitcher_note: In his third start back after a seven-week stint on the DL, Halladay struggled early against Atlanta. Doc allowed three runs on six hits -- two home runs -- over seven innings. A positive sign is that he set down the last 10 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is an innings-eater who has lasted at least six innings in his last seven starts. In four starts since coming off the disabled list, Saunders has a 4.15 ERA. This will be Saunders' first appearance against the Phillies this year.

home_pitcher_note: Lee looked like his old self in his last outing, shutting out the Nationals over seven innings on Tuesday to earn just his second win. The former Cy Young Award winner allowed just five hits, struck out seven and walked only one.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill has struggled to find consistency this year. He pitched well in his last start, as he allowed just one run on six hits over six innings against the Dodgers. He allowed four runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Phillies on April 25.

home_pitcher_note: Worley will be trying to build off his previous start vs. the Nats, when he went seven innings for the first time since June 26. Pitching with bone chips in his elbow that will be removed after the season, his ERA in his past seven starts is 5.05.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets has been a revelation for the Braves, compiling a 1.45 ERA in his first four starts after being out of baseball for more than a year. On Wednesday, Sheets pitched into the seventh for the first time since undergoing Tommy John surgery in 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels will be looking to get back on a roll. The Phillies have won just one of his past seven starts. He's 1-3 with a 3.51 ERA in those games. In his past two starts, he's 0-2, but the team has also scored one run or fewer twice during that span.
away_pitcher_note: Minor led all National League pitchers in opponents' batting average (.172) and opponents' on-base percentage in July. He opened August by tossing 3 2/3 scoreless innings in a rain-shortened start against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick went back into the rotation after Joe Blanton was traded, but it remains uncertain how long he'll stay there. In 14 starts this season, he has a 4.54 ERA and a .285 opponent's batting average.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson won his 100th game with Atlanta on Friday, throwing a season-high 116 pitches while allowing four hits and an unearned run over 7 1/3 frames vs. Houston. He has won his past five decisions and has a career record of 192-101.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay is coming off one of his best starts of the season. He shut out the D-backs on Saturday, allowing just three hits over seven innings. It was a positive sign for Doc, who hadn't won since coming off his right lat injury.
away_pitcher_note: Owner of the league's top winning percentage, Lohse continues to lead the rotation. Even when he isn't sharp, he finds ways to keep his team close. Lohse has made 17 quality starts and 11 of his last 12 fall in that category.

home_pitcher_note: It's hard to believe Lee has only two wins in mid-August, but here we are. Lee takes the mound against the Cards in search of win No. 3. In his last outing, a no-decision against the D-backs, he lasted eight innings, but gave up three home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook has won each of his last four starts, putting him within one win of his 2011 total. Westbrook will come into the start plenty fresh, having thrown just 79 pitches Monday. Westbrook's start incurred an early end because of a pinch-hit need.

home_pitcher_note: Worley's stomach started bothering him just before his last start, in which he struggled and lasted only 3 2/3 innings in a loss to the Braves. He will look to bounce back against St. Louis and even his record on the season.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn's last nine starts have had a streak of inconsistency, as he's either been dominant or subpar. There has been little middle ground. Getting through the first inning is key for Lynn, too. Of the 53 runs he's allowed, 18 have scored in the first.

home_pitcher_note: It wasn't a clean shutout performance, but Eovaldi will take it. In his last start, he threw five-plus scoreless innings in New York, but he walked six. He lost to the Phillies on July 16, giving up three runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels pitched his first shutout of 2012 and fifth of his career in his last start against the Braves. The left-hander allowed just five hits, struck out six and did not issue a walk in a dominant performance.

home_pitcher_note: In his last four starts, Johnson is 2-1 with a 1.75 ERA, giving up five runs in 25 2/3 innings. He's struck out 26 over that span, but is coming off a loss vs. the Mets. JJ beat the Phillies on June 29, giving up one run in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick struggled Wednesday in a loss to the Braves at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed seven hits, six runs, three walks and one home run in just 3 1/3 innings. Kendrick is in the rotation after the Phillies traded Joe Blanton to the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: The big inning cost Buehrle as he continued his quest for win No. 10. Buehrle, who has at least 10 wins in each of the last 11 years, gave up four runs in the sixth as Miami fell to the Dodgers. In his last five starts, he is 0-3 with a 6.84 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay is coming off consecutive wins for the first time since his first two starts of the season. Doc has pitched great in his last two outings, allowing just two hits and one run in a win against the Cardinals on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada remained winless in his 20th appearance and 14th start at Houston on Saturday, allowing four runs and seven hits in four innings. He allowed five runs in four innings of a loss to the Phillies on July 25.
away_pitcher_note: Save a couple mistakes, Lee pitched well enough for his team to win in his start against the Cardinals on Saturday. Lee remains winless at home this season, so maybe the road will be kinder to him on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo has pitched at least seven innings in three straight starts, all Brewers victories. He has met the definition of a "quality start" in 19 of his 24 outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Worley lasted only 5 1/3 frames in his last outing, a no-decision vs. the Cards. In 12 starts since coming off the DL on June 4, the righty, who is pitching through bone chips in his elbow, is 3-5. He's 4-3 with a 2.59 ERA in nine road starts in '12.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers is coming off a Coors Field nightmare in which he surrendered more earned runs in two-plus innings -- eight -- than he had allowed in his previous 62 innings of work, spanning nine starts and one appearance in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels threw a shutout Monday in Miami. He became just the third Phillies pitcher in the last 20 seasons to throw consecutive shutouts. He joined Cliff Lee, who threw three straight last season, and Cory Lidle, who threw two straight in 2004.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf has lost three of his last four decisions and has one win since April after allowing six earned runs in five innings on Tuesday. He gave up at least four runs and nine hits in each of the three most recent losses.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick rebounded from a poor start Aug. 8 against Atlanta -- it seemed like he could be moved to the bullpen as a result -- to throw seven scoreless innings Tuesday against the Marlins at Marlins Park. He allowed five hits and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay is 2-2 with a 2.25 ERA in his last four starts, showing much improvement from earlier this season when he was injured. He allowed six hits, three runs, one walk, one home run and struck out seven in seven frames Wednesday in a loss to Miami.
away_pitcher_note: Leake is coming off of his best outing of the season vs. the Mets, as he went the distance for the second time in his career, and 2012. He threw first-pitch strikes to 21 of 30 batters, and retired 17 of the final 19.

home_pitcher_note: He had 12 strikeouts and allowed no walks and three home runs Thursday in a 7-4 loss against the Brewers. Lee was just the fourth pitcher since 1900 to have a 12-strikeout, zero-walk, three-home run game.
away_pitcher_note: During a span of five starts in July, Bailey was 4-0 with a 1.43 ERA and a 3.53 ERA overall. In four starts since July 31, he's 1-2 with an 8.24 ERA while allowing 35 hits. Bailey is at his career-high in innings and starts in the Majors.

home_pitcher_note: Worley, who is pitching with a bone chip in his right elbow, has not lasted more than 5 1/3 innings in four of his last five starts. He also has a 5.35 ERA in seven starts since the All-Star break, and is hoping for improvement against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo threw 109 pitches and lasted 6 1/3 innings vs. the Cubs Friday, but had one inning extended by a two-out error and another by a defensive play not turned. He already has nine wins, which ties his total for all of 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed eight hits, three runs, one walk and struck out 10 in 7 2/3 innings in Saturday's win over Milwaukee. In a season without clear-cut favorites, Hamels could make a push for the NL Cy Young Award if he pitches well the rest of the way.
