home_pitcher_note: Scheppers was 6-2 with a 1.88 ERA in 76 relief appearances last season before winning a spot in the rotation in Spring Training. He is the first pitcher since Fernando Valenzuela in 1981 to make his first MLB start on Opening Day.
away_pitcher_note: With Cole Hamels unavailable, Lee gets the ball on Opening Day against his former club. Lee had a strong Spring Training, posting a 2.55 ERA in six starts. Manager Ryne Sandberg said it was an "easy call" to go with Lee.

home_pitcher_note: Perez was 10-6 with a 3.62 ERA in 20 starts for the Rangers last season. He was also the losing pitcher in the AL Wild Card tiebreaker. He had a 6.23 ERA over four starts in the Cactus League. Opponents hit .234 off him.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett got a late start to spring after joining the team in February, but he showed improvement in each Grapefruit League outing. The right-hander has a career 3.94 ERA against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Ross has been a reliever for the past two years, but he won a spot in the rotation by going 1-0 with a 1.27 ERA in five Spring Training games. A second-round pick in 2008, Ross was a starter for three years in the Minors.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick hopes to return to form after struggling terribly the final few months of last season because of a right shoulder issue. He has been healthy this spring and hopes to carry those good feelings into the season.

home_pitcher_note: Wood's goal is to reach 200 innings, which he did for the first time last year. The lefty has a career 2.11 ERA in three starts against the Phillies, one reason he was inserted in the No. 4 spot. Also, it's a chance to let him start the home opener.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies signed Hernandez with the hopes he can enjoy more success leaving the American League for the more pitcher-friendly National League. Results were mixed in Spring Training, but the Phillies hope he can just be consistent.

home_pitcher_note: Samardzija got a no-decision in his Opening Day start despite throwing seven scoreless vs. the Bucs. His goal this year is to be more efficient with his pitches, and he did that, throwing 89. It may mean fewer strikeouts, but results in more frames.
away_pitcher_note: Lee certainly hopes to rebound in a big way from Monday's effort on Opening Day in Texas. He allowed 11 hits, eight runs, one walk and struck out just one in five innings, uncharacteristic for one of the game's top lefties.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva made his season debut in the 10th inning on Opening Day and served up a walk-off homer to the Bucs' Neil Walker. Not exactly how he wanted to begin the year. This will be his first start of the season. Last year, he was 1-7 in 15 starts.
away_pitcher_note: He made his Phillies debut Tuesday in Texas, allowing seven hits and one run, with two walks and three strikeouts in six innings. He hopes to build on that as the Phillies play without injured lefty Cole Hamels.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick pitched splendidly Wednesday in Texas, but the bullpen could not preserve the victory. He allowed five hits, one run, one walk and struck out four in seven innings for a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse owns a lifetime 2.98 ERA against the Phillies and a respectable 3.26 ERA at Citizens Bank Park, where he briefly pitched for the home team in 2007. He's coming off an eight strikeout performance against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick pitched splendidly Wednesday in Texas, but the bullpen could not preserve the victory. He allowed five hits, one run, one walk and struck out four in seven innings for a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse owns a lifetime 2.98 ERA against the Phillies and a respectable 3.26 ERA at Citizens Bank Park, where he briefly pitched for the home team in 2007. He's coming off an eight strikeout performance against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez threw well in frigid conditions in his Phillies debut Friday at Wrigley Field. He allowed three hits, two runs, one walk and struck out five in 5 1/3 innings, leaving with a lead as Phillies went to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Garza took a no-hitter into the seventh inning of his Brewers debut, but he lost to the Braves on one pitch -- a fastball that Chris Johnson hit into the Milwaukee bullpen. Garza needed only 90 pitches to get through the eighth.

home_pitcher_note: Lee bounced back from a rough start Opening Day with a strong showing Saturday at Wrigley Field. He allowed 10 hits and struck out six in seven scoreless innings to lead the way in a 2-0 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada worked 5 2/3 effective innings against Boston, but he needed 102 pitches, partly because Mike Napoli worked two 10-pitch walks. Estrada walked three in all, a total he reached only four times in 21 starts last season.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett hopes to recover from a rough start Sunday in Chicago, where he allowed five hits, eight runs (four earned) and six walks with three strikeouts. It will be his first home start since signing with the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: The innings leash is longer for Fernandez after he was limited as a rookie last year. He threw 108 pitches (one shy of a personal high) in 6 2/3 innings in beating the Padres. Fernandez has allowed one earned run in 12 2/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Pettibone is going to be the Phillies' temporary fifth starter until Cole Hamels rejoins the rotation as early as April 22. Pettibone made 18 starts last season, going 5-4 with a 4.04 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi is getting swings and misses and upping his strikeout totals. In 13 innings, he has 14 K's and has shown overpowering stuff. He had a shutout going into the seventh in his last start, a loss to San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Brewers slugger Ryan Braun roughed up Kendrick on Tuesday, hitting two of his home runs against him at Citizens Bank Park. Kendrick allowed nine hits, six runs (four earned) and two walks and struck out two in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: It's been a hard-luck start for Alvarez, who comes off a tough loss to open the road trip at Washington. In 5 2/3 innings, he allowed three runs (one earned) and struck out four. His fastball was effective at 94 mph.

home_pitcher_note: He allowed seven hits, four runs, one walk and one home run Wednesday in a loss to Milwaukee. He struck out nine Brewers, picking up eight with his changeup. The nine strikeouts were the second most of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Santana gave up only three hits in eight scoreless innings during his Braves debut, a 4-3 win against the Mets on Wednesday. His first 20 pitches against New York were strikes, setting a Major League record.

home_pitcher_note: Lee allowed eight hits, three runs and struck out eight in six innings Thursday against the Brewers. Lee didn't get the run support he needed, and therefore had to take an early exit as the Phillies needed a pinch-hitter.
away_pitcher_note: Hale struggled to command his sinker as he allowed four earned runs and lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Mets on Thursday. His sinker could prove to be a valuable weapon in the offensive-friendly Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lee allowed eight hits, three runs and struck out eight in six innings Thursday against the Brewers. Lee didn't get the run support he needed, and therefore had to take an early exit as the Phillies needed a pinch-hitter.
away_pitcher_note: Despite struggling to get a feel for his slider, Teheran has notched three straight quality starts to open 2014. Teheran owns a 5.79 ERA against the Phillies in four career outings that include three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett learned Monday he has an inguinal hernia, but he said he plans to pitch with the injury the remainder of the season. He has walked 14 in 16 innings so far, which is a ratio that must improve.
away_pitcher_note: Wood has eclipsed the 100-pitch mark in back-to-back starts but managed to give up only three earned runs in 12 innings between the two outings. He has surrendered leadoff homers in the first inning of two of his three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chatwood came off the disabled list (strained left hamstring) and gave up four runs in six innings against the Giants in his first 2014 start. He was efficient, throwing 74 pitches, and was removed in an offensive substitution.
away_pitcher_note: Pettibone, who opened the season with Triple-A Lehigh Valley, made his 2014 debut Saturday in a victory over the Marlins, allowing two runs (one earned run) on eight hits and one walk while striking out five in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles took a 4-0 lead into the fifth inning against the Padres on Monday, but gave up four hits -- including two doubles and a triple -- to see the lead diminish to one run in a game the Rockies lost. But he had a good strike zone performance.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed three runs (two earned runs) on six hits and three walks while striking out seven in six innings Sunday against the Marlins. He threw 115 pitches, the most he had thrown since Aug. 24, 2012.

home_pitcher_note: Nicasio threw 31 pitches and gave up two runs in the first inning against the Padres in his last start, but he allowed only two hits from the second through the sixth, finishing with 99 pitches and earning the win.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez kept the game close Monday against the Braves at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed four hits, two runs, six walks and struck out three in six innings. A two-run homer to Evan Gattis forced him to leave in the hole.

home_pitcher_note: From his years with the Pirates, Maholm is successfully familiar with the Phillies, going 5-3 against them lifetime. He's coming off a quality start in San Francisco and pitching on a normal five-day cycle.
away_pitcher_note: Lee would like more run support after suffering the loss despite allowing one run and striking out 13 in a complete-game Wednesday against the Braves. He is the only pitcher in baseball history to lose two games like that.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu fired seven scoreless innings in San Francisco. The guy doesn't know what a slump is, having never gone more than two consecutive starts without a quality start.
away_pitcher_note: To compensate for pitching with an inguinal hernia, Burnett shortened his stride by about six inches. He responded with seven shutout innings, scattering three singles and walking two while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: He's giving up more solo homers than last year, but Greinke also is on a run of 16 straight starts of at least five innings allowing no more than two runs. He's 10-1 during the roll.
away_pitcher_note: It is not official yet, but Hamels is expected to make his 2014 debut against the Dodgers. He opened the season on the disabled list as he recovered from inflammation in his left shoulder.

home_pitcher_note: Now that he's becoming a ground-ball pitcher, Haren is doing more with less. He was the first Dodger to pitch into the eighth inning in his last start against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick pitched well enough to win Saturday at Coors Field but took the loss. He allowed six hits, three runs and struck out three in seven innings in a 3-1 defeat. He hopes for a little more run support this time at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Collmenter was shifted to the rotation to take the spot of Randall Delgado. In his two starts he is 0-2 with a 6.30 ERA. Last time out it was a three-run homer by Yasiel Puig that spoiled an otherwise good start.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez hopes to bounce back after allowing nine hits, six runs, one walk and striking out three in just four-plus innings Sunday at Coors Field. He entered the afternoon with a 3.86 ERA, making it his worst start of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo was set back this spring by a bulging disc in his back and is just now rounding into the form most pitchers have at the end of Spring Training. He allowed five runs in 5 1/3 innings last time out against the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Lee continues to roll. He is 2-2 with a 1.20 ERA in his last four starts. In 30 innings in those four starts, he has allowed 33 hits, four earned runs, one walk and has struck out 37.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has pitched well at times in each of his starts this year, but has yet to do it for his entire outing. Last time out, a three-run homer by Mike Olt hurt him as the Cubs beat him, 9-2, at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett gave the Phillies a chance to win Tuesday against the Dodgers at Dodger Stadium. He allowed six hits, two runs, one walk and struck out five in 6 2/3 innings. He also picked up a career-high three hits.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels makes his first start of the season at Citizens Bank Park after making his season debut Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, where he allowed six hits, two runs, one walk and struck out five in six innings of a Phillies loss.
away_pitcher_note: Niese's ERA is down to 2.45 after throwing 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball last time out, against the Cardinals. He allowed just one run in 15 2/3 innings against the Phillies last season but is 2-4 with a 4.50 ERA for his career at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has yielded three earned runs or less in his last three starts, but has allowed 36 hits in 30 2/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Colon's ERA may be 4.50, but more than half the runs against him came in one start. In his other four outings, he holds a 2.33 ERA with 23 strikeouts and one walk. Colon has pitched in more career games at Veterans Stadium than Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lee wasn't at his best vs. the D-backs and was hit hard for five runs in three innings. He settled down to retire the final nine batters he faced and was replaced after six innings. He has walked only four in 41 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg took advantage of ample run support vs. the Padres last Friday. He allowed seven hits over seven shutout innings and struck out 11, the 14th time he's fanned 10 or more.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett is 3-0 with a 0.83 ERA in his last three starts, despite pitching with an inguinal hernia. He has allowed just 14 hits and three walks in his last 21 2/3 innings. He has struck out 18.
away_pitcher_note: Roark was practically unhittable his last time out, retiring the first 16 batters he faced en route to the first complete game of his young career, a three-hit shutout, as the Nationals cruised to a 4-0 victory over the Padres last Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez moves up in the rotation to fill in for Cole Hamels, who is out with the flu. The right-hander has not started since April 25, when he allowed four earned runs in six innings in a loss to the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez received a no-decision in his last start after pitching six innings, allowing three runs on five hits and striking out nine batters against the Astros on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has yielded three earned runs or less in his last three starts, but has allowed 36 hits in 30 2/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Happ will be making his first start of the season and could be part of a temporary six-man rotation if things go well. He has worked 4 1/3 innings out of the bullpen, allowing three hits and two earned runs

home_pitcher_note: Hamels was scratched from his scheduled start on Sunday because of the flu, but the Phillies are confident the ace will be ready to go against Toronto. He struggled with command in has last start, walking five in 4 2/3 innings against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Hutchison allowed four runs on five hits and one walk during his last start against the Royals. The big blow came in the seventh when he allowed a two-run double to Alcides Escobar, but Hutchison was still able to go a season-high seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle continued his strong start to the season with another impressive outing vs the Royals. He allowed just two earned runs on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings. He has won all but one of his six starts this year and has allowed just 10 earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Lee allowed one earned run in seven innings Friday against the Nationals. He has a 1.67 ERA (eight earned runs in 43 innings) in six starts since he allowed eight runs on Opening Day, but just three wins to show for it.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey appears to be settling into a groove after a slow start to the season. He has recorded three consecutive quality starts, but only has one win to show for it, in part because of the prolonged struggles of Toronto's bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett allowed one run in six innings Saturday against the Nationals. He continues to dominate. He has a 0.98 ERA (three earned runs in 27 2/3 innings) with 25 strikeouts and five walks in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Mejia took a 6-0 lead into the fifth Saturday at Colorado but lasted 4 1/3 innings, giving up eight runs, including Nolan Arenado's grand slam, in what became an 11-10 Rockies win.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez enjoyed his best start of the season Sunday against the Nationals at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed four hits, three walks and struck out three in 7 1/3 scoreless innings, lowering his ERA from 5.74 to 4.50.

home_pitcher_note: Gee has thrown a career-high scoreless streak of 16 innings, including six Sunday at Colorado where he allowed six hits and won, 5-1, giving him back-to-back scoreless starts for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick has lost eight-straight games in a 13-start span since Aug. 13, 2013. He has a 4.78 ERA in that span, although the Phillies bullpen has blown three wins and he has received some poor run support in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Long gone are worries about Niese's shoulder and elbow. All the left-hander has done is thrive, particularly lately. Over his last four outings, Niese has posted a 1.01 ERA with 21 strikeouts and seven walks, re-establishing himself as the staff ace.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed 10 hits, five runs, a walk and two home runs in six innings Tuesday against the Blue Jays at Citizens Bank Park. That followed a shaky performance a week earlier vs. the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Lee hopes to bounce back from a forgettable performance Wednesday in Toronto. He cruised through six innings, allowing just one run, but allowed five in the seventh inning in a 10-0 loss to the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Shoemaker will make his second career Major League start. He was called up from Triple-A Salt Lake after Hector Santiago was removed from the starting rotation this week. He is 1-0 with a 6.31 ERA and in five Minor League starts.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett had been on a roll until he allowed nine hits, seven runs, two walks and struck out four in an ugly loss Thursday to the Blue Jays. He had allowed just three earned runs in 27 2/3 innings in his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: The righty continued his hot start, throwing seven innings of two-run ball in a no-decision his last outing. Richards fanned six and is undefeated in seven starts, while posting the best strikeout rate of his career.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed four hits, four runs, two walks and struck out four in 5 1/3 innings Saturday against the Mets at Citi Field. Kendrick is still looking for his first win, but poor run support has much to do with that.
away_pitcher_note: A sinkerball pitcher, Simon struggled to keep the ball down vs. the Rockies on Saturday. The result was his worst start of the year -- a season-low three innings and a season-high five runs, including three homers.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels threw a career-high 133 pitches in seven innings Sunday against the Mets. He allowed seven hits, one run, three walks and struck out 10. He said he felt fine afterward, but an extra day's rest should help.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey gave up only a solo homer over 7 1/3 innings in Sunday's win over the Rockies. He began his delivery with his hands over his head, a mechanical sequence he had not used since 2009. "I needed something to get my timing back," he said.

home_pitcher_note: Lee has pitched well this season, but that hasn't translated into wins for the Phillies. The club has lost his past three starts, despite Lee posting a 3.10 ERA in 20 1/3 innings over that span. He has a 1.55 ERA at home but is 0-3.
away_pitcher_note: Cingrani will be activated from the disabled list for the start. He last pitched on April 30 but lasted only four innings vs. the Cubs as he showed decreased fastball velocity. He went on the DL the following day with mild left shoulder tendinitis.

home_pitcher_note: After a successful Major League debut Wednesday, DeSclafani gets another start in place of Jose Fernandez. He allowed two runs on seven hits over six innings in a 13-3 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett struggled with his command, which led to a high pitch count Tuesday against the Angels. He allowed seven hits, three runs, five walks and struck out six in five innings. He threw 113 pitches in the process, dropping to 2-3.

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi had a rough outing his last time out, giving up season highs of six runs and nine hits over 4 1/3 innings, his shortest outing of the year, in a loss to the Giants last Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed three runs in seven innings Friday against the Reds. He has not won a game in 15 starts dating back to Aug. 11. The Phillies have been shut out five times and have scored one run or fewer in eight of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Alvarez has allowed 10 runs in 10 innings on the road since pitching a shutout in his last home start, a 3-0 decision over the Mets two weeks ago. He has two shutouts, both in Miami, this year.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels picked up his 100th career win on Saturday against the Reds. He allowed three hits, one run, two walks and struck out 10 in seven innings, following up nicely after throwing a career-high 133 pitches on May 11.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez rejoins the rotation after the Phillies skipped his last start because of a couple days off last week. He has pitched out of the bullpen, becoming one of Ryne Sandberg's more reliable arms.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw has two hurdles. He's coming off a disaster in Arizona (seven runs in 1 2/3 innings). And during batting practice on Wednesday, he took a Justin Turner line drive off his right shin. He said he's fine, but the leg has been bandaged.

home_pitcher_note: Buchanan makes his big league debut against the Dodgers. One of the Phillies' bright spots in Spring Training, Buchanan, who went 5-1 with a 3.98 ERA in nine starts in Triple-A, takes Cliff Lee's spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Haren had given the Dodgers more than they expected from a fourth starter, but he's allowed three home runs in his last two starts after allowing only two in his first seven starts. And there is concern about back stiffness.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett allowed six hits and two runs in 6 2/3 innings April 22 against the Dodgers at Dodger Stadium, but Burnett's last three starts have been rough. He has posted a 6.75 ERA and pitched past the fifth inning once.
away_pitcher_note: Keep Beckett in mind for comeback player of the year if he keeps this up. He's had bad luck in the win department, but the 2.89 ERA is no fluke coming off serious surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick allowed six runs in 5 2/3 innings Wednesday in a loss to the Marlins to make him 0-10 with a 5.11 ERA in 15 starts since Aug. 11, 2013. The first inning has been a problem. He has a 9.00 ERA in the first this season.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin gave up three runs and struck out four in 5 2/3 innings in his last start, a loss to the Giants. Two of the four hits were homers. But Chacin, after missing April with a shoulder strain, is gradually improving.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed three runs on six hits and one walk while striking out six in seven innings Thursday against the Marlins. He earned a no-decision in a 4-3 loss, but he has been pitching better lately after a slow start.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had not given up a hit and faced the minimum through three innings before a rain delay ended his start vs. the Giants. He hasn't given up a run in his last 12 innings and has allowed one hit in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez pitched well in Friday's 2-0 loss to the Dodgers. He allowed seven hits, two runs, four walks and struck out three in 6 1/3 innings, but got no run support. He hopes for a little more on Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles pitched well enough to win in his last start, walking one and surrendering only two earned runs in six innings vs. the Braves. However, he was disappointed in his six strikeouts, expressing a desire to pitch to contact.

home_pitcher_note: Buchanan impressed in his big league debut Saturday against the Dodgers. He allowed five hits, two runs and struck out two in five innings at Citizens Bank Park, keeping his composure as Cliff Lee's replacement.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander threw 6 2/3 innings of three-run ball against Arizona on Saturday, his longest outing since last September. Wheeler's efforts to improve his command generally and 4.3 walks-per-nine-innings rate specifically are ongoing.

home_pitcher_note: He allowed 11 hits and six runs in seven innings Sunday against the Dodgers. He has a 6.26 ERA (16 earned runs in 23 innings) in his last four starts after posting a 2.06 ERA through his first seven.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander was sharp in his third Major League start on Sunday, striking out 10 and allowing one run in six innings against the D-backs. Montero, 23, will be making his first start on the road.

home_pitcher_note: After 10 consecutive losses dating back to Aug. 6, Kendrick held the high-powered Rockies offense scoreless through 6 2/3 innings to earn the win. He has now delivered quality starts in six of ten appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Rapidly becoming one of the unluckiest pitchers in baseball, deGrom is winless in three starts despite a 1.83 ERA. That mark is the lowest for any Mets pitcher through three career starts since Dillon Gee posted a 1.80 ERA in 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels pitched well at times Tuesday against the Rockies, but he could not put hitters away at the right moment. He allowed three hits, four runs, two walks and a three-run home run, with four strikeouts in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Niese cruised through five innings against the Pirates on Tuesday but couldn't get through the sixth. He exited with two outs after surrendering a total of four walks, three hits and two runs. It was his second-shortest outing of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez allowed two runs on six hits and five walks with four K's in 5 2/3 innings Wednesday against the Rockies. He has done the job as the No. 5 starter, despite being skipped and pitching out of the bullpen at times.
away_pitcher_note: With nine strikeouts over 7 1/3 shutout innings, Colon's last outing was arguably his best of the season. He's now given the Mets two straight good starts after stumbling through two of his previous three. Colon has not faced the Phillies this year.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann's ERA rose from 2.92 to 4.07 in four starts since May 5. In his last outing, Zimmermann allowed four runs on eight hits in five innings in an 8-5 loss to the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Buchanan has posted back-to-back quality starts to begin his Major League career. The 22-year-old yielded four runs (three earned) on seven hits in Thursday's loss to the Mets, and will hope for more run support against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg didn't allow an earned run over six innings in his last start, a 9-2 victory over the Rangers. He struck out nine to earn his fourth win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett had a wild night Friday against the Mets, but he kept the Phillies in the game in a 14-inning victory. He allowed five hits, five runs, six walks and struck out 11 in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fister won his third straight start after allowing two runs in six innings in a 10-2 victory over the Rangers on Saturday. Fister will face the Phillies for the second time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick did well to limit the Mets in his 113-pitch effort on Saturday. He allowed four earned runs, but was one strike away from his seventh quality start. Kendrick will have to fare better in the first inning, where he has a 9.82 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto is the Major League leader in innings with 91 he and leads the National League with 1,300 pitches thrown. The Reds haven' t been too concerned with him wearing down because he's pitched efficiently for the most part.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels did not factor in the decision his last time out, despite holding the Mets to two runs (one earned) on six hits and four walks, while striking out eight. The Phillies are now 1-7 with the 30-year-old on the mound in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Simon has given up three runs or fewer in nine of 11 starts but it's important for clubs to get to him early. This season, he has yet to allow a run after the fourth inning (25 2/3 innings total).
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez has been adequate as a fifth starter, looking at his 4.03 ERA. But he is putting a tremendous strain on the bullpen. He has pitched more than six innings just twice in 10 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey tossed six innings, allowing three runs on five hits, walking one and striking out seven in a win over the Giants on Tuesday. He is winless in his career against the Phillies, with an 0-4 record and a 4.41 ERA in nine starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Buchanan easily endured the worst start of his brief big league career Tuesday in a loss in Washington. He allowed 10 hits, seven runs, two walks, two home runs and struck out six in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett had a 2.06 ERA in seven starts through May 3, but he is 1-4 with a 7.25 ERA in six starts since. He allowed 10 hits, eight runs, four walks and struck out three in six innings Wednesday against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy allowed two runs on five hits over six innings in his last start against the Pirates. He walked one and struck out seven. Kennedy's ERA is currently about 1 1/2 runs lower than it was a year ago with the D-backs and Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels allowed five hits, two walks and struck out seven in 7 2/3 scoreless innings in an 8-0 victory Friday over the Reds. He faces San Diego on Thursday. He is 8-2 with a 2.39 ERA in 14 career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing one earned run in five of his six starts in May (3-1, 2.08 ERA), Ross was tagged for a season-high six runs (five earned) in 5 2/3 innings Friday against Washington. But he still logged seven strikeouts for the seventh time in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick hopes to get going the right way after struggling the past few starts. He is 1-3 with a 5.02 ERA in his past six starts dating to May 10. Many of those runs have been scoring in the first inning, which needs to change.
away_pitcher_note: Stults had the shortest start of his career in his last outing on Sunday against Washington, lasting just 2 1/3 innings while giving up eight hits and six runs. In his last four starts he has given up 18 runs in 19 innings for an ERA of 8.53.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez allowed four hits, four runs, three walks and two strikeouts in four innings Saturday against the Reds. He has pitched more than six innings in just two of 11 starts this season, putting a strain on the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta was much more efficient in his last start, holding Miami to three hits in six shutout frames. Chicago is protective of his right shoulder, lifting him after 93 pitches. He's 1-1 in two starts vs. the Phils, last facing them in a Sept. 1 win.

home_pitcher_note: Buchanan had one bad inning in Sunday's loss to the Reds. He allowed four runs in the fifth and it cost him. Buchanan has allowed 11 runs in 12 innings over his past two starts. He hopes for better against the Cubs.

away_pitcher_note: The Nationals overcame a rocky outing from Scherzer vs. the Braves. Scherzer battled through six innings, surrendering four runs on six hits with three walks and six strikeouts.

away_pitcher_note: Easily the Mets’ most successful starting pitcher through two rotation turns, Syndergaard will look to build on his success against the Phillies. All he did against them last year was go 2-0 with a 1.46 ERA, 15 strikeouts and two walks in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson hopes to bounce back from his worst start of the season Friday against the Nationals, when he allowed six runs (five earned) in three innings. He had allowed just two earned runs in 11 2/3 innings in his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Colon scored his 219th career win last time out, matching Pedro Martinez for the second-most in history among Dominican-born pitchers. He’ll look to surpass his countryman against a Phillies club that already beat him once earlier this month.

away_pitcher_note: Nola hopes to bounce back from the worst start of his career. He allowed seven runs in five innings Saturday against the Nationals. He uncharacteristically walked three batters, and all three runners scored.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson surrendered no earned runs on eight hits over 11 innings in his first two starts, then was touched for five runs (four earned) on 11 hits in five innings in Minnesota on Monday. He’ll look to get back on track at home.

away_pitcher_note: Since Eickhoff allowed six runs in four innings against the Red Sox in Boston on Sept. 6, he is 3-2 with a 1.34 ERA in seven starts. He allowed two runs in seven innings Monday in a loss to the Mets.

away_pitcher_note: The last time Hellickson faced Washington, he fared worse than he did in his rough follow-up outing against the Mets. Unable to make it out of the fifth in his last two starts, he will look to return to his Opening Day form.

away_pitcher_note: Nola hopes to bounce back against the Nationals after allowing a career-high seven runs against them April 16 at Citizens Bank Park. But he hopes seven innings of one-run ball Friday against the Brewers have him on track.

away_pitcher_note: Kluber was in vintage form on Saturday, when he held the Tigers to one run over eight innings in his first win of the season. The righty allowed just two hits and ended with 10 strikeouts and no walks.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff has one of the most effective breaking balls in baseball, but he ran into trouble with it Sunday. The Brewers had two doubles and a homer against it, after he allowed only two extra-base hits off the pitch in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Bauer moves into the rotation spot vacated by righty Carlos Carrasco, who is out four to six weeks with a hamstring injury. Bauer logged 64 pitches (3 1/3 innings) in relief of Carrasco on Sunday in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez has been a bright spot for the Phillies, striking out 25 in 15 scoreless innings in his first two starts. He hasn’t been as dominant since, but he allowed three runs in six innings in a Tuesday win vs. Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Though his line on Wednesday - 5 1/3 innings, seven hits, four runs - didn’t indicate it, Wainwright was pleased with his improved command. In particular, he found he was able to get late life on his pitches for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson had his best start of the season Wednesday against the Nationals, allowing just two hits in seven scoreless innings. Hellickson has only faced the Cardinals once. He earned a win against them in 2011.

home_pitcher_note: Wacha threw a career-high 114 pitches in his last start and featured his best fastball-changeup combination yet this season. He struck out nine in the seven-inning start, more strikeouts than he’s had in a game since June 9, 2015.
away_pitcher_note: Nola had his best start of the season in his last outing, holding the Nationals scoreless and allowing just two hits over seven innings. The right-hander lowered his ERA by nearly a run, to 3.55, in the process.

away_pitcher_note: Morgan makes his second start since replacing right-hander Charlie Morton, who will miss the remainder of the season following left hamstring surgery. Morgan struck out seven in five innings against Cleveland.

away_pitcher_note: Eickhoff is hoping to be a little sharper against the Cardinals. After allowing a career-high seven runs April 24 in Milwaukee, he grinded through six innings Saturday against the Indians, allowing three runs.

away_pitcher_note: Velasquez pitched six scoreless innings Sunday against Cleveland, becoming the only pitcher to have three starts with six or more innings, no runs and three or fewer hits allowed. Opponents have hit just .164 against him.

away_pitcher_note: Hellickson struggled to keep the ball in the park Monday at St. Louis, giving up three home runs in 5 1/3 innings. He’s given up seven home runs in 26 1/3 innings and 19.4 percent of the fly balls.

away_pitcher_note: Nola was dominant, allowing two-hits over seven shutout innings at St. Louis on Tuesday. He has a 20-inning shutout streak and opponents are hitting just .176 off of him. Nola has been tough on the road, posting an ERA of 0.64.

away_pitcher_note: Morgan has not gone past five innings in two starts this season. He lasted just four frames in his last outing last Wednesday at St. Louis. Morgan gave up three runs on six hits with two strikeouts and two walks.

away_pitcher_note: Eickhoff has yielded six hits and three runs in each of his last two outings. He hasn’t earned a win since throwing seven innings of four-hit shutout ball on April 13 against the Padres.

away_pitcher_note: Velasquez has pitched very well this season despite stumbling a bit in his last outing. In Miami, the righty gave up seven hits and four runs over six innings of work, but he settled down. It was his first start this season with a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson received a no-decision in Philadelphia's 4-3 win over Miami on Saturday, allowing three runs on eight hits -- two of them homers -- over 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off one of his worst starts of the season, Finnegan received a no-decision in a 13-7 loss to Milwaukee last Saturday when he gave up five runs (three earned) on seven hits, including three home runs, in five-plus innings.

home_pitcher_note: Last time out, Nola gave up three runs on six hits with five strikeouts and a walk through six innings in the Phillies' 6-5 win over the Marlins on Sunday.

away_pitcher_note: With six innings in a no-decision on Monday vs. the Pirates, Straily has continued to show dependability since moving into the rotation. He works hard to  throw strikes while trying to retire batters in three pitches or fewer.

away_pitcher_note: Perhaps the 116 pitches Conley threw on April 29 in his 7 2/3 hitless innings vs. Milwaukee are catching up to him. The lefty has gone 9 1/3 in his last two starts, and his four innings in a rematch with the Brewers was a rough outing.

away_pitcher_note: Koehler is coming off back-to-back strong starts, in which he allowed a total of two runs in 12 2/3 innings vs. the Phillies and Nationals. The righty allowed 11 baserunners vs. Washington on Friday but pitched around trouble in a no-decision.

away_pitcher_note: Wisler has looked more like a front-line starter as he has pitched into the eighth inning in each of his past three starts. The promising right-hander will be facing the Phillies for the second time in 10 days.

away_pitcher_note: Morgan bounced back nicely from the worst start of his career (3 2/3 IP, 7 ER) vs. Cincinnati. He allowed only two runs over six innings against the Braves but finished with one strikeout.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, the Giants shut out the Cubs and Hendricks took the loss despite giving up one run over 5 1/3 innings. He has a 2.28 ERA in four home games.
away_pitcher_note: Eickhoff has shown he can succeed a couple different ways as a pitcher. He’s done it relying on his fastball and curve but also has found success mixing in his slider and change. Last start, he pitched seven scoreless against the Braves.

away_pitcher_note: Velasquez is coming off his shortest outing of the season, giving up three runs on nine hits over four innings in Detroit. He has a 2.25 road ERA in May, but all three of his road starts in May have been no-decisions.

away_pitcher_note: Roark tossed seven scoreless innings against the Phillies at Nationals Park on April 28, but he didn’t get a decision as Washington lost the game, 3-0. This will be Roark’s first start at Citizens Bank Park this season.

home_pitcher_note: Nola (4-3, 2.86 ERA) has faced the Nationals twice this season, taking the loss after surrendering seven runs in five innings April 16 and getting a no-decision when he threw seven scoreless frames April 28.

home_pitcher_note: Morgan (1-3, 6.67 ERA) gave up a season-high three home runs in a loss to the Cubs last time out. He has lost three consecutive starts.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is 5-1 with a 2.38 ERA in eight career starts against the Phillies. Since joining the Nationals in 2015, Scherzer is 4-0 with a 1.88 ERA vs. Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff held his own and turned in the best start the Phillies had all series against the Cubs’ MLB-best offense, lasting six innings and allowing four runs, while striking out seven for the first time since April 24.

home_pitcher_note: It’s been an up-and-down season for Velasquez, whose highs have been Everest-esque (16 K SO vs. SD) but also come with outings like his last against the Cubs, who hammered him for two HRs and seven runs in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson has pitched into the eighth inning in three of his last four starts and delivered four consecutive quality starts, continuing his run as the Brewers' best pitcher this season. Only one of his five wins have come on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson turned in perhaps his best start of the year Monday against the Nationals, tossing seven innings of one-run ball. But he was pulled for a pinch-hitter after only 79 pitches, so he should be fresh for this start.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra has pitched at least six innings in five of six starts since a promotion from Triple-A, including three quality starts. The Brewers won his first five outings before falling to the Cardinals in the last homestand.

away_pitcher_note: Peralta has a 5.83 ERA in five starts against the Phillies, but he pitched a gem in his only outing at Citizens Bank Park, allowing two runs over seven innings in 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Morgan was solid through five vs. the Nats last time out, but he got rocked for four runs on two homers in the sixth. He failed to record a quality start for the fifth time in seven starts. Morgan will be tested to limit the long ball vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Lester went the distance in his last outing, vs. the Dodgers, holding them to four hits and striking out 10. It was his 28th career double-digit-K game. He’s 5-0 with a 1.71 ERA in seven career starts against the Phillies, including a win on May 27.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff has been the Phillies' hard-luck pitcher this season. He’s made seven of 11 quality starts but has only two wins to show for it; the Phils have averaged 2.58 runs per nine innings while he's been on the mound.

away_pitcher_note: The 37-year-old right-hander has continued his late-career resurgence early in 2016. Over his last two starts, Lackey has given up just one run in 13 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Hellickson struggled in his first start against the Nats this year, but he has since turned in two of his best outings against them, going seven innings and striking out eight in each, allowing a total of one run and five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Roark is coming off his shortest outing of the season last time out against the Reds, who tagged him for five runs on seven hits in three innings. But he often has pitched deep, completing at least six innings in all but three of his 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nola put a runner on base each of his six innings last start against the Brewers, but he didn’t let any of them score. Nola left the game having recorded his ninth straight quality start, a streak only matched by the Giants’ Madison Bumgarner.

home_pitcher_note: Ross has dominated the Phillies twice this season, earning two victories with a 0.61 ERA, although both were at Citizens Bank Park. In his last outing against the White Sox, he issued a season-high four walks and allowed five runs in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morgan’s spot in the Phillies’ rotation has been tenuous after his recent struggles, but he allowed three runs in six innings against the Cubs. It might have helped his cause, but he will need to keep it up.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey has been working on his secondary pitches a lot of late and it helped him survive 5 1/3 IP during his last start vs. Detroit. The knuckleball wasn't working that day, but he still found a way to win. He's 5-4 with a 3.03 ERA all-time vs. PHI.
away_pitcher_note: Eickhoff is on a bit of a roll after allowing just one run in seven innings Tuesday in a victory over the Cubs. He has a 2.76 ERA (10 earned runs in 32 2/3 innings) over his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Stroman allowed four runs in 5 1/3 and picked up a no-decision in Toronto's 6-5 loss against Baltimore. The 25-year-old has allowed 17 runs in his last three starts, and has seen his ERA rise over a run in that time.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin will make his Major-League debut in place of the injured Vince Velasquez. Acquired in exchange for Jimmy Rollins in December 2014, Eflin is the Phillies' No. 9 prospect, according to MLBPipeline.com.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson struggled against the Nationals on Friday, giving up seven runs on nine hits, three of them home runs. The loss snapped his streak of six straight starts of three runs or fewer. He has a 3.45 ERA in 15 career starts against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Estrada gets the ball against the Phillies after another quality start his last time out. Estrada pitched six innings and allowed three runs in a no-decision against the Orioles and has allowed five hits or fewer in nine straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Nola endured maybe his worst outing of the season Saturday against the Nationals, lasting only 3 2/3 innings while allowing four earned runs. He still ranks 12th in the Major Leagues in strikeout rate, having fanned 26.5 percent of batters faced.
away_pitcher_note: Happ picked up his team-leading seventh win on Saturday against the Orioles, despite a shaky start in which he allowed four runs -- including three home runs -- over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morgan gets the ball looking to improve on his last start against the Nationals. Morgan allowed three runs on five hits over 6 2/3 innings in a game which Philadelphia eventually lost, 5-4.
away_pitcher_note: Ray had his longest outing of the season last time out against Miami, matching a career high with 7 2/3 scoreless innings. He looks to win consecutive starts for the first time this year in his first career start against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff looks to build off his dominant outing against Toronto, in which he held the Blue Jays to three hits over six shutout innings. He has allowed just three runs over his past three starts, spanning 19 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke won for his sixth straight start with seven two-run innings against the Dodgers. He is 4-0 with a 1.54 ERA in five road starts and 6-1 with a 2.68 ERA in eight career games (seven starts) against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin, one of the Phillies’ top prospects, certainly hopes for much better Sunday. He made his Major League debut Tuesday against the Blue Jays and allowed nine hits and nine runs in just 2 2/3 innings in a loss to Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Bradley allowed a career-high three homers against the Dodgers last time out, his third consecutive loss. He'll now face the Phillies, the team he suffered his first career loss against in 2015 after allowing four earned runs in two innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson has been in a bit of a funk lately. He allowed four runs in six innings Wednesday against the Blue Jays. He is 0-2 with a 7.41 ERA (11 earned runs in 14 innings) in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Miller will make his first big league start since May 24. He was placed on the DL after that start with a sprained right index finger. Miller made a pair of rehab starts with Class A Visalia.

home_pitcher_note: Duffey has yet to regain his poise after a strong start to the season and has given up at least four earned runs in each of his last six starts. In his last start on June 15 against the Angels, he struggled with falling behind batters.
away_pitcher_note: Nola hopes to get back on track after struggling mightily in his last two starts. He has failed to pitch at least four innings in both starts as his ERA has jumped from 2.65 to 3.51 in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Gibson pitched well enough to earn his first win of the season on June 16, allowing just one run through six frames against the Yankees, but two of the runners he left on base in the seventh came around to score on a Didi Gregorius homer.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies committed three errors behind Morgan in his last outing, and he allowed three home runs before getting pulled after 4 1/3. In each of his last two starts, however, Morgan has set and matched a career-high with eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco has a long history against the Phillies. He is 8-6 with a 3.75 ERA in 22 appearances (19 starts) against them.
away_pitcher_note: Eickhoff has been the sole bright spot in the Phillies’ rotation. His last start, though, he joined the rest of the staff by allowing two homers. He should be happy to see the Twins, who have scored the fewest runs in the American League.

home_pitcher_note: To say that Peavy has turned his season around is an understatement. After recording an 8.21 ERA in his first nine starts, he has compiled a 1.76 ERA in his last five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin rebounded from a rocky MLB debut by going 5 2/3 innings and limiting the D-backs to two runs in his first start at Citizens Bank Park. He’ll have another road test in his next outing, facing the first-place Giants at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Bumgarner lengthened his streak of games with two earned runs allowed or fewer to 12, matching Fred Anderson's third-best franchise streak.
away_pitcher_note: Keep an eye on Hellickson as the Aug. 1 Trade Deadline approaches. He is a top trade candidate for the rebuilding Phillies, so the better he pitches down the stretch, the better it could be for the Phillies’ front office.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies have been rough on Cueto in their nine career meetings. His record against the Phillies is 1-4, to go with a 5.05 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies hope Nola can get things figured out against the Giants. He has a 15.83 ERA in his last three starts, and was unable to pitch four or more innings in any of them.

home_pitcher_note: Ray is coming off a rough outing in which he allowed four earned runs on four hits in 5 1/3 innings. The lefty had given up just two earned runs over his previous 13 2/3 innings in a pair of wins.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez rejoins the rotation after spending most of June on the DL with a strained right biceps. The Phillies never considered the injury serious, but they plan to be careful with one of their prized young starters.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke has won his last seven decisions over his last eight starts. He was in line to win his eighth straight last time out against the Rockies before the bullpen coughed up a lead in the eighth.

away_pitcher_note: Command has been a major concern of late for Gonzalez, who walked five of the 11 batters he faced in a blowout loss to the Rays on Tuesday. The southpaw is struggling with an 8.44 ERA in June.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin just finished a fantastic June (5-0 with a 1.76 ERA in five starts). Four of those wins followed Phillies losses, including two after three-game losing streaks. One followed a four-game skid.
away_pitcher_note: Two starts ago, Cobb showed flashes of what the Orioles expected when they signed him this offseason, but he took a step backward his last time out, allowing five runs on eight hits in 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nola probably cinched a spot on his first National League All-Star team after holding Washington to five hits and one run in 7 2/3 innings on Thursday. Nola is the first Phillies pitcher with 10 or more wins before July 1 since Cole Hamels in 2012.
away_pitcher_note: Ramirez has made one start this season, a 4 1/3-inning outing against the Red Sox on June 13. He threw five scoreless innings against the Mariners last Thursday, and owns  a 3.88 ERA in 14 starts with Triple-A Norfolk.

home_pitcher_note: Williams took a step back on Saturday, giving up four runs over 4 2/3 innings against his hometown Padres. He pitched well against the Phillies in April, allowing two runs on one hit and five walks while striking out seven over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta scuffled against the Nats in his last start: 1 2/3 IP, seven runs allowed on seven hits and three home runs. The bright side: He followed up a one-plus-inning outing against the Nats in May with just one earned run in his next 19 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After a strong June, Taillon gave up four runs (three earned) on seven hits and three walks in 4 2/3 innings against the Padres on Sunday. His last outing vs. Philadelphia was his shortest of the season as he allowed five runs over 1 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta hopes to get back to the form that made him so successful in May, when he posted a 0.90 ERA in five starts. He has a 6.16 ERA in six starts since, although the Phillies' defense has led to nine unearned runs and extended innings in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Kingham faltered on the mound and in the field on Monday, giving up seven runs (five earned) on eight hits while committing two errors in three innings during a 17-1 loss to the Dodgers. He has a 2.89 ERA in three starts at PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will make his 2018 debut in Sunday’s series finale against the Pirates. Because of a doubleheader Monday in New York and an injury to Vince Velasquez, the Phillies needed an arm for Sunday. Anderson is 5-3 with a 4.15 ERA in Triple-A.

home_pitcher_note: Another victim of a low-scoring offense, Wheeler is 0-4 over his last 11 starts, despite a 3.76 ERA and 67 strikeouts in those 66 innings. The Mets will push Wheeler back a day in the rotation, hoping he can provide length in a doubleheader.
away_pitcher_note: Following three consecutive starts of fewer than five innings to finish May, Eflin has been arguably the team’s best pitcher since. He is 6-0 with a 1.91 ERA in his past six starts, striking out 34 and walking six in 37 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his only two starts for the Mets this season, Oswalt has not made it past four innings. He owns a 7.94 ERA overall and is looking to get his first career win on Monday in Game 2 of the Mets’ doubleheader against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Nola has not only evolved into the Phillies’ ace, but he has developed into one of the best starting pitchers in Major League Baseball. Not bad for a pitcher projected to be a No. 3-type starter in the big leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Gagnon will make his Major League debut on Tuesday against the Phillies. The 28-year-old owns a 2.45 ERA in his last five starts at Triple-A Las Vegas and is looking to continue this success in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: De Los Santos will make his Major League debut against the Mets. He is the Phillies’ No. 11 prospect, according to MLB Pipeline. The Phils acquired De Los Santos in December from the Padres in exchange for shortstop Freddy Galvis.

home_pitcher_note: deGrom has allowed three or fewer runs in 15 straight starts and leads the big leagues with an ERA of 1.79. He is also second in the National League in strikeouts with 142. deGrom holds a lifetime record of 6-1 in 12 games started against the Phils.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez is expected to rejoin the rotation after landing on the 10-day disabled list July 1. He got hit on the right arm by a line drive June 30. Velasquez memorably picked up the ball and threw left-handed to record the out at first base.

home_pitcher_note:
Gausman took a no-decision in Minnesota his last time out after going five innings and allowing three runs on five hits, including a homer. He has been 
one of the Orioles' most consistent starters, with quality outings in three of his past four.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta has pitched a combined 4 1/3 innings in his past two starts, allowing 10 runs (eight earned runs). In between those two outings he pitched an inning in relief in a 13-inning victory over the Nationals on July 1.

home_pitcher_note: Chen’s road woes are glaring, as the lefty had his away ERA rise to 10.47 after yielding seven runs at Washington. In Miami, it’s been a different story. In six starts at Marlins Park, Chen’s ERA is 1.89. Chen has dropped three straight decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta returned to form Saturday in a victory over the Pirates at PNC Park, allowing just two runs in seven innings. He walked one and struck out eight. It was Arrieta's first win since May 29.

home_pitcher_note: Richards went 3 2/3 innings at Washington in his last start, walking a career-high seven. At Marlins Park, the rookie is 1-2 with a 4.44 ERA in five starts. Richards' last win was four starts ago, on June 23 at Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Nola learned last Sunday that he made his first National League All-Star team. The Phillies had the option of pitching him this Sunday, but by pitching him Saturday, it made him eligible to pitch Tuesday in the All-Star Game.

home_pitcher_note: In his last 15 starts, Urena is 2-7 with a 3.96 ERA, with a WHIP of 1.17. Urena's two-seam fastball has become a weapon, and the pitch averages 95.7 mph, well above the MLB average of 92.3 mph.
away_pitcher_note: De Los Santos fills in for Zach Eflin, who headed to the disabled list Saturday with a blister on his throwing hand. The 22-year-old is 9-3 with a 1.89 ERA and 87 strikeouts in 16 starts at Triple-A Lehigh Valley this season.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta finished the first half with three solid starts before the All-Star break. He is 2-0 with a 1.89 ERA in those starts, allowing just four earned runs in 19 innings. He has pitched seven innings in each of his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander started on Opening Day, and he gets the ball first in the second half as well. Richard chewed up 124 innings in the first half, the most by a Padres starter since Tyson Ross and Ian Kennedy did so in 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Pivetta rebounded a bit in his final start before the break, but he has an 8.25 ERA in his last four appearances (three starts). The Phillies are counting on a strong second half from him as he pitches in a pennant race.
away_pitcher_note: With Brad Hand off to Cleveland, Ross is one of the Padres’ most attractive trade pieces. Set to become a free agent this offseason, Ross has been San Diego’s most reliable starter this year, aside from a couple shaky outings early in July.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez pitched six scoreless innings July 11 in his first start back from the 10-day disabled list (bruised right forearm). His only career start vs. the Padres was on April 14, 2016, when he pitched a complete game shutout at home.

Eflin is back after missing his last scheduled start before the break with a blister on his pitching hand. He’s been a major bright spot for the Phillies, going 6-0 with a 2.32 ERA in seven starts since early June.
away_pitcher_note: Stripling rode an 8-2 first half -- including a league-best .800 winning percentage -- to his first-career All-Star appaerance. Stripling hurled six shutout innings against the Padres in his last start before the break.

home_pitcher_note: This is Nola’s first start since the All-Star Game. In one scoreless inning, he struck out two and got Mike Trout to pop out. Nola will look to continue a first-half performance in which he tied his career-high 12 wins and recorded a 2.30 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maeda consistently kept the Dodgers in games in the first half and has not allowed more than three runs in a start since May 11 versus the Reds. His most recent appearance came out of the bullpen, during which he earned a win on July 15.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta struggled Friday against the Padres in his first start back from the All-Star break, but the Phillies hope to lean on the veteran right-hander in the second half as the Phillies pursue their first postseason berth since 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Buehler rejoins the Dodgers rotation after being sent to Triple-A prior to the All-Star break. He's made just one big league start since June 9 and owns a 3.45 ERA across 11 appearances (10 starts) this season.

home_pitcher_note: Mahle gave up six runs on eight hits with three walks and three K's in 5 2/3 frames his last time out vs. the Bucs in a four-run 6th that proved to be his demise. The 6th has been a thorn in Mahle's side as he owns a 9.31 ERA in that frame this year.
away_pitcher_note: Set to make his MLB debut, Suarez will become the first lefty starter for the Phillies since Adam Morgan on Sept. 28, 2016. In three starts since being promoted from Double-A Reading to Triple-A Lehigh Valley, Suarez, 22, has allowed just one run.

home_pitcher_note: DeSclafani gave up three runs on six hits in 4 1/3 frames in his last outing vs. the Bucs. He battled a rain delay and gave up two HRs. He has failed to go six innings in 3 of his past 4 starts but has boosted the rotation since coming off the DL.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta recorded nine strikeouts while walking none his last time out, but a rough first inning stained his day. He has a 6.60 ERA since the beginning of June and will look to find the form that earned him a 3.26 ERA through May.

home_pitcher_note: Harvey was roughed up in his last start against the Pirates and gave up eight runs on eight hits, including four home runs. The outing snapped a string of five consecutive starts without a loss. Harvey went 4-0 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez, in his most recent start, completed the seventh inning for the first time since July 30, 2017, and fanned seven Padres in the scoreless outing. He owns a 2.38 ERA over his last six starts, a span in which opposing batters have hit .134.

home_pitcher_note: Castillo threw 5 1/3 innings in his last outing vs. the Cards. The righty gave up one run on four hits, with five strikeouts and a walk. Castillo has allowed three runs or fewer in his past 4 starts and is searching for his first win since June 22.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin’s 2 2/3-inning outing Monday marked his shortest start since his debut in June 2016. The Dodgers tagged him for three homers. Eflin will look to get back on track after finishing the first half with wins in six of his seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Price’s start vs. the Orioles lasted an inning before the game was postponed due to rain. Despite a rough July with 6.43 ERA this month, he’s been solid since the All-Star break, with five strikeouts and no runs allowed in 6 1/3 innings vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Nola had his shortest home outing of 2018 last week when he allowed three runs to the Dodgers over five innings. Still, with 12 wins, a 2.42 ERA and an opposing batting average of .199, Nola has been one of baseball’s best starting pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: Pomeranz allowed six hits, four runs, two homers and two walks in 4 2/3 innings vs. the O's. Pomeranz’s second start since recovering from left biceps tendinitis will test him against the likes of Brian Johnson, who has impressed as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta is looking to finish a solid July. He is 3-0 with a 3.18 ERA in five starts this month. This followed a scintillating May (0.90 ERA) and a forgettable June (6.66 ERA). Arrieta’s presence in the rotation should only help in the stretch run.

home_pitcher_note: Gabe Kapler issued Pivetta a vote of confidence following a loss last weekend in Cincinnati. Pivetta is 1-6 with a 6.84 ERA in 10 starts since June 1, but the Phillies point to his xFIP, which ranks among the game’s best.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez opens August for the Marlins with his sixth Major League start since being called up at the end of June. The righty was roughed up in his last outing against the Nationals, surrendering four runs on nine hits in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez has been quietly on a roll. In eight appearances (seven starts) since allowing 10 runs against the Brewers on June 8, he is 3-1 with a 2.48 ERA. Opponents have hit .163 against him in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie was dominant in his last outing on Saturday -- 3 hits over 6 shutout innings to go along with 8 strikeouts. Richards has flown a bit under the radar but has been Miami's best starter of late. He's 1-0 with a 2.30 ERA in his last 5 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin had been on a roll from June through early July, but the results have not been there lately. He is 0-1 with a 6.92 ERA in his last three starts. He has allowed five home runs in 13 innings in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Urena finally broke out of a season-long funk on Sunday, giving up just one hit over six innings as part of a two-hit shutout of the Nats to earn his first win since June 15. It was also his first home win since last September.

home_pitcher_note: Nola, who was the Phillies' lone All-Star representative, pitched beautifully Monday against the Red Sox, allowing just one run in eight innings. He is 3-4 with a 3.79 ERA in nine career starts against Miami.
away_pitcher_note: Straily encountered some bad luck in his last start, allowing eight runs (five earned) in 3 2/3 IP at Atlanta. It was the first time in seven starts he didn't pitch into at least the sixth. On April 30 vs. the Phils, he gave up 4 runs in 4 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After two straight shaky starts, Godley threw a gem last time out against the Rangers. He allowed just two hits and a walk while striking out 10 in seven shutout innings. It was his finest performance of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta went 4-0 with a 2.80 ERA in six starts in July, capping the month Tuesday at Fenway Park. He allowed just one run and struck out seven in seven innings against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke suffered the loss in his last start against the Giants, but deserved a better fate as he allowed just two runs over six innings. Over his last eight starts, Greinke is 6-1 with a 1.37 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies believe Pivetta’s 6.42 ERA over his past 11 starts is not indicative of the way he has pitched or will pitch down the stretch. He has struck out 73 and walked 17 in 54 2/3 innings in that 11-start span.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin picked up the win in his last start, though he did not have his best stuff. The left-hander allowed three runs on seven hits while striking out eight in six innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez is living up to his potential. He has a 2.18 ERA (11 earned runs in 45 1/3 innings) in eight starts since he allowed 10 runs to the Brewers in early June. He has struck out 45 and walked 18 in that span.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old right-hander is slated for his big league debut after posting a 1.84 ERA in 10 starts in the Minors this season. A third-round pick in the 2015 Draft, Nix is rated as the Padres' No. 14 prospect per MLB Pipeline.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin needed just 85 pitches to get through eight innings of work against the Marlins on Aug. 4. He surrendered two homers, though, the second of which prevented him from going the distance.

home_pitcher_note: Lockett was done in by one rough inning in Chicago last Saturday. He allowed five runs in the second, but held the Cubs scoreless otherwise in five frames. With a temporary six-man staff, Lockett could be pitching to keep his spot in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Nola is the Phillies’ ace, but he is still looking for his first win since the All-Star break. He has posted a 2.88 ERA in four starts since he was the Phillies’ lone representative at the All-Star Game.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander hasn’t completed six innings since returning from a right hip strain in mid-June. But he owns a 3.48 ERA over his last seven starts. Lucchesi struck out nine Cubs over 5 2/3 innings in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta pitched eight scoreless innings Monday against the D-Backs, but the bullpen blew the lead in the ninth and the Phillies lost in 14 innings. But Arrieta is 4-0 with a 2.28 ERA in a seven-start stretch since the end of June.

home_pitcher_note: Pivetta pitched well in April and May but struggled in June and July. His first two starts in August, however, have looked like his first two months, which is encouraging. He has allowed two runs in 12 innings, striking out 13 and walking one.
away_pitcher_note: After a lights-out start against the Yankees, Porcello was roughed up last time out, getting tagged for seven runs in four-plus innings in Toronto. It was the third time in his past five starts that Porcello gave up at least four runs.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez struggled in his last start against the D-backs, as he lacked life on his four-seam fastball. But he otherwise has been a bright spot in the Phillies’ rotation, posting a 3.18 ERA in 15 starts since the end of April.
away_pitcher_note: Eovaldi will seek a bounceback start after going only 2 2/3 innings and allowing eight runs (four earned) his last time out against the Orioles. In his two previous starts, the righty didn't allow a run in 15 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suarez got the win in his first Major League start, despite giving up four runs on six hits in five innings against the Reds. The left-hander gave up two homers in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Mets manager Mickey Callaway has said that as long as Oswalt continues to pitch well, the Mets will make space for him in their rotation. He hasn’t disappointed so far, posting a 3.68 ERA and 1.23 walks per nine innings over his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin was sent to Triple-A to make room for Justin Bour, not for any lack of success. The righty has a 4.91 ERA since the All-Star break and held the Padres to two runs over six innings last time out.
away_pitcher_note: After missing two starts with a strained flexor-pronator muscle in his left forearm, Matz will come off the DL to face the Phillies for the third time in his career. He went 0-1 with a 2.53 ERA in the two prior outings, both at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: The All-Star righty snapped a four-start winless stretch last time out by firing six scoreless innings against the Padres. He’s held the Mets to three runs in 18 innings over three starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: While Syndergaard hasn’t been at his dominant best too often this season, he has quietly gone 4-1 with a 3.56 ERA since the start of July. Those numbers include 24 strikeouts, six walks and only one home run in 30 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta is coming off a tough start, having allowed five runs in five innings to the Padres last weekend in San Diego. The former Cy Young Award winner is 9-7 with a 3.33 ERA in 23 starts in his first season with the Phils.
away_pitcher_note: All eyes will be on deGrom every time he takes the mound from here on out, as he pursues the National League Cy Young Award. He has gone 21 consecutive starts allowing three runs or less, putting him three shy of Dwight Gooden’s club record.

home_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old Pivetta held baseball’s best offense to one run over six innings last time out, though he got a no-decision against the Red Sox. He’ll look to build off three strong August starts after struggling for much of June and July.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas pitched into the sixth inning for the first time this season in his last start, offering a glimpse of the lefty's potential. The team hopes to give Vargas as many innings as possible down the stretch.

home_pitcher_note: After struggling for more than a month, Roark has become one of the Nats' most consistent starters lately. In his past five starts he has posted a 1.77 ERA with 28 strikeouts and five walks and gone 5-0.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez allowed four hits and four walks in just 2 1/3 innings during his last start. He'll look to regain the form he carried from July into August, when in a span of five appearances he posted a 0.71 ERA with 22 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg returns from the disabled list to make his first start since July 20 after missing about a month with a pinched nerve in his neck. After he tossed a 70-pitch simulated game last week, the Nats determined he did not require a rehab start.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin is expected to be recalled and added to the active roster prior to Wednesday’s game. After a shaky two-run first inning, Eflin fared fine during his last start, allowing four earned runs over 6 2/3 innings to earn a win against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer seems poised to be locked in a duel for the NL Cy Young Award for the rest of the season as he aims to capture what would be his third straight. He has made one start against the Phillies this year with 6 1/3 innings of one-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Nola’s Cy Young Award-caliber season continued in his last outing, when he allowed a run and struck out 11 in seven innings against the Mets for his 14th win, marking the fifth time he’s reached double-digit strikeouts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Borucki will look to bounce back from the roughest outing of his young career. In his last start, at Yankee Stadium on Sunday, Borucki could not get out of the first inning as he allowed six runs on four hits and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Arrieta pitched six one-run innings against the Mets in his last outing, the lone run produced in part because of an errant pickoff throw. He struck out six and walked none. Since a rough June, Arrieta has posted a 2.82 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez returns from the disabled list to make his first start since June 21, when he pitched just one inning against the Angels. He has a 4.52 ERA in 15 starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: The native Canadian faces the Blue Jays for the second time in his career and the second time this season. He allowed two hits in five innings in a 5-3 loss to Toronto on May 27 at Citizens Bank Park, striking out seven and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada has pitched into the sixth inning in his past four starts. He has a 5.40 ERA in his five starts since coming off the disabled list on July 30.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez has a 4.15 ERA in his last five starts, and he has lasted more than four innings in just two of them. That included Tuesday's start vs. the Nats, when he lasted four innings. That was in part because of a nearly two-hour rain delay.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin needs to get back on track. He has a 5.59 ERA (23 earned runs in 37 innings) in his last seven starts, dating to July 9. The Phillies are 2-5 in those games. He allowed 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings Wednesday against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg makes his second start since returning from the DL, after allowing five runs in four innings Wednesday against the Phillies in D.C. Strasburg threw 84 pitches in that game and blamed a lack of endurance for a velocity dip in the fourth
