away_pitcher_note: Scherzer gets another chance at the Phillies, after losing 2-0 Thursday at Nationals Park. Those were the only two runs he has allowed in his past three starts. The Nats are 6-0 when Scherzer has started at Citizens Bank Park, and he has a 1.65 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta allowed four runs in six-plus innings Friday in Toronto, but he has pitched well for more than a month. After a rough June, Arrieta is 4-3 with a 3.13 ERA in 10 starts. Opponents have hit .233 against him in that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez hopes to build on his last start against the Mets, when he allowed one run in seven innings. He had allowed 13 runs in the two starts before that. This will be his third start of the season against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies tout Pivetta’s FIP and xFIP, but the overall results have not been there lately. He has allowed 11 runs in 10 1/3 innings in his last two starts. He has a 5.92 ERA in 11 appearances (10 starts) since late June.
away_pitcher_note: Quintana has been tough to figure out. His last outing vs. the Reds was a perfect example. He was solid for three innings, then needed 36 pitches to get through the fourth. Quintana is 5-6 with a 3.91 ERA on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Maybe it is coincidence, but Eflin is 1-1 with a 6.46 ERA in three starts since the Phillies optioned him to Triple-A earlier this month, giving them an extra bat off the bench for a few days.
away_pitcher_note: Hendricks held the Reds to two hits over seven innings to pick up his 10th win in his last outing. He will hate to turn the calendar, as he is 15-3 all time in August. He lost to the Phillies on June 5, giving up five runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies moved up Nola’s start by one day so he could have an extra start at home. There is a reason for that. He is 9-0 with a 1.94 ERA in 13 starts this season at Citizens Bank Park.
away_pitcher_note: Lester took a no-decision in his last outing against the Mets but he's on a good roll with a 2.04 ERA in his last three starts. The left-hander is 7-0 with a 1.64 ERA in nine career starts against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Urena hit some rough patches in August. His ERA in five starts for the month spiked to 5.33. For the season, the right-hander has performed better at home with a 4.45 ERA. But his mark at Marlins Park is 1-9. After the break, his ERA is 5.09.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez allowed two runs in five innings Sunday in a victory over the Blue Jays, but lately he has struggled to pitch deep into games. He has a 5.87 ERA in his past four starts, pitching four or fewer innings in three of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Record aside, Richards has shown steady improvement, and the rookie now has more strikeouts than innings pitched. He's fanned 103 in 101 1/3 innings. In his past seven starts, he has struck out 46 in 38 2/3 innings, with an ERA of 3.49.
away_pitcher_note: Since pitching eight scoreless innings against the D-backs on Aug. 6, Arrieta is 0-3 with a 6.30 ERA (14 earned runs in 20 innings). He is 1-1 with a 4.91 ERA in three starts this season against Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Alcantara will make his second start for Miami. In his Fish debut, he went five innings on June 29 vs. the Mets, giving up one run on three hits, walking five while striking out one. Alcantara pitched eight games for the Cards in '17, all in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta grinded through five innings against the Cubs his last time out, allowing just one run with six strikeouts against maybe the NL's best lineup. The right-hander has now pitched at least five innings in eight of his last 9 starts.

away_pitcher_note: The National League Cy Young Award candidate allowed four runs in a start for just the third time this season in Sunday’s loss to the Cubs. He is 3-0 with a 1.44 ERA in four starts this season against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Recently bemoaning his lack of mechanical consistency, Syndergaard spent significant time working on it between starts with fine results. He pitched the first complete game of his career last time out in San Francisco, holding the Giants to two hits.
away_pitcher_note: It might or might not be a coincidence, but since the Phillies optioned Eflin to Triple-A in August in a roster move that allowed them to carry an extra player without Eflin actually missing a turn in the rotation, he is 1-2 with a 6.20 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Nola hopes to build upon a brilliant 2018, when he finished third for the National League Cy Young Award. He gets his second consecutive Opening Day start. The last Phillies pitcher to have more than two? Roy Halladay from 2010-12.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran will join Warren Spahn as the only Braves pitchers to make at least six consecutive Opening Day starts. The right-hander has posted a 2.73 ERA in his previous five season openers.

home_pitcher_note: Pivetta is the sabermetrician’s pick to click in 2019. He has great stuff, so while he posted a 4.77 ERA in 33 appearances (32 starts) last season, he also posted a 3.80 FIP. A step forward would be huge for the Phillies’ rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson, who is ranked the club's No. 7 prospect, has thrived since developing a changeup last year, but his slider is what impressed the Braves most this past spring.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies are hoping for a bit of a resurgence for Arrieta in his second season in Philly. He was 9-6 with a 3.11 ERA through his first 22 starts last season. He finished 1-5 with a 6.35 ERA in his final nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Blessed with the highest upside among the Braves’ highly-regarded young pitchers, Wright exceeded expectations throughout an impressive spring. He’ll be making his first start and looking to validate his status as MLB Pipeline’s 30th-best prospect.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will face the Phillies on Tuesday as he makes his first start vs. former teammate Bryce Harper. Scherzer struck out 12 over 7 2/3 innings on Opening Day, the most whiffs in franchise history to start the season.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin went 11-8 with a 4.36 ERA in 24 starts last season, but the Phillies believe he will be better in 2019 because they believe in the predictive power of Fielding Independent Pitching. Eflin posted a 3.80 FIP last year.

home_pitcher_note: After a few down seasons spent battling injuries, Sanchez enjoyed a resurgent 2018, posting a 2.83 ERA in 136 2/3 innings with the Braves, earning a two-year deal with the Nationals this winter.
away_pitcher_note: Nola did not have his best stuff on Opening Day, walking a career-high five batters, but he battled and allowed only one run in six innings in a win over Atlanta.

away_pitcher_note: Odorizzi tied a career high with 11 strikeouts and allowed only one hit -- a Hanley Ramirez solo homer -- over six innings in a stellar season debut Saturday against the Indians. The 11 strikeouts matched his career best, set on May 9, 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta struggled with his command on Sunday in his season debut against the Braves, but perhaps only because of cold and windy conditions. He walked six in six innings in a game that featured a combined 19 walks and three hit batsmen.
away_pitcher_note: Pineda threw four shutout innings Sunday on only 40 pitches in his first appearance since July 2017. With Martin Perez pitching in relief on Friday, Pineda will likely get a full start this time around instead of being followed by Perez in a "piggyback" role".

home_pitcher_note: Eflin pitched brilliantly in his season debut on Tuesday in Washington. He tied a career-high nine strikeouts in five scoreless innings. He threw his slider a lot, getting five swings and misses with the pitch. It has become a weapon for him.
away_pitcher_note: Berrios didn't feel he had his best stuff on Tuesday but was pleased with his adjustments, as he lasted seven innings against an aggressive Royals lineup. He allowed seven hits and struck out only four, but limited the damage to three runs.

away_pitcher_note: Sanchez had his season debut cut short after he took a line drive off his hip, which left a bruise, but he doesn’t expect it will be an issue in this start. This will be his fourth consecutive start against the Phillies, dating back to last season.

home_pitcher_note: Nola has not been sharp in his first two starts, allowing seven runs in nine innings, walking seven and striking out 10. It is no reason to panic, but Nola's start against the Nats is worth watching closely because he is such a key to the season.

away_pitcher_note: This will be Hellickson's first start of 2019. He had a brief stint in the bullpen to begin the season, where he appeared in one game, tossing two innings and giving up two runs.

away_pitcher_note: Arrieta pitched well in seven innings Saturday against the Twins, throwing just 75 pitches, but he allowed three runs in a loss. Arrieta got one swing and miss, tying the lowest swing and miss rate of his career. No reason to worry, Arrieta said.

away_pitcher_note: Arrieta had a 2.25 ERA in his first four starts, but he has posted a 5.29 ERA in his last three. Still, he allowed just two earned runs in six innings Saturday in a loss to the Nationals. He has also pitched at least six innings in seven of his eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Keller took a no-decision in his most recent outing on Sunday at Detroit, allowing two earned runs over 5 1/3 innings, walking five and striking out six. This will be his first career appearance against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin will attempt to extend his stretch of strong starts, having surrendered only one run in at least seven innings pitched in each of his last two appearances. He'll be making his first career start against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Nola is coming off a strong outing -- allowing just three hits and one run over six innings in an 11-1 win over the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching five scoreless innings behind an opener last time out, Peralta will start this time as the Brewers recover from a 15-inning game on Saturday against the Cubs. Peralta's trouble typically comes in the first inning.

away_pitcher_note: Catcher Yasmani Grandal was right when he said Woodruff was close to a breakout. After pitching to a 5.81 ERA through his first five starts, he has limited opponents to three earned runs over 16 innings his last three times out.

away_pitcher_note: Gray earned the win when he held the Phillies scoreless over six innings in their last matchup on April 21. He is 2-2 on the road this season with a 4.40 ERA, and he is winless in his career at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Nola lasted just three innings following a 52-minute rain delay on Monday vs. the Brewers. It marked the third time in nine starts this season that the Phillies' ace has pitched four or fewer frames -- something he didn't do once in 2018.
away_pitcher_note: Senzatela gave up four runs and seven hits over six innings in his last outing against the Phillies on April 20. After that loss, he has recorded a win in two of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff struggled for the first time this season on Tuesday against the Brewers, allowing five runs in just four innings. That matched the total number of runs he had given up in his first 30 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland won against the Phillies on April 18, when he struck out seven and allowed only two hits in six scoreless innings. He also did not allow a walk. The lefty is 1-1 with a 3.71 ERA in three day games this season.

home_pitcher_note: Quintana will be making his ninth start of the season. He's struck out 50 while walking only 15, and his 51 1/3 innings pitched are a team high.
away_pitcher_note: After going the distance in two of his previous three starts, Eflin allowed four runs in five innings vs. the Brewers on Thursday. Still, the right-hander has a 1.80 ERA over his last four outings.

away_pitcher_note: Last time out, Walker won his first game as a Met, throwing seven shutout innings on 95 pitches against the Nationals. It was by far Walker's most efficient outing of the season; he'll be looking for more of that sort of thing in Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin will make his sixth start of the season, facing the Mets for the first time since 2019. Through 11 starts versus the Mets, Eflin has a record of 3-4 with a 5.21 ERA. On Tuesday, the righty gave up nine hits, his most since July '19.
away_pitcher_note: Peterson will face the Phillies for the third time in five starts, which might be an issue if not for his ability to adjust. After the Phillies tagged him for six runs in his season debut, Peterson fired a quality start against them a week later.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez will get a third consecutive start in place of left-hander Matt Moore, who has not pitched since being placed into COVID-19 protocols. Velasquez has a 5.40 ERA in his first two starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Houser originally was scheduled to start Sunday's series finale against the Dodgers, but the Brewers opted for a late change that pushed Houser back a day, which means he'll face the Phillies instead on an extra day of rest.

home_pitcher_note: Nola hopes history repeats itself against the Brewers. He is 3-0 with a 2.97 ERA in six career starts against Milwaukee. After throwing the first nine-inning shutout of his career on April 18, Nola has a 4.85 ERA in his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lauer earned a second start after tossing five scoreless innings in a sparkling team debut against the Dodgers on Thursday following a callup from the alternate training site. Lauer threw 73 pitches in that game and should be available to increase that number if he pitches well.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson did something on Friday that no Phillies starter other than Aaron Nola, Zack Wheeler and Zach Eflin has done this season: Anderson threw a pitch in the sixth inning. He hopes this is a step in the right direction.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies' offense has one of the Majors' 10 highest strikeout rates entering the series and Peralta is a strikeout pitcher, ranking in the top four among Major League qualifiers with a 40.2 percent K%.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler suffered from some bad defense in a long first inning Saturday against the Mets, but he recovered and did not allow another for six more innings. Wheeler is 1-1 with a 2.90 ERA in five career starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Woodruff has delivered five consecutive quality starts, the sort of stability that's crucial for a team fighting so many injury issues. He's allowed only one earned run in 18 career innings against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has pitched into the sixth in five straight starts, but he hasn't yet put two strong starts together. His best start of the season was completed April 9, when he limited the Phillies to one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin continues to pound the strike zone and keep the Phillies in games. He has walked just two batters in 38 2/3 innings this season, and one of those walks was intentional. His 1.3% walk rate is second-best among all qualified starters.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson had thrown 15 2/3 consecutive scoreless innings before allowing at least one run in each of the last three innings completed against the Blue Jays on Sunday. The rookie hurler relies heavily on what has consistently been a reliable changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez earned his fourth consecutive start in place of left-hander Matt Moore after allowing only one run in six innings in Monday's 4-3 victory over the Brewers. It was the second time since 2019 that Velasquez completed six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ynoa has become one of the game's top stories this year. The right-hander has allowed two runs or fewer in five of six starts and he has homered in both of his past two games.
away_pitcher_note: Nola threw 114 pitches in six innings Tuesday against the Brewers. He is 11-6 with a 3.03 ERA in 21 career starts against the Braves, although he is 2-4 with a 3.97 ERA in eight starts at Truist Park in Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Fedde is 2-4 with a 5.26 ERA in eight appearances (seven starts) in his career against the Phillies. He allowed five runs in as many innings in his last start on Wednesday vs. the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies have gotten just enough from Anderson in his last two starts. They won both games. But Anderson still has not pitched more than five innings in any of his first six starts. They would love to see him pitch deeper.

home_pitcher_note: Over 11 career starts against the Phillies, Lester is 8-1 with a 1.92 ERA. The only loss occurred in his last outing against them -- May 23, 2019, with the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler threw the second shutout of his career Thursday against the Brewers. He has reached the ninth inning in two of his last three starts. He has a 1.88 ERA during that stretch, striking out 23 and walking four in 24 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Since joining the Nationals, Corbin is 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA in six starts vs. the Phillies. He allowed three solo home runs in his last start on Friday against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin continues to pound the strike zone, which is a big reason for his strong start. He has walked only three batters in 45 1/3 innings in his first seven starts. And one of those walks was an intentional walk. He has struck out 42.

home_pitcher_note: Matz is still looking to recapture his April form, when he opened 4-0 with a 2.31 ERA. In his three starts since, he's pitched to a 9.22 ERA and been hurt by the long ball, but he feels he's close to making the right adjustments.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez allowed one run in 5 1/3 innings Saturday in a loss in Atlanta, but he continues to pitch well since he replaced left-hander Matt Moore in the rotation last month. Velasquez has a 3.20 ERA in his four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kay keeps his turn in the rotation as the Blue Jays continue to search for a long-term solution at the back end of the starting five. away_pitcher_note: Nola threw a career-low 58 pitches in four innings in Sunday's loss to the Braves. Since he threw a shutout on April 18 against the Cardinals at Citizens Bank Park, Nola is 2-1 with a 5.09 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ray is coming off a 10-strikeout performance against Atlanta and has reached 9 K's in three of his past four starts. Throwing harder with a curveball that hitters keep swinging through, Ray is on a roll of late.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson pitched for Toronto last season before signing a one-year deal with the Phillies over the winter. Anderson retired 15 of 16 at one point in Tuesday's win over the Nats in D.C., but he is still looking to record an out in the sixth inning this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler deserved a better fate Wednesday in DC. A defensive gaffe allowed the Nats to score their second run against him in six innings. Still, he has a 2.10 ERA in his last four starts, striking out 30 and walking five in 30 innings.
away_pitcher_note:

away_pitcher_note: Trevor Rogers will be looking for his third straight win when he takes the mound against the Phillies. In Rogers' last outing, against the D-backs, he went six innings and allowed one run on four hits. He also struck out seven and walked two.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez has been a nice surprise since he replaced left-hander Matt Moore in the rotation during April. In five starts, Velasquez has a 2.84 ERA. He has allowed one run in each of his last three starts, pitching at least 5 1/3 innings in each of those three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The last time through the order, Sandy Alcantara gave up eight runs in 1 1/3 innings against the Dodgers making it the shortest outing the Marlins starter had delivered through his nine starts. The righty held a 2.72 ERA before his quick exit.

home_pitcher_note: Since throwing the first nine-inning shutout of his career on April 18 against the Cardinals, Nola is 2-2 with a 4.58 ERA in five starts. He has allowed fewer than three runs in only one of those starts.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has at last rounded into form, notching a 1.61 ERA in his last four starts. Peréz labored in a start at Philly last season, walking six and allowing five hits and four runs over five innings in a no-decision.

away_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing righty has been inconsistent of late and he allowed six hits and four runs in five innings in his last start. Opponents are hitting .247 against him this season. He is 1-1 with a 4.05 ERA in five starts at Citizens Bank Park.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler is 2-0 with a 1.70 ERA in his past five starts. He has struck out 40 and walked five in 37 innings in that stretch. Wheeler's fastball command has been excellent, which has allowed him to work consistently ahead in the count.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will try to get out of the rut he has been in of late, in which he has given up four runs or more in three of his last four starts. Rodriguez was marvelous in his one previous start at Philadelphia, striking out 12 while allowing one run in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers went a career-high 7 2/3 innings in his last start, holding the Phillies to one run on five hits. He picked up his 100th career strikeout in the outing, and became the third-fastest Marlin to achieve the milestone.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin has struck out 57 and walked five in 57 1/3 innings this season as he continues to pound the strike zone with success. He has pitched six or more innings in each of his nine starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: After a career-worst outing (1 1/3 IP, 8 ER) against the Dodgers, Alcantara bounced back with six scoreless innings vs. the Phillies. He struck out nine, walked three and allowed just two hits.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez was scratched about 20 minutes before his scheduled start Thursday because of numbness in his right index finger. It has happened before, but the Phillies said Friday that Velasquez was fine, so he is expected to make his start against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Neidert was recalled to make a spot start with Jordan Holloway on the injured list. In three starts this season, Neidert was unable to complete five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Since Nola threw the first nine-inning shutout of his career on April 18 against the Cardinals, he is 2-3 with a 5.19 ERA in six starts. The Phillies are 2-4 in that stretch, and they need better from Nola if they want to get on a roll.

away_pitcher_note: Howard's fastball averaged 95.3 mph and touched 97.3 mph in his first two innings Saturday against Boston. It averaged 92.9 mph after that, which is a continuing and troubling trend for Howard, who suffered from those drop-offs last season, too.

home_pitcher_note: Yarbrough will make his seventh start of the season. He's faced the Phillies twice at home, owning a 2.25 ERA. In his last outing, the southpaw allowed three solo homers through six innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Wheeler not only has been the Phillies' best pitcher this season, he has been their best player. He dominated the Red Sox in 7 1/3 innings on Sunday, striking out a career-high 12 batters and allowing one run on three hits and one walk.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh will take the mound for his third start of the season as the Rays look for a series victory against the Phillies. McHugh has a 4.02 ERA through 15 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin has pitched six or more innings in each of his 10 starts this season. It is the longest streak by a Phillies pitcher since a 12-start streak by right-hander Aaron Nola from April 10-June 12, 2018.

away_pitcher_note: Velasquez continues to impress since he replaced Matt Moore in the rotation in April. He has a 2.30 ERA in six starts. He pitched six scoreless innings Tuesday against the Marlins. It was his first scoreless start of six-plus innings since 2018.

home_pitcher_note: Gray threw six innings in a 3-0 win over the Nationals on Thursday. He allowed two hits with one walk and struck out five. The key to getting several outs was his effective slider. He got several ground-ball outs, including five hit back to him.
away_pitcher_note: Nola allowed one run in six innings on Wednesday against the Marlins, but the past few weeks have been a grind. Since his April 18 shutout against St. Louis, he is 2-3 with a 4.65 ERA in seven starts. The Phillies are 2-5 in that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler struck out a career-high 14 batters Saturday against the Rays. He joins Curt Schilling and Steve Carlton as the only Phillies pitchers with three consecutive games with 10-plus strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer is 5-1 with a 2.63 ERA in his eight starts in Philadelphia since joining the Nationals in 2015. The Nats are 7-1 in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Howard makes his third start since replacing Chase Anderson in the rotation. He has a 3.86 ERA in his first two starts, although he has struggled with his velocity the deeper he pitches into the game. It is worth watching as he progresses.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals are undefeated in Ross' career starts vs. the Phillies. He is 2-0 with a 1.75 ERA against the NL East rival.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez had a 2.30 ERA in his first six starts after rejoining the rotation April 23, but he suffered his worst start Monday against the Reds, allowing six runs in just three innings. He hopes to get back on track this weekend.
away_pitcher_note: Voth gets the start as the Nationals go with a bullpen day in the series finale. He has added versatility to the Nats' pitching staff with the ability to throw multiple innings.

home_pitcher_note: Last Tuesday, Nola became the ninth pitcher in Phillies history to record 1,000 strikeouts. He is the third Phils pitcher to reach 1,000 before turning 28: Nola (27 years, 362 days), Steve Carlton (27 years, 137 days) and Cole Hamels (27 years, 174 days).
away_pitcher_note: Smyly will make his second start against the Phillies, who accounted for the first of the five times the lefty has allowed at least two homers in a game this year. His 2.70 home runs per nine innings would rank as the league's worst if he had enough innings to qualify.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin has not pitched since May 30 as the Phillies try to keep him fresh for the six-month season. He has already thrown 68 innings this year after tossing 59 innings last season.
away_pitcher_note: Davidson earned another start after limiting the Nationals to one hit over 5 2/3 scoreless innings on Thursday. The lefty's command issues didn't prove to be a problem as he managed to pitch around five walks. This will be his fourth career start.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler has pitched like a National League Cy Young candidate this season, but he sure could use a little help from his teammates. Wheeler suffers from some of the worst run support in baseball among qualified starters.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson held the Dodgers hitless through the first four innings of Friday's start, but he was chased during the fifth and needed 98 pitches to record 13 outs. The young hurler did not complete five innings in either of his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: After Velasquez posted a 2.30 ERA in his first six starts this season, he has an 11.57 ERA in his last two, allowing nine runs in just seven innings. The Phillies hope it is nothing more than a temporary blip.
away_pitcher_note: Taillon is coming off a no-decision against the Red Sox in which he allowed three runs on six hits over 5 1/3 innings. Taillon has pitched to a 3.52 ERA over his past three starts, spanning 15 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nola's 4.06 ERA after 13 starts is his slowest start since 2019, when he had a 4.63 ERA after 13 starts. For one reason or another, he has been struggling lately. He has a 4.97 ERA in nine starts since throwing a shutout in April.
away_pitcher_note: Germán has allowed three or fewer runs in each of his past nine outings and in 10 of his 11 starts this season. Last time out, he tossed 5 2/3 innings of one-run ball in a no-decision against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Gonsolin will make his second start of the season. He didn't make it out of the second inning on Wednesday vs. the Pirates after he issued five walks and allowed one earned run and two hits in 1 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Spencer Howard had the shortest of his three starts his last time out against the Nationals. Howard allowed one unearned run, two walks and one hit in 2 1/3 innings. The 24-year-old has a 2.89 ERA in 9 1/3 innings as a starter this season.

home_pitcher_note: Urías continues to show his value in his first full season as a starter. He’s tied for the MLB lead in wins. Urías has yielded 10 home runs and only 11 walks over 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: His last start may have been the bounce-back outing Zach Eflin he needed. He scattered eight hits while allowing just one run in six innings against the Braves. Eflin is searching for his first win since May 7, as he has gone 0-4 in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw bounced back in his last start Friday vs. Texas with six innings, one unearned run, three hits and one walk. Before then, he combined for 10 runs, 15 hits and four walks over two starts. Opponents are hitting .214 vs. Kershaw.
away_pitcher_note: In eight of his last nine starts, Zack Wheeler has completed seven or more innings. Wheeler went eight scoreless innings and struck out 12 batters his last time out. He has allowed two runs in 15 1/3 innings in June after posting a 2.08 ERA in six May starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto was charged with the loss after giving up five runs (four earned) over 5 1/3 innings in his last start against the Nationals on Sunday. He is 1-5 with a 5.30 ERA in 12 career starts against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling in back-to-back starts, Velasquez rebounded last weekend against the Yankees, allowing two runs in five innings. Velasquez has been mostly solid as a starter, posting a 3.95 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wood picked up his first win since May 16 on Monday, when he fired six innings of two-run ball against the D-backs. He is 3-3 with a 3.36 ERA in 14 career appearances against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: After posting a 5.68 ERA in six starts, Nola finally got the pitching performance he needed on Sunday against the Yankees. He pitched 7 2/3 scoreless innings to sweep New York. It was only the second time the Phillies won a Nola start since May 4.

home_pitcher_note: Long will make his first Major League start on Father's Day. The 25-year-old lefty pitched behind an opener in his first two appearances for the Giants, giving up five runs over nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching six or more innings in each of his first 10 starts, Eflin has pitched fewer than six in two of his last three. Eflin prides himself on pitching deep into games, so he hopes to get back on track against San Francisco.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler looks like a lock to make his first National League All-Star team, consistently pitching deep into games, racking up strikeouts and giving the Phillies a chance to win. If he keeps it up, he should be in NL Cy Young consideration.

away_pitcher_note: Fedde is riding a streak of 20 consecutive scoreless innings. He last faced the Phillies on May 11, when he struck out four and allowed three runs in five frames.
